title: Packers S Xavier McKinney: I see what's going on with officiating and it's killing us
summary: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur got heated with officials several times during Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions, but he didn't want to make them the focus of his postgame comments.
full_text: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur got heated with officials several times during Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions, but he didn't want to make them the focus of his postgame comments. LaFleur said there were "some tough calls," but that his team needed to rise above them. Among those tough calls were two roughing the passer penalties and an unnecessary roughness call on defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt for a hit that came without a clear whistle to stop play as Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown got up to continue running. While LaFleur didn't want to unload on the officials, safety Xavier McKinney was more willing to go there. He said it is not "great officiating" and that the calls are "kind of f—-ing up" the team's games. McKinney knows that could earn him a monetary penalty from the league, but he said he's fine with that because he feels he's telling the truth. "I would rather get fined and try to help my team out because I see what's going on, and it's killing us," McKinney said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com. "We all see it. We all see what's going on. Everyone sees what's going on, the fans see what's going on, we see what's going on when we're out there." All of the calls can't explain everything about the loss — Packers rookie Trey Smack missed a 26-yard field goal and had a 35-yarder blocked at the end of drives that could have also been finished with touchdowns — but McKinney's comments make it clear that they played a role.
author: Josh Alper

title: John Harbaugh: Sunday was a pivotal game, our guys took the bull by the horns
summary: The Giants came into Sunday's game in Houston off a tie and a loss that led to a quarterback change and oddsmakers installed them as heavy underdogs as a result.
full_text: '' The Giants came into Sunday's game in Houston off a tie and a loss that led to a quarterback change and oddsmakers installed them as heavy underdogs as a result. That proved to be a miscalculation. The Giants led for much of the first half and moved back in front in the fourth quarter before the Texans were able to rally and send the game to overtime. The Giants defense forced a stop and two big runs by Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary gave them a walk-off 27-21 win in their final game before the bye. Skattebo, Singletary, and Tyrone Tracy combined to run 28 times for 180 yards while J.J. McCarthy went 20-of-28 for 252 yards as part of a full-team effort that earned praise from head coach John Harbaugh after the game. Harbaugh said that people were "going to find out about who they are" in this game and that the players "took the bull by the horns" to improve to 4-2-1. "The two most important games of the season will be coming up after we come back from the bye, which will set the direction for the rest of the season really," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. "But we're going to be in this thing until the end now. This was a pivotal game. This was a really high-pressure game for our team. We didn't talk about that, but they all knew how important this game was, and they responded accordingly." Regardless of what happens on Monday night or next week, the Giants know they'll be in first place when they return to the field against the Eagles in Week 9. They'll follow that with a quick turnaround to the Commanders on Thursday night, which gives them a chance to take the NFC East by the horns at the start of the second half. Sunday's performance provided plenty of reason to think they can do exactly that.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kevin O'Connell: We're confident we're not far off offensively
summary: With the 49ers and Chiefs losing on Sunday, the Vikings are the last unbeaten team standing in the NFL and they are in some rare company when it comes to how they're winning games.
full_text: With the 49ers and Chiefs losing on Sunday, the Vikings are the last unbeaten team standing in the NFL and they are in some rare company when it comes to how they're winning games. The Vikings have scored 10 touchdowns in their six wins and, per ESPN, they are tied for the third-fewest touchdowns during a 6-0 start in NFL history. On Sunday, the team scored its only touchdown to take their first lead of the day in the fourth quarter and they finished their 16-10 win over the Colts with 275 yards of offense. After the game, head coach Kevin O'Connell pointed out near misses in the passing game and penalties as things that kept the offense from finding a groove and said that there's strong belief that things are going to fall into place. "I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," O'Connell said. "The far off changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going." The Vikings will kick off November with a trip to Detroit before moving on to face the Bills, Packers, 49ers and Falcons over the rest of the month. That makes it an ideal time for them to make a move from "not far off" to clicking in a way that will allow them to remain at the front of the NFC playoff race.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Tomlin supports Dan Campbell's late fourth-down decision
summary: Mike Tomlin has no qualms regarding a decision from Dan Campbell that may have seemed curious on the surface.
full_text: Mike Tomlin has no qualms regarding a decision from Dan Campbell that may have seemed curious on the surface. Facing fourth and one from the Detroit 24 with 4:53 to play, Campbell opted to go for it. The play resulted in a two-yard loss, and a very short field for the Packers. “I thought we would get it, number one," Campbell said after the game. "I really believed we would get that. Number two, I knew we would get the ball back if it didn’t work out. Those were the two thoughts." After Sunday night's Chiefs-Seahawks game, NBC's Mike Tirico asked Tomlin for his take on Campbell's decision. " It centers around elite quarterback play ," Tomlin said. "When you got elite quarterback play, and particularly when you're playing elite quarterback play, you want to make sure your guy at least has a chance to have the ball at the end of the game. And that's what that decision appeared to be about for me. If he punts that ball the way Jordan Love and company has been operating, it's not possible, it's probable that they're gonna matriculate the ball down the field and win the game. And so what he did by going for it, he was either gonna be successful and keep the ball for his quarterback, or he was at least gonna give his quarterback an opportunity to answer. I was always ready to make that decision when I had Big Ben [Roethlisberger], for example, and I was facing another elite quarterback." The Lions got the ball back because their defense stiffened, forcing a field goal try. And because the Detroit special-teams unit blocked the 35-yard try. But even if the Packers had scored a touchdown, the drive started with 4:50 to play. The Lions would have had a chance to answer. And that's only if the Lions first failed to gain a yard on fourth down by handing it to Jahmyr Gibbs. It's another tangible example of the key differences between analytics and feel. The coach, considering all circumstances, knew it was the right call. That said, the age of analytics had made it much easier to do something that would have once been ignored as unconventional, since reliance on the math has torn down the wall between what is and isn't "normal" for a coach to do. And Tomlin's past actions give his words even more credence. Via NBC Sports research, Campbell was the first coach to go for it on fourth down inside his own 25 in a tie game since Week 1 of the 2014 season. That day, Tomlin's Steelers ran a fake punt from their own 20 in a 27-27 game against the Browns. It happened with 9:48 to play in a 27-27 game. The play worked, the drive later stalled at the 50, and the Steelers won with a walk-off field goal, 30-27.
author: Mike Florio

title: Nick Emmanwori: Seahawks' defense was motivated to stop Kenneth Walker
summary: Walker entered Sunday night averaging 133 rushing yards a game. The Seahawks held him to 36 yards.
full_text: Heading into Sunday night in Seattle, the story of the game was Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker, who was off to an outstanding start to this season after leaving the Seahawks in free agency. After the game, the story was the Seahawks' defense shutting Walker down. Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori admitted after the game that he and his teammates were motivated to hold Walker in check, knowing how many people were criticizing the Seahawks for letting the reigning Super Bowl MVP leave for Kansas City in free agency. "I ain't gonna lie, I did," Emmanwori said. "I'm not gonna sit here and lie. I definitely did want to hold him under 100. I don't really listen to all the media noise but that was my motivation. I know a lot of dudes on defense, that was their motivation, too, to stop him under 100 and play lights out on defense and I think we did that." The Seahawks did more than just hold Walker under 100 yards. They held him to 36 yards on 14 carries, by far his worst game of this season and almost 100 yards below his average heading into Sunday night of 133 yards per game. Meanwhile, the Seahawks' much-maligned rushing game had a big night, with running back Emanuel Wilson gaining 100 yards and a touchdown and the Seahawks as a team gaining 153 rushing yards — more than triple the Chiefs' total. The Seahawks won 20-3, and the defense was disappointed because they wanted it to be 20-0. "We put on a clinic," Emmanwori said. "I know the defense, a lot of dudes were upset that we didn't give them a zero. That was our goal, give them zero. We definitely could've accomplished that. But that just says what type of defense we are. There's a lot of talk out there about what type of defense we are, if we've still got it or whatever. But we don't really pay attention to that, and we knew what we was fitting to do. None of us, we didn't lose any sleep about any offense or who we're facing." Who they were facing was the player who led the way as they won the Super Bowl eight months ago. But now he's in a different uniform, and the Seahawks wanted to show that they're the same Super Bowl team without him that they were with him.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Anthony Richardson doesn't regret his recent arrest for marijuana posession
summary: Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson was arrested last week for marijuana possession — presumably without taking a plutonium-powered Delorean back to 1955.
full_text: Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson was arrested last week for marijuana possession — presumably without taking a plutonium-powered Delorean back to 1955. The Colts, as explained by James Boyd of The Athletic , made Richardson available to speak to reporters after Sunday's loss at Minnesota. Via Boyd, Richardson was asked whether he regrets the incident. “ I enjoy life ," Richardson said. "I don’t really regret a lot of things I do. I appreciate my life. I appreciate God waking me up every morning." Richardson also said this about the incident, per Stephen Holder of ESPN: "I know my character , God knows my character, my family knows me. So I don't need to explain anything else." Given the widespread legalization of marijuana possession and use in 2026, Richardson has no general reason to believe that possessing or using marijuana reflects poorly on his character. More specifically, however, the arrest exposes him to discipline under the substance-abuse policy. From Section 2.3 of the policy: "Absent aggravating circumstances, discipline for a first offense will be a suspension without pay for up to four (4) regular and/or post-season games." It sounds ridiculous in this day and age, but Indiana has yet to join the many states that have abandoned outdated marijuana laws (except, apparently, while smoking it on the air during a TV show originating there). Now, unless Richardson avoids a conviction, a guilty plea, a no-contest plea, or a diversion program arising from the incident, Richardson will eventually be facing a four-game suspension and the significant loss of revenue coming from it. Because, again, players who are suspended lose 100 percent of their income during the suspension — unlike owners. If Richardson's case isn't resolved until 2027 (a bench trial was set for January 4 ), and if he signs somewhere next year even for the league minimum based on his experience of $1.26 million, he'll lose $280,000. Hopefully, the next CBA will be further tweaked to eliminate this provision from the substance-abuse policy. It's outdated, it's onerous, and it creates bizarre outcomes where players who have no control over where they're drafted are subject to the inconsistencies of the laws in the state where the late-April sorting hat has sent them to reside.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba on pace to break Calvin Johnson's yardage record, with a game to spare
summary: After his huge performance on Sunday night, the Seahawks' star receiver has 867 yards through seven games.
full_text: Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is on pace to break Calvin Johnson's NFL record for receiving yards in a season. And Smith-Njigba is on pace to do it without even needing the 17th game of the season. Through seven games this season, Smith-Njigba has 867 receiving yards. That's a pace of 123.9 yards per game. When Johnson set a new NFL record with 1,964 receiving yards in 2012, it was a 16-game season, so Johnson averaged 122.8 yards per game. So if Smith-Njigba keeps at his current pace, he'll break Johnson's record in the 16th game of the season, when he would be at 1,982 games. Smith-Njigba could break Johnson's record without even needing the benefit of the 17-game season. Smith-Njigba's 17-game pace is 2,106 yards, which would give him the only 2,000-yard receiving season in NFL history. Last season Smith-Njigba was the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year, but this season he's been even better. He's on his way to what might be the best season any wide receiver has ever had.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dan Campbell: I thought we'd get fourth-and-1, if not I knew we'd get the ball back
summary: Dan Campbell made the most Dan Campbell-like decision he could make on Sunday when the Lions faced fourth-and-1 at their own 24-yard line with the score tied and 4:53 remaining in the fourth quarter: He went for it.
full_text: Dan Campbell made the most Dan Campbell-like decision he could make on Sunday when the Lions faced fourth-and-1 at their own 24-yard line with the score tied and 4:53 remaining in the fourth quarter: He went for it. Campbell may be the only coach in the NFL who would have gone for it in that situation, and it didn't work, as Jahmyr Gibbs was tackled for a loss of two yards, putting the Packers in range for what would ordinarily be a chip-shot field goal to take the lead late in the fourth quarter. But while the decision didn't work in the moment, it turned out OK for the Lions, who blocked the Packers' field goal attempt and then marched down the field for a game-winning field goal of their own as time expired. Campbell explained his thinking after the game. "I thought we would get it, number one. I really believed we would get that. Number two, I knew we would get the ball back if it didn't work out. Those were the two thoughts," Campbell said. That's solid reasoning. Only needing a yard with Gibbs and a good offensive line, it's easy to see why Campbell thought his team would get it. But the second point is more important: Campbell wanted to ensure that the Lions would get the ball back with time to score. If the Lions had punted, there was the risk that the Packers would not only score on their subsequent possession, but run the remaining 4:53 off the clock and score with no time left. By giving the Packers the ball back deep in their own territory, Campbell at least knew the Packers wouldn't be able to mount a long drive that took all the remaining time off the clock. Instead, after the Packers missed that field, it was the Lions who took over with 3:21 remaining and a long field ahead of them, and the Lions' long drive allowed them to run out the clock before kicking their game-winning field goal. Campbell was wrong when he thought his team would make the fourth-and-1, but right that his team would get the ball back. And when his team got the ball back, it won the game.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sunday Night Football: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Seahawks defense dominate Chiefs, win 20-3
summary: Smith-Njigba had 150 yards while Seattle's defense stifled QB Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City's offense all night.
full_text: The defending Super Bowl champions looked like they could ride their defense to another title on Sunday night. Seattle's defense and receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba were the stars on Sunday night, as the Seahawks defeated the Chiefs 20-3. Kansas City was held off-balance throughout the night, leading to one of the lowest-scoring outputs of the Mahomes era. The Seahawks held the Chiefs to just 11 first downs, 213 yards, and 3-11 on third down. While no one had contained Kenneth Walker all year, the Seahawks were able to slow down their former running back. Walker rushed 14 times for 36 yards, averaging a paltry 2.6 yards per carry. He entered Sunday’s game averaging 6.3 over Kansas City’s first five contests. Mahomes finished the game 19-of-33 for 165 yards with an interception, working out to a 58.3 passer rating. Mahomes has finished with a worse passer rating in just four other regular-season starts in his career. As noted by the NBC broadcast, this was the first time the Chiefs did not even reach the red zone in a Mahomes start — including the postseason. Tight end Travis Kelce led with four receptions for 44 yards. He moved into fifth place all-time in receptions, but that’s likely little consolation given the result. On the other side, Sam Darnold finished 20-of-28 for 257 yards with a touchdown and an interception. That pick nearly led to Chiefs points at the end of the first half, but Harrison Butker’s 58-yard field goal attempt fell short. That was one of two misses from Butker, who also sent a 45-yard attempt wide right midway through the fourth quarter. That would have put the Chiefs down by seven with 8:33 to go. After the miss, Seattle put the game away with Emanuel Wilson’s 21-yard touchdown run. The Seahawks finished with 24 first downs, 410 total yards, and 11-of-16 on third down. Smith-Njigba set the pace, catching nine passes for 150 yards with a touchdown. The reigning AP offensive player of the year has registered at least 100 yards in six of his seven games so far this season, with five performances of at least 120 yards. The game’s result leaves the Vikings as the lone unbeaten team entering Week 8, as the 49ers also lost to the Falcons earlier on Sunday. Back above .500, the 4-3 Seahawks will host the 5-2 Bears next Monday night. Now at 5-1, the Chiefs will be back on the road next week to face the 5-2 Broncos on Sunday afternoon.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Travis Kelce moves to No. 5 all-time in receptions, passes Marvin Harrison, Cris Carter
summary: The Chiefs have been mostly stymied on offense throughout Sunday night’s matchup with the Seahawks.
full_text: The Chiefs have been mostly stymied on offense throughout Sunday night’s matchup with the Seahawks. But the unit did make some history in the fourth quarter of the contest. Tight end Travis Kelce moved into No. 5 all time in receptions with 1,103, passing Marvin Harrison. He had tied Harrison (1,102) and Cris Carter (1,101) earlier in the contest. Kelce has a long way to go to the next player on the list, as Jason Witten is at No. 4 with 1,228 career catches. Jerry Rice is atop the list (1,549), followed by Larry Fitzgerald (1,432), and Tony Gonzalez (1,325). With 13:11 in the fourth quarter, quarterback Patrick Mahomes found Kelce over the middle on third-and-6 to move the chains. Kelce ended up taking the historic catch 19 yards. With the reception, Kelce now has three receptions for 41 yards so far on Sunday. The Chiefs trail Seattle 13-3 midway through the fourth quarter.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Rashid Shaheed questionable to return to Seahawks-Chiefs with knee injury
summary: The Seahawks have an injury concern with one of their key weapons.
full_text: The Seahawks have an injury concern with one of their key weapons. Seattle announced receiver/returner Rashid Shaheed is questionable to return with a knee injury. Shaheed did not return the second-half kickoff, with Tory Horton performing those duties. Shaheed had a 32-yard punt return during the first half. UPDATE 10:35 p.m. ET : Shaheed has been downgraded to out. Additionally, running back Velus Jones Jr. is out with a hamstring injury.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Vikings register highest blitz rate of Next Gen Stats era, at 85.2 percent
summary: The blitz-happy Vikings defense took their habit to the highest level on Sunday against the Colts.
full_text: The blitz-happy Vikings defense took their habit to the highest level on Sunday against the Colts. Via NBC Sports research, Minnesota blitzed on 85.2 percent of the Colts' dropbacks on Sunday. It was the highest rate by any team in the Next Gen Stats era, which dates back to 2016. The effort limited the Colts to 64 net passing yards, thanks to four sacks that erased 44 yards. The challenge comes from the confusion created by the Brian Flores defense. The offense never knows who is and isn't coming until the snap. It forces the blockers to quickly diagnose the situation, and it requires the quarterback to process his reads before he gets knocked down. Minnesota needed that. The run defense wasn't getting it done on Sunday; the Colts gained 154 yards on the ground. By the time the final drive came, the Colts had no choice but to throw — and Minnesota's relentlessness forced quarterback Daniel Jones into his lone turnover of the day, a game-sealing interception. And that was enough to deliver a 16-10 win, moving the Vikings to 6-0 for the first time since 2009. While also extending Minnesota's winning streak to 11, the second longest in franchise history.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kirk Cousins: "If I'm not the best option, I don't want to be out there"
summary: As the Raiders were rattling off three straight wins to start the season, the decision to ride with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins was looking like the right way to go.
full_text: ''' As the Raiders were rattling off three straight wins to start the season, the decision to ride with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins was looking like the right way to go. Now that the Raiders have lost four in a row, it's fair to wonder whether the time for rookie first-rounder Fernando Mendoza's time to play is coming. Cousins was asked about the possibility of being replaced by the first overall pick in the draft after Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Ras. "It's really the same every day that it was in March or April," Cousins told reporters. "I mean, nothing changes in the sense that if I'm not the best option then I don’t want to be out there, either . I want our football team to have the best chance to win games, and if [in] the first OTA if that had become apparent, I would have been the first one to say, 'Yeah, you can't play me.' "So nothing changes, you know, and the organization will do what they feel is best. I feel that, you know, Fernando's done a great job and has a great future ahead, and I try to go out there and play as well as I possibly can help us win and give him a great example to learn from, until he does go out there eventually." At some point, however, it's less about who gives the team the best chance to win and getting Mendoza ready to try to win in 2027. Likewise, the powers-that-be could decide to give the team a spark by making a change — before the losses stack to the point at which a playoff berth is unrealistic — even before Medoza is technically the better performer.
author: Mike Florio

title: Broncos DT Zach Allen says he'll be fine after hurting hamstring
summary: Broncos defensive tackle Zach Allen offered a positive update on his health after Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
full_text: Broncos defensive tackle Zach Allen offered a positive update on his health after Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals. Allen had to leave the game late in the fourth quarter after injuring his hamstring. Allen remained on the sideline until the end of the game and told reporters at a press conference that he'll "be fine" moving forward. Allen had three tackles and three quarterback hits against the Cardinals on Sunday. He had 21 tackles, 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble coming into the game. The Broncos also saw wide receiver Jaylen Waddle leave the game in the fourth quarter and there's been no word about his condition heading into Week 8 at this point.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos will be without Pat Surtain II for third straight game
summary: The Broncos will be without cornerback Pat Surtain II again on Sunday.
full_text: The Broncos will be without cornerback Pat Surtain II again on Sunday. Surtain was listed as questionable to play against the Cardinals after returning to practice this week, but he landed on the team's inactive list on Sunday afternoon. It is the third straight game that Surtain has missed with an ankle injury. Quarterback Sam Ehlinger, safety Talanoa Hufanga, offensive lineman Kage Casey, tight end Dallen Bentley, defensive lineman Jordan Jackson, and defensive lineman Tyler Onyedim are the other inactives for Denver. Safety Budda Baker is active for the Cardinals after being tagged as questionable due to a groin injury and an illness. Cornerback Max Melton was also questionable and he will not play due to a knee injury. Running back Jeremiyah Love, offensive lineman Jon Gaines, safety Andrew Wingard, and defensive lineman Walter Nolen were ruled out on Friday. Quarterback Carson Beck and offensive lineman Albert Reese are the other inactives.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bo Nix's 62-yard TD run puts Broncos up 13-6
summary: Ryan Fitzpatrick might have a higher opinion of Bo Nix than he did the last time he saw the Broncos quarterback on the field.
full_text: Ryan Fitzpatrick might have a higher opinion of Bo Nix than he did the last time he saw the Broncos quarterback on the field. Nix broke loose for a 62-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter of Sunday's game in Arizona and the Broncos lead the Cardinals 13-6 as a result. It was the longest play of the season for the Broncos and it was their first run of at least 20 yards all year. Nix only had 37 rushing yards this season before that big play and the lack of threat as a runner had some wondering if his ankle was all the way back from last season's injury. That question was part of a diatribe from Fitzpatrick last Thursday that concluded with the Prime Video talking head calling Nix's play "garbage" so far this season. Sunday's touchdown certainly didn't fit that description and the Broncos hope that it's a sign of things to come for the quarterback.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos up 13-6 at halftime in Arizona
summary: The Cardinals defense was able to hold the Broncos in check for most of the first half of Sunday's game in Arizona, but one big play has made the difference for the visiting team.
full_text: The Cardinals defense was able to hold the Broncos in check for most of the first half of Sunday's game in Arizona, but one big play has made the difference for the visiting team. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix broke loose for a 62-yard touchdown run on a scramble in the second quarter. That broke a 6-6 tie and the Broncos forced a pair of Cardinals punts to head into halftime with a 13-6 lead. Denver only managed 98 net yards on their other 28 offensive plays in the first two quarters and they were 1-of-7 on third downs on their way to three punts of their own. Nix is 10-of-19 for 72 yards through the air and their eight non-Nix running plays have netted 30 yards. The Cardinals haven't been any better on offense. They have 117 yards and both of their field goals came after drives that moved inside the Broncos' 10-yard-line. Their eight plays inside that territory have resulted in four yards and falling short in that area joins Nix's big plays as the reason why the Cardinals are trailing at home.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos stretch lead to 27-13 at end of third quarter
summary: Explosive plays were in short supply for the Broncos in the first six weeks of the season, but they've found them in this Sunday's trip to Arizona.
full_text: Explosive plays were in short supply for the Broncos in the first six weeks of the season, but they've found them in this Sunday's trip to Arizona. Quarterback Bo Nix's 62-yard touchdown run in the second quarter staked the team to a 13-6 halftime lead and they came up with two more in the third quarter. Running back RJ Harvey caught a short pass from Nix and followed his blockers to an untouched 52-yard touchdown that put the Broncos up by 14 points. After a Cardinals touchdown turned it back into a one-score game, Nix found wide receiver Marvin Mims for a 47-yard gain that set the Broncos up inside the 10-yard-line. A pass interference penalty moved them to the 1-yard-line and running back JK Dobbins scored on the next play. That was also the final play of the third quarter and the Broncos are now up 27-13 in Arizona.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos beat Cardinals 30-16, extend winning streak to three games
summary: Bo Nix bounced back in Sunday's road win.
full_text: The discourse surrounding Broncos quarterback Bo Nix after Week 6's overtime win over the Seahawks was negative, but that's unlikely to be the case after this Sunday's game. Nix ran for a 62-yard touchdown and went 15-of-29 for 222 yards and another touchdown to lead the Broncos to a 30-16 road win over the Cardinals. The win extends the team's winning streak to three games and leaves them at 5-2 heading into next Sunday's home game against the Chiefs. The Chiefs blew the Broncos out in Week 1, but a Denver win next week would set up a good race in the AFC West over the second half of the season. More of the big plays that the Broncos used to fuel Sunday's win would make that a likelier result. In addition to Nix's touchdown, the Broncos saw running back RJ Harvey break a short pass for a 52-yard touchdown and wide receiver Marvin Mims picked up 47 yards to set up a JK Dobbins touchdown run. Those are three of the four longest plays of the year for the Broncos and the team will be looking to build on that in the weeks to come. A less positive development for the Broncos were a pair of late injuries. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle hurt his chest and defensive lineman Zach Allen hurt his hamstring late in the fourth quarter and neither player returned. That will make their status something to watch as they head into their date with Kansas City. The Cardinals got 10 catches for 111 yards and a touchdown from tight end Trey McBride, but they never really recovered from failing to score touchdowns on two first half trips inside the Broncos' 10-yard-line. A last-ditch effort in the final two minutes brought them back to the Denver 1-yard-line, but the Broncos defense held and the game came to an end after Nix kneeled out the clock. Arizona is now 2-5 and they'll head to Dallas for a game against the Cowboys next Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean Payton: Reverse that led to Jaylen Waddle injury was an "awful" play call
summary: Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Sunday's game against the Cardinals after suffering a chest injury on a fourth quarter play that head coach Sean Payton would like to have back.
full_text: Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Sunday's game against the Cardinals after suffering a chest injury on a fourth quarter play that head coach Sean Payton would like to have back. Payton tried to get the ball to Waddle on a reverse that saw quarterback Bo Nix flip the ball to the wideout in the backfield. Waddle couldn't handle the flip and stayed down after jumping on the ball to avoid a turnover. Waddle did not return to the 30-16 win and Payton chastised himself for the call without being asked about it in his postgame press conference. "It was awful," Payton said. Payton didn't offer a detailed update on Waddle's condition and it will be something to monitor as they move toward their Week 8 date with the Chiefs.
author: Josh Alper

title: Christian Watson, Matthew Golden are delivering for the Packers
summary: Although Green Bay's running game should get a boost on Sunday with the return of Josh Jacobs, the passing game is getting it done.
full_text: Although Green Bay's running game should get a boost on Sunday with the return of Josh Jacobs, the passing game is getting it done. Receivers Christian Watson, with 538 yards, and Matthew Golden, with 501, are the first Packers teammates to have more than 500 yards receiving through six games of a season in franchise history. Quarterback Jordan Love is fueling it. He and Bills quarterback Josh Allen are the only players with two or more total touchdowns in every game this season. If Love does it again at Detroit, he'll join Brett Favre (1995) and Aaron Rodgers (2011) as the only other Packers quarterbacks to do that through the first seven games of a season. In the years when Favre and Rodgers did it, they won the NFL MVP award. The Packers, who started 1-2, are looking for their fourth straight win. They haven't lost since the boo-inducing Lambeau Field opener on a Thursday night against the Falcons.
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers' top two centers are questionable to return
summary: Packers running back Josh Jacobs' first carry of the season has taken center Sean Rhyan off the field.
full_text: Packers running back Josh Jacobs' first carry of the season has taken center Sean Rhyan off the field. Jacobs and Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson rolled over Rhyan's left ankle from behind. The Packers list Rhyan as questionable to return with an ankle injury. Jacob Monk, who lost his starting right guard job after three games, replaced Rhyan at center. But he didn't last long, leaving with a quadriceps injury. Monk, too, is questionable to return. John Williams went in at center for the Packers' second series. Williams had not previously snapped in any game, including the preseason. The Packers did just fine, driving 74 yards in 12 plays to tie the game 7-7 on Tucker Kraft's 14-yard reception from Jordan Love. Love is 10-of-14 for 122 yards and a touchdown. The Packers should have scored on their first possession, but rookie Trey Smack missed a 26-yard field goal.
author: Charean Williams

title: Lions lead 7-0 as Jameson Williams scores TD, Trey Smack misses 26-yard field goal
summary: The Packers' offense did its job on the first possession of today's game in Detroit.
full_text: The Packers' offense did its job on the first possession of today's game in Detroit. Packers kicker Trey Smack did not. After the Packers marched deep into Detroit territory and had first-and-goal, the Lions' defense held, and Smack and the field goal team came onto the field for what should have been a chip shot. But after the Packers were called for delay of game and moved back five yards farther, Smack missed a 26-yard field goal. It was a disappointing ending to a good first drive, one on which Jordan Love threw the ball well and Savion Williams and Matthew Golden both made big plays. Packers running back Josh Jacobs, playing his first game of the season after the NFL allowed him to return from the commissioner's exempt list following a domestic violence accusation, had three carries for four yards on the drive. On the Lions' first drive, Jared Goff looked great, completing all three of his passes for 68 yards, the last of which was a 16-yard touchdown toss to Jameson Williams. It's 7-0 Lions.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Lions lead Packers 10-7 at halftime
summary: The Lions lead the Packers 10-7 at halftime, but they had a chance to make it more before halftime.
full_text: The Lions lead the Packers 10-7 at halftime, but they had a chance to make it more before halftime. Detroit drove 85 yards on 12 plays to the Green Bay 12 before Jahmyr Gibbs fumbled at the 8. Gibbs had the ball knocked out of his hand by his teammate, center Cade Mays. Linebacker Isaiah McDuffie recovered for the Packers with 19 seconds left in the half. It was the Lions' second turnover this season, their first since Gibbs lost a fumble in Week 1. The Packers stopped themselves, too, going 3-for-4 on fourth down in the first half, but the miss was a big one. They reached the Detroit 7 and faced a fourth-and-4. Instead of kicking the field goal, Matt LaFleur opted to go for it and Jordan Love threw a short pass to Matthew Golden, who was stopped for no gain. The Lions have outgained the Packers 239 to 206. Jared Goff is 13-of-17 for 204 yards and a touchdown, a 16-yard throw to Jameson Williams. Amon-Ra St. Brown has seven receptions for 135 yards. Gibbs has nine carries for 37 yards and three catches for 18 yards. Goff has passed Derek Carr (41,245) for the third-most passing yards through 11-career seasons in NFL history. Love is 16-of-26 for 191 yards and a touchdown, a 14-yard throw to tight end Tucker Kraft. Seven players have at leat one catch. Packers running back Josh Jacobs has five carries for 8 yards in his 2026 debut. He returned from paid leave this week. Packers defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt (ankle) is questionable to return. The Packers lost their top two centers on the opening drive, and Sean Rhyan (ankle) and Jacob Monk (quad) are questionable to return.
author: Charean Williams

title: Josh Jacobs' TD gives Packers 14-10 lead after Lions' second lost fumble
summary: Dan Campbell wasn't happy with the way the first half ended.
full_text: Dan Campbell wasn't happy with the way the first half ended. The Lions coach will be less thrilled with how the second half began. The Lions, who entered with only one fumble, have lost two fumbles in the last 1:07 of game time and center Cade Mays was responsible for both. Mays ran into running back Jahmyr Gibbs and knocked the ball out with 19 seconds left in the first half and the Lions on the doorstep of the end zone. On the second play from scrimmage in the second half, Mays had an aborted snap. Linebacker Isaiah McDuffie recovered both. McDuffie's second recovery set up Josh Jacobs' 25-yard catch-and-run to the end zone. Jacobs, who is making his 2026 debut after returning from paid leave, tip-toed the sideline. His touchdown has the Packers on top 14-10 with 12:14 left in the third quarter. Jacobs has six carries for 12 yards and three catches for 42 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jameson Williams scores second TD, Lions lead 17-14
summary: Jameson Williams' second touchdown of the day has the Lions back in the lead.
full_text: Jameson Williams' second touchdown of the day has the Lions back in the lead. The Lions wide receiver scored on a 10-yard reception after getting a 16-yard touchdown in the first half. It's the second game in a row Williams has scored two touchdowns. The Lions lead 17-10. Detroit drove 80 yards in 10 plays after the Packers took a 14-10 lead after the Lions' second fumble of the game. Center Cade Mays was responsible for both fumbles, though that's not the way it goes down in the stats. Mays inadvertently knocked the ball out of Jahmyr Gibbs' arm with 19 seconds left in the first half and then had an aborted snap on the second snap of the second half. The Lions have outgained the Packers 314 to 248. Goff is 18-of-22 for 262 yards and two touchdowns, and Williams has five catches for 91 yards and two touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Lions beat Packers 20-17 on last-play field goal
summary: The teams combined for 739 yards but only 37 points as they went a combined 3-of-9 in the red zone.
full_text: The Packers-Lions game was drunk. The officiating might have been drunker. The Lions prevailed 20-17 on a 22-yard field goal by Jake Bates on the final play. The Lions are 4-2 and the Packers 4-3. The teams combined for 739 yards but only 37 points. They were a combined 3-of-9 in the red zone, had a combined three turnovers and three times turned it over on downs. The Lions inexplicably went for it on fourth-and-1 at their own 24 with 4:53 left in a tie game. Keisean Nixon stopped Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs for a 2-yard loss, setting up the Packers in field-goal range. Green Bay reached the Detroit 17 before rookie kicker Trey Smack missed his second field goal of the day and his seventh of the season. His 35-yard attempt was blocked by DJ Wonnum with 3:21 left. He also missed from 26 yards earlier in the game but made a 43-yarder with 7:10 left to tie it at 17-17. The Lions then drove 71 yards in 10 plays, with Gibbs taking a knee at the Green Bay 3 to set up a last-play field goal. The Packers had two questionable roughing the passer calls, including one on Karl Brooks on the game-winning drive. Brenton Cox Jr. also had one in the second half. Jordan Love had a questionable grounding call. Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes had a questionable unnecessary roughness penalty. Fox analyst Tom Brady was critical of all four calls. The Lions gained 415 yards, with Jared Goff going 22-of-32 for 303 yards and two touchdowns. Jameson Williams had five catches for 91 yards and two touchdowns. Amon-Ra St. Brown led the way with nine receptions for 153 yards. Gibbs had 29 carries for 116 yards and five catches for 27 yards but lost a fumble, his second of the season. Packers linebacker Isaiah McDuffie recovered both Lions' fumbles. Love was 27-of-45 for 274 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. Brian Branch had the pick in his return from an Achilles injury that ended his 2025 season. Josh Jacobs, who was returning from unpaid leave that kept him out six games, had 11 carries for 36 yards and five catches for 55 yards and a touchdown but couldn't come down with a catch in the end zone on the Packers' final drive. Christian Watson caught five passes for 57 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Matthew Stafford touchdown pass gives Rams 7-0 lead over Raiders
summary: It took the Rams a drive to warm up, but they have been able to take an early lead over the Raiders.
full_text: ''' It took the Rams a drive to warm up, but they have been able to take an early lead over the Raiders. Matthew Stafford hit Davis Allen for a 3-yard touchdown pass to go up 7-0 with 6:25 left in the first quarter. Stafford has started the game 6-of-6 for 38 yards with the score. While he’s dealing with a calf issue, Puka Nacua has three catches for 26 yards and took a carry 7 yards. Blake Corum also has 14 yards on three carries and an 8-yard catch. Raiders kicker Matt Gay missed a 51-yard field goal wide left on Las Vegas’ previous possession to keep the team off the board.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Davis Allen's second TD catch gives Rams 14-3 lead over Raiders
summary: The Rams have extended their lead in Las Vegas.
full_text: ''' The Rams have extended their lead in Las Vegas. Tight end Davis Allen caught his second touchdown of the day to put Los Angeles up 14-3 over the Raiders with 10:01 left in the second quarter. The score capped a 12-play, 80-yard drive that took 5:50 off the clock. Matthew Stafford has started the game hot, as he’s completed 12-of-14 for 96 yards with two touchdowns. Puka Nacua has five catches for 45 yards. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum have been able to get going in the run game, with Williams gaining 24 yards on four carries so far. Corum has 14 yards on three carries, with the Rams as a team averaging 5.6 yards per attempt. Raiders tight end Ian Thomas is questionable to return with a shoulder injury.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Matthew Stafford becomes Rams leader in TD passes, first to be No. 1 for two teams
summary: For the second time in his career, Matthew Stafford has reached No. 1.
full_text: ''' For the second time in his career, Matthew Stafford has reached No. 1. With his 11-yard touchdown pass to Puka Nacua in the second quarter, Stafford became the Rams’ all-time leader in passing touchdowns. He is also the Lions’ franchise leader with 282 touchdowns in 165 games. Los Angeles leads the Raiders 21-3 in the second quarter. He is the first player to hold the franchise record for touchdown passes for two of the current 32 NFL clubs. On Sunday, Stafford passed Roman Gabriel who held the previous record with 154 touchdown passes in 130 games from 1962 to 1972. Stafford now has 155, accomplishing the feat in 81 games. On Sunday, he threw two touchdowns to Davis Allen before his throw to Nacua. On Sunday, Stafford is 15-of-17 for 126 yards with three touchdowns so far in the first half.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Eagles vs. Cowboys prediction, odds, pick: Dallas visits injury-ravaged Philadelphia on Monday Night Football
summary: Dallas has dropped two straight games, but Philadelphia enters the NFC East matchup without Jalen Hurts
full_text:
In the Week 7 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Philadelphia Eagles play host to the division rival Dallas Cowboys .
Philadelphia has lost four consecutive games after starting the season 2-0, and enters this game ravaged by injuries. Not only is Jalen Hurts out in the wake of blood clots being found in his calf and lungs, but DeVonta Smith , Dontayvion Wicks , Nolan Smith and more will also miss the game, while Saquon Barkley , Landon Dickerson , Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt are all questionable.
Dallas has lost back-to-back games in dispiriting fashion, with its offense sputtering at the worst possible time, combining for 29 points against the Buccaneers and Packers after scoring 30-plus in each of the previous three games. The defense was already under fire early in the season, and now the Cowboys have questions on the side of the ball where they were supposed to be elite.
Which of these two teams will stop their losing skid? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Dallas has struggled badly on offense over the last two weeks. The Cowboys did total over 300 yards against both the Buccaneers and the Packers, but those totals are misleading. They were entirely unable to deal with blitzes for essentially all of both contests, and that failure brutally undermined their passing attack. ( Dak Prescott , typically excellent against blitzing defenses, went just 20 of 38 for 194 scoreless yards when confronting extra rushers in those games.) They also ran the ball for a mere 98 yards combined in those two games, despite the fact that star guard Tyler Smith returned to the fold.
The struggles came a bit as a surprise considering the Cowboys had previously been cooking offensively, racking up yardage and points through the first four weeks of the season. But both Todd Bowles and Jonathan Gannon came out with a plan that toyed with Dallas' protection rules up front, and the Cowboys found themselves unable to respond. They'll need a significantly better plan on Monday night, but it's notable that the Eagles blitz far less often than the Bucs and Packers did against the Cowboys.
The Bucs and Packers sent extra rushers after Prescott on 38.8% of his dropbacks in Weeks 5 and 6, per Tru Media. The Eagles have blitzed just 24.1% of the time so far - the fourth-lowest rate in the NFL . Vic Fangio would have to significantly depart from his modus operandi for Philadelphia to employ a strategy similar to the one that dominated Dallas over the last two weeks. For what it's worth, Philly has blitzed on at least 38% of opponent dropbacks just once since Fangio became the team's defensive coordinator. It would be wildly out of character to break out such a strategy here - but it's one worth pursuing considering Dallas' struggles.
Philly checks in 20th in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, allowing opponents to complete only 60.4% of passes at an average of 7.0 yards per attempt, but giving up eight touchdown passes against just three interceptions and being helped along by 14 opponent drops - second-most in the league.
Cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell , Riq Woolen and Cooper DeJean are tough to beat, but they have also been asked to cover for too long on some dropbacks because of the Eagles' inability to generate pressure. Philly has gotten a sack, hit or hurry on only 32.9% of opponent dropbacks, and they rank below-average in both average time to pressure and average time to throw. Quarterbacks, in other words, have been fairly comfortable in the pocket. And if you let Prescott get comfortable in the pocket, he can pick you apart with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , among his other targets.
The Cowboys seem highly unlikely to find success running the ball, which they haven't done all year. Javonte Williams has seven rushing touchdowns, but he's also averaging only 3.7 yards per carry, down considerably from his 4.8 average last season. The offensive line is not clearing rushing lanes for him, and he's not making anybody miss to make up for it. It's a brutal combination, and with Philly allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, it's not an advantageous one here.
The Eagles enter this game just about as banged up as possible on offense. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is out. His top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, are also out. Guard Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve, though he has been designated to return and listed as questionable for this game. Running back Saquon Barkley is questionable as well, and his top two backups — Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley — are on injured reserve.
Without Hurts under center last week, the Eagles operated with a pass-heavy bent. Tanner McKee dropped back to throw 48 times, and while some of that was due to game script and some of it due to Barkley's absence, it's worth noting that he had previously made two Week 18 starts and dropped back to pass an average of 44 times in those games as well. The Eagles can't use the quarterback run game with McKee under center like they can with Hurts, and the rest of their run-game efficiency is likely to suffer as a result of not presenting that threat to the defense. It's somewhat reasonable to expect them to be pass-heavier than we're used to here.
That may not be the case if Barkley returns to the lineup, but it is at least somewhat difficult to parse what the Eagles would prefer to do in that situation. Barkley has actually averaged 5.5 yards per carry in each of the two games he's made it through healthy this season. The problem is that the rest of the backs have been extremely inefficient in his absence and he wasn't efficient before leaving the other two games due to injury, either. He fully practiced on Friday for the first time since his hamstring injury, but the team may not want to load him up with too many touches in his first game back in the fold.
Every team that is humanly capable of running the football (i.e., not the Texans or Packers) has done so at will against the Cowboys this season, with Dallas' other five opponents each piling up at least 165 yards on the ground. Opponents have clipped the Cowboys for 4.7 yards per carry, with running backs and quarterbacks alike able to find considerable room to run against a disappointingly friendly Dallas front. If the Eagles can get Barkley (or Dameon Pierce ) going early, they might be able to lean on the Cowboys and prevent the game from turning into the kind of track meet that Dallas' offense would prefer.
Opponents have also generally been able to throw all over the Cowboys, though it will obviously be difficult for the Eagles to do so while down their top two receivers and multiple of their expected starting offensive linemen. It'll be Makai Lemon , Darius Cooper and Dallas Goedert as McKee's top targets here. It'll be interesting to see if the Cowboys send Joey Porter Jr . to follow one of Cooper (who plays outside) or Lemon (usually in the slot, where he would match up more often with Caleb Downs ), as well as how they align their secondary now that Cobie Durant is set to return and potentially push the struggling (to say it kindly) Daron Bland to the bench.
If the Cowboys can put any semblance of pressure on McKee, he could struggle badly. He's just 16 of 45 for 179 scoreless yards in his career when under duress, with a 15.1% sack rate as well. The Cowboys don't rush the passer particularly well, but with the current state of Philly's offensive line, that could change on Monday night.
I just don't think the Cowboys should be favored by more than a field goal against anybody right now, given how they're playing on both sides of the ball. I'll take Dallas to win given the state of the Eagles' offense, but I can't see the Cowboys blowing anyone out in their current state.
Prediction: Cowboys 24, Eagles 20
author: Jared Dubin

title: Cover 32: There is a very clear Jonathan Taylor trade destination, plus game balls, biggest gaffes from Week 7
summary: Why Cincinnati should make a blockbuster offer for Jonathan Taylor, plus Week 7 game balls for Joe Burrow and Malik Willis
full_text:
Like an object in your rearview mirror, the NFL trade deadline is closer than it appears. Tuesday will mark two weeks before the Nov. 10 deadline, and there will be a tsunami of rumors and reports about the comings and goings of players between now and then. Key among them will be All-Pro running back Jonathan Taylor , arguably the biggest prize of this cycle.
The Indianapolis Colts are a clear seller as the deadline approaches. Before Week 7, the club fired general manager Chris Ballard. Then, a loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday has since dropped the franchise to 2-5 on the year and has them on a three-game losing skid. They have two more games before the deadline, traveling to Jacksonville next week to face the Jaguars , who are 4-2 and will be coming off their bye week. In Week 9, they'll host the Dallas Cowboys .
On the lookahead lines, Indy is a 7.5-point underdog to Jacksonville and a 1.5-point underdog at home to Dallas, so the oddsmakers have them favored to go 0-2 over that stretch. That'd bring them to 2-7 on the season as they reach the deadline, which would only further embolden them to sell off major pieces as they look to refill the cupboard to better jumpstart their rebuild.
So, who should target Taylor and pull the trigger on a blockbuster to bring him to town? Isn't it obvious?
The Cincinnati Bengals should be pushing their chips into the middle of the table to try and land Taylor. The back is the missing piece that could help take Joe Burrow back to the Super Bowl and, this time, win it.
On Sunday, Cincinnati pulled off a comeback victory over the Baltimore Ravens thanks to a second-half explosion from the offense. Burrow threw for four touchdowns over the final two quarters as part of a 35-0 run to move them to 4-2 on the season and put them firmly in the mix in the AFC North race.
Burrow's touchdown barrage and 249 passing yards in the second half were awe-inspiring. It's also unsustainable.
What was missing from Cincinnati's victory was a running game, and that's been a common theme for the team throughout the first half of the regular season. As a team, the Bengals are averaging 82.9 rushing yards per game, which ranks in the bottom third in the NFL. Their 3.6 yards per carry average is also lackluster. Moreover, Cincinnati has just 44 rushes that have gone for five-plus yards and a league-low five explosive rushes (12-plus yards).
The combination of Chase Brown and Samaje Perine isn't giving the Bengals a rushing attack that opposing defenses need to worry about. Brown is averaging a career-low 3.5 yards per carry, while Perine's 4.1 yards per carry is his lowest since 2022.
For a team in a Super Bowl-or-bust window, this is a clear area of need, and there is a clear answer currently on the trade market in Taylor. So far, Taylor has 11 explosive rushes, and his 2.89 yards per carry after contact is better than the 2.46 yards per carry after contact the Bengals are averaging.
Taylor could be Cincinnati's version of the trade the San Francisco 49ers made leading up to the 2022 deadline when they landed star running back Christian McCaffrey . He proved to be the central engine of the Niners' second half as they reached the NFC Championship, and that has remained the case over the last handful of years, including a Super Bowl LVIII appearance.  Taylor is every bit as capable of making that type of impact on the Bengals, and Cincinnati is at the precise moment in the franchise's history to go all-in and outbid the rest of the league for the star back.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
After not registering a single touch last week, Skattebo emerged from John Harbaugh's doghouse and redeemed himself in Week 7 as the Giants took down the Texans in overtime. The second-year back was at the center of the winning effort, including a 42-yard rush in overtime that helped springboard New York. His 124 rushing yards are a career high.
The longest run of Cam Skattebo's career puts the @Giants in striking distance in OT... NYGvsHOU on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VslWlQGb0V
The Miami Dolphins are finally in the win column. The Dolphins enjoyed their first win of the Jeff Hafley era, going into MetLife Stadium and taking down the Jets , 28-25. Willis did damage with both his arm and his legs in the winning effort and is the second quarterback in franchise history with a passing touchdown and a rushing touchdown in consecutive games.
Malik Willis lowers his shoulder for the touchdown MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TVRwL1sULm
The Vikings linebacker was all over the place in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts to keep Minnesota undefeated on the year at 6-0. Cashman's 4.5 sacks on the season are already tied for his career high, while the Vikings defense is allowing just 12.3 points per game so far this season (fewest in the NFL).
"This is a group that honestly no matter how well we've played this season, we aren't satisfied." @EvanWashburn catches up with Blake Cashman after the Vikings defense seals the game to improve to 6-0 pic.twitter.com/BpeQIPTZNc
The Browns ' first-round rookie had his coming-out party in Week 7, tallying career highs across the board. In the 27-34 win over Tennessee to move Cleveland to 5-2 on the season, Concepcion was a central figure in the offense. His 10 targets were a season-high, as were his 129 receiving yards. Todd Monken even got him going in the ground game as he carried the ball three times for 23 yards, another season high.
KC Concepcion showing off his speed 🏃 CLEvsTEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qZVlUdpPyU
Burrow was perfect in the second half of Cincinnati's win over the Ravens on Sunday. He orchestrated a 35-0 run over the final two quarters to erase a 13-0 halftime deficit. In the second half, Burrow completed 16 of 18 throws for 249 yards and four touchdowns, giving him a perfect 158.3 passer rating over that stretch.
Burrow dropped that one right in the bucket for Tee CINvsBAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0cTT0jvKqS
Bates was one of the main faces of a strong defensive effort by the Falcons as they handed the 49ers its first loss of the season. Both of his turnovers came in the second half, with the interception preventing a scoring opportunity as he approached the Atlanta 10-yard line. Then, his forced fumble on George Kittle effectively ended the game. This was Bates' sixth career game with an interception and a forced fumble, tied for the second-most in the NFL over the past 40 seasons and trailing only Rod Woodson (7).
This interception by Jessie Bates III is UNREAL. SFvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/R4UDkkfGcb
One of the big momentum shifts, as the Ravens allowed 35 unanswered second-half points to the Bengals, came in the opening seconds of the fourth quarter. At the time, Baltimore was trailing Cincinnati 14-13, but had the ball on the Bengals 12-yard line. That led to a decision for coach Jesse Minter, facing a fourth-and-2. He could either opt to keep the offense on the field in hopes of moving the sticks and eventually finding the end zone. Either that, or he could kick it to retake the lead and make it a 16-14 game.
While keeping the offense on the field (which is what he ended up doing) can be argued, the play call was ... puzzling. The Ravens called a passing play on the fourth-down attempt, and Tyler Huntley , who was filling in for the injured Lamar Jackson , failed to connect with rookie tight end Josh Cuevas and turned the ball over on downs. Cincinnati took possession and scored six plays later to extend its lead.
Ravens decide to go for it on 4th & 2 and can't convert. pic.twitter.com/OAARWnsV2d
This is a scenario where the obvious answer is the right one—just give the ball to Derrick Henry . That is why you have a back of his caliber,…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFL Week 8 early odds: Undefeated Vikings gain respect, Chiefs-Broncos line flips
summary: Minnesota is gaining ground ahead of its NFC North showdown with Detroit, while the Chiefs-Broncos and Eagles-Commanders lines have flipped
full_text:
It took seven weeks for a lone undefeated team to emerge in the NFL . The Vikings are the last unbeaten standing after taking down the Colts to move to 6-0, while both Kansas City and San Francisco fell on Sunday.
Minnesota's strong start to the year is now being reflected in the betting odds, as they are getting respect as a true NFC contender. For instance, the Lions opened as a 4.5-point favorite at home against the Vikings for Week 8, but that has started to move towards Kevin O'Connell's club. Now, Detroit is a 3-point favorite.
That is just one of the many swings that we're seeing in the Week 8 odds now that the final chapters are being written in Week 7. As we gear up for a new week in the NFL, let's take a look at the early odds for the slate and see who the oddsmakers have coming out on top.
Note : New Orleans, New York ( Giants ), San Francisco, and Houston are on the bye in Week 8.
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted
Panthers at Packers (Thursday)
Panthers +170, Packers -205
Cardinals +240, Cowboys -298
Falcons +105, Buccaneers -125
Browns +160, Steelers -192
Patriots -380, Dolphins +300
Eagles +154, Commanders -185
Bears at Seahawks (Monday)
Green Bay is a 4.5-point favorite at home and looking to improve its 2-1 ATS record at Lambeau Field. Carolina is coming off a demoralizing loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday, where they surrendered 43 points. The Panthers are 2-1 ATS on the road this season, but that loss has shaken the confidence of bettors. The line opened at Packers -3, but it has since jumped up a point and a half. The total has also held at 47.5. In Packers games this season, the Under is 5-2, which includes a 2-1 record at home. The Under is 3-0 in Panthers road games.
Dallas initially opened as a 10.5-point home favorite, but that line has dipped below the touchdown threshold to -6.5. That could be due to questions about the Cowboys' defense and Arizona's ability to sneak through the back door. Dallas will also be playing on a short week after facing the Eagles on Monday night in Philly. The Cowboys are 1-1 ATS at home this season, while the Cardinals is 3-1 ATS on the road. The total for this game jumped up to 51.5 after opening at 49.5. Between these two clubs, the Over is 8-5.
Buffalo is coming off its bye, so it'll have a rest advantage over Baltimore. However, the Ravens are slated to get Lamar Jackson back in the fold after missing the previous three games. That's likely why this line is at -3.5 in favor of the Bills. Josh Allen's team is 4-2 ATS this season, which includes a 2-1 ATS record at home. Baltimore is 2-1 ATS on the road. Given Jackson's return, the Over will likely be a popular play, even at 52.5. This season, the Over is 5-1 in Bills games.
The Jets initially opened as a 1.5-point favorite at home, but it's now the Raiders who are laying 1.5 points on the road. This comes after New York lost in Week 7 to the previously winless Dolphins, which may have shaken the confidence of the betting public. While they may have lost on Sunday, the Jets have been a strong bet this season, owning a 4-2-1 ATS record (2-1 ATS at home). The Raiders are 2-1 ATS on the road this season, but this will be the first time they've been a road favorite. The Jets covered their only game this season as a home underdog. The total jumped up a point to 42.5 after opening at 41.5. The Over is 5-2 (71.4%) in Raiders games this season.
The Bucs are a 1.5-point favorite as they host the Falcons. Baker Mayfield didn't need to do much in his return as he passed for just 64 yards in a 43-13 win over the Panthers. While they got the ATS win on Sunday, Tampa Bay is 2-5 ATS on the year, which includes a 0-4 ATS mark at home. Atlanta is 2-1 ATS on the road. The total jumped up to 44.5 after opening at 43.5. Between these NFC South rivals, the Over is 8-6.
Pittsburgh will be at a disadvantage, as they are returning to the United States after playing a game in France. That said, they still are a 3.5-point favorite over the Browns in what will be a pivotal AFC North matchup. Pittsburgh is 5-2 ATS this season, which includes a perfect 3-0 ATS record at home. The Browns are 2-2 ATS on the road. Scoring isn't expected to be prolific in this game as the total sits at 39.5. title: Can the Vikings actually win the Super Bowl with this offense? You're telling me there's a chance
summary: Minnesota has one of the NFL's worst offenses and a defense playing at a historically dominant level -- the 2015 Broncos provide a blueprint, but there are reasons to be skeptical
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are 6-0, which is remarkable for one very obvious reason: their offense, by any objective measure, is anemic. They've scored all of 10 touchdowns this season. Their kicker, Will Reichard , has 63 points. Everybody else on the roster? Sixty-two.
Sunday against the Colts offered more of the same. Kyler Murray threw for 150 yards, the offense scored a lone touchdown, and Minnesota won anyway, 16-10. Indianapolis quarterback Daniel Jones managed 108 passing yards, threw an interception and was sacked four times. The Vikings have now won 11 straight games dating to last season, despite scoring just 21 touchdowns during that stretch, the fewest in an 11-game winning streak in NFL history.
At this point, there's no debating whether Brian Flores is an elite defensive coordinator. But here's a question worth considering: Is he so good that his defense can drag this offense all the way to a Super Bowl ? I know, this sounds ridiculous – even for the terminally online, where hyperbole, hype and mock outrage are the fuel that keeps the internet running.
But this is not that. Just ask the 2015 Denver Broncos .
Eleven years ago, Denver started 6-0 with a 39-year-old Peyton Manning who looked nothing like the quarterback who'd won five MVP awards. His arm strength had diminished, injuries had taken their toll, and a makeshift offensive line wasn't helping. Manning threw nine touchdowns and 17 interceptions in 10 games before a foot injury opened the door for Brock Osweiler .
Denver's defense, led by Von Miller , DeMarcus Ware and a loaded secondary, made up for the offense's shortcomings. The Broncos finished 25th in offensive EPA per play but beat the Steelers , Patriots and Panthers on their way to winning Super Bowl 50.
But here's the fine print: Minnesota's offense ranks 31st in EPA per play, and its minus-0.148 mark is considerably worse than Denver's minus-0.063 in 2015. The Vikings aren't just struggling offensively. They're playing at a historically bad level.
Still, the Broncos established that winning a championship without consistently good quarterback play isn't impossible. And Minnesota's defense is performing at a level worthy of the comparison.
Since 2011, only two defenses have completed a season with better EPA/play than Minnesota's current plus-0.195: the 2019 Patriots and 2020 Rams . That's 480 completed team-seasons, and the Vikings' six-game performance? It would rank No. 3. Overall.
Historically dominant defenses, 2011–2026
Flores has taken an already aggressive approach to another level. Minnesota blitzes on 71.8% of dropbacks, nearly 28 percentage points more frequently than the next-closest team this season. Its 47.1% pressure rate ranks among the NFL's best, and opponents are averaging just 12.3 points per game.
Against the Colts, Flores blitzed on 85.2% of dropbacks, the highest single-game rate since 2013. Indianapolis managed 48 yards in the second half.
And the Vikings don't need to blitz to dominate. They lead the NFL in defensive EPA per play when rushing four or fewer defenders. But there's a difference between making life miserable for opposing quarterbacks and being asked to singlehandedly win games every week. That's effectively what Minnesota's defense has done through six games.
The 2026 Vikings rank 31st in offensive EPA/play, 29th in passing yards per game and 31st in touchdown rate per drive. And that minus-0.148 EPA/play? It would rank 22nd-worst among those same 480 team seasons going back to 2011.
And this isn't just a Kyler Murray problem. The 2025 Vikings finished at minus-0.111 EPA/play, and the offense has become even less efficient in 2026. Murray didn't inherit the Kirk Cousins offenses that ranked fifth and sixth in EPA/play in 2019 and 2020. He inherited a mess. And so far, it's somehow worse.
The run game has been respectable, ranking 12th in yards per game. The passing game? Not so much. Murray is averaging just 162.3 passing yards per game, and Minnesota scores touchdowns on only 13.8% of its possessions, 31st in the NFL.
So how long can a defense keep winning games when its offense contributes so little? Three teams from the last decade faced similar challenges, and their seasons ended in three very different ways.
How far can an elite defense carry a bad offense?
The 2019 Steelers are the cautionary tale. Ben Roethlisberger suffered a season-ending elbow injury in Week 2, leaving Pittsburgh with Mason Rudolph and undrafted rookie Duck Hodges (!) at quarterback. Injuries elsewhere on offense compounded the problems. The Steelers' defense, featuring TJ Watt and Minkah Fitzpatrick , kept them competitive, but Pittsburgh finished 8-8 and missed the playoffs. Their offense ranked 31st in EPA per play, the same as Minnesota's this season. I know we now joke about Mike Tomlin never having a losing season, but I was serious when I said he should've won Coach of the Year after willing this team to eight wins.
The 2023 Browns provide a more encouraging comparison. Cleveland lost Nick Chubb , Deshaun Watson and key offensive linemen to injuries, eventually cycling through five starting quarterbacks. Joe Flacco provided an unlikely off-the-couch, late-season spark, while Jim Schwartz's defense helped the Browns finish 11-6. Cleveland's minus-0.145 offensive EPA/play is the closest historical comparison to Minnesota's, and its defense was lights out. But the Browns' wild ride didn't last long once they reached the postseason; the Texans beat them 45-14 in the wild-card round.
Three teams. Three outcomes. And proof that even an elite defense can't guarantee much if the offense consistently struggles.
There's another reason not to dismiss the Vikings' Super Bowl chances: They're already 6-0.
Of the 14 teams that opened a season with six consecutive wins going back to 2013, all 14 reached the playoffs. Seven made the Super Bowl, though only the 2015 Broncos won it all.
Not surprisingly, Minnesota has outperformed expectations, but not by a wildly outrageous margin, at least according to something called Pythagorean expected wins. The formula uses points scored and allowed to estimate how many games a team should have won . Based on their 125 points scored and 74 allowed, the Vikings have an expected 4.7 wins, compared with their actual 6-0 record. That's a better mark than the 2015 Broncos, who also started 6-0 but had just 4.1 expected wins through six games. And, as we've established, Denver went on to win the whole thing.
How far did these 6-0 teams go?
At 6-0, the Vikings have already given themselves plenty of breathing room. Even a 5-6 finish would leave them at 11-6, and there's little reason to believe the wheels are about to fall off Flores' defense.
But getting to the playoffs and winning three or four games against the NFC's best teams are two different conversations. And that brings us back to the original question: Forget about making the playoffs – that feels almost inevitable at this point. Let's get nuts: Can these Vikings actually win the Super Bowl?
The Broncos proved it's possible. The Steelers and Browns showed how quickly things can go sideways. Minnesota's defense is playing well enough to make a championship run – no doubt about it – but its offense is asking even more of Flores than Denver asked of its defense a decade ago.
The good news for Minnesota? At 6-0, there's time to figure it out. And with Flores making life miserable for opposing quarterbacks, O'Connell and Murray don't need to turn this into a top-five offense. They just need to make it replacement-level.
Because right now, the Vikings look like a Super Bowl contender on one side of the ball and a team headed for a top-five draft pick on the other. Something's got to give.

title: NFL Week 7 grades: Falcons earn solid 'A' mark, while Panthers flop with a resounding 'F'
summary: We're grading every game from Week 7 that has been played so far
full_text:
Welcome to the Week 7 grades!
We have somehow hit the final Sunday of October, and when you look at the NFL standings , there are definitely a few surprises. For one, the Cleveland Browns are in first place in their division.
