author: John Breech

title: Cam Skattebo says he's going to keep breaking NFL rules after getting flagged for rarely enforced penalty
summary: Skattebo made it clear he intends to keep seeking out contact
full_text:
Cam Skattebo's running style might be illegal at times, but he's not going to change his ways. The Giants running back delivered a huge game in New York's 26-21 overtime win over the Houston Texans , but he sparked some controversy early in the game.
During the first quarter, Skattebo got called for one of the most surprising penalties of the week. The Giants running back got flagged for a rarely enforced unnecessary roughness, with the officiating crew ruling that he had lowered his helmet to draw contact.
Cam Skattebo was penalized for this run... pic.twitter.com/tEHPezmJ3F
The 15-yard penalty was surprising because officials don't usually flag an offensive player for lowering their helmet. Heading into Week 7, they had only thrown four penalty flags all season for lowering their helmets, and only one of those came against an offensive player. That other player was Houston's Foster Moreau , but he was flagged for making a tackle on a punt return in Week 2, so Skattebo is the only player to have been penalized while playing offense.
On one hand, Skattebo was bound to get penalized at some point because he's a human battering ram who seeks out contact with defensive players. Despite his running style, this was the first time in his career that he had ever been flagged for lowering his helmet, but it might not be his last.
Following the game, the Giants running back was asked whether he might change his running style to avoid future penalties, and apparently, he's not planning to change anything.
"The NFL loves to post me when I do stuff like that but then also wants to take stuff from me," Skattebo said in his postgame comments . "I'm going to run the ball like I want to run the ball. If I'm going to continue to get flags for it or fined for it, guess I'm going to play for free."
In layman's terms, Skattebo is still planning to truck over defenders whenever he has the ball. The problem with this plan is that there's a good chance Giants coach John Harbaugh won't like it. Now that Skattebo has been penalized, officials will likely be on the lookout for him to possibly lower his head going forward, and if he gets flagged, it will cost the Giants 15 yards.
If Skattebo continues to get flagged because he's unwilling to change his ways, that will almost certainly draw the ire of Harbaugh, which is not what the running back needs, because he's already been in the doghouse this year. He had zero touches in Week 6, but he made up for that with a huge game against the Texans, rushing for 124 yards and a touchdown on just 17 carries .
If Skattebo doesn't want to end up back in Harbaugh's doghouse, he'll probably need to slightly adjust his running style so he doesn't get flagged going forward.
author: John Breech

title: NFL Week 7 overreactions: Panthers have season's worst loss? Dan Campbell was right? Ravens to miss playoffs?
summary: Plus, did the Vikings choose the right quarterback?
full_text:
There had been few more encouraging starts to the season than the Carolina Panthers . Even though they were only 3-2 through six weeks, the Panthers' offense was humming, and Bryce Young had taken a huge step forward. Combine that with a faltering NFC South, and it looked like the Panthers were already on their way to a second straight division title.
And then came this week. Buccaneers 43, Panthers, an emphatic reminder that things are rarely what they seem in the NFL . And that Week 6 is way too early to even pencil in anything as far as the playoffs go. With that, we get to overreactions and reality checks. Carolina got the latter served, cold, on Sunday.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
There is simply no other way to state it. This was one of the most stunning displays -- or lack thereof -- we've seen in the NFL of late. Add in the opportunity that the Panthers had at home, plus everything else this game represents, and it's a truly awful Sunday from Carolina.
Bryce Young threw two interceptions and got sacked five times, one of which resulted in a Calijah Kancey scoop and score. Remember all those terrible outings from the first two years of his career where he looked completely overwhelmed from a physical perspective? This looked very much like that.
97 with the SACK 😤 94 with the TOUCHDOWN 🙌 📺: #TBvsCAR on FOX pic.twitter.com/6xGVyQBoFl
🚨 FOURTH TAKEAWAY 🚨 📺: #TBvsCAR on FOX pic.twitter.com/AZG8Avz2EY
Young was truly awful in every aspect. His pocket escapability wasn't up to par, and Todd Bowles overwhelmed -- there's that word again -- him throughout the afternoon.
But really, the Buccaneers overwhelmed the Panthers in every aspect. Carolina had one carry of 15+ yards ... and it was by backup quarterback Kenny Pickett in garbage time. Young didn't get much help from anyone up front; the Buccaneers registered 13 pressures and had six quick pressures (2.5 seconds or faster). That might get worse, too: Right tackle Taylor Moton suffered a fractured fibula, got carted off and is out indefinitely.
The defense might have been even worse. The Buccaneers ran for 258 yards -- their fourth-most ever -- and three touchdowns. Oh, and we can't leave out special teams, where the Panthers had a blocked extra point returned for two points and a muffed punt. Find a way a team can get embarrassed, and the Buccaneers did it to their division rival.
Every team has bad weeks, but this was more worrisome in the big picture. Young and the offense have now had a middling week and a bad week since their Week 5 bye. The offensive line has given up the most pressures and the most quick pressures in the NFL. The defensive line now ranks dead last in yards per carry allowed (5.2) and is dealing with significant injuries to both of its cornerbacks.
The Panthers have been brought back to Earth, and they've brought the rest of the division back into things. With a chance to separate from the pack, the Panthers still lead the NFC South at 3-3 but are just a half-game up on the 3-4 Falcons , with the 2-5 Buccaneers and 2-5 Saints also still in a not-very-inspiring division race.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
The Lions beat the Packers 20-17 Sunday despite a horrific failed fourth-and-1 at their own 24-yard line late in the fourth quarter.
Keisean Nixon and the Packers force a turnover on downs! GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XrT82gvFEh
Lots of people were probably pulling their hair out saying "What is Dan Campbell thinking?!"
Well, he explained what he was thinking: "Well, I thought we would get it, number one. I really believed we would get that. Number two, I knew we would get the ball back if it didn't work out. And those were the two thoughts."
Here's why it's defensible. To his first thought, the Lions were two-for-three on fourth-and-1 this season and are 10-for-14 since the start of last season.
But when they didn't get it, his second thought came into play. The Lions had all three timeouts with nearly five minutes remaining. The Lions would have almost certainly gotten the ball back with significant time/timeouts left, no matter what happened. In fact, the short field for the Packers basically worked in the Lions' favor.
Would you rather have him punt the ball away and give the Packers the ball with five minutes and 40-50 yards to go to reach field-goal range? There's a solid chance the Packers score with basically no time left and/or the Lions use up all their timeouts in that scenario.
Would I have gone for it there? Probably not. But Campbell's logic is legitimate here, and analytical models supported it or had it as a toss-up .
It ended up working out, too. The Packers had to settle for a field goal attempt, which was blocked, and the Lions drove down and won on a walk-off field goal. But even if Trey Smack's kick had gone in, the Lions would have had the ball with 3:21 left and all three timeouts, only down three. Campbell would take that every day of the week.
Don't think "Oh, there's dumb Dan Campbell making a dumb, over-aggressive decision." It was defensible at worst and completely reasonable -- and maybe even the right choice -- at best. And guess what? His team won!
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
In arguably the best performance of his young career, J.J. McCarthy threw for 252 yards in a 27-21 overtime win over the Texans . He made some truly exquisite throws and didn't have a single turnover, an issue that had plagued him with the Vikings . Meanwhile, the Vikings slugged out a 16-10 win over the Colts . Minnesota is 6-0, but the offense continues to be stop-and-start to put it nicely.
To not put it nicely -- and, frankly, more accurately -- it has been bad. Minnesota's 10 touchdowns are the fewest by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions . Only the Chargers score a touchdown on a lower percentage of their drives this season. Only Cam Ward and Daniel Jones have a lower touchdown rate than Kyler Murray this season. That's bad company. The traditional run game has been poor, and while Murray has had some big plays, but down-in and down-out, it's been very poor.
Kyler Murray with a 35-yard run to pick up the first down 🏃 INDvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GSqLond1o9
But 1) it's been one game for McCarthy, so let's not go overboard, and 2) it just wasn't working out in Minnesota for him. It wasn't. He was bad in training camp. He was bad in the preseason. He was bad and/or hurt last season.
Sometimes players need a change of scenery. Sam Darnold needed many. And, again, it's too early to deem McCarthy a success story in New York. Vikings fans can want a better offense and realize it wasn't going to happen with McCarthy.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
For the first time since 1996, the Ravens have blown a double-digit halftime lead. This week, they led the Bengals 13-0 at halftime before losing 35-13 .
Yes, that's a 35-0 second half for Cincinnati, the team's best and most important half in a long, long time. The Bengals are 4-2 and, after looking completely asleep in the first half, they looked like a Super Bowl-caliber outfit in the second half.
Baltimore was once again without Lamar Jackson , though he's expected back next week. His return can't come soon enough. The Ravens are now 4-3, which is fine, but they're 0-2 in the AFC North. Their offense looks like one of the best in the NFL with him and one of the worst without him. Add in that the defense has struggled in crucial situations -- 29th in yards per play allowed and just one sack in second halves this year -- and you get a team that has limited margin for error.
Jackson and the Ravens will face the Bills next week and then the Jaguars . They need to win one of those two -- at least -- to get back on track, and then an easier stretch (Chargers, at Panthers, Texans, Buccaneers) ensues. I'd bet on Baltimore figuring it out with Jackson back.
Overreaction or reality: Reality

title: NFL Week 7 winners and losers: Cam Skattebo, J.J. McCarthy lift Giants; Aaron Glenn's seat heats up
summary: One of the New York teams is in much better shape than the other. Plus, what happened to the Panthers?
full_text:
Week 7 in the NFL placed a wedge between the two New York teams. The Giants are riding high as the leaders of the NFC East, while the Jets reached a new low with a loss to the league's worst team. Cam Skattebo and J.J. McCarthy are heralded this week for keeping the Giants' offense in surprisingly excellent shape, and at the same time, Aaron Glenn is feeling the heat from the Jets' fanbase amid a 2-5 start to the campaign.
That dichotomy encapsulates the highs and lows of Week 7. This deep into the season, teams that suffer bad losses can feel truly helpless. The Jets are not alone in their misery as other squads slipped multiple games below .500 with them. And on the flip side, those who are at or near the top of their division should feel as though they will compete for a playoff berth.
Here are the biggest winners and losers from Sunday's action in the NFL.
Call it the Cam Skattebo redemption game . One week after John Harbaugh relegated him to the bench, the New York Giants running back amassed 124 yards and a touchdown in a bounce-back effort against the Houston Texans . He broke loose for a 42-yarder, which set the Giants up to win in overtime. Plus, it was the first 100-yard game of his career. Skattebo also held onto the ball, which should put him back in his coach's good graces after he opened the year tied for the most fumbles by a non-quarterback through six weeks.
SKATTEBO BREAKS FREE FOR 42 YARDS NYGvsHOU on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CqU4A2DpOE
It also seems that the Giants have a quarterback. Those who panned the trade for J.J. McCarthy after Jaxson Dart suffered his season-ending knee injury could not have foreseen such a brilliant start to McCarthy's tenure in New York. Last week, he passed for 243 yards in a single quarter. This week, the oft-criticized former first-round pick went a clean 20-for-28 for 252 yards.
This is McCarthy's fifth win in as many starts dating back to his time as the Minnesota Vikings ' No. 1 quarterback. If he can keep it up, this is precisely the kind of upside the Giants bet on when they made the low-risk investment in McCarthy. They can win with him and more than salvage a season that could have been lost when their Week 1 starter had his campaign cut short.
With the win, the Giants are 4-2-1 and are the only team in the NFC East with a winning record. When Week 7 is complete, they will hold a 1.5-point lead in the division. Someone has to win the worst division in the NFL, and the Giants thus far are the top candidate to do so.
It is never a good look to be the team on the losing end of a winless opponent's first victory. The Jets were on the wrong side of the 28-25 result at MetLife Stadium.
The New York faithful booed their team off the field at halftime and were less than pleased two quarters later. The angst directed toward coach Aaron Glenn is palpable, and the pressure on him has never been higher. Following back-to-back losses and perhaps the most disappointing defeat of his tenure, there is very little he can sell that his fanbase would buy. If he is fired at some point this year, this is the kind of game that will explain his ouster.
The Jets are now 2-5 and will be underdogs in at least two of their next three games: at home against the Las Vegas Raiders , on the road at the Kansas City Chiefs and back home to face the Buffalo Bills . This could get quite a bit worse before it gets better.
Good luck making sense of the Atlanta Falcons , because this might be the league's most up-and-down team. When it all clicks as it did in Week 7, the star talent is obvious, and they can beat anyone. This is also the same team that lost by 31 points to the Carolina Panthers earlier in the year and entered Sunday on a two-game losing streak. The 29-20 upset of the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers was one of those boom games and is now the best victory in the NFL this season.
The formula by which the Falcons secured the impressive win highlighted exactly why they are among 2026's most pleasant surprises. Michael Penix Jr . threw three touchdown passes and continues to show flashes of being a potential franchise quarterback. And the defense forced four turnovers and remains a stunningly effective unit despite the absences of James Pearce Jr . and Jalon Walker . Pearce will be back from suspension on Nov. 8 and should take the group to even greater heights. The Falcons may well be the No. 1 team in the NFC South by then.
All the Carolina Panthers needed to do to maintain a commanding lead in the NFC South was beat the division's worst team at home. That should not be too big of an ask for a squad with a dark horse MVP contender in Bryce Young , right? Apparently not, because the Panthers not only failed to take care of business against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers but also lost in devastating fashion by 30 points. It was a complete no-show from Dave Canales' team, which fell behind by 27 points at halftime after surrendering a 26-point second quarter to the Buccaneers.
This was a chance to effectively put the Buccaneers in a coffin and separate from a New Orleans Saints team that lost earlier in the day in Paris. A win was also necessary to stay a couple of steps ahead of the dangerous Atlanta Falcons, who pulled off an upset of the San Francisco 49ers. The opportunity passed them by as the NFL's sixth-worst run defense allowed a whopping 258 yards to Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell , Sean Tucker and the rest of the Tampa Bay attack.
The Panthers also lost veteran offensive lineman Taylor Moton to a fractured fibula. The starting right tackle is out indefinitely, Canales said after the game.
He still was not especially consistent, but Bo Nix enjoyed his biggest game of the year. He delivered explosive plays both through the air and on the ground in the Denver Broncos ' comfortable 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals . Nix was easily among the least inspiring quarterbacks from Weeks 1-6 and ranked 31st in QBR entering Sunday, but he took the first step in rebounding from that slow start with 222 passing yards (his second-most of the year) and two total touchdowns against the maligned Arizona defense.
Perhaps the performance should be taken with a grain of salt, given the low caliber of competition. But maybe something clicked with Sean Payton calling plays again for the third week. Nix logged explosive passes of 52, 47 and 27 yards and delivered the most exciting play of the game with a 62-yard touchdown run. That was the longest rushing score by a quarterback since 2022 and nearly tripled Nix's season total in yardage.
BO NIX 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN RUN DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sxC4uWF33r
It is no coincidence that Nix's best game of the season came at the same time as the Broncos' most lopsided victory. If he performs like this — closer to his 2025 form — moving forward, Denver will feel great about its chances of returning to the postseason.
Dan Campbell's baffling fourth-down call put this game on a silver platter for the Green Bay Packers , but a special teams snafu threw that opportunity away in a 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions . When the Lions turned the ball over on downs at their own 22-yard line in a tie game with 4:53 to play, it looked as though a poor coaching decision would cost them. Instead, Trey Smack had his potential go-ahead field goal tipped at the line of scrimmage, and it sailed wide right to set Detroit up with a game-winning drive.
That added insult to injury after Smack already missed a field goal earlier in the game. He booted a chip shot wide right from 26 yards out on the Packers' opening possession to begin his disastrous day. Smack, a rookie sixth-round pick, was phenomenal at the start of the year and made his first five attempts with a long of 59 yards. He is suddenly down to just 11-for-16 on the season with four misses in his last two games.
In turn, the Packers slipped to last place in the uber-competitive NFC…

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers reveals NFL once had a completely different plan for its international games
summary: Rodgers is now the first quarterback to play an international game in three different countries in three straight years
full_text:
No quarterback is as well-traveled, at least when it comes to football, as Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers . The four-time MVP is the first quarterback in NFL history to play an international game in three different countries in three straight seasons. He played in London, England, in 2024; Dublin, Ireland, in 2025; and Paris, France, in 2026.
After Rodgers' Steelers won 16-10 in the NFL's first game in Paris , the quarterback revealed that when the NFL and the NFL Players Association were negotiating a new collective bargaining agreement in 2020, they almost had a different plan for international games. The NFL and its players' union were in talks to hold an international week in which the 16 games for its 32 teams would take place in 16 different locations around the world. With all games outside of the United States that week, the season would be 16 games long, and each team would have two bye weeks. Rodgers said those conversations died when owners pushed for a 17th regular-season game, which did come to fruition in 2021.
"The reach of the league is fantastic, and I think I always wanted to be a part of it," Rodgers said postgame. "I think it'd have been phenomenal for the game. Now, the owners wanted to push for 17 games for the extra revenue because they care so much about player safety, but it would have been nice."
Where could the NFL have played 16 international games? Rodgers sees multiple opportunities in North America, South America, Europe and even the Middle East. The only barrier he saw to the league making a groundbreaking effort to expand its global reach is money.
"I think there are great opportunities for expansion in those things," Rodgers said. "It'd be awesome to see them, you know, have an international week because I think it's great for the game and the expansion of the game. And I wish there was a mandate, though, from the league [that] they would have to open up their pocketbooks too, and they're maybe a little tight on money and stuff. I think they should mandate every team coming over Sunday or Monday to really enjoy the culture and the place you're going. You could do events in those cities and outreach stuff and community work. But they won't because they're tight [with money]."
The 22-season NFL veteran didn't go abroad in his first 17 seasons with the Green Bay Packers , but he finally experienced the chance to play internationally for the first time in London in his final season with the Packers in 2022. After three straight years playing a game overseas with the New York Jets and the Steelers, Rodgers couldn't be a bigger proponent of the NFL's international initiatives.
"You know, I said it earlier this week: 'I wish we could have come over and enjoyed the sights both in Ireland and in France for a little more time,'" Rodgers said postgame, via Front Office Sports .  "But it's great the way the game is growing."

title: Christian McCaffrey injury: 49ers' RB says leg 'just died' on him during loss to Falcons
summary: McCaffrey expressed his frustrations with his limitations during the game
full_text:

Christian McCaffrey appeared to aggravate his leg in the first quarter, then went to the medical tent and eventually to the locker room in the second quarter. He was initially listed as questionable, but he returned to start the third quarter. Losing McCaffrey for any amount of time significantly impacts the offense, considering he is consistently the team's leading rusher.
After the game, the four-time Pro Bowler gave an update and explained what happened with his leg.
"I have no idea. It sucks, because I feel like I was going on a run there, and my leg just died on me," CMC said . "I was trying to get it going for the whole rest of the game, but it just sucks trying to play like that."
He added some reassurance on his health, saying, "I know I'll be alright, but it's just really frustrating."
McCaffrey had a diminished workload when he returned to the field. Before going down with the injury, he had four carries for 29 yards and one touchdown. His first rushing attempt back from the locker room was a loss of two, and he finished the game with seven carries for 39 yards and one touchdown. He also finished with six receptions for 61 yards, clocking three receptions for 45 yards before the injury.
His 39 rushing yards are his second-fewest this season, while his 61 receiving yards are his best in 2026. For someone whose job uses their legs the most, having their legs feel like they "died" doesn't seem positive, but the RB didn't seem concerned about the long term.
The 30-year-old has a long history of injuries, and any sign of him not looking 100 percent will give his fanbase flashbacks, and not the good kind. The Niners have suffered numerous significant injuries this season and cannot afford to lose any more star players.
The 49ers have a bye coming up, which could work in McCaffrey's favor. Whether this injury will linger beyond Sunday will be known once the weekly injury reports come out.
In Week 7, the 49ers offense was without wide receivers Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Demarcus Robinson (IR), De'Zhaun Stribling (IR) and Ricky Pearsall (IR). title: J.J. McCarthy, Cam Skattebo seize second chances as John Harbaugh's surprising Giants keep rolling
summary: McCarthy impressed in his first start for New York, and Skattebo responded emphatically to his Week 6 benching
full_text:
When J.J. McCarthy got traded from the Vikings to the Giants , he called it "a shock" but also "an opportunity to take advantage of."
When Cam Skattebo received zero touches in Week 6 -- one week after a costly fumble -- he admitted he wasn't expecting the lack of involvement , but it also forced him "to kind of step back and look at it and figure out why."
Every NFL player faces pivotal moments -- make-or-break situations where they must dig deep and find a way to respond. Both challenges and opportunities in one. These were McCarthy's and Skattebo's. And in their biggest moments thus far in their young careers, they made their stand.
"I think that's exactly the story," John Harbaugh said about his team responding. "I mean to that's the point. It tells you who they are. You might have thought before the game 'We're gonna find out about our guys. We're gonna find out about who they are.' And we did."
In his first start with New York, McCarthy threw for 252 yards and had no turnovers, and in his return to prominence in the lineup, Skattebo ran for 124 yards and a touchdown as the Giants upset the Texans 27-21 in overtime. Skattebo's 42-yard rumble -- the longest run of his career -- set up Devin Singletary's walkoff score.
The longest run of Cam Skattebo's career puts the @Giants in striking distance in OT... NYGvsHOU on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VslWlQGb0V
Before the overtime bursts, though, McCarthy put on a laser show against one of the NFL's most talented defenses. He smartly leaned on Malik Nabers (seven catches, 111 yards), who is looking very much like he's back to pre-ACL tear form, and made several truly outstanding throws.
J.J. McCarthy looks like a completely different QB in New York, making big time throw after big time throw. 20/28, 252 PASS YDS, 0 TD, 0 INT vs Texans With McCarthy at QB, the 4-2-1 Giants are now the favorites to win the NFC East. pic.twitter.com/friJD0TZ7D https://t.co/tw9oUKWXsH
McCarthy completed five throws of at least 15 yards downfield after completing six last week as a sub. The 11 completions are his most in a two-game span in his career ... and he didn't even sub in for Jameis Winston until the fourth quarter last week.
This is what the Vikings had hoped McCarthy would be when they drafted him: an athletic quarterback with a live arm able to access every part of the field. For McCarthy to do this, given the circumstances -- traded just weeks earlier, making his first start on the road against a really good defense -- was shockingly impressive.
"It's that thing: It's guys have scars," Harbaugh said. "He has scars. He's been wounded. He's been wounded. He's been battered. But you heal stronger, and you become better because of it, so you should be grateful."
Skattebo, meanwhile, ran over, around and through Houston's defense. His 7.3 yards per carry represented the best of his career, and he credited the offensive line for opening up holes; his 65 yards before contact were the most in any game in his career. He also told the team's postgame show that he had ball security on his mind, which wasn't the case against Washington.
The common denominator between McCarthy's and Skattebo's performances? Harbaugh, the man who gave both players opportunities: Skattebo an opportunity to learn, McCarthy an opportunity, period.
The end of Harbaugh's time in Baltimore was defined by disappointment. After 18 years and a Super Bowl triumph with the Ravens , Harbaugh watched a Tyler Loop field goal sail wide in Week 18 last year, ending Baltimore's playoff hopes. He never got Lamar Jackson and co. over the hump. His reputation took a major hit in turn.
But perhaps it took too big of a hit. This coach has won 184 games. He won double-digit games 11 times in 18 years in Baltimore. That included his first year, when he turned a 5-11 team from 2007 to an 11-5 team in 2008. He knows how to build a winner and sustain a winner.
The early returns are that he's doing it again in New York. The Giants are 4-2-1, two wins ahead of anyone else in the NFC East. The Giants have won with Jaxson Dart , Jameis Winston and, now, McCarthy as starting quarterback. They're the first team since the 2016 Patriots to have three different winning starting quarterbacks within the first seven games of the year.
And this one meant as much as any regular-season win has. Just look at how Harbaugh reacted:
HUG ME BROTHA pic.twitter.com/j6tdcOwp0J
"I'm having a lot of fun," Harbaugh said, a smile coming to his face. "I'm having a lot of fun. There was a little dancing in the locker room."
McCarthy used that "fun" word, too.
"It was a lot of fun. So much fun to be out there playing football, but with this group, it makes it that much more fun, that's for sure."
And that's what these Giants were Sunday: fun. Fun to see McCarthy shining in a spot no one could have envisioned him in just a few weeks ago, when he was sitting on the Vikings' bench. Fun to see Skattebo ripping off big gains and Nabers making wild catches. Fun to see Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux wreaking havoc.
Fun to see that, after losing their quarterback in Week 2, they're still playing well and still winning. Everything could have gone off course after Dart's injury. Instead, the Giants will head into their bye with their heads held high, in first place in their division and with meaningful football ahead.
"It's a reward," Harbaugh said. "Now you've got to make something of it. It doesn't mean anything if you don't build on it, right? Well, it means something, but it doesn't mean we're gonna win a championship yet. It means we have an opportunity.
"... We're gonna be in this thing until the end."
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Cam Skattebo redemption game: Giants RB returns with stellar performance after benching
summary: Fresh out of the dog house, the second-year back erupted for 124 yards and set up Devin Singletary's overtime touchdown to revive New York's run game
full_text:
The much-maligned New York Giants running back room showed up in a big way during their Week 7, 27-21 overtime victory over the Houston Texans . Just one week after Cam Skattebo recorded zero carries in a one-score loss to the New Orleans Saints , he returned to the lineup and rushed for a career-high 124 yards and one touchdown on 17 carries.
ESPN reported before the game that Skattebo was expected to take over the Giants' backfield after he was seemingly benched in Week 6 following a costly fumble in overtime of the Giants' Week 5 tie with the Washington Commanders . Skattebo said he was "taught a lesson," and when overtime came this week, he was the hero instead of the disappointment.
In the extra period, the second-year back broke loose for a 42-yard gain, which set up a Devin Singletary 30-yard game-winning touchdown. This made the Giants the only team in the past 35 years to register 30-plus yard runs on consecutive plays in overtime, per CBS Sports Research. The Giants had zero 30-yard rushes on their first 461 offensive plays this season. Sunday marked the first game since 1950 where the Giants saw four different players score rushing touchdowns, as Skattebo, Singletary, Tyrone Tracy Jr . and Jameis Winston all found the end zone.
SKATTEBO BREAKS FREE FOR 42 YARDS NYGvsHOU on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CqU4A2DpOE
SINGLETARY SEALS IT 🔥 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/NEB091GEyG
The Giants really needed this performance. From John Harbaugh, to Skattebo, to the running back room at large. One week after New York's running backs combined for just 34 rushing yards, they hit 180 yards this week. The running back group was a major talking point after Najee Harris was booted from the team after being critical of Harbaugh's rotation.
"It's hard to get in a rhythm with one or two plays," Harris said, via The Trentonian . "The first couple runs will be like, 'OK, how are they playing it?' And then the next ones will be, 'OK, this is how you attack it.' But if you're getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there's nothing you could do. That's why I'm saying, 'I don't know.' I've never been through none of this before."
Harbaugh told reporters he understood why Harris was frustrated, but maintained that playing time had to be earned. So did Harris' roster spot, apparently.
"I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance," Harbaugh said. "A Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be. That would be great, and we haven't. Our run game hasn't earned that yet, and none of those guys have. My advice would be to any player, and it's all the guys, we had the same conversation. I've had the same conversation with all the running backs, the receivers, it's no different than any position, but do the most you can with the opportunities you get. Make the most of those opportunities, and you're sure to get more opportunities. You know? Do something."
Skattebo said this past Friday that Harris' release proved "nobody's safe," including himself. While he established himself as a fan favorite during his rookie season, becoming one of just five players to rack up 400 rushing yards and 200 receiving yards through the first eight games of the season, he failed to rush for more than 60 yards in each of his past five games with zero touchdowns. With a new regime, Skattebo had to prove himself once again.
"I think when we go on the field, and we perform, if we're not performing, we understand there's a possibility of not being here," Skattebo said . "And if I don't perform, I know there's a possibility of me not being here."
It's safe to say Skattebo earned some points with Harbaugh and the staff on Sunday. The Texans entered Week 7 with the No. 3 rush defense in the NFL , allowing just 83 rushing yards per game. However, Skattebo out-physicaled DeMeco Ryans ' unit in their own building this week.

full_text:
Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . has scored his first touchdown as a member of the Houston Texans , doing so in Week 7 against the New York Giants . He made it to the end zone in his second game with the team, after being traded on Oct. 11 from the Arizona Cardinals .
The former No. 4 overall pick caught the pass from a QB he has caught numerous touchdowns from: His former college quarterback, C.J. Stroud . Watching the two connect for a TD was a blast from Ohio State past.
Here's a look at the big play:
Marvin Harrison Jr. gets his first touchdown as a Texan! NYGvsHOU on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1zvTlVie4i
The 6-yard touchdown came as the first half was winding down and, paired with the ensuing two-point conversion, tied the game at 14 all. The touchdown was his first reception of the game.
Harrison caught one touchdown for the Cardinals in four games, a TD that also just so happened to be against the Giants. He is the first player to score a touchdown against the Giants with two different teams in the same season since Herschel Walker did it in 1989 as a member of the Dallas Cowboys and Minnesota Vikings .
In four games with the Cardinals, Harrison had five receptions on 13 targets for one touchdown. Last week, in his Houston debut, he had three receptions on four targets for 34 yards.
The Texans are currently 2-4 and on a two-game winning streak as they look to turn their season around.

title: Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield gets unexpected help from World Series team to make return after injury
summary: Mayfield is returning after missing three games with a thumb injury to his throwing hand
full_text:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is making his return this week against the Carolina Panthers , after missing the last three games with a right thumb injury. And to make his return to action a little easier, he got an assist from a World Series team.
Mayfield will wear a custom glove to help protect his throwing thumb, given to him by the Tampa Bay Rays training staff. The Buccaneers reached out to Nike, which made a custom protective glove for MLB star Mike Trout. The inquiry led the Rays, who are playing in the 2026 World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers, to offer to help.
The Rays sent a member of the equipment staff to the Bucs' facility to meet with Mayfield and make the glove for him.
According to the Tampa Bay Times , clubhouse attendant Nick Bond modified a wide receiver glove by removing material around the thumb and adding an insert for protection. Two gloves were made: one with hard plastic and another resembling a soft cast.
Here is a look at the glove:
Here is the glove #Bucs QB Baker Mayfield will wear to protect his dislocated thumb, with thanks to the @RaysBaseball training staff. pic.twitter.com/nUtenahRUy
"[It's] not restricting because it's on the backside. ... For me, just getting used to it. I don't feel the difference. It's just like me wearing a glove," Mayfield said.
Rays equipment manager Tyler Wall spoke to the abilities of Bond and their plan for the glove.
"I said our guy can do anything," Wall said. "They worked together and kind of Frankensteined a glove together, working with their trainers, Baker and Nick Bond. [It's] not hard enough to restrict the thumb but enough for protection. So he built a pocket around the thumb and inserted it. It worked pretty good."
The Rays are currently down 2-0 against the Brewers, but even as they prepared for this weekend's games, they were able to extend some help to another Tampa team.
The Buccaneers sit at 1-5 on the season, losing two of the three games Mayfield missed. But their poor record is not all because of Mayfield's absence. Even when he was playing, Mayfield was struggling, with 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. The season's hope isn't over quite yet, thanks to the rest of the NFC South struggling as well.
The Panthers, who Mayfield played for in 2022, lead the division at 3-2, followed by the 2-4 Atlanta Falcons and 2-4 New Orleans Saints .

RELATED: ENSHRINE FITZGERALD THEN LOSE The Cardinals have been a roller coaster this year. The new offense is going to take a while to get going, but there are glimmers of hope in every contest. In the end, the Broncos made a statement by beating Arizona 30-16 in another game where the offense drives the field and cannot score touchdowns. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS LB Jack Gibbens – This just might be the Cardinals’ best defensive player. Each week, he is either the #1 tackler or close to the top. He stuffed RB Jonah Colemand in the second quarter after just a three-yard gain. He hit RB J.K. Dobbins on the goal line, but Dobbins slid off all tackles and fell into the end zone. Led all tacklers with seven. A national TE day tuddy from 85 himself 🙂‍↕️ 📺:CBS pic.twitter.com/g9VTPhm16c — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 25, 2026 TE Trey McBride – The talented tight end is a default entry each week. He is undoubtedly the best offensive player the Cardinals have. Proof of that is the hurdle in the fourth quarter. Led all receivers with 13 targets, 10 receptions for 11 yards and one score. K Chad Ryland – Another good day for Ryland who, once again, scored the majority of offensive points with nine as he connected on field goals of 30, 26, and 41 yards. After McBride, Ryland has been the offense MVP this year. How sad is that? Larry Legend forever stamped in AZ Cardinals history ❤️ pic.twitter.com/hUQha7MD5U — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 25, 2026 Larry Fitzgerald Enshrinement – First, the Hall of Fame, and now enshrined in Arizona Cardinals history forever. You gave your all, Larry. We still love you. ——————————————————————————— GEEKS Lack of receiver play – Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne are both exceptional receivers, yet Wilson only caught four balls all game. Bourne had six targets, but was only able to corral three catches for just nine yards. Jalen Brooks had one catch. These are all good pass catchers, and yet aren’t being utilized. No rushing attack – This is a huge breakdown for this offense. Yes, their best offensive lineman, Paris Johnson, is out for the year, but this group must be more consistent on running plays. Good teams run for more than 94 yards in a game. What was all that hype about when Tyler Allgeier was signed during the offseason? Eight rushes for 19 yards? TOUCHDOWN, RJ HARVEY 💨 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/RQIx2hqozk — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 25, 2026 Too many huge plays – The 62-yard run by QB Bo Nix in the second quarter. A 52-yard catch-and-run by RB R.J. Harvey early in the third stanza. Nix to WR Marvin Mims for 47 yards later in the quarter. 27-yard completion to WR Jalen Waddle in the fourth quarter, followed by a 19-yard completion to WR Courtland Sutton two plays later. All in one friggin’ ballgame? Fourth-and-goal – This was disappointing, but really, the odds of the comeback were not in Arizona’s favor down 30-16 with 52 seconds remaining. RG Conner Hayden had his man blocked, but DE Malcolm Roach could not get any penetration and did the only thing he could: get a paw up. The pass was blocked, and that, was that. Continued Red Zone disasters – This Cardinals offense can move the ball up and down the field. However, they cannot punch it into the end zone. This is a continuing saga. They got down to Denver’s 11, 7, and 23 without scoring a touchdown. Drives of 14 plays and 10 plays. While the Broncos were scoring six points a pop, Arizona was getting half that. The scoreboard will get away from you quickly with that strategy. Got him 📺:CBS pic.twitter.com/SCgf7jyLgL — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 25, 2026 Pass rush – Where is it? One sack all day? Limited pressures? One QB hit? Josh Sweat two tackles. Roy Lopez one tackle. L.J. Collier one tackle plus one batted pass. Darius Robinson played well and netted four tackles with the game’s only sack. Are missed tackles just what this defense does now? Penalties! Penalties! Penalties! – The best way to take one step forward and two steps back is to get a bunch of penalties. This team collects yellow flags. 11 accepted penalties for 114 yards is a game destroyer. Three holding calls, one false start and neutral zone infraction, a rare offensive facemask call, and a delay of game while sitting on the two-yard line. Who does that? ———————————————————————————– Bird Seed – What’s another word for Thesaurus? Third down efficiency – Going 3-for-11 is not what good teams do. That is a stat of what bad teams have. CB Kalen King – Played well and had the second-most tackles with six. Made a good play on the third-and-five play in the second quarter with the pass intended for Waddle that ended up a four-yard gain and a punt instead of moving the sticks. He also came through late in this same quarter with the Broncos facing a third-and-four. King nailed Harvey for just a two-yard gain. The 47-yard pass completion in the third quarter was stopped by King as he ran down Mims. He later became injured in the fourth quarter. Stopping the run – The Broncos busted out for several great runs, including the 62-yard run by Nix and Jonah Coleman’s 15-yarder for a key first down. Where were any Cardinals defenders when Nix left the pocket? It was like the entire field was wiped clean until he got inside the five-yard line. There weren’t any trailing defenders whatsoever. The Broncos ran up the gut way too many times and ended the contest with a 6.1 yards per carry average.

title: Arizona Cardinals enshrine Larry Fitzgerald in Ring of Honor… also lose to Denver Broncos
summary: I don’t want to be too negative, but it was nice of the Denver Broncos to host the Larry Fitzgerald Ring of Honor celebration… Anyways. The Arizona Cardinals inducted Larry Fitzgerald into their Ring of Honor, and retired his jersey, meaning no one will wear the number 11 again for the Cardinals. On the field, […]
full_text: Arizona Cardinals fans cheer from the stands with signs for former player Larry Fitzgerald as the team takes on the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Oct. 25, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co I don’t want to be too negative, but it was nice of the Denver Broncos to host the Larry Fitzgerald Ring of Honor celebration… Anyways. The Arizona Cardinals inducted Larry Fitzgerald into their Ring of Honor, and retired his jersey, meaning no one will wear the number 11 again for the Cardinals. On the field, it wasn’t fun. The Cardinals gave up two huge plays to the Denver Broncos, a 62-yard Bo Nix touchdown run and a 52-yard R.J. Harvey screen pass for a touchdown, and the Broncos tied their season high in points, had their second most yardage of the season, and held the Cardinals to only 16 points in a 30-16 win at State Farm Stadium, which more resembled Empower Field at Mile High south. The Cardinals finally scored a touchdown for the first time in over 100 game minutes, that one went to Trey McBride, just like the last one did in their loss to the Detroit Lions. Bam Knight averaged nearly seven yards per carry, Trey McBride had 10 receptions for 111 yards and a touchdown, but the Cardinals could not sustain drives, and the final drive was a microcosm of their season, five plays inside the one yard line thanks to Denver penalties, and then a fourth down play after a sack took them back to the five, and no points. The Cardinals redzone offense was 11-23 coming into the game, and were 1-5 today, making them a disastrous 12-28 on the season. Just another game where there is a complete failure on all sides of the football, which is disappointing coming off the win in Los Angeles, but more disappointing because of how they played in what should have been a great day celebrating the Cardinals and their legend, Larry Fitzgerald.

full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 08: Larry Fitzgerald speaks during the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Enshrinement Ceremony at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 08, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the Arizona Cardinals, they have a select group of special players in their history. While Larry Fitzgerald is the 20th to be inducted into the teams Ring of Honor, what makes the induction really special is not just that he joins those 19 other members in the teams Ring of Honor, it is that he is only the sixth player in team history to have his number retired. Fitz joins tight end J.V. Cain (88), two-way player Marshall Goldberg (99), tackle Stan Mauldin (77), safety Larry Wilson (8), and of course Pat Tillman (40). No one will ever wear 11 while playing for the Arizona Cardinals again. Fitzgerald is the 16th player who spent all or a significant part of his career with the Cardinals and is the first one who is truly Arizona in his career. This is going to be a special time that allows the fans to celebrate one of not just the greats in Cardinals history, but also in NFL history. Congrats to Larry Fitzgerald.

title: Week 7 snap reactions: Falcons fight off their demons and finish
summary: The Atlanta Falcons finally won a home game, and they did it the only way they know how, by giving you a heart attack. Here are the Week 7 snap reactions. National Tight Ends Day Tommy Rees celebrated the occasion by getting his tight ends involved; every one on the active roster finished the game […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 25: Nick Muse #87 of the Atlanta Falcons reacts after a touchdown reception during the second quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons finally won a home game, and they did it the only way they know how, by giving you a heart attack. Here are the Week 7 snap reactions. Week 7: Atlanta Falcons vs San Francisco 49ers https://t.co/bunziB0sVH pic.twitter.com/DnGiWeIXbx — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 25, 2026 National Tight Ends Day Tommy Rees celebrated the occasion by getting his tight ends involved; every one on the active roster finished the game with at least one catch. Kyle Pitts led the way, scoring another touchdown and marking three straight games with at least one. Nick Muse came in with one career catch and left with two and a touchdown, and Austin Hooper and Charlie Woerner got active to the tune of 3 receptions for 30 yards. We’ve been waiting for Rees to lean on his tight ends more, and we were rewarded. Every day should be Tight Ends Day for this offense. Welcome to the National Tight Ends Day touchdown party, @kylepitts__ SFvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/xisNvvBH2q — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Defense holds off the comeback The 49ers moved the ball well in the second half, but two critical defensive stops saved the day. With their backs up against their own end zone, the Falcons prevented the 49ers from scoring and sacked Brock Purdy on 4th down . Later, after the Falcons offense went three-and-out again, rookie LB Kendal Daniels turned the tide with a sensational interception, shutting down the 49ers comeback hopes. He later scooped up a fumble caused by Jessie Bates III, officially ending the game. The defense forced four turnovers today, and that was the difference. It wasn’t always pretty, but the defense got it done when it mattered most. @AtlantaFalcons rookie Kendal Daniels gets his first career interception in the clutch SFvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9BtAUNZQLm — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Special Teams still killing the team The opening return from Branch was great to see, but I think I speak for everyone when I say it’s getting exhausting watching this unit play bad football. Teams are almost guaranteed to start with the ball on the 35, and after having little issue on the punt team, Jake Bailey shanked a punt at the worst possible moment. Nick Folk missing an extra point attempt was the cherry on top. Luckily, the offense and defense carried the load today, but this unit keeps making costly mistakes week in and week out. Michael Penix Jr. is growing In back-to-back weeks, Penix has thrown three touchdowns and zero interceptions; this was the third such game of his career, and the first in a win. Growth isn’t linear, and while the quarterback would like a few throws back, that’s how every quarterback feels at the end of the game. The young quarterback is looking more comfortable week to week, and while his mobility will never be elite, he looked a tad more limber today, and I expect that to continue as he gets further away from the knee injury. The offense can’t stall out during the middle of the fourth, but it is nice that the QB wasn’t the main reason for those negative series. Michael Penix Jr. throwing chart pic.twitter.com/F7nD7Hp3Kt — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 25, 2026 The Falcons are now 3-4; their season is far from over, and the NFC South is still wide open . Atlanta needed to prove they could finish, and with this win under their belt, they proved they could do it. Enjoy the win!

title: Falcons – 49ers instant recap: A delightful upset against an undefeated team
summary: An undefeated 49ers team coming to town, where the Falcons had yet to win, seemed like a recipe for disaster. Even with the 49ers mightily banged up, they had gone 6-0 to this point and the Falcons had been struggling. It was not always pretty and it certainly wasn’t easy, but these Falcons showed an […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 25: Drake London #5 of the Atlanta Falcons celebrates with teammates Austin Hooper #81 and Chris Blair #19 after scoring a touchdown against the San Francisco 49ers during the fourth quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images An undefeated 49ers team coming to town, where the Falcons had yet to win, seemed like a recipe for disaster. Even with the 49ers mightily banged up, they had gone 6-0 to this point and the Falcons had been struggling. It was not always pretty and it certainly wasn’t easy, but these Falcons showed an incredible amount of talent, heart, and savvy in this one to come away with a 29-20 win. The defense forced four turnovers, the offense put together some impressive drives, special teams finally gave Atlanta favorable field position, and Atlanta got their first home win of the 2026 season against a formerly undefeated team. It was a glorious, messy win that once again reminded us of what this team can be, and a sorely needed one after two tough losses in a row. Who knows what this team can be when all is said and done, but the tenacity and will on Sunday was a thing of beauty and hopefully is a sign of better days to come. With the Panthers getting smoked by the Buccaneers, Atlanta is right back in the division and has all the opportunity in the world in front of them. What a day. Here’s a drive-by-drive recap of the game you just watched. 1st Quarter Atlanta kicked it off to open things up, and the 49ers got a seam and took it across the 35 yard line. The 49ers opened up their drive with a jump offsides by Trent Williams. Christian McCaffrey evaded defenders and picked up five yards before Xavier Watts got him. McCaffrey then plunged up the middle, with the Falcons reacting late to the delayed handoff and allowing him to run for almost a first down. McCaffrey then slinked through the middle of the line and picked 14 yards. A quick pass to McCaffrey over the middle got 16 yards and another first down. Kendal Daniels then got Kaelon Black for a small loss. Purdy then hung in with pressure lagging and found McCaffrey again for 24 yards. Black then got the handoff and got four yards, with Atlanta dropping him just shy of a touchdown. Black was then stopped cold by LaCale London as he ran up the middle. On his third straight carry, the Falcons stopped Black again. McCaffrey then leaped over the top of the defense and got far enough to score the touchdown on fourth down. 7-0 49ers. Zachariah Branch finally broke one, getting a lane and running 61 yards on the kickoff return. Bijan Robinson took it 11 on first down, and followed that up with seven more yards. Michael Penix Jr. then tried to hit Branch on second down, but didn’t connect. On 3rd and 3, Bijan got tackled for a three yard loss by Fred Warner. Nick Folk hit the 39 yard field goal try to make it 7-3 49ers. The 49ers got it past the 30. McCaffrey made a fully extended sideline grab for five yards. Black then took it for a yard before London got him. Purdy then hit George Kittle for a first down. An all-out rush on first down then took down Purdy, as Maason Smith got home for a sack. Smith then deflected the Purdy pass. A quick swing pass to the fullback was stopped by Harold Perkins Jr., setting up a punt. Jahan Dotson made the fair catch at about the 10. Bijan took the opening handoff for three yards. A quick swing pass to Robinson went nowhere with a defender right in his face, and he lost three yards. A 12 men in the huddle penalty backed the Falcons up. Penix then hit Austin Hooper for nine yards. Punt, and the 49ers caught it around the 38 yard line. 2nd Quarter Purdy rolled out and got Kittle for a first down. Black ran for a first down, and the 49ers declined a neutral zone infraction on Jared Ivey. Black then rolled for about seven yards before Daniels got him. Then Black got loose and ran for a 30 yard touchdown to put the 49ers up 14-3. Penix scrambled for two yards and then hit Bijan for a 15 yard pickup and a first down. Bijan took it six yards, and then Bijan was stymied for a gain of a yard. Penix then hit Drake London for a first down. Penix then found Charlie Woerner for nine yards, with Woerner spinning through contact. Bijan then fought through contact for another first down. A flip to Bijan was then flipped to Branch on the reverse, who ran for eight yards to the sideline. A swing pass to Khalil Herbert picked up 19 yards and almost went for a score, with Chris Blair with a tremendous box out block. The Falcons challenged the spot but didn’t win the challenge. Penix then hit a wide open Nick Muse for a touchdown. 14-9 49ers after Nick Folk doinked the extra point try. The 49ers got to the 30 on their return. Purdy tried for Brandin Cooks, his first throw to a receiver, and missed. Black then pushed his way through the pile for seven yards. Purdy then hit on the sideline for a first down. A toss to Black was stopped after maybe a yard. An end-around to Jacob Cowing went for ten yards. Purdy under pressure was able to flip it to Jordan James, who got 11 yards and a first down. James then took another carry and pushed his way forward for close to eight yards, but fumbled with an assist from Xavier Watts; the 49ers got it back. On the next carry, Black ran into the defense and fumbled with an assist from Maason Smith, with Gervon Dexter recovering. Penix hit London on first down for seven yards. A faked handoff to Robinson gave way to a pass under pressure to Kyle Pitts, who got two yards. A direct snap to Woerner went for a first down (really). Bijan then rolled ahead for five yards. Bijan then plunged ahead for a first down. Penix under pressure found Muse for a yard. Penix then hit Pitts for six yards. Penix then tried to get Jahan Dotson crossing over the middle, but Dotson just didn’t catch it. The Falcons got the 49ers to jump offsides on fourth down, somehow. Penix then got Branch, who dove forward for a first down. Penix then got a first down throw to Dotson. Then Penix hit Bijan on the sideline, who just got out of bounds with seven seconds yet. Penix then threw it out of bounds in the direction of London with two seconds left. Folk then hit the 33 yard field goal try to make it 14-12 49ers. 3rd Quarter Khalil Herbert dropped the kickoff but didn’t let it slow him, rolling past the 40 yard line on the kickoff return. A quick flip to Pitts got the Falcons started with nine yards. Bijan plunged ahead for about five yards. Then Penix hit Hooper for 11 yards and a first down, with Hooper getting in a nice stiff arm. Robinson took a delayed handoff for a yard. Pitts then reeled in a short screen pass as Penix was pressured, picking up three yards. Penix then found London over the middle, who stayed on his feet forever because he’s Drake London. Herbert then took the handoff for a couple of yards. London then caught another one over the middle and plunged forward to the five yard line. On the next play, Penix calmly rolled out and hit Kyle Pitts for a touchdown, Pitts’ fourth scoring grab in the past three weeks. 19-14 Falcons. Jordan James got past the 30 before DeMarcco Hellams got him. A diving Jordan Watkins got the 15 yard first down grab. xDexter then took down McCaffrey for a loss. Kittle then caught a first down. Purdy had forever on a rollout and hit a tight end for a first down. A swing pass to Black went for a four yard loss after Perkins got him. Then Purdy threw an interception on what was intended to be a throwaway to Jessie Bates. A slant to London went for eight yards, and London exited for a check after a 49ers defender went helmet-to-helmet with him. Bijan then took it three yards for a first down. Robinson then rolled for over 25 yards, but a holding call on Atlanta backed it up. Penix then skipped one to the sideline looking for Chris Blair. Penix then hauled one back downfield for Dotson, looking for a deep completion, but…

title: Intriguing players to watch in Falcons vs. 49ers
summary: As the Atlanta Falcons look to rebound from a two-game skid against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers, several players will be in the spotlight. If the Falcons pull off the upset and become the first team in 2026 to beat the 49ers, these five players will need to shine brightest. Bijan Robinson You can bet […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 18: Atlanta linebacker Kendal Daniels (53) reacts prior to the start of the NFL game between the Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons on October 18th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images As the Atlanta Falcons look to rebound from a two-game skid against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers , several players will be in the spotlight. If the Falcons pull off the upset and become the first team in 2026 to beat the 49ers, these five players will need to shine brightest. Bijan Robinson You can bet the Falcons will make a concerted effort to feature running back Bijan Robinson in Week 7. He’s coming off just nine carries against the Chicago Bears , the lowest total in his last 17 games. With backup Brian Robinson also out , expect a hefty dose of Bijan early and often. On top of that, the Falcons face 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey, who has mentored and served as an offseason workout partner in recent years, meaning the student will face even more pressure to outshine the master. It’s no understatement to say that if the Falcons can feature Robinson early and often, they’ll massively increase their odds of pulling off the upset. Kyle Pitts With Sunday marking National Tight Ends Day, the spotlight will also be on Kyle Pitts. Pitts has generally been productive on this invented annual football celebration, most notably with a dominant 163-yard performance during his rookie season. He’ll have another chance to cement his holiday legacy and build on a strong fourth-quarter performance against the Bears, which helped the Falcons roar back from a 24-point deficit last week. If that late-game performance can be a springboard into four quarters of similar production against the 49ers, it’ll definitely increase the odds of the Falcons pulling off the upset. Kendal Daniels & Harold Perkins Rookie linebackers Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins will have to fill the large shoes of Divine Deablo, who will be out Sunday . Daniels is listed as questionable but appears ready to suit up against the 49ers despite a scary neck injury that had him carted off in last week’s loss to the Bears. He’ll wear the green dot in Deablo’s stead as the team’s every-down defensive signal-caller. Meanwhile, Perkins will likely remain a part-time starter in nickel subpackages, while Josh Woods gets the early-down snaps in base and big nickel looks. Regardless of their usage, both will have their hands full as the Falcons look to slow down McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle. Perkins’ speed and coverage prowess were on full display three weeks ago against Saints TE Juwan Johnson, and he’ll need to repeat that performance to keep Kittle in check. Daniels’ propensity to blow up screens will also come into play as the team tries to slow down the dual threat McCaffrey out of the backfield. A.J. Terrell After four weeks on I.R. , the Falcons should get a big boost by the return of their top coverage player , A.J. Terrell. His return and nickel corner Billy Bowman’s absence will prompt the team to reshuffle its cornerback room this week. Will Avieon Terrell or Mike Hughes fill Bowman’s shoes at nickel ? Will C.J. Henderson, also returning from injury, be in the mix at the other outside cornerback spot? It leaves several questions at cornerback, but one isn’t about how valuable the elder Terrell will be to defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich’s plans against the 49ers. Terrell’s ability to lock down whoever remains of the 49ers’ injury-depleted receivers gives Ulbrich a huge boost, letting him focus the remaining 10 defenders on containing playmakers like McCaffrey and Kittle. This makes Terrell a critical part of keeping a lid on the NFL’s No. 3 scoring offense . Will these players shine and help the Falcons pull off the upset and take down the 49ers? Can you name any more Falcons that intrigue you in this matchup?

title: Falcons vs. 49ers: What will Week 7’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?
summary: It’s become danger time for the Atlanta Falcons, who have sandwiched their two impressive and feel good victories in prime time against the Saints and Packers in between a pair of two game losing streaks which have them stuck inside a hole, and they better get moving to maneuver their way out quick. The Birds […]
full_text: It’s become danger time for the Atlanta Falcons, who have sandwiched their two impressive and feel good victories in prime time against the Saints and Packers in between a pair of two game losing streaks which have them stuck inside a hole, and they better get moving to maneuver their way out quick. The Birds once again laid an egg in a home game which resembled at best a neutral sight battle and at worst an absolute Bears fan takeover, against Chicago. Things don’t get any easier as they now host the undefeated San Francisco 49ers, led by two Falcon coaches of yesteryear in Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris, who are looking to bury their former employer’s season. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the San Francisco 49ers in Week 7, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win It will be one of the bigger upsets in the NFL season up to this point and they will bring the 1972 Miami Dolphins one step closer to their yearly champagne celebration, which happens after the final undefeated team suffers its first blemish. This one would bring about memories of 2019, when the 4-9 Falcons went to the Bay and upset the 11-2 Niners in one of the shocks of the season. This ship that is Atlanta’s season may start to get steadied just in time to avoid the impending iceberg that’s now clearly visible in the distance. The Birds would move to 3-4 with a chance to pull themselves back to the surface with a game against the struggling Buccaneers next week as they navigate the difficult portion of the schedule. The first place Carolina Panthers currently play the Bucs this week. Atlanta could get to within one game in the loss column if Tampa pulls off an upset. They would also shake away from the New Orleans Saints if the Kellen Moore led team stumbles in its game against Pittsburgh, played in Paris this weekend. If the Falcons lose Things will be derailing in real time as even a victory against Tampa next week (which is not a given) won’t be able to put them in a decent position. They would be 3-5 with games against the Bengals and Chiefs before the bye week and games against the Lions and Vikings on the other side of the bye. It doesn’t get much more brutal. Needless to say, at this point we will already need to start looking at Atlanta’s potential draft position moving forward, as 2-5 would be justification enough to do so. There’s a large cluster of 2-4 teams in the league right now, and any who lose this weekend will likely be in top 10 draft pick placement for the time being. Raheem Morris would continue what seems to have become a tradition of a former Falcons head coach who was fired returning to Atlanta the very next season and beating the Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Dan Quinn came back as Cowboys defensive coordinator and won in 2021, Arthur Smith came back as Steelers offensive coordinator and won in 2024, and now Morris will have come back as 49ers defensive coordinator and won.
author: Adnan Ikic

title: Ravens Monday hangover discussion: recovering from collapse vs. Cincy
summary: We aren’t even close to the holiday season. Heck, we haven’t even made it to Halloween! And there are still almost two months until Festivus, the holiday created by Seinfeld that comes on December 23. But after Sunday’s loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, Baltimore Ravens fans deserve an early chance to air their grievances. In […]
full_text: Oct 25, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter reacts during the second quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We aren’t even close to the holiday season. Heck, we haven’t even made it to Halloween! And there are still almost two months until Festivus, the holiday created by Seinfeld that comes on December 23. But after Sunday’s loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, Baltimore Ravens fans deserve an early chance to air their grievances. In todya Nikhil’s grievance: I’ll have to dive into the film to dissect what went wrong in coverage beyond individual mistakes, but on offense, the short-yardage issues are absolutely inexcusable. What is most frustrating is the variety of mistakes. A one-yard distance was extended to six after a false start three times. Derrick Henry was stuffed (again). After a couple of conversions, Declan Doyle got too cute with his play-calling. Tyler Huntley and Ja’Kobi Lane failed to connect on a potential touchdown that Lamar Jackson probably completes. Which brings me to the obvious: yes, the Ravens should be better in short-yardage in Jackson. And yet, it was already a problem when he was on the field. The solution comes from identifying the failures. Opponents are already stacking the box on third-and-short waiting to swallow up Henry – why run him into the pile when the pile includes Dexter Lawrence? Doyle found early success with two-RB ‘pony’ packages featuring Henry and Justice Hill, but the Bengals were ready when he went back to the well for a third time. The element of deception was lacking on Hill’s second-quarter sweep; Zay Flowers had only been eye candy, so the defense barely reacted to his jet motion. That actually would have been the time to mix in a sweep and keep the menu open for the rest of the game! As for the penalties, we’re well beyond the acceptable adjustment window for a new staff and a new scheme, even including the grace period for changes along the offensive line and at quarterback. (That last part matters less when full-year starters are committing the pre-snap fouls.) The Ravens have actually improved post-snap in the last three weeks, but after just two pre-snap penalties in Atlanta, they have 12 in their last two weeks. Like I said: well past acceptable.

title: We asked, you answered: early grades for the Ravens’ new coaching staff
summary: Last week, Baltimore Beatdown asked Ravens fans to grade Jesse Minter’s new coaching staff through six weeks on the job. At the time, the team was 4-2 coming off a loss to the Browns featuring another blown double-digit lead in the second half. In previous weeks, though, the Ravens closed out games against the Colts […]
full_text: Last week, Baltimore Beatdown asked Ravens fans to grade Jesse Minter’s new coaching staff through six weeks on the job. At the time, the team was 4-2 coming off a loss to the Browns featuring another blown double-digit lead in the second half. In previous weeks, though, the Ravens closed out games against the Colts and the Titans and showed their mettle in tight wins over the Cowboys and the Falcons. Those results earned the coaching staff a B- overall grade from Baltimore Beatdown readers in last week’s survey: Minter and his staff came in with Super Bowl expectations, and through six games, the Ravens did not look consistently look like a true championship contender. There were two clear reasons for hope: the offense getting healthier, and positive adjustments from Minter as his first-year defense settles in. However, the team was still dealing with the second-half demons they tried to exorcise by firing John Harbaugh. It took some luck – a seven-second miracle and an overtime coin flip, to be exact – to reach four wins, and Baltimore’s record could just as easily be 2-4. So, all told, 4-2 is meeting but certainly not exceeding expectations this early in the seasons. Variance between B and C is probably based on different weights for injuries and expectations for improvements. Frequent commenter jack aka potato jones sums it up: I gotta give em a solid B. They obviously haven’t been perfect, but we’re seeing improvements with penalties and defense, and they’ve made the best of a terrible OL situation for the most part. I feel like an A would be at least a 5-1 record so B feels right. Of course, these grades would likely be drastically different after Sunday’s loss to the Bengals – firmly in the C range, likely with a sharp bump in D’s and as many F’s as A’s (if not more). The same will likely be true of fans’ overall confidence in the team’s direction, which was up at 79% after beating the Falcons before dropping to 48% following the Browns loss. After the catastrophe vs. Cincy, this number will plummet, potentially into the single-digits unless there is a positive update on Lamar Jackson by the middle of the week. But betting markets are hardly so fickle. The Ravens are still in a similar range to win the Super Bowl ( +1100, via FanDuel Sportsbook ) though their win total and playoff odds have taken a hit as they fall behind in the AFC North. Winning the division is not out of reach, but Baltimore probably has to sweep their remaining four matchups to do it.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Top takeaways from Ravens’ Week 7 loss to Bengals
summary: The Baltimore Ravens gave up 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals in the second half of Sunday’s game, resulting in their second AFC North loss in a row. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s takeaways from the game: Where are the Ravens’ leaders? With respect to the Ravens’ veteran players and coaches, it is clear that […]
full_text: Oct 25, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Cincinnati Bengals halfback Samaje Perine (34) holds back Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey (44) during the second half at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens gave up 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals in the second half of Sunday’s game, resulting in their second AFC North loss in a row. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s takeaways from the game: Where are the Ravens’ leaders? With respect to the Ravens’ veteran players and coaches, it is clear that leadership is lacking in Baltimore. For better and for worse, Lamar Jackson cures virtually all ills on the offensive side of the ball. He keeps his teammates focused and makes the impossible plays when they are necessary. But who is that on the Ravens defense? They have a laundry list of names – Kyle Hamilton, Roquan Smith, Marlon Humphrey, Calais Campbell, Nnamdi Madubuike – but they are all polished, well-spoke players, perhaps to a fault. Who is on the sidelines holding their teammates accountable – loudly, aggressively, if need be? Ray Lewis, Ed Reed, and Terrell Suggs may be nearly impossible to live up to, but they represent the standard nonetheless. Seeing some of those legends chime in during the game on social media made me cringe in embarrassment for the team. And, yes, the coaches deserve a glance here, too. Minter is occupied during the game, sure, but but keeping his players in the game should be Anthony Weaver’s bread-and-butter. – Nikhil Mehta Defensive coaching disappeared in the second half Cincy’s first half offense struggled, in no small part due Baltimore’s pass rush consistently collapsing the pocket around Joe Burrow. Even on plays that weren’t finished with sacks, he had to throw the ball away multiple times, leaving the Bengals’ two primary targets in Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase quiet on the stat sheet. When the second half rolled around, the Bengals initially adjusted by getting the ball out quickly. The Ravens defense kept dropping additional guys back in coverage and rushing three or four, and giving Burrow all day to pick apart the zone defense over the middle of the field. Tee Higgins was out there bullying the secondary, and Burrow picked on Keondre Jackson as he tried to fill into a larger role. Some struggles are expected, even forgivable, against this tough offense, but Jesse Minter’s play0calling showed no aggressiveness to put second-half pressure on the Bengals when they needed to. By the time Cincy came away with their second touchdown, the DBs were looking around at each other like they did not even know the play call. Communication on the back end was a key hallmark of the failures in Zach Orr’s tenure, and today felt like it was a reoccurrence of those old issues. – Kevin McNelis Short yardage situations are (still) a massive issue . The Ravens’ offense cannot operate at its true potential when short-yardage situations feel like pushing a boulder up a mountain. Derrick Henry has been extremely ineffective on short runs this season, both due to his own lack of push and consistently being hit in the backfield. Baltimore needs to look at another back to carry the ball in such situations going forward, whether that is Justice Hill, Rasheen Ali, or Adam Randall when he returns from injured reserve. I would not be opposed to trading for a power back either at this point. – Dustin Cox
