title: Ravens discussion: instant reactions to 2nd-half collapse vs. Bengals
summary: The Baltimore Ravens appeared to be on their way to another surprising win with Tyler Huntley at the helm of their offense, taking a 13-0 lead into halftime against the Cincinnati Bengals. But Baltimore’s defense completely folded in the second half with no support from an offense that managed just two first downs after their […]
full_text: Oct 25, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) makes a catch for a touchdown during the second half against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens appeared to be on their way to another surprising win with Tyler Huntley at the helm of their offense, taking a 13-0 lead into halftime against the Cincinnati Bengals. But Baltimore’s defense completely folded in the second half with no support from an offense that managed just two first downs after their first drive on the third quarter. The Bengals dropped 35 unanswered points, leading to a dismal 35-13 final result that leaves the Ravens at 4-3 heading into a tough stretch with two games against division-leading teams in the next 11 days. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to Sunday’s loss: Nikhil Mehta Jesse Minter and Anthony Weaver should have to watch that second half before every single one of their defensive meetings for the rest of the season. Allowing four straight touchdown drives out of halftime – three of at least 65 yards – is completely inexcusable for what is supposed to be one of the better defenses in the NFL. On every play, the Ravens seemed to be a second behind, unable to finish plays in the backfield or limit explosive passes over the top. Those struggles distracted from another woeful second half from an offense that simple cannot get out of its own way with procedural penalties. Vega Ioane’s knee injury also seemed to have a major impact with a steep drop-off in right guard play to Emery Jones. But regardless of his personnel issues, Declan Doyle’s inability to figure out short yardage is maddening. Even when Lamar Jackson is back, this team has major issues that currently will keep them far from the AFC North crown. Stephen Bopst I’m not really sure where you go from here if you’re the Ravens. I don’t know if the stats would support this but this must be one of the more stark performance differences between a second half and first half in NFL history. The Ravens completely dominated the first half – but it didn’t matter. Predictably, they fell apart the moment the second half started allowing the Bengals to score touchdowns on every drive. Offensively, the Ravens couldn’t do much in the second half and couldn’t convert in short yardage or in the red zone – even when the offense was productive. Even if Lamar Jackson comes back healthy, there’s no way to have optimism about them. The offensive line can’t hold a block, the defense can’t tackle, and the pass rush completely disappeared in the second half. This looks like the same team from last year that’s been covered up by an easy schedule. It might be an overreaction, but Jesse Minter and Eric DeCosta’s seats should be warming up a little. Kevin McNelis The fanbase used to be angry about this. Then they became numb. Now, I think we might all actually be expecting the blown leads. I’m grateful that Lamar is expected back next week, but he’s going to need to put on a master class if they have any hope of keeping pace in the next couple of games. I don’t know what the plan was in the second half on defense, but the absences of Tavius Robinson, Jaylinn Hawkins and Roquan Smith (for a potion of the half) should never have had an impact like that. To have an opponent score touchdowns on five straight possessions is inexcusable. Back-to-back weeks of getting humiliated on defense by division opponents has this defense looking mentally broken, and I’m not sure how they fix it. Dustin Cox The Ravens being this helpless without Lamar Jackson is not a good sign for this team going forward. I truly do not understand how the defense could allow 35 points in the second half after shutting the Bengals out through the first two quarters. Missed tackles, blown coverages, and a lack of finishing sacks has haunted this unit for years now and I am completely lost on how Jesse Minter is supposed to go about fixing it. Giving up plays to a talented Cincinnati offense was always expected, but 35 points in one half is simply inexcusable with the resources invested into the defense and a highly-touted defensive head coach now. On offense, I would love to say that the issues boiled down to Jackson’s absence, but the problems go beyond just quarterback play. The offensive line continues to be a revolving door due to injuries, with Vega Ioane being the latest, while Short-yardage situations feel impossibly hard. Derrick Henry, when not getting hit behind the line of scrimmage, has not looked like usual dominant self outside of a few games this season. Declan Doyle needs to seriously consider giving another running back the ball on short-yardage runs going forward. Getting Jackson back next week will help tremendously, but Minter, Doyle, Anthony Weaver, and Anthony Levine Sr. all have some serious soul searching to do after these past two losses. Zach Canter The Ravens are a bad team right now. The roster needs a massive reset. Lamar Jackson doesn’t add enough to fix what happened here. The offensive line is too soft to get a yard when it’s 3rd/4th-and-short, and losing Vega Ioane isn’t enough to take the entire blame there. The scripted plays and drives on offense were great again, but Huntley once again couldn’t do much outside of that and they didn’t convert in the red zone enough. The defense pissed down their leg in the second half once more, giving up 35 unanswered. I’m over blaming coaches. We blamed Harbaugh and Orr and Monken and Roman and Macdonald (early in his career). Now everybody wants to be mad at Minter and Doyle. But I’m over it. The players aren’t good enough. They are mentally and physically soft. Minter and Doyle aren’t perfect. But eventually players need to be held accountable.

title: Ravens discussion: last-minute predictions for Week 7 vs. Bengals
summary: It’s almost time for the Ravens’ Week 7 matchup with the Bengals! Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s last-minute predictions: Nikhil Mehta Like the Falcons, the Bengals seem like an especially bad matchup for the Ravens. Baltimore’s offensive line finally has their best five, but it is still Cam Jurgens’ first game snapping to Tyler Huntley in […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Tyler Huntley #5 of the Baltimore Ravens plays against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s almost time for the Ravens’ Week 7 matchup with the Bengals! Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s last-minute predictions: Nikhil Mehta Like the Falcons, the Bengals seem like an especially bad matchup for the Ravens. Baltimore’s offensive line finally has their best five, but it is still Cam Jurgens’ first game snapping to Tyler Huntley in a new offense. And he has to deal with Dexter Lawrence. On defense, well, we’ve seen this movie before Joe Burrow to Ja’Marr Chase for first down or a touchdown at all of the worst moments. But I picked against the Ravens in Atlanta, and Derrick Henr X-factor: Ja’Kobi Lane. Huntley needs a big, quarterback-friendly target that he can trust with contested catches, whether he’s trying to push the ball downfield or hit a hot read against the blitz. Lane has proven he can operate in traffic over the middle with a good feel for picking up the requisite yards for a first down. This feels like a good week for his first regular-season touchdown. Score prediction: Ravens 24, Bengals 21 Frank Platko With no Lamar Jackson, the Ravens’ offense will again be limited. Therefore, the onus will be on their defense to carry the load, as they did last week, but forcing turnovers may be necessary. If the Ravens’ defense can come up with a takeaway or two and give their offense a short-field to work with, that could make a huge difference. Their pass rush against Joe Burrow needs to be relentless and effective to disrupt the Bengals’ lethal passing attack. X-factor: Cam Jurgens. Expecting great results from Jurgens in his first game as a Raven, coming off a concussion, may be unfair. However, the Ravens will need him to hold his own in a tough matchup against DT Dexter Lawrence. If Jurgens is overwhelmed in one-on-one matchups with Lawrence, the latter might wreck any chance of offensive success for the Ravens. Score prediction: Ravens 17, Bengals 24 Kevin McNelis Last week wasn’t pretty, and while they get multiple pieces a little healthier, they’re now down Tavius Robinson and still without Lamar Jackson. It doesn’t bode well as they face a well-rounded Bengals team that’s given the secondary fits even when the Ravens have managed to win against them over the past few seasons. Derrick Henry’s success was limited last week, and maybe the offense can mix it up a little bit more than they did last week, but they’re going to need the defense to make some plays and set up short fields if they want to have any hope of winning this game. The next guys up in Zion Young, Mike Green, and Keondre Jackson filling in for Jaylinn Hawkins can prove that they deserve bigger spots by stepping up and making big plays in the expanded roles. X-factor: I’d even venture to give Keondre Jackson my X-factor player for this game based on how important the back end of the defense is going to be as they face the Bengals receivers. My heart has hope, but my head feels like it knows where this game goes. Score prediction: Bengals 27, Ravens 16 Dustin Cox Any game without Lamar Jackson will be tough to win for the Ravens, but a divisional matchup with a Bengals team fresh off a bye week is an especially difficult hurdle to overcome with a backup quarterback. If Baltimore wants to pull off the upset with Tyler Huntley on Sunday, then getting the run game going with Derrick Henry is absolutely paramount to sustaining offensive success. Henry was bottled up against the Browns a week ago and Huntley was unable to carry the load with his arm. If the Ravens can get a classic Henry performance, then they should have a real chance against the Bengals. Baltimore’s defense has played better in recent weeks, but Sunday will present their toughest challenge yet with Joe Burrow throwing to Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. The Ravens’ secondary has done a good job of eliminating explosive plays down the field, but Chase and Higgins will put that to the test. I predict a respectable fight from the Ravens, but without Jackson, I do not foresee Baltimore’s offense having enough juice to keep up with Cincinnati’s passing attack over the course of four quarters. X-factor: Trey Hendrickson. Hendrickson is surely chomping at the bit to get back at his former team on Sunday. While the secondary will need to be at their best, an effective pass rush would go a long way in preventing Burrow from having a field day through the air. Score prediction: Bengals 27 Ravens 20

title: NFL predictions: Ravens need Trey Hendrickson revenge game vs. Bengals
summary: The Baltimore Ravens let a 10-0 lead slip away in Cleveland in Week 6. Their Tyler Huntley-led offense disappeared after a strong start, placing a hefty burden on a defense that just could not hold in the fourth quarter. In Week 7, the Ravens host the Cincinnati Bengals. Huntley will start once again with Lamar […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Trey Hendrickson #91 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he takes the field against the New Orleans Saints prior to an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens let a 10-0 lead slip away in Cleveland in Week 6. Their Tyler Huntley-led offense disappeared after a strong start, placing a hefty burden on a defense that just could not hold in the fourth quarter. In Week 7, the Ravens host the Cincinnati Bengals. Huntley will start once again with Lamar Jackson’s high ankle sprain sidelining him for a third straight contest. News of his absence shifted Baltimore to 2.5-point home underdogs (via FanDuel Sportsbook). Here’s how Jesse Minter’s squad can beat the odds and secure their fifth win of the season: Baltimore’s offense runs through The King The Bengals’ new-look run defense has some obscene splits in the run game. They have stuffed opposing rushers and allowed explosive runs at the highest rate in the league, per Next Gen Stats. They are also allowing 1.47 yards over expectation/attempt and 2.62 yards before contact/attempt, both league-highs by a considerable margin. The contrasts continue depending on the gap. Between the tackles, opposing rushers are averaging just 3.3 yards per carry as opposed to 6.0 to the outside. The middle is closed for business, almost entirely thanks to Dexter Lawrence. The offseason trade acquisition has been as advertised to start his Bengals tenure, dominating the trenches next to fellow veteran addition Jonathan Allen. If nose tackles eat space in the trenches, Lawrence is Joey Chestnut. There is no running around him, and there is certainly no running through him. Instead, Declan Doyle needs to embrace one of the NFL’s time-honored offensive strategies: run away from the defense’s best player. Derrick Henry still gets the edge better than any 6-foot-3, 252-pounder has any business, and attacking the outside will take pressure off Cam Jurgens in his first start as a Raven. Few players are as familiar with Lawrence’s abilities as the former Eagles center. He knows there is no beating Lawrence. There is no stopping his 6-foot-5, 350-pound frame. But he can be slowed by an agile center who can wall him off on outside zone runs and force him to chase plays laterally. Jurgens has to beat Lawrence to the spot and dig in long enough for Henry to get by. From there, The King can attack a Bengals secondary that has struggled to tackle this season. Ravens need a Trey Hendrickson revenge game On the defensive side of the ball, the Ravens need another one of the NFL’s time-honored traditions: a revenge game. Trey Hendrickson downplayed his first matchup against his former team this week, but one line from his Thursday presser stood out: “As a Christian, I forgive.” But did he forget? Hendrickson has openly expressed his frustration with the Bengals during their multiple contract standoffs. He finally has a chance to stick it to the team that backed up the Brinks truck for their top offensive players but could not reward the NFL’s sack leader across the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Hendrickson’s matchup with Bengals left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. will be most crucial on third downs – Baltimore’s mortal enemy on defense this year. The former Raven’s overall pass-blocking metrics hold up, but he collapses in true pass sets – Pro Football Focus’ metric measuring standard dropback passing plays. Brown has allowed 11 of his 12 pressures and all three of his sacks in true pass sets, which will typically come in those third-and-long situations the Ravens need to solve. But the Bengals have coaches, too, coaches who will use tight end Drew Sample and running backs Chase Browns and Samaje Perine to chip Hendrickson. The Ravens have two potential counters. The first is using the focus on Hendrickson to set picks and free up other rushers, potentially Nnamdi Madubuike or a second-level blitzer looping to the outside. Jesse Minter will also have at least one opportunity for a more extreme call – overload pressure on the right side with Hendrickson dropping into coverage. This has to be deployed in the right moment against the right offensive formation, but Burrow has proven he can be baited into interceptions before. Hendrickson just needs to get some tips from Marlon Humphrey on catching with a wrapped hand. Now, it’s your turn! Put on your coaching cap and tell us how you would scheme up a Ravens win against the Bengals?
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Many in Bills Mafia demand better out of Buffalo in 2026 despite 5-1 record
summary: Longtime fans of the Buffalo Bills knew well the story heading into the 2026 NFL season: that anything short of the Super Bowl was bound to be met with copious skepticism. Due to that continued and lofty central plot, it’s reasonable to expect that two things are true of Bills Mafia: Each moment of success […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 18: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills throws a pass during the game at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Bills defeated the Raiders 33-30. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Longtime fans of the Buffalo Bills knew well the story heading into the 2026 NFL season: that anything short of the Super Bowl was bound to be met with copious skepticism. Due to that continued and lofty central plot, it’s reasonable to expect that two things are true of Bills Mafia: Each moment of success is likely to share the stage with criticism, and many fans will be measured in their approval due to a repeated belief that the worst outcome of “been there, done that” is the team’s ultimate destiny. It does seem absurd that quarterback Josh Allen has yet to even make a Super Bowl, let alone hoist a Lombardi Trophy. Yet when you consider the absurdity of the franchise failing to win a Super Bowl with an enviable core of Pro Football Hall of Fame players, things seem less crazy. Right now, the Bills probably have two championship-caliber players in Allen and running back James Cook III. I’d even throw in the offensive line for this equation because, without those five or six guys… likely pain. One might be willing to consider a few others on offense, but the old adage that any player’s best ability is availability holds true. The offense is humming along at a breakneck pace, able to overcome almost every challenge. Then there’s the defense, which might be generously described as a work in progress propped up by the Renaissance play of outside linebacker Greg Rousseau, potential-star defensive tackle Deone Walker, and steely veteran cornerback Christian Benford. That’s a solid core at all three levels, right? Certainly, but there’s far too much “but” to consider quite a few starters around them. The real crux of the issue is the defensive backfield and inside linebacker core. Yes, the defense is adapting to a new scheme we’ve been told is operating in hybrid fashion this season under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. The trouble is that mulligans don’t exist in the NFL, so every project and test comes with accountable results. That’s great for development’s sake, but relies on an offense that can continue putting up decently north of 30 points a game. With Josh Allen, all things appear possible. It’s just not a historically sustainable model. The great thing is that the mold was broken when Allen and One Bills Drive got to work. To his credit, Allen willingly addresses the pink elephants in the room. He knows the team has to improve in all three phases to become a more cohesive unit that feeds off one another. That’s the necessary path to take if they hope to catch even a glimpse of the required luck for Super Bowl glory. It’s Week 7, and still far too early to consider the game on February 14, 2027. You know the subject isn’t going away, and that it’s bound to remain the centerpiece of any conversation about Allen and these Bills. Akin to The Legend of Zelda so long ago, you and your friends probably couldn’t stop obsessing over finally getting to and defeating Ganon until it finally happened. You assuredly left your NES on all day while at school just so you didn’t lose any progress. As true as it was then of Zelda, there are no Contra codes for Josh Allen and the Bills. It’s all or nothing with their one best shot in 2026. That’s precisely why so many within Bills Mafia are hesitant to say they’re confident that One Bills Drive is headed in the right direction.The results of our latest confidence poll revealed that just 60% of Bills fans remain confident in the team’s direction under head coach Joe Brady and president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane. There are truths to be told how confidence swings drastically from week to week, all due to the quality of opponent and way in which a fan’s team wins. It’s true the Bills didn’t blow out the Las Vegas Raiders, which many still believe are not as talented as even their somewhat surprising 3-3 record implies a third of the way through the season. It’s probably true that every Bills fan would have signed up for 5-1 in the preseason, yet reality has re-shaped the way confidence is handed out. It might be time for more Bills fans to stop worrying about how Buffalo wins, and instead focus on the fact that the team does continue winning. If you interview 10 fans, five of them probably worry the Bills won’t continue winning against better teams — might even be six of those 10 fans, if you go by these results. We’ll continue asking Bills Mafia if they’re confident in the team each week of the season. It’s a fun exercise that fosters quality conversations at Buffalo Rumblings. We also realize that the answer lies in events months down the road rather than the here and now. Speaking of the here and now… One Bills Drive welcomed back veteran cornerback Tre’Davious White this past week, signing him to the practice squad. It’s a move to help bolster a defensive backs group that could use additional mentoring and a push to play better every down. We understand that White will ramp up to playing condition while on the practice squad before the team signs him to the 53-man active roster. White played rejuvenated football in 2025, though that was under the direction of former head coach Sean McDermott and a very familiar scheme. Leonhard’s scheme presents White with a new challenge for the 31-year-old now entering his 10th NFL season. We were curious to know what Rumblers thought of the team signing White, perhaps nudged by any expectations of what it meant for the rest of Buffalo’s cornerbacks… or maybe even safety. Is White simply back as an insurance policy, a sideline mentor, and someone who raises the floor for a Bills team desperately seeking shutdown play beyond Benford? We’ll find out in time, which explains why most voters are please with White’s signing but perhaps still unsure of what it means to the defense. Leading the way were the 39% of voters who gave the signing a “B.” Beyond that lead were the 31% of votes landing on “C,” and then the 22% of votes registering an “A” for White’s return. A small total of 8% of votes gave the move a “D” (5%) or “F” (3%). It’s officially goalie season again in Western New York! We close with results from one of SB Nation’s national polls this week. Which team with at least four wins is the biggest fraud? Well, you can be sure a lot of this comes down to allegiances, at least beyond the leading team. How unfortunate it must be for those born into Cleveland Browns fandom. The Browns lead these results with 33% of the vote as the biggest four-win frauds. Interestingly, the Minnesota Vikings come in second with 20% of the vote, while the New England Patriots make the list in its most favorable spot and last with just 4% of voters believing the Pats are four-win frauds. New England still made the list, however. Think you’ve got what it takes to make a play with the Buffalo Bills in 2026? Head over to FanDuel Sportsbook now and put it to the test !

title: The Optimist: I’ve got nothing
summary: There are not many good words that can be honestly ascribed to the Carolina Panthers abysmal 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. I’m not going to waste your time searching for them. The Panthers offense looked like their game plan was to see how far they could push a clown car with no wheels. […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 25: Zyon McCollum #27 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers hands a ball to a fan after an interception during the first half of a football game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are not many good words that can be honestly ascribed to the Carolina Panthers abysmal 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. I’m not going to waste your time searching for them. The Panthers offense looked like their game plan was to see how far they could push a clown car with no wheels. The Panthers defense looked like they couldn’t figure out how to defend the most one-dimensional offense they will ever see. With any luck, they were caught peeking ahead at the Green Bay Packers. An inexcusable sin is suddenly our greatest hope. Consistency, as always, is our greatest challenge. The same team this season has given up 258+ yards twice this season (258 against the Bucs and 291 vs Chicago) and held Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs to a combined 116 yards on 31 carries. Bryce Young was keeping statistical company with prime Peyton Manning and Drew Brees before he turned the ball over three times yesterday. Those three turnovers directly led to 11 more points than Young generated during the game. One game is not a trend and it doesn’t define a season. It can absolutely be cause for concern. All of the goodwill and optimism coming off of a two-week winning streak has now vanished. The Panthers will, once again, need to earn their fans back. The Bucs were low and provided a prime opportunity to for the Panthers to cement their intentions for a winning season. Baker Mayfield could hardly complete a pass downfield and that was what stood between them and their first three game winning streak since the 2021-Sam Darnold season. A win yesterday would have put the team in a strong position atop the NFC South and put them more than one game above .500 for the first time since that 2021 season as well. Instead, they proved that every game this season is likely to be a struggle. Poor protection—whose future looks worse with Taylor Moton’s fractured fibula —complemented poor run defense and whatever exactly that effort from the Carolina special teams unit was. None of these are flaws that are we can expect the team to snap back from with any immediacy. They will show up in every game to varying extents. The best news of the weekend is that the NFC South remains so hilariously bad that the Panthers are still in sole possession of first place in the division. At 3-3, all the Panthers have to do for now is beat the Green Bay Packers on Thursday Night Football. The 3-4 Atlanta Falcons have the opportunity to take the lead with a win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Tampa and a Panthers loss while the 2-5 New Orleans Saints are on a bye as they come home from Paris. This division is chaotic, but that also means it is forgiving. Yesterday was a terrible, demoralizing loss that imperiled our hopes for an NFC South repeat, but it didn’t sink them entirely. There is a lot of season left to play, so let’s all wash the taste of this game out and see what Thursday brings. Deep breaths, everybody. Let’s not burn everything down until it is cold enough outside to be worth it.

title: Panthers vs Buccaneers: Recap and reaction
summary: The Carolina Panthers defense regressed to Week 1 levels as they dropped an absolute stinker to the Tamp Bay Buccaneers, 43-13. First Quarter The Bucs won the toss and actually elected to take the ball first. They went with a heavy dose of Bucky Irving, and he diced up the Panthers, as is usually the […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - OCTOBER 25: Carolina Panthers quarter back Bryce Young (9) fumbles the ball in a pass attempt from a hit by Tampa Bay Buccaneers Payne Durham (87) during an NFL football game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Carolina Panthers on October 25, 2026 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers defense regressed to Week 1 levels as they dropped an absolute stinker to the Tamp Bay Buccaneers, 43-13. First Quarter The Bucs won the toss and actually elected to take the ball first. They went with a heavy dose of Bucky Irving, and he diced up the Panthers, as is usually the case. He carried the ball eight times and caught another pair of passes. There weren’t any huge plays. The defense just couldn’t get him to the ground without letting him slip away for a few extra yards. He eventually capped off the drive with a touchdown run. The Panthers went to their lead back to start, but they couldn’t sustain their drive. They quickly had to punt the ball back. The Bucs spelled Irving with Kenny Gainwell, and he was quite a bit easier to tackle. The Bucs matriculated out to midfield, but Bobby Okereke was able to blow up a third down run to the outside and force a punt. David Moore went back to do his only job, which is to catch the punt. He did not catch the punt. Instead, it bounced off his chest and was recovered by the Bucs. The quarter ended with Tampa Bay inside the five yard line. Second Quarter Tre Tucker slipped on a second down carry and then Okereke jumped up to knock away a Mayfield pass on third down. It led to a field goal and 10-0 score. A few plays into the ensuing Panthers drive, Chuba Hubbard ripped off a big run down the left side, but it was called back for a Tommy Tremble hold. Bryce Young was sacked on each of the next two plays. On the second, the ball popped out and was scooped up by Calijah Kancey for a touchdown. The Panthers were quickly in a 17-0 hole. The Panthers needed something to inject some life into the offense, and they got it. Hubbard added a couple more nice runs, and that set up Bryce Young to hit Darren Waller over the top for a 50 yard touchdown. The momentum could not have been any more short lived. The extra point was blocked and run back for a two point score. To throw salt in the wound, the Panthers were called for sideline interference on the return. The next Buccaneers drive looked a lot like the first. They basically opted out of the passing attack. Both backs were able to rip through the Panthers defense and pick up big chunks of yards. Gainwell set up the offense inside the ten. A few plays later, Irving walked in for his second touchdown of the day. The offense found themselves in the same spot they were in a few minutes prior, needing a big drive to get momentum back on his side. Instead, Bryce Young threw an inaccurate pass and Jalen Coker stumbled, and Young’s pass went straight to Zyon McCollum for an easy interception. It was more of the same after that. Irving and Gainwell kept picking up little chunks of yards to keep the chains moving and milk the rest of the clock. With under ten seconds left, Baker Mayfield drifted backwards to buy enough time to allow Tez Johnson to break away from Akayleb Evans for a wide open touchdown. It was 33-6 in favor of the Bucs going into the half. Third Quarter The Panthers got the ball first coming out of the half. The first play resulted in a first down to Tetairoa McMillan. The third was a sack where Rasheed Walker got driven back into Young, and Taylor Moton had his legs landed on in the process. The fourth was another sack where Young had three defenders bearing down on him within about a second. The defense finally held and forced a punt, that kind of seemed preferable to Tampa. They tallied their third sack in four plays on the first play of the drive. A few plays later, Young threw yet another interception for the Panthers fourth turnover of the game. The Buccaneers seemed content to just lay on the ball and kick a field goal, and that’s what they did. Bryce Young found John Metchie over the middle for a nice gain, then Chuba Hubbard powered for five yards to get the ball into Tampa Bay territory for the first time in the game. There were six minutes left in the third quarter. They drove all the way inside the ten yard line. They were faced with a 4th and 1, and Young hit Brycen Tremayne in the worst spot—right in the hands. Tremayne dropped the most basic of catches and turned the ball back over to the Bucs. The Bucs were able to run the ball out from in front of their own end zone to bring the quarter to an end. Fourth Quarter Why are you still reading this? There was no chance of the Panthers making the game worth watching at this point. They couldn’t disrupt the Bucs ground game, so the Bucs just worked the ball down the field and killed the clock. Eventually the dam broke and Tre Tucker broke free for a 46 yard touchdown completely untouched. Kenny Pickett took over for Young with the game beyond out of hand. He had a nice completion to Mitchell Evans to set up a touchdown run by Anthony Tyus for his first career score. The backups were able to get a stop, even when the Bucs went for it on 4th and 1. The offense used the opportunity to buff up their penalty numbers with a hold. The drive ended in a turnover on downs, and that effectively ended the game. Overview It was a disaster of a game from start to finish. The defense looked like it did in Week 1. The front got no push against the run, so there were few to no opportunities to make stops in the backfield. Instead, just about every Bucs run picked up three to four yards at minimum. They only threw the ball 11 times, which is an abusrdly low number for a team to score 43 points. Unlike the Bears game, the rest of the team imploded around the defense to contribute to the badness. Dave Canales said it at halftime—everything that could go wrong, did go wrong. If there’s any good news, it’s that the Panthers don’t have time to dwell on this. They have a short week to prepare to face the Packers in Lambeau on Thursday.

full_text: TAMPA, FL - JANUARY 03: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) scrambles for yardage during the Regular Season game between the Carolina Panthers and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on January 03, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers have gotten some good quarterback so far this season. They faced Cooper Rush and the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2 and the Tanner McKee-led Eagles in Week 6. Both of those games were wins. For a while, it looked like the Panthers were going to be the beneficiary of another backup quarterback situation. Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield left the team’s Week 3 game against the Vikings with a dislocated thumb. The most optimistic side of his recovery timeline had him back just in time for this game, and that’s where he ended up. In his absence, the Bucs turned to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. While his personal production is somewhat muted, it’s a lot better than you’d typically expect for an undrafted rookie quarterback just a few weeks into his NFL career. He even led the Bucs to a win over the Cowboys, which remains their only win of the season. So that brings us to our question, is the return of Baker Mayfield good news or bad news for the Carolina Panthers? MY TAKE: At first glance, this seems like an obvious answer. Baker Mayfield has been a very good quarterback since he found a home in Tampa, and Daniels is an undrafted rookie. However, the circumstances make this a little bit murkier of a take. Daniels has a better QBR than Mayfield in their starts this season, and he’s a much more dynamic runner. Mayfield hasn’t played a game in nearly a month and is going to be taking his first live reps since he dislocated the thumb on his throwing hand. I’m not a quarterback, but I think throwing thumbs are important. All that said, I think Mayfield’s return is bad news for the Panthers. It’s not as bad as it maybe would have been if previous versions of Mayfield were playing, but I think there’s more that can go wrong from a Panthers perspective against him. We know how much he feeds off having a chip on his shoulder, and I think there’s only one team that he holds more ire towards than he does the Panthers. He could come out and flop given everything that’s going on, but I can’t fully trust that he’s not going to get revved up and do some nonsense to give the Panthers a hard time.

title: Zero to 35: The Bengals’ second half vs. Baltimore Ravens belongs in the history books
summary: It was an extremely frustrating first half of football for the Cincinnati Bengals in Baltimore on Sunday, with questions looming about their 2026 playoff viability. Heading into the locker room at the halfway mark with a 13-0 deficit, very little was working on both sides of the ball. Whatever the message and adjustments were during […]
full_text: It was an extremely frustrating first half of football for the Cincinnati Bengals in Baltimore on Sunday, with questions looming about their 2026 playoff viability. Heading into the locker room at the halfway mark with a 13-0 deficit, very little was working on both sides of the ball. Whatever the message and adjustments were during halftime worked beautifully (Joe Burrow said in a CBS postgame interview that Ja’Marr Chase was the most vocal), as the Bengals came out determined to change the course of the game. They did so with immense gusto, throttling the Ravens with 35 unanswered points in the final two quarters, while disallowing Baltimore to score again. How rare was that? The Bengals are only the 10th team in NFL history to be shut out in the first half and still score 35+ points in the second half. Their 35 second-half points are the most by a team shut out in the first half since the Minnesota Vikings scored 39 points in Week 15 of 2022 to complete the largest comeback in NFL history (trailed 33-0) against the Indianapolis Colts. Cincinnati’s Demolition Began on Offense The Bengals received the third-quarter kickoff and promptly moved down the field. Joe Burrow started to gain momentum, hitting Mike Gesicki for a touchdown to start the avalanche. Burrow started the game just 6-of-12 passing for 43 yards through the first two quarters. As the Bengals shifted to working less under center in the second half, Cincinnati’s star quarterback went 16-of-18 for 249 yards and four passing touchdowns. Ja’Marr Chase caught fire late with an electric 33-yard gain off of a short pass, and a touchdown grab a few plays later. Tee Higgins was incredible in this contest, grabbing six catches for 148 yards and a touchdown—all in the final two quarters. Cincinnati also found some semblance of the run game on Sunday, getting 55 yards and a touchdown on 15 combined carries from Samaje Perine and Chase Brown. While it’s not eye-popping, there were a couple of crucial runs that converted first downs to continue the Bengals’ barrage of Baltimore. Don’t Forget About the Defense The defense had some issues in the first half, namely on two huge conversions on third-and-long (one for a 48-yard touchdown reception by Zay Flowers) in the first two quarters. However, they did hold Baltimore to two field goal attempts when it looked like more points would have been scored. But the Bengals’ defense ended up swarming the Ravens’ offense, netting four sacks, an interception, and a stop on downs deep in their own territory in the second half. Dexter Lawrence and Co. also clamped down on Derrick Henry all day, limiting him to just 2.6 yards per carry on 17 attempts. Cincinnati’s defensive smothering of Baltimore led to this second-half sequence of Ravens’ offensive possessions: Punt (following a Bengals touchdown) Turnover on Downs Punt Interception Turnover on Downs Special Teams Continues to show up Evan McPherson didn’t have a field goal attempt opportunity, but he was 5-of-5 on extra point attempts (all in the second half). Through six games, he remains perfect on all field goal and extra point attempts. Ryan Rehkow was a bit of an anomaly with his performance, as he punted well in the first half. Baltimore had three first-half drives start at their own 3-yard line, their own 6-yard line, and their own 12-yard line. He didn’t get an opportunity to punt in the second half, with the Bengals charging for five touchdowns. While he had a bad drop early on, Dohnte Meyers atoned for the mistake with a big 31-yard punt return when the Bengals were down 13-7 in the third quarter. A Complete Team Comeback While the deplorable first half was a team effort, it was a rally by the whole team to flip this game on its head. Kudos to the Bengals coaches and players for lighting a fire under everyone at halftime, and perfect execution in all phases for the final two quarters of the game. Some cynics may point to Lamar Jackson’s absence and/or the Ravens’ penchant for having second-half troubles this season, but there are no easy wins in the NFL—much less in the AFC North.

This rivalry somehow keeps getting more personal. This will be Trey Hendrickson’s first time facing the Bengals since the two sides had the most dramatic offseason contract argument in a very long time. There is no love lost between these two sides. Joe Burrow and this offense will be looking to continue their efficiency. Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins appear to be healthy after getting banged up in Week 4 and playing through Week 5. Those three being on the field will be super important. What may be more important is how this defense handles the Ravens’ offense. Containing Derrick Henry will be vital. The run defense was a huge weakness the past two weeks they played. Meanwhile, Baltimore’s pass rush has quite the rotation, so how Cincinnati helps out the left side in protection could be the difference in the game. I do think the defense will benefit from Jackson not playing. The bye week truly came at a wonderful time for Cincinnati, so, on top of getting a bit more healthy — they’ve had time to analyze what did and did not work on both sides of the ball. Hopefully that plays out for a road win that would go a long way towards their odds at the playoffs and maybe even the division in a scrappy rivalry bout. Bengals 30, Ravens 25

title: Browns Week 7 win over Titans revealed 3 things about the team
summary: The Cleveland Browns recorded another win this season, much like many of their previous wins. It came down to a fourth-quarter drive that ended in a field goal, giving the Browns the win. This 27-24 win brings Cleveland to 5-2. They now have as many wins as they had throughout the entire 2025 season. This win was important to keep them at the top of the AFC North, but it also revealed interesting […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns recorded another win this season, much like many of their previous wins. It came down to a fourth-quarter drive that ended in a field goal, giving the Browns the win. This 27-24 win brings Cleveland to 5-2. They now have as many wins as they had throughout the entire 2025 season. This win was important to keep them at the top of the AFC North, but it also revealed interesting things about this team. One of the biggest takeaways from this game is that the Browns’ ability to drive down the field and secure a fourth-quarter win is no fluke. It is a pattern. This is the fifth time this season that Cleveland has had this type of result. Andre Szmyt has been a huge part of the Browns’ success in these game-winning drives with his ability to make a kick in a crucial moment. The running game has started to find its rhythm in recent weeks and had a solid showing against the Tennessee Titans. Quinshon Judkins rushed for 96 yards, his best performance of the season thus far. When the team establishes the running game, it helps open up the rest of the offense. The rookies are continuing to shine. Against the Titans, KC Concepcion had his breakout game. He recorded eight receptions for 129 yards and added three rushes for 23 yards. His versatility is exciting to watch, and it is clear that when the offense puts the ball in his hands, he can make exciting things happen. Let me know what you think in the comments – What did the Browns win over the Titans reveal about this team?

title: Browns winners, losers for Week 7: Cleveland wins another nail-biter
summary: The Cleveland Browns are off to a good start in 2026 with a 5-2-0 record. But not to beat a dead horse, the loss to the lowly New York Jets two games ago shows that good teams must take home victories against the bad clubs, namely the Tennessee Titans. Coming into this contest, Cleveland has […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are off to a good start in 2026 with a 5-2-0 record. But not to beat a dead horse, the loss to the lowly New York Jets two games ago shows that good teams must take home victories against the bad clubs, namely the Tennessee Titans. Coming into this contest, Cleveland has wins over the Baltimore Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers, who share the division lead with the Browns. RELATED: BROWNS VS. TITANS RECAP Tennessee came into this matchup as being known as either the worst team in the league or at least the second-worst. At 1-6-0, one has to wonder how they were able to muster a single victory and perhaps have their sights on the first overall draft pick. But that is how these lesser teams will sneak up and take away a win that the Browns need. Cleveland got back quite a few of their injured players, including their top two running backs, Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson. Good thing, because this Browns’ run game has been awful. In the end, the Browns drove down with just 58 seconds on the clock and got into field goal range, and K Andre Szmyt booted his second successful kick of the game to win it 27-24. So, who played well for the Browns? Who didn’t? BROWNIES (Winners) WR KC Concepcion – When the Texas A&M receiver was taken at the bottom of the first round in this year’s draft, there were questions about his size and whether other receivers on the board were better options. Today, he balled out to the tune of 129 yards on just eight receptions. No touchdown catches, but he had key first-down receptions all game. With 7:03 left in the first quarter, a screen pass was led up front by OT Spencer Fano and C Elgton Jenkins, which gained 38 yards. human embodiment of heart pic.twitter.com/pgYWGN9nv5 — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 25, 2026 Midway through the second quarter, Concepcion crossed all the way across the field to catch the pass that gained 17 yards. On the Browns’ next possession, he took it for 21 yards to Cleveland’s 45. Two plays later, he beat the CB Marcus Harris for 32 yards to the Titans 20-yard line that would set up a touchdown. Concepcion did drop a sure touchdown on a perfect throw from QB Deshaun Watson in the third quarter on a third-and-five. With 5:06 remaining in the contest, Concepcion took the jet sweep for 18 yards that landed the Browns on Tennessee’s nine-yard line. On the next play, Watson scampered to go ahead 24-17. 10 targets, 8 receptions for 129 yards. a VERY happy #NationalTightEndsDay to Harold! #CLEvsTEN on CBS pic.twitter.com/48bZxZ8SxJ — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 25, 2026 TE Harold Fannin – For most of the game, Fannin got a pass here and there. A 12-yard gain in the first quarter. Converted a third-and-five late in the second quarter for 21 yards that set up the field goal right before the half. A lost fumble. But the game’s biggest play was his rumble-and-stumble on the final drive, as he gained 36 yards and took the ball from Cleveland’s 37 to the Titans’ 19-yard line. Was it Fannin’s YAC abilities, or the failure of the Tennessee defense to bring Fannin down? We don’t know, or care. When they finally tackled him, the Browns were in field goal range. Nine targets, six catches for 91 yards and a 15.2 average per catch. Are we all in agreement that Fannin hasn’t been used enough? LB Quincy Williams – This dude was everywhere. Great defense on the second, third, and fourth down attempts from the one right before the half. He is credited with the stop on second down. Hit Pollard for a one-yard gain early in the second quarter. On Tennessee’s first possession of the third quarter, Williams busted through after reading run and nailed Pollard for a two-yard loss. Two plays later on a third-and-one, he combined with DE Isaiah McGuire to stop Pollard on a run up the middle for no gain. The Titans had a third-and-14 in the third quarter, and after the completion to TE Daniel Bellinger, Williams made the stop after just four yards that forced a punt. Tied for the lead in tackles with 10. DESHAUN WATSON GO AHEAD TUDDY pic.twitter.com/KuhyT1ebzs — McNeil (@REFLOG18) October 25, 2026 QB Deshaun Watson – Let’s all say it: Watson played a great game. Not always pretty or perfect, but he played well. The long ball to Concepcion that was dropped was a perfect toss. His touchdown run was like his Clemson days. He had a ton of throws that ended up going for 20+ in this game and found open receivers. Excellent sneak in the second quarter. That's Watson's first 300-yard game in Cleveland — Zac Jackson (@AkronJackson) October 25, 2026 And his ability to escape the pocket was incredible. Only one sack, and yet it could have been 7 or 8. The interception was just plain dumb; yeah, we get it. And he completely stared down WR Denzel Boston, and the defender just waited. The rookie receiver, as Monken noted, also didn’t run the proper route. After Tennessee tied the game at 24-all, Watson had 58 ticks left on the clock. Six-yard completion followed by eight yards. Then the strike to Fannin, who did the rest. Amazing with almost no time. 25 for 36 for 308 yards, no TD passes, one pick, one TD run, sacked just once, with an 84.0 QB rating. Three rushes for 19 yards and a score. No quit in this dude. Offensive line – If you paid any attention to the offensive line when it was a passing play, the pocket remained intact for most of the game. Watson had plenty of time to survey the field and was the reason that there were so many long catch-and-run plays. LG Zion Johnson had a couple of penalties, so that is concerning. But guys like Fano, Jenkins, and RT Tytus Howard kept guys out of the backfield. OT Dawand Jones did a good job once he spelled Howard. Just one sack all game is not like the Browns are used to. Remember, it wasn’t long ago that the New York Jets grilled Watson for eight sacks. Great game for this group. Starting running backs – Funny how when your #1 and #2 running backs return, the running game suddenly exists. Quinshon Judkins was a beast, and later Dylan Sampson reeled off some big gains. It began in the first quarter on first down when Judkins took off for 30 yards with Fano leading the way to the Titans’ 5-yard line, and then scored on the very next play. before vs after 🤪 pic.twitter.com/Jq7nIZRwWo — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 25, 2026 The six-yard TD run in Quarter 2 was through the hole developed by Fano and LG Williams. Judkins bullied his way for a first down on a second-and-one early in the third quarter. He took a short pass from Watson as the period was winding down, and on the next play exploded for 15 yards down to Tennessee’s 31. 17 carries for 96 yards, two scores, and a 5.6 average per carry. Sampson dinked and dunked in the first half and was an afterthought, which left him rested for the final two quarters. He went 22 yards late in the third quarter, which got Cleveland almost to midfield. Then had the all-important 19-yard run with 5:59 left in the game that got the Browns to Tennessee’s 27. Sampson had 6 rushes for 45 yards. Welcome back, fellas. Defense fourth-and-one stop – The Titans scored a touchdown, but it was ruled the runner’s elbow was down short of the goal line. The ball was placed at the one. Second down, LB Williams and Sam Kamara stood up QB Cam Ward for no gain. On third down, Adin Huntington was credited with a sack when he stopped Ward for minus a half-yard. That brings up fourth down. Titans kick a field goal, right? Nope. The ball was snapped, and DE Jared Verse came for the right side and grabbed the legs of Pollard, who was leaping. This stopped all of his momentum, and then LB Winston Reid made the stop. Turnover on downs, and another feather in the defense’s cap. FROWNIES (Losers) Playing down – The Titans came into the game with a single win and were considered to be one of the three worst teams in the league. Yet, they stayed with Cleveland, had a lead early, ran the ball with consistency, converted key third downs, and had a good…

title: Browns Week 7: A few key takeaways from victory over the Titans
summary: The Cleveland Browns took the Week 7 victory over the Tennessee Titans in a game that was a struggle back and forth between the two AFC teams. Now 5-2, the Browns remain at the top of the AFC North heading into Week 8, after their fifth fourth-quarter drive that led to a victory. A few […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns took the Week 7 victory over the Tennessee Titans in a game that was a struggle back and forth between the two AFC teams. Now 5-2, the Browns remain at the top of the AFC North heading into Week 8, after their fifth fourth-quarter drive that led to a victory. A few key takeaways from Week 7’s win: Poor start, again, on both sides The Browns have now been outscored 60-13 in 1st quarters this season. There is still 5:32 to go in the 1st q of the Titans game 😂 — Nick Wilson (@NickWilsonSays) October 25, 2026 Cleveland’s rushing touchdown was their first 1st-quarter touchdown of the season. Inconsistency with rookies; new coaches in top positions A tale as old as time in the NFL: inconsistency is regular when you have a lot of rookies; on top of that, HC Todd Monken, OC Travis Switzer, and DC Mike Rutenberg are all first-timers in their big roles. A win is a win, as everyone gets more experience. A variety of players got involved early on offense It was helpful to see six players get three or more touches on offense, plus QB Deshaun Watson having three rushes, including a touchdown. When all the weapons can get involved, in a variety of ways, things go well. Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson, KC Concepcion, Harold Fannin Jr., Denzel Boston, and Jerry Jeudy all had three or more catches and/or runs. Week off does Quinshon Judkins good The second-year back looked far more explosive early in the game, after missing Week 6. On Cleveland’s second drive, Judkins had a 30-yard gain and finished off the drive with a solid touchdown run. Overall, Judkins had 96 yards on 17 carries with two touchdowns, with a 5.6-yard-per-carry average. Ref who throws the most flags plus undisciplined Browns Four penalties on Cleveland in the first quarter led the announcers to share that the official in this game has thrown 40 more flags than any other. Given the Browns’ struggles with discipline, not a great combination. Cleveland had eight penalties; Tennessee had five for the game. Huge replay and 4th-down stop early in the 2nd quarter RB Tony Pollard looked like he got in for a touchdown; three plays later, the Browns were taking the ball back thanks to a huge 4th-down stand, helped by a good play by DE Jared Verse. The game went from being 21-7 to Cleveland turning in a 99-yard drive, tying the game 14-14. Concepcion breakout game Despite a big drop that would have been a touchdown, the Browns’ first-round receiver had his breakout game. Eight catches for 129 yards and three rushes for 23 yards, Concepcion not only had some big plays but had some key first-down plays as well. If he had held on to the perfect Watson throw, it would have been a perfect game for the rookie. Moving Fannin around sets up inside routes, leading to success Cleveland’s offense moved some players around in Week 7, including lining up Fannin in different locations that led to different matchups for other receivers and running backs. It also led to Fannin’s best game of the year, six catches for 91 yards. Defensive adjustments showing up in the 2nd quarter Rutenberg may play a little too much zone early (and, in this game, late), but his adjustments throughout games are very obvious and great to see. The Browns run different defenses as the game goes on, especially after struggling early in most games. Passing offense finding itself, run game helping Two simple stats: Watson threw for 308 yards, and the run game had 183 yards. That is a complete offense. Defense has perfected the Peanut Punch More and more, the Cleveland defense is looking to get the ball out, rather than just tackling. “The ball is oxygen/air” has been said on more than one occasion. Tyson Campbell made the play in the third quarter: Tyson forces the fumble and Ronnie scoops it up! #CLEvsTEN on CBS pic.twitter.com/iqVEr7Esdh — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 25, 2026 Focus, effort concerns in the 3rd quarter/playing with a lead Again, an issue with a young team, but Cleveland’s focus and effort were questionable in the third quarter. More penalties and a lack of urgency. The Browns have been more productive when trailing in games, which isn’t what good teams do in the NFL. Dylan Sampson’s return adds juice to offense It might take a while for him to be fully integrated, but this screen to Sampson showed what he adds to the Cleveland offense: haven't you heard? Samp is back 🔥🔥🔥 #CLEvsTEN on CBS pic.twitter.com/C3OXE25AHF — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 25, 2026 A 20-yard rush in the fourth quarter helped push the Browns offense into scoring position, another explosive play by the second-year back. Sampson ended up with nine touches for 77 yards. Mason Graham, Grant Delpit left the game injured Not a great sign watching the star defensive tackle limping off the field in his first game back after an injury. Thankfully, he was able to return a few plays later. Delpit helped make a tackle, but then the officials stopped the game to have him removed from the field due to concern for injury. Thankfully, both were able to return to the game. Run game inconsistent While Cleveland was able to put together a good final box score, the run game continues to have too many plays where backs are either dancing behind the line or dealing with defenders at or behind the line of scrimmage. A little more consistency would help a more dominant game on the scoreboard. Harold Fannin getting more involved is helpful Important to note a second time, Fannin was huge late in the game. While he is required to do more blocking (more on that in a second), his presence is something other teams struggle to match up with in the passing game. Fannin also fights for extra yards, including a key play late in the game that led to the game-winning field goal. Malachi Corley’s run game blocking was key Providing the second tight end role, Corley was on the field for a lot of the important runs Cleveland’s offense had. Corley allowed Fannin to run more routes. Zone defense bites defense late in the 4th Quarter Two straight plays where a receiver was wide open; Ward missed one but not the other, putting Tennessee in the red zone late in the game and allowing them to tie the game. Deshaun Watson finally throws for 300 yards That's Watson's first 300-yard game in Cleveland — Zac Jackson (@AkronJackson) October 25, 2026 Browns fans would love a more comfortable win… but 5-2 is GREAT Listen, some fans are no longer in our 20s… or 30s… or 40s… or 50s… (I am somewhere in that group). It would be nice for Cleveland’s stress levels and hearts if the Browns could win a little more convincingly. Then again, it is way better to win than lose, right?! title: Browns rookie WR hits historic mark against Titans
summary: The Cleveland Browns have had several notable wide receivers in franchise history. Dante Lavelli and Mac Speedie in the 1940s and 1950s. Gary Collins and Paul Warfield in the 1960s. Reggie Rucker and Dave Logan in the 1970s. Webster Slaughter, Brian Brennan, and Reggie Langhorne in the 1980s. But very few had a day during […]
full_text: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have had several notable wide receivers in franchise history. Dante Lavelli and Mac Speedie in the 1940s and 1950s. Gary Collins and Paul Warfield in the 1960s. Reggie Rucker and Dave Logan in the 1970s. Webster Slaughter, Brian Brennan, and Reggie Langhorne in the 1980s. But very few had a day during their rookie seasons like the one KC Concepcion had on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Concepcion lit up the Titans for 129 receiving yards, a total that puts him at No. 8 on the franchise’s all-time list for receiving yards by a rookie wide receiver in a single game. Derrick Alexander holds the franchise record of 171 yards, set in 1994 in a game against the New York Giants. Concepcion looked to be on track to top Alexander, but just missed a deep pass in the third quarter and was shut out in the entire second half. He still contributed, however, as a key run in the fourth quarter set up a Deshaun Watson touchdown. Unlike Concepcion, Alexander’s record day came in a Week 13 loss as the Browns committed five turnovers and committed 11 penalties. Alexander finished with seven receptions, including a 60-yarder with about five minutes remaining that set up a game-tying touchdown. That was actually one of two big days that season for Alexander, as he had a 136-yard game against the Arizona Cardinals in a Week 3 victory. The new Top 10 for most receiving yards by a Browns rookie, according to statemuse.com , is now: Derrick Alexander, 171 yards in 1994 Mohamed Massaquoi, 148 yards in 2009 Derrick Alexander, 136 yards in 1994 Kevin Johnson, 135 yards in 1999 Webster Slaughter, 134 yards in 1986 Greg Little, 131 yards in 2011 Kevin Johnson, 131 yards in 1999 KC Concepcion, 129 yards in 2026 Paul Warfield, 126 yards in 1964 Paul Warfield 123 yards in 1964 Concepcion now has 30 catches for 315 yards on the season. title: Browns vs. Titans Week 7 recap: Last-second, close game win for Cleveland
summary: The Cleveland Browns traveled down to Nashville to face off against the Tennessee Titans in Week 7. Sitting at 4-2, the Browns are hoping to match pace with the Pittsburgh Steelers, who won their early Sunday matchup in Paris, France. Cleveland got good news in pregame with the inactive report having CB Denzel Ward and […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns traveled down to Nashville to face off against the Tennessee Titans in Week 7. Sitting at 4-2 , the Browns are hoping to match pace with the Pittsburgh Steelers, who won their early Sunday matchup in Paris, France. Cleveland got good news in pregame with the inactive report having CB Denzel Ward and LB Quincy Williams active for the game . Usually, DBN’s founder Chris Pokorny provides you with these amazing game recaps, but he will be out for Week 7, so today’s might look a little different than you are used to. Don’t worry, Chris should be back for Week 8. 1st Quarter Not sure what it is about Cleveland’s defense, but they continue to struggle out of the gate. More zone coverage and a run defense that was torn apart for 60 yards, including a 36-yard gallop by RB Tony Pollard for an opening-drive touchdown. The Browns offense started off smoothly with a couple of first downs, but a bad hold by RB Quinshon Judkins pulled one back, before rookie WR Denzel Boston ran a poor route, leading to QB Deshaun Watson throwing an interception and the Titans getting the ball already in scoring position. Pollard cashed Tennessee’s second drive in for an early 14-0 lead with 8:35 left in the first quarter. WR KC Concepcion picked his way to a big gain on third down for 23 yards, and a big first down near midfield. That was followed by a big Judkins run, 30 yards, for a first down at the five-yard line. The second-year back put it in the end zone on the next play, pulling the game to 14-7. Cleveland’s defense finally got a stop on Tennessee’s next drive, forcing a three-and-out. A special teams penalty forced the Browns next stop to start inside the 10-yard line. A drop by Boston on third down forced a Cleveland punt from deep in their own end zone. 2nd Quarter Titans had moved into scoring position heading into the second quarter, after a 17-yard gain by rookie WR Carnell Tate . The Browns defense continued to be picked apart, with Pollard seemingly getting the third score of the game, but replay showed that he did not get in. Cleveland’s defense then stiffened up, getting three straight stops, including stopping Pollard short on fourth down, forcing a turnover. Two quick first downs, on throws to Boston and Concepcion, got the Browns out of the shadow of their own end zone. Then, on another third down, TE Harold Fannin Jr. was fighting for yards after what looked like a catch and proceeded to fumble the ball near midfield. The play was reviewed, but there was not enough evidence to overturn the turnover. On the next play, CB Denzel Ward picked off QB Cam Ward , giving the Browns offense the ball at the 23-yard line. Concepcion accounted for 53 yards on two receptions early on the next drive, putting Cleveland in scoring position with under five minutes left in the half. On 4th and 1, the Browns QB sneak kept the drive going (on top of an offsides flag). A little creativity, a fake to Conecpcion and a handoff to Judkins, led to Cleveland’s second touchdown. An Andre Szmyt extra point tied the game at 14-14. The Titans offense then went three-and-out, with Ward overthrowing Tate on third down. Giving the Browns the ball back with just under two minutes left. Cleveland had two timeouts, taking over at the 26-yard line. Tennessee’s punter Tommy Townsend was injured on the punt, which could change the team’s options at fourth down. Townsend walked off the field with a limp. Watson bought a little time and kept his eyes downfield, hitting Fannin for 21 yards on third and eight. With one timeout, Cleveland had the ball in field goal range before Concepcion’s eighth catch put the ball at the 20-yard line. With 18 seconds left and the Browns without timeouts, HC Todd Monken called three plays to try to get a touchdown, but instead put the offense in position for a go-ahead field goal by Szmyt. Cleveland headed into the locker room with a 17-14 lead. 3rd Quarter Based on warmups, the Titans might be without their punter, which would force kicker Joey Sly to punt as well. The zone read play held Tennessee’s defender enough to help Judkins get a 10-yard gain for the Browns second first down of the second half, pushing Cleveland’s possession near midfield. OT Tytus Howard left the game during the Browns first possession of the second half. Dawand Jones stepped in as the right tackle as Howard went to the locker room. Concepcion was wide open deep, but the rookie dropped what looked like it would be a touchdown, leading to another Cleveland punt to start the third quarter. A perfect throw by Watson that should have led to points. A penalty for too many men on the field as the Titans were looking to punt extended the home team’s first drive of the second half after the defense had looked like they had forced a three-and-out. CB Tyson Campbell then stripped Tate a few plays later, with S Ronnie Hickman recovering the fumble. Unfortunately, two holding calls on OL Zion Johnson , one accepted and one declined, forced the Browns out of field goal range and into another punt, which rolled into the end zone for a touchback. Slot corner Myles Harden joined Howard in the locker room, replaced by Mekhi Blackmon , in the middle of the third quarter. After Ward escaped a ton of pressure to avoid a huge sack, Slye, the Titans kicker, did an admirable job of punting in the place of Townsend, with Tennessee downing the kick inside the 20. A well-timed and set-up screen to RB Dylan Sampson pushed Cleveland’s next possession to midfield. Sampson, back from injured reserve for the first time this season, looked explosive in picking up 22 yards on the play, which was followed by two Judkins gains (one pass, one run) that combined for 23 yards heading into the fourth quarter. 4th Quarter Heading into the fourth quarter, the Browns were outgaining the Titans 364-203. Tennessee DT Jeffrey Simmons chased down Watson on a key third down, forcing a field goal attempt that Szmyt pushed right, with a loud doink as part of the miss, keeping the score 17-14. On the Titans next possession, Pollard was able to find space, despite a strong push by the Browns defense, for a 17-yard gain. On the play, DT Mason Graham limped off the field, but returned a few plays later. Cleveland’s defense was able to force a field goal attempt, which Slye hit to tie the game at 17-17 with 8:41 left in the game. Big run gains by Sampson and Concepcion put the Browns in scoring position, with a Watson run on a zone-read adding another touchdown. A Szymt extra point pushed Cleveland’s lead to 24-17 with 4:34 left in the contest. A strong return to the 37-yard line by Tennessee’s Chimere Dike helped the Titans late fourth-quarter possession start off in good position. Ward missed a wide-open tight end on third and eight late in the fourth quarter, a likely touchdown. On the next play, Ward took a huge hit on fourth down, but another wide-open receiver put the ball in scoring position at the 17-yard line. At the two-minute warning, Tennessee was down seven points but in position to tie the game in the redzone. A back shoulder throw to Tate, who was pushed out of bounds at the one-yard line, with Harden in coverage, with just over a minute left. Pollard pushed forward for his third touchdown of the game, with Slye’s extra point tying the game with 58 seconds left. The Browns offense took the ball, with three timeouts available, at the 31-yard line with 53 seconds left. A 36-yard catch-and-run by Fannin got the Cleveland offense down to the 19-yard line, with a field goal attempt to win the game. Szmyt hit the 32-yarder for a 27-24. Join us in the comments, especially with your GIF reactions, to the Browns moving to 5-2 in 2026

full_text: A competitive contest between the Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans started out as anything but in Week 7. The Titans took a 14-0 lead and looked like they would pull to 21-7 due to turnovers, but the Browns defense stepped up after a replay called back a Tony Pollard touchdown. Cleveland ran the score to 17-14 going into halftime, helped by CB Denzel Ward’s interception and solid offensive production. On the Browns first offensive possession of the third quarter, the team was able to put together a drive that crossed midfield. Unfortunately, right tackle Tytus Howard was injured during the drive and was helped off the field, replaced by veteran Dawand Jones for the rest of the initial second-half possession. Howard limped into the blue tent on Cleveland’s sideline, with no immediate word on his condition from the team. On the next drive, Howard was seen walking to the locker room. Jones was the Browns’ fourth-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft, but has ended each of his first three seasons with injuries. Late in the third quarter, the team announced that Howard was questionable to return due to a concussion. Early in the fourth quarter, DT Mason Graham stayed down on the field and was seen limping off. Graham, returning after missing a few weeks due to a knee issue, looked to be in pain as he left the field. Thankfully, Graham returned a few plays later, but S Grant Delpit was removed by the officials after helping make a tackle. Delpit returned on the next Titans possession. We will keep you up to date on Howard’s condition as information becomes available.

title: Cowboys at Eagles: Score predictions for Week 7
summary: Dallas heads into Philadelphia for Monday Night Football with both NFC East rivals sitting at 2-4 and desperately needing a win. The Eagles have lost four straight and will again be without Jalen Hurts, while Dallas arrives after back-to-back defeats of its own. This feels like a game where whichever struggling offense finds answers first […]
full_text: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Dallas heads into Philadelphia for Monday Night Football with both NFC East rivals sitting at 2-4 and desperately needing a win. The Eagles have lost four straight and will again be without Jalen Hurts, while Dallas arrives after back-to-back defeats of its own. This feels like a game where whichever struggling offense finds answers first will take control. When Eagles has the ball Philadelphia should try to take as much responsibility away from Tanner McKee as possible. McKee threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in his first start against Carolina, but the Eagles produced only 35 rushing yards without Saquon Barkley. Barkley is expected to return from his hamstring injury on Monday, and that immediately becomes Dallas’ biggest concern. The Cowboys have allowed 899 rushing yards at 4.7 yards per carry so far this year, so Philadelphia should test that weakness early rather than asking its backup quarterback to throw the ball 40-plus times again. Dallas’ plan should be almost the opposite and crowd the line of scrimmage to control Barkley and force McKee to beat them. DeMarvion Overshown’s return is important because his speed gives Dallas more ability to cover running backs and tight ends while Dee Winters will miss time with an Achilles strain. Once Philadelphia reaches obvious passing situations, Christian Parker can become more aggressive with disguised pressures against an inexperienced quarterback. Dallas has only eight sacks through six games, so this is a matchup where the front needs to finally turn pressure into results. When Dallas has the ball Dallas needs to change what it has been doing. The Cowboys have scored only 29 points across their last two games, and Green Bay pressured Dak Prescott 21 times while Dallas managed only 48 rushing yards. Too often the offense has become predictable, with Prescott dropping back while receivers run longer-developing routes and the defense already knows pressure is coming. Brian Schottenheimer needs more motion, quick throws, screens and route combinations designed to get CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens the football in space. Philadelphia has only eight sacks this season, so Dallas cannot allow another pass rush to suddenly look dominant. Javonte Williams also needs to become part of the answer. Dallas threw 54 passes at Green Bay and almost completely abandoned the run after Williams scored in the third quarter. Philadelphia is allowing four yards per carry, so there should be enough opportunity to maintain balance and prevent the Eagles from simply attacking Prescott. Lamb and Pickens still give Dallas the biggest individual advantage in this matchup, but the play design has to help them rather than asking Prescott to constantly solve everything after the snap. If Dallas uses tempo, motion and shorter concepts to make Philadelphia hesitate, the explosive plays should eventually follow. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (3-3) It’s hard when l have so little faith in the Cowboys. I think it’s going to be a low scoring error filled contest. Dallas is desperate for a win. I’ll risk picking them. DAL 19 PHI 16 Brandon Loree (4-2) The Cowboys are at a crossroads moment in their season. Get a win, and it steadies the ship for at least a week and makes people take them a bit more seriously. If they lose, this team might be more broken than we realize. Playing in Philadelphia is never easy, but the roster is so beaten up and vulnerable that this Dallas team should still be able to take advantage. I think we’ll see them lean on the run game a bit more and show more balance on offense. The Cowboys showed last year on opening night. They weren’t afraid to play a primetime game in Philly. The Cowboys are just a better team than Philly right now, so I have them winning 24-19. Dyllan Rivers (3-2) Finally a get right week where Dallas actually gets right. The Cowboys offense rebounds with a balanced attack against a defense that won’t stack the line of scrimmage like we saw against the Buccaneers and Packers. The defense plays it’s best game of the season. Dallas takes care of business against a horrible Eagles team, 31-17. Matt Holleran (3-3) The Eagles look like a mess both on and off the field, but the Cowboys don’t look much better. After how bad they’ve been the past two weeks I have no faith in Dallas coming into this matchup. I see Philly’s defense holding down this struggling Cowboys’ offense leading to a low-scoring matchup that the Eagles win. Give me Philadelphia, 20-17. Mike Poland (2-4) I’m taking Dallas to finally stop the slide on Monday night. Philadelphia has lost four straight, Jalen Hurts is out, and Tanner McKee will be making only his second start of the season. That gives Christian Parker a very clear defensive plan to load the box against Saquon Barkley, make McKee beat you through the air and become aggressive on obvious passing downs. Let’s go Cowboys to win 27-17.
