title: Cowboys at Eagles: Offensive, defensive impact players in Week 7
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have dug themselves into a hole they may or may not be on to climb out of. This Week 7 matchup against their division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles, will tell a lot about their desire to win and how the rest of the season will play out. A win keeps their playoff […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have dug themselves into a hole they may or may not be on to climb out of. This Week 7 matchup against their division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles, will tell a lot about their desire to win and how the rest of the season will play out. A win keeps their playoff hopes alive, a loss all but ends things. In order to secure the “W” this week the Cowboys need all hands on deck and need each and every player to be at their best. There are those who will be more impactful than others, hopefully swaying the game in the Cowboys favor. Below is the offensive and defensive player we believe will impact the game for the better this week. Offense – QB Dak Prescott The past two games against the Buccaneers and Packers haven’t been kind to Dak Prescott. He’s thrown for just two touchdowns and four interceptions, and has been under constant pressure nearly every single play when he takes the field. He’s facing a defensive matchup this week in the division rival Eagles who are currently ranked 19 th against the run, 26 th in past defense, and allowing only 22.8 points per game (16 th in the league). We believe he will make a huge positive impact on the outcome of the game this week. This is a must-win game for the Cowboys and No. 4 knows it. Out of any other QB in the league he knows the strengths/weaknesses of the Eagles defense as well as anyone, and how to exploit them. This knowledge should serve him well this week, especially if they follow the Buccaneers/Packers example with a blitz-heavy game plan. Everything seems to be going against him heading into this Week 7 matchup, playing in hostile territory and coming off back-to-back poor performances, but we believe this is the week he’ll start to turn things around. Defense – LB DeMarvion Overshown DeMarvion Overshown was expected to be a big part of the Cowboys defense this year, but unfortunately he’s missed most of the season after sustaining a hamstring injury in the season opener against the Giants. He’s been rehabbing ever since to get back on the field and is finally expected to make his triumphant return this week against the Eagles. It actually couldn’t come at a better time now that Dee Winters will miss an unknown amount of time after picking up an injury last week against the Packers. Overshown’s sideline-to-sideline speed and unfulfilled game-changing ability could potentially be the spark that finally helps ignite Christian Parker’s defense. No. 0 possesses the talent to impact the game in the Cowboys favor in a multitude of ways, but sadly reoccurring injuries have kept him from hitting his true potential. This week he could be the equalizer that helps contain Saquon Barkley, who is returning to the lineup after missing last two games with a hamstring injury. We fully expect Overshown to shine in his return to the field.
author: Brian Martin

title: Cowboys defense playing like the 2nd half defense from last week is key
summary: The Dallas Cowboys need a statement win of some sorts, in the worst way. Normally winning at their biggest current rival, the Philadelphia Eagles, would count as one. With both teams sitting at 2-4 coming off a loss, this game being the one that will put a wrap on week seven in the NFL is […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys need a statement win of some sorts, in the worst way. Normally winning at their biggest current rival, the Philadelphia Eagles, would count as one. With both teams sitting at 2-4 coming off a loss, this game being the one that will put a wrap on week seven in the NFL is far from a battle of two teams anyone would call contenders right now. The only statement to possibly be made would be a claim by either team in primetime to stay in the dreadful NFC East race, which the Cowboys should still be interested in . The Cowboys defense put up a solid effort in the second half at the Green Bay Packers. If the defense continues on any sort of upward trajectory, they’ll get a golden opportunity on Monday night to end their two-game slide. A return to divisional play might also be what Dak Prescott needs to lead the offense closer to where they need to be, but the pressure to not lose this game to a depleted Eagles side is also turned up to the point of being difficult to factor into which team will play looser and make more winning plays. Let’s get to our weekly scenarios for what the Cowboys need to do to reach 3-4, or what could extend their losing streak to three games. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Philadelphia Eagles if… …they get the ball back to the offense on third downs. A big part of the reason the Cowboys defense gave up 17 points in the first half of their last game was not getting the Packers offense off the field on third and long. A big part of holding them to six points in the second half was getting more pressure on Jordan Love and finishing the possessions with third-down stops. The Eagles have only played one full game with McKee starting in place of Jalen Hurts, but come out of that game leading the NFL in percentage of drives ending in a punt at 51.6%. Going hand in hand with this, they also are last in the league in average distance to go on third down with 8.4. Their longest pass play against the Panthers last week in a 25-14 home loss was 19 yards to Devonta Smith, who was targeted a game-high 14 times but caught seven for 75 yards. Philadelphia punted on their first five drives, with a trio of three and outs that totaled a net of one yard and 3:35 of game clock. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer did not give the most inspiring answers this week when it comes to why his team’s been so easily taken out of the run game that’s supposed to be a critical component to their entire identity. Unfortunately, the expectation coming into Monday remains that the game script has to stay on track in a way it hardly ever does in a NFL game for the Cowboys to find any balance. With the Eagles also missing starting running back Saquon Barkley in that Panthers game, they too had an ugly looking run/pass split of 13 rushing attempts and 45 passes for McKee. Having Barkley back against the Cowboys on Monday night will certainly help, but the Cowboys objective should still be finding ways to force the Eagles offense into third and longs. If they finish them to get the ball back into Prescott’s hands, perhaps even with advantageous field position, the Cowboys can look like they know what they’re doing again. Both the Cowboys and Eagles defenses come into this game allowing the same 11.6 yards per reception defensively, which is tied for the seventh worst, and fractions away from being even further down a list neither defensive coordinator wants to be on. In the coaching battle of Vic Fangio against his former top assistant Christian Parker, the Cowboys must make Fangio worry much more about the big play over the top compared to how much Parker can send pressure and force the ball out of McKee’s hand. One of the keys to the Cowboys being able to get to these plays comfortably is being able to trust the run game on early downs, and the bigger key to doing that is getting the Eagles offense off the field whenever a third down opportunity presents itself. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Philadelphia Eagles if… …they can’t tackle Saquon Barkley. The Eagles have been without star running back Saquon Barkley for their last two games. Barkley is trending towards returning against the Cowboys, which will be a real confidence builder for McKee being able to turn and hand the ball to him. Barkley is second in the NFL so far this season in time behind the line of scrimmage at 3.14 seconds per carry. This is a runner that’s a bit less of a home run threat like he was when he propelled the Eagles to the Super Bowl, but this patience can still be deadly. Getting penetration from the defensive interior to make stops against a running back trapped in the backfield has not exactly been a strength of the Cowboys defensive tackle group of Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, and Otito Ogbonnia. There were real positives in this area against the Packers though, so watching which way this trends against the Eagles could be a real deciding factor for Monday night. If Barkley is able to break the line of scrimmage and get after the Cowboys linebackers and secondary players, the missed tackles from these groups that doomed the Packers loss could do the same for this road test. The Cowboys own offense is struggling right now. The idea at least lives on for now though (we think) that their opponents still have to respect what the Cowboys offense could be, making it harder to imagine this being a game the Eagles can just completely take the air out of the ball and lean on Barkley all night. Both Barkley and McKee will have to make plays, but if the former really gets going, the odds of both go up at the same time. The likes of Williams, Clark, Ogbonnia, along with Jaishawn Barham, DeMarvion Overshown making his return from injury, Markquese Bell and the other secondary defenders need to find ways to bring Barkley to the ground when given the chance. The Cowboys need to take the hostile Eagles crowd out of this game and save their already-fading hopes on this 2026 season.

title: Cowboys at Eagles: A breakdown of the problems in Philly
summary: As the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles renew their rivalry on Monday night, I renew our series of 5 Questions articles with Brandon Lee Gowton from Bleeding Green Nation. Here’s our Q&A. Blogging The Boys: What’s your take on the whole Jalen Hurts medical situation and how it was handled? Also, does Hurts still have a […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images As the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles renew their rivalry on Monday night, I renew our series of 5 Questions articles with Brandon Lee Gowton from Bleeding Green Nation . Here’s our Q&A. Blogging The Boys: What’s your take on the whole Jalen Hurts medical situation and how it was handled? Also, does Hurts still have a future in Philly? Bleeding Green Nation: There’s so much we don’t know. I wish there was more transparency with exactly what happened. I’m glad to see the NFLPA is calling for an investigation into the matter. If there’s nothing nefarious to hide, everyone should be interested in sharing as much information as possible (with respect to Hurts’ privacy preferences). I hope the situation was truly handled properly and the result that came to pass was an unavoidably unfortunate outcome. It’s a real shame his season is suddenly over. Does he still have a future in Philly? That much isn’t clear even as it relates to his medical situation. There seems to be confidence that he’ll make a full recovery, which is what everyone is rooting for. But there’s a non-zero chance he can never play football again. That much seems unlikely at the moment but it’s not impossible. Assuming he is able to play football again, it’s hard to say for sure. Hurts has a no-trade clause, so it’s not like the organization has the ability to ship him out against his will. Nor do I get the sense they’re rushing to do that. But he’s reaching a point in his contract where it makes sense for the Eagles to either 1) extend him or 2) decide to move on. Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie loves Hurts. And he should. Hurts won Super Bowl MVP and wasn’t far off from another. Does Howie Roseman feel similarly? There are some doubts about that much. And it’s his job to think about Hurts differently than Lurie does. One must also consider what Hurts desires moving forward. How does he feel about how his situation was handled? Does he trust the Eagles? There’s a lot to unpack here moving forward. It’s hard to say with certainty that he’ll be the Eagles’ starting quarterback in 2027. At this point in time, I tend to think it’s more likely than not. But I can’t say with 100% certainty that it’s a lock. BTB: What’s the story on Nick Sirianni? Is he the coach next year? What’s your personal take on him as coach right now? BGN: The way things are currently trending, I don’t think Nick Sirianni will be the Eagles’ head coach next year. When you consider that he’s never previously missed the playoffs and ranks among the top head coaches in NFL history in terms of winning percentage, dismissing him might seem crazy. But Lurie already went against precedent by bringing Sirianni back for 2026. The Eagles’ 2025 offense was one of the team’s worst since 2000. In all other years where their offense was similarly ineffective, the head coach got fired (2012, 2015, 2020). It’s not hard to see why Sirianni wouldn’t be fired less than one year after he won a Super Bowl. But I tend to think that Lurie will not be so patient to tolerate another terrible offense, which has been the case in 2026. Sirianni is not the play-caller, no, but that’s because he really struggled in that capacity back in 2021. His hand-picked OC struggled in 2025 and he clearly hasn’t been capable of helping Sean Mannion find answers in 2026. BTB: It feels like a lot has gone wrong for Philly this year. What are the biggest things going wrong besides the Jalen Hurts situation? BGN: If you want the full scope, BGN alumnus Jimmy Kempski came up with an “ Eagles season from hell tracker ” that lays out all the crazy stuff going on with the team this season: To put it more succinctly: the offense totally stinks and is super injured while the defense is underperforming lofty expectations. Sometimes it’s just not your year. And that much is easier to swallow given the Eagles’ sustained success in recent years. But this season sure seems doomed. Maybe the Eagles do enough to win a very weak NFC East but 1) I doubt it and 2) who cares. BTB: Who is Tanner McKee and what kind of QB is he? BGN: You don’t recall McKee from him going 3/4 for 54 yards, two touchdowns, zero interceptions, and a 156.2 passer rating in a 41 to 7 win over the Cowboys in Week 17 of the 2024 season? The same year the Eagles went on to destroy the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX? The Eagles originally selected McKee with a Day 3 pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. He’s shown some promise in limited opportunities over the years, which led to him being Hurts’ primary backup in 2025. McKee did not play well in the Eagles’ Week 18 game last year when the team rested their starters. But no one really expected the team to then trade for Andy Dalton and have him compete with McKee for the QB2 job. That competition went as far as the lead up to Week 1 and Dalton began the season as Hurts’ backup with McKee settling for the emergency third quarterback role. Dalton then briefly had to play in Week 3 while Hurts was being checked for a concussion … and he threw an interception on his one and only career pass attempt for the Eagles. Dalton was then demoted to QB3 with McKee overtaking him. McKee is now the starter after an offseason where the Eagles did him wrong by limiting his reps and destroying his confidence. He’s looked worse this year than he ever did before. He’s a pocket passer who is capable of getting the ball out quick and making some nice throws. But he has athletic limitations and the consistency hasn’t really been there. He also probably needs an especially strong support system to have success and that’s not just really there for him right now given how injured the Eagles are on offense. BTB: Who do you think wins the game and why? Give us your score prediction. BGN: Earlier this week, I predicted an Eagles win. The injury report isn’t making me feel good about that much since the Birds could be without their top two receivers (DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks) and their top tight end (Dallas Goedert) among other key players. But, whatever, it’s not like the Cowboys are great. Maybe the Eagles’ defense, which has been able to keep the team in games prior to falling apart late after getting gassed because the offense can’t stay on the field, actually gets some good turnover luck and produces some takeaways. Maybe the Eagles’ terrible offense finally comes alive against this dreadful Dallas defense. A win here hardly makes me feel like the Eagles’ season is back on. But it might make for one fun night, at least. Eagles 23, Cowboys 21.

They were giving up 168.4 rushing yards per game before Week 6, including 241 to Tampa Bay, which helped bring Mike Pettine onto the staff as a senior defensive assistant. Dallas did hold Green Bay to 57 rushing yards on 26 carries in the 23-13 loss at Lambeau, and Clark pointed straight at that. “I think it all started right there with the run game, stopping that,” Clark said after the game , adding that it got the Packers into “longer passing situations.” NFL predictions: 3 bold takes on the Cowboys at Eagles – Dave Halprin, Blogging the Boys Three spicy hot takes that could happen Monday night. He does have three touchdowns, but he also has a fumble and the crushing miscue that led to the game-ending interception last week. His YAC is a measly 45 yards this year. title: Sean Payton says they need to get RB Jonah Coleman more touches
summary: The Jonah Coleman takeover is happening! The Broncos ‘ fourth-round rookie running back was activated off the injured reserve ahead of today’s game vs. the Cardinals and quickly became an impact player for the offense. He led the Broncos’ ball carriers in rushing with 9 carries for 54 yards while averaging an impressive 6.0 yards […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman (20) celebrates on the field after defeating the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Jonah Coleman takeover is happening! The Broncos ‘ fourth-round rookie running back was activated off the injured reserve ahead of today’s game vs. the Cardinals and quickly became an impact player for the offense. He led the Broncos’ ball carriers in rushing with 9 carries for 54 yards while averaging an impressive 6.0 yards per carry. Coleman displayed good vision, had plus short-area burst, ran with power, and looked like the Broncos’ best running back by far. After the game, Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters that they “got to get him (Coleman) more touches. Definitely”. Sean Payton on Jonah Coleman: "Got to get him more touches. Definitely" — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) October 25, 2026 Coleman had 11 total touches for 69 yards and led the Broncos backfield in touches, snaps, and routes, and could be in store for a larger workload moving forward, according to Payton. The talk after the game is about how Coleman should be the Broncos’ starting back, but it seems like that change already happened today. It was only a matter of time. Dobbins was impressive last year before his injury, but he seems to have lost a step and is posting career-worst numbers across the board. He has scored a touchdown in three straight games and should have a role on this offense moving forward, but this should be Jonah Coleman’s backfield now and moving forward. If the Broncos can get this sort of production from Coleman moving forward, it will be a huge boost to their offense. They had little to no run game this season, and defenses have not been respecting their run game. Coleman producing like this changes that and makes life easier for quarterback Bo Nix, who showed off his running ability today with a 60+ yard untouched touchdown run. If the Broncos want to win a Super Bowl, they NEED a run game. Coleman provides that, while second-year back RJ Harvey can be a playmaker in the pass game while offering some speed/juice on occasion as a runner. This also should quiet the talk about trading for a back like Jonathan Taylor, but still, that could be viewed as a big “win now” move by the Broncos, and we’ll see how that progresses in the coming days/weeks. At the end of the day, it appears that Jonah Coleman has taken over the Broncos’ backfield and could see a larger workload moving forward. The fourth-round rookie has flashed his talent ever since he was drafted and he’s on the verge of being a second-half breakout player for the Broncos.

title: Winners and Losers from the Denver Broncos’ 30-16 victory over the Arizona Cardinals
summary: Was this a “get right” game for the Broncos? It sure seemed like it. We saw vintage Bo Nix, the run game flashed, big plays by Waddle, Mims, and Sutton, and the defense held tough for most of the game. After a long week of discourse over Bo Nix and the Broncos offense, the media-driven […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos leaves the field after defeating the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Was this a “get right” game for the Broncos? It sure seemed like it. We saw vintage Bo Nix, the run game flashed, big plays by Waddle, Mims, and Sutton, and the defense held tough for most of the game. After a long week of discourse over Bo Nix and the Broncos offense, the media-driven narrative is dead for at least this week. The Broncos are now 5-2 and have won 18 of their last 21 games. Good times in Mile High! A two-score victory? Lots of winners being handed out today, but there are still a few losers coming out of this game. So, with all that said, here are your winners and losers from the Broncos’ 30-16 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. WINNER – QB Bo Nix After a week of bullshit from all corners of the media, Nix responded well against the Cardinals. He finished 15 of 29 for 222 yards, 1 passing touchdown, 74 rushing yards, and another touchdown. He had two big plays: a 62-yard rushing touchdown as well as a 52-yard passing touchdown to running back RJ Harvey on a screen play. Nix looked confident, made some big throws, and led the offense to 30 points on the road. BO NIX RUNS FOR A 62 YARD TOUCHDOWN!!! pic.twitter.com/ldbOsKgX0R — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 25, 2026 Was it a perfect game? No. He had some misthrows; the offense had some drops, and the offense started a little slow. However, he bounced back and played well for most of the game and again led the Broncos to 30 points. After a week where his play was called “disrespectful” and Payton was questioned if Nix should be benched, Nix responded and silenced the haters. It was a ridiculous media-driven narrative anyways. WINNER – RB Jonah Coleman and RB RJ Harvey Jonah Coleman has arrived. After the game, head coach Sean Payton told reporters that he has to get “Coleman more touches” moving forward, and he has certainly earned them. He led the Broncos ball carriers in rushing with 9 carries for 54 yards. Coleman showed the vision, burst, acceleration, and power needed to be a starter in the NFL and had the best overall performance of any back this season by the Broncos. He should be their starter moving forward, RJ Harvey also gets a winner for me due to his play in the receiving game. He took a well-timed screen play vs. the blitz untouched for a 50+ yard touchdown. RJ HARVEY UNTOUCHED 52-YARD TOUCHDOWN Beautiful play call vs. the blitz pic.twitter.com/dG7uwKLRlA — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 25, 2026 Coleman should be the Broncos’ starting running back. He passes the eye test and results speak for themselves. Also, Harvey has been the Broncos’ best playmaker this season and once again had a big explosive play for a touchdown. They need to lean on this one-two punch moving forward. LOSER – RB JK Dobbins Dobbins played okay today and scored a touchdown for the third straight game. However, the reality is, he should not be the Broncos’ starting running back. He currently has a career-low in YPC and averaged just 3.8 on the ground today while Coleman had 6.0. Add in Payton saying Coleman needs to get more touches, and you have Dobbins stock trending in the wrong direction. Sean Payton on Jonah Coleman: "Got to get him more touches. Definitely" — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) October 25, 2026 With that said, Dobbins looked his best today and had a nice run wiped out by one of the many flags in this game. However, the eye test tells you everything. He looks slow and lacks that extra gear to get away from defenders, while Coleman has that speed, burst, vision, and power. It’s time to make the switch. WINNER – WR/KR Marvin Mims Jr. A great time for Marvin Mims to have the best game of his season. He had a couple of nice returns and had 53 yards in the passing game. Most of that came on a 47-yard reception, which led to a touchdown by the Broncos. NIX FINDS MIMS FOR A BIG GAIN pic.twitter.com/KZfZESG5GC — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 25, 2026 With Waddle leaving the game with an injury and Bryant sidelined, the Broncos need more of these explosive plays by Mims moving forward. LOSER – Penalties The Broncos had 11 penalties for 114 yards today, which is not good. This has been an issue throughout the Sean Payton era; however, the officials were awful in this game. They had bad and inconsistent calls on both sides and had an impact on this game. One of their worst calls was on, you guessed it, cornerback Riley Moss, who was flagged for a field-flipping defensive pass interference on a play where… no DPI happened. For whatever reason, this keeps happening with Moss. The refs hate for Riley Moss continues. How in the hell is this DPI?? pic.twitter.com/rE18DnYURF — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 25, 2026 After the game, Payton was asked about the officials in this game, and he had an interesting comment on their performance. He told reporters, “I am never going to criticize the officials. At one point I said, ‘You are doing your best to turn the TV audience off. You are on a roll.'” They were genuinely bad and had missed calls on both teams, but thankfully, it did not end up costing the Broncos the game. WINNER – LB Alex Singleton Singleton has been playing good football lately. Sure, he still has his struggles, but he was all over the field today and had 19 total tackles, including a late-game sack of Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett, which took them off the 1-yard line. Tackle stats don’t matter too much, but Singleton has played well in recent weeks, and most importantly, hasn’t been missing many tackles. He does have his issues in coverage from time to time, but overall, I think he has been playing solid football for the Broncos WINNER – Nik Bonitto The stat line shows 1 tackle and 0 sacks, but his impact was felt throughout the game. Bonitto had a career-high 13 pressures vs. the Cardinals and was close to multiple sacks. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett was just annoyingly good at getting the ball out. Nik Bonitto generated a career-high 13 pressures in Week 7 against the Cardinals, the most pressures by any player since Nick Bosa in Week 6, 2024 (14). Bonitto recorded 12 of his pressures across 27 matchups against Cardinals LT Jayden Williams. #DENvsAZ | #BroncosCountry pic.twitter.com/B1o0MY8my6 — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 25, 2026 The Broncos did have 3 total sacks, but they should have had more if we’re being honest. Gotta credit Brissett for getting the ball away and avoiding the sack, but the Broncos’ pass rush was getting home throughout the game. LOSER – Whoever was covering Trey McBride 10 receptions for 111 yards and 1 touchdown. McBride saw 13 total targets, and the Broncos did not have an answer for him no matter who was in coverage. He’s the best tight end in the NFL for a reason, but I had hoped the Broncos would do better against him. Still, the Broncos held the Cardinals to 16 points and limited the damage, but Vance Joseph’s struggles vs. elite tight ends continue. Other notable Winners and Losers WINNER – FB Adam Prentice: Blocked punt! LOSER – CB Ja’Quan McMillian: He should of had 3 INTs today but developed short-term Hufanga-itis and dropped all three gimme INTs (We still love J-Mac and this is mostly a joke, don’t get too upset). WINNER – Broncos red zone defense: They held the Cardinals to just 1 touchdown in 5 red zone attempts. They bent but did not break. WINNER – Que Robinson: He’s a stud. LOSER – Injuries: Waddle (chest) and Allen (Hamstring) left the game late with injuries and did not return. Waddle’s looked the worse of the two, but we will have to wait for updates on both. LOSER – The refs: They sucked. LOSER – Brandon Jones: He has been solid for the Broncos but had multiple missed tackles today. WINNER – The George Paton guys: Que Robinson, Kris Abrams-Draine,…

title: 7 things we learned from the Broncos 30-16 over the Cardinals
summary: That was the Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos we’re accustomed to seeing. The Broncos dominated in a 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals, improving their record to 5-2. It’s what you would call a get-right game for Denver’s offense, and it was the most complete game of the season. Here’s what we learned from […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with Jaylen Waddle #17 after scoring a touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals during the third quarter at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images That was the Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos we’re accustomed to seeing. The Broncos dominated in a 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals, improving their record to 5-2. It’s what you would call a get-right game for Denver’s offense, and it was the most complete game of the season. Here’s what we learned from Sunday’s win over the Cardinals. Bo Nix was fantastic This was a get-right game for the Broncos offense, but it was that for Nix in a big way. I’m sure it was still disrespectful, though. In all seriousness, that was the best game Nix has played this season. He was simply fantastic against an Arizona defense that shut down Matthew Stafford last week. Nix finished the game 15-for-29 passing for 222 yards and a touchdown. The Broncos quarterback also had seven carries for 73 yards, including a 62-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. It was that run where Nix finally showed off the running capability. It also sparked him and the offense in the second half. There are still some areas for Nix to improve upon, and he was far from perfect, but this was the game that he needed. Denver’s offense was balanced and effective It helps to have your quarterback play his best game of the season, but the whole offense was much better against the Cardinals on Sunday. It didn’t start that way, especially in the first quarter. But after Nix’s rushing touchdown, the offense finally clicked. The Broncos had four possessions in the second half, three resulted in points, and two ended in touchdowns. By the way, the 52-yard touchdown by RJ Harvey was the perfect play call by Sean Payton. And it was a great execution by Nix and Harvey, as well as the offensive line and the rest of the offense, to get that into the end zone. The offense must improve on third down (3-for-11), but Denver ran a balanced attack on Sunday. The Broncos had 56 total plays, resulting in 29 passes and 26 rushes. Jonah Coleman is your No. 1 running back If there was any doubt Coleman needs to be the No. 1 running back for Denver, it’s gone. The rookie was outstanding on Sunday. He finally got the running game going for the Broncos. Coleman also picked up a blitzer in pass protection. The rookie running back had nine carries for 54 yards, averaging six yards per carry. Coleman also had two receptions for 15 yards. As Payton said to the media after the game, “Got to get him more touches. Definitely.” Nik Bonitto brought the pressure Don’t let the sack numbers fool you, Nik Bonitto was unreal on Sunday. While Bonitto didn’t record any sacks, just one quarterback hit, and one tackle, he finished with a career-high 13 QB pressures. That’s the most in the NFL since Nick Bosa in Week 6 2024, when he got 14. Speaking of the defense … Defense brought the pride It may not have seemed like much, but I loved the Denver defense standing tall and keeping the Cardinals out of the end zone late in the game. For the rest of the game, the Broncos did what they do and pressured the quarterback. Denver finished with three sacks and 13 quarterback hits. Malcome Roach led the way for the Broncos with four QB hits, three tackles, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Alex Singleton did his thing Entering Sunday’s game, the Broncos linebacker led the NFL in tackling. His game on Sunday won’t hurt him. And he just does what he does. Singleton had 19 tackles (12 solo), two QB hits, one sack, and one tackle for loss. NFL officiating is just bad The refs hate for Riley Moss continues. How in the hell is this DPI?? pic.twitter.com/rE18DnYURF — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 25, 2026 This could be an evergreen statement and included in every one of these, but Sunday was bad. And it’s not just bad penalties, they’re seeing things that aren’t even penalties now. This is not to excuse the Broncos and their 11 penalties, but come on. As Payton said to the media after the game: “I am never going to criticize the officials. At one point, I said, ‘You are doing your best to turn the TV audience off. You are on a roll.”

title: Instant reaction: Explosive plays help Broncos notch fifth victory of the season over Cardinals
summary: The Denver Broncos entered their Week 7 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals with a 4-2 record. The Broncos hoped this would be the game everything would fire on all cylinders. For the most part, that’s what happened in their 30-16 victory over the Cardinals. Here are some instant reactions from today’s matchup. First half issues […]
full_text: Oct 25, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) scores a touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals during the first half at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Denver Broncos entered their Week 7 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals with a 4-2 record. The Broncos hoped this would be the game everything would fire on all cylinders. For the most part, that’s what happened in their 30-16 victory over the Cardinals. Here are some instant reactions from today’s matchup. First half issues continue for Broncos on offense This Sunday’s matchup versus the Cardinals provided the opportunity for Bo Nix and the Broncos’ offense to finally find their way. Earlier in the week, I noted some of the issues Nix has experienced this season. One of them was first down passing where there has been significant regression compared to 2024 and 2025. Head Coach Sean Payton clearly tried to find a way to improve that in the first half against the Cardinals. On most first downs early in the game, Payton opted to throw the ball. Unfortunately, outside of a handful of passes, there was not much success to be found and Denver’s offensive endeavors suffered due to it. Nix went 10-of-19 in the first half for 72 passing yards. The offense had just six first downs. Moreover, were once again abysmal on third down sporting just one conversion on seven attempts. The Cardinals entered today’s matchup with one of the worst run defenses in the NFL. In three of their first six games, they had allowed at least 140 yards on the ground. With that in mind, I figured this would be a point of emphasis for Denver, especially with Jonah Coleman’s return. However, Denver opted to just run the ball nine times in the first half. Nevertheless, one of those runs was a huge play. It proved to be catalyst that helped jumpstart several encouraging drives for Denver as the game progressed. Let’s talk about that! But explosive plays made all the difference when it mattered The offense began to click late in the first half. Nix’s remarkable 62-yard touchdown scamper in the second quarter was the spark that ignited Denver’s offensive efforts the rest of their game. For all the hullabaloo surrounding Nix’s ankle—he seemed quite spry on that inspiring play. In the second half, Denver’s penchant for big plays continued. A well-timed screen pass by Nix to RJ Harvey against the blitz went for 52-yards and earned Denver their second touchdown of the game. This is something I’d like to see more of moving forward. When you get Harvey in space great thing usually happen. He’s incredible in that regard. In the final minutes of the third quarter, Nix was able to hit Marvin Mims Jr. on a 42-yard catch-and-run that got them in the red zone. That drive was topped off with a short yardage touchdown by J.K. Dobbins that put Denver up by multiple scores. In the final thirty minutes of play, Denver was more consistent with running the ball—especially with Coleman. I thought the rookie running back had a very strong comeback performance. In turn, that opened up some opportunities for Nix and the Broncos’ aerial attack down the field. All things considered, this was the “get it right” game the team needed on offense. It wasn’t perfect and they have some issues to still sort out, but they scored the most points of the season. I’m happy to see they finally had some explosive plays that had been absent from their efforts in the first six games. Denver’s defense plays well in first half, gives up ground in the second half The Cardinals came into Sunday’s matchup banged up on the offensive side of the ball. They didn’t have Jeremiyah Love at running back and that definitely put more pressure on quarterback Jacoby Brissett. In the first half, the Broncos’ defense played great. They held Brissett to just 53 yards through the air and allowed just 117 yards of total offense. Outside of a 29-yard run given up to Bam Knight, their run defense was strong. They excelled on getting off the field on third down with Arizona netting one conversion on eight attempts. Finding a way to limit Trey McBride was one of my keys to the game. In the first half, McBride had just four catches for 20 yards. He would go on to be the focal point of Arizona’s offensive attack in the second half and ended up with 11 catches for 111 yards and a touchdown. There were a few big chunk plays given up by Denver’s defense in the final two quarters. With a double-digit lead, I think Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph was a little bit more conservative with his playcalling in the second half. Even so, the performance was good enough to help Denver win. That goal line stand to end the game was quite nice to witness. Though I’d like to see some of those pressures turn into sacks moving forward. They’ll need the pass rush to come up in a big next weekend in their rematch at home versus the Kansas City Chiefs. Special teams answered the call and helped with the field position battle A key to victory I discussed earlier in the week was the need for special teams to step up. It’s basically been the Jeremy Crawshaw show for most of the season with very little impact returns on kicks or punts. That changed today. Mims had several good returns that gave Denver great starting field position. He finished the game with over 100 kick return yards this afternoon with a long of 39 yards. Additionally, Adam Prentice’s blocked punt in the third quarter that gave Denver tremendous field position. Kicker Wil Lutz hit all three of his field goals and all three extra points. Kudos to Special Teams coach Darren Rizzi and his players today. Their efforts were sound and played a big role in Denver’s fifth victory of the season. Adam Prentice with the block 💪 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/6Rbiw5VTDS — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 25, 2026

summary: The Denver Broncos needed a ‘get right’ type game on offense and that is what we got in their road win over the Arizona Cardinals today. Bo Nix found his legs and found the throws down the seam to put up nearly 400 yards in total offense. Nix would finish 15/29 for 222 yards and […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos runs for a touchdown during the second quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos needed a ‘get right’ type game on offense and that is what we got in their road win over the Arizona Cardinals today. Bo Nix found his legs and found the throws down the seam to put up nearly 400 yards in total offense. Nix would finish 15/29 for 222 yards and a touchdown pass while adding four carries for 75 yards and another touchdown. At 5-2, the Broncos are knocking the Kansas City Chiefs doorstep with them coming to Denver next week. Nix starts the game off with a 20 yard pass to Courtland Sutton pic.twitter.com/t5RuJyyIHi — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 25, 2026 However, the offense would go into hibernation for the rest of the quarter. They were aided by good field position to put up two field goal drives, but by and large they were ineffective on offense again to start a game despite the six point lead. Broncos 6, Cardinals 0. Full first quarter recap . Second Quarter The Broncos offense woes continued throughout the second quarter, while the officiating crew came to the aid of the Cardinals with one of the worst defensive pass interference calls ever to help Arizona get back into the game on back-to-back drives. After tying things up, the Broncos offense needed a spark and a spark they got from Bo Nix. Feeling pressure, he jumped through the middle of the line and took off only to find there were not Cardinals defenders to be found on his way to a 62-yard touchdown scramble. This won't help his aDot 🤓 https://t.co/AeOa1R4BI9 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 25, 2026 With the game’s only touchdown, the Broncos went into halftime up 13-6 over the Cardinals. Broncos 13, Cardinals 6. Full second quarter recap . Third Quarter The big plays continued for the Broncos to start the second half. The Cardinals were threatening across midfield, but Denver’s defense made a stop where Adam Prentice blocked the ensuing punt to set Denver’s offense up with good field position. Two plays into that, Bo Nix hit RJ Harvey on a screen pass who knifed his way through the Cardinals defense for a 52-yard touchdown catch and run to put the Broncos up by two touchdowns midway through the third quarter. RJ HARVEY UNTOUCHED 52-YARD TOUCHDOWN Beautiful play call vs. the blitz pic.twitter.com/dG7uwKLRlA — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 25, 2026 After giving up a touchdown drive, the Broncos’ offense needed to come back out and try to get back up by two scores. Jonah Coleman started things off nicely with a few solid runs to get the Broncos near midfield where Ninx would find Marvin Mims Jr. open down field. Mims would break a tackle and scamper for 47 yards to setup a first and goal. NIX FINDS MIMS FOR A BIG GAIN pic.twitter.com/KZfZESG5GC — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 25, 2026 J.K. Dobbins would cap the drive with a one yard plunge to put the Broncos back up by two touchdowns at the end of the third quarter. Broncos 27, Cardinals 13. Full third quarter recap . Fourth Quarter Despite it being very early in the fourth quarter, the Cardinals seemed to be moving into desperation mode going for it on a fourth and very long. The Broncos defense was there to shut them down and get the ball back into Denver’s hands. Great read by KAD to get the stop and force a turnover on downs pic.twitter.com/X6pZkwqKGt — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 25, 2026 The Broncos run game spearheaded by Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins began to wake up, but the penalty problems also began to wake up. Dobbins had a 15 yard run wiped out by an illegal shift penalty. The good news is, the Bo Nix ‘get right’ game was today as he fired a bullet down the middle of the field to Jaylen Waddle for a 27 yard gain into field goal range. The vibes were high on that drive and it seemed like nothing could slow Nix down. On a designed rollout he found an open Courtland Sutton for another chunk gain to the Cardinals 13 yard line. A penalty again slowed them down and after getting those yards back faced a third and ten where Nix was immediately pressured and had to throw it away to settle for the field goal and 17-point lead halfway through the fourth quarter. Arizona put up some garbage time drives, but the clock kept chugging away to the Broncos victory in Week 7 and the defense made the plays it needed to in order to secure the victory. Broncos 30, Cardinals 16.

title: Discussion: Is Dan Campbell taking too many risks?
summary: Whether you trust the odds or trust your gut, there is no denying that critical decisions at pivotal moments can win or lose you a football game. Football is a game of risk, but some coaches try to minimize it while others try to capitalize on it. Dan Campbell and the Detroit Lions have been […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions looks on against the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Whether you trust the odds or trust your gut, there is no denying that critical decisions at pivotal moments can win or lose you a football game. Football is a game of risk, but some coaches try to minimize it while others try to capitalize on it. Dan Campbell and the Detroit Lions have been classified as high rollers since he was hired as head coach—is it time to change? The Lions defeated the Green Bay Packers in their Week 7 tilt, but things could have turned out far different if not for a few key moments. If the Packers had converted one or both of their failed field goals, the Lions would have needed a touchdown, not a field goal, on their final drive. If the Packers had converted on a few of their deep shots, the Packers likely put up more than 17 points. If the officiating had been less strict with roughing the passer or more strict with pass interference, perhaps some drives would have flipped from success to failure or vice versa. In such a close matchup, one decision can alter the outcome of the game. We nearly saw that happen on Sunday when the Lions boldly attempted a fourth-and-1 at their own 24-yard line . With around five minutes left in the game, the win probability would have swung wildly based on the play’s outcome. Had Detroit converted, they would have had a fresh set of downs with a chance to drain the clock and march downfield for a game-winning field goal. With a failed conversion, Green Bay would have been set up deep in Lions territory with a great chance to take the lead via field goal or touchdown. It was only natural that both outcomes happened. The Packers stopped Jahmyr Gibbs for a loss on the play, yet their subsequent four-play drive ended with a missed field goal, aided by a tip from DJ Wonnum. Detroit promptly marched down the field and drained the remaining three minutes to set up a Jake Bates game-winner. In a way, the Lions were both punished and rewarded for their risk taking. Had the Lions punted outright, Green Bay likely would have drained more of the clock on their next drive, potentially keeping the ball out of Detroit’s hands. Campbell said as much in his post-game press conference: Dan Campbell on why he went for it so deep in his own zone at the end of the game. 2 reasons: "I thought we would get it." "I knew we would get the ball back if it didn't work out." — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) October 25, 2026 However, now that the Lions have a playoff-caliber roster, wouldn’t it make sense to tone down the risky plays and let the roster’s talent speak for itself? For a team that had already shot themselves in the foot twice with fumbles, committing two turnovers on downs only added to the circus that was this game. Wouldn’t it make more sense to trot out the kicker for easier points, or the punter booting one to flip the field? Taking too many risks can backfire and cost you a game. Today’s Question of the Day is: Is Dan Campbell taking too many risks? My answer: I do not think so. In the early years of Campbell’s head coaching tenure, many people saw the risk-taking mindset as a byproduct of a bad roster. If the Lions wanted to win games, they needed to roll the dice. They nearly did so against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 7 of the 2021 season, a game in which the Lions ran two fake punts and a surprise onside kick . For one, after having watched Campbell since 2021, it seems clear that the risk taking in 2021 was just as much about his identity as it was about the roster. This isn’t to say that Campbell is keen to take a risk whenever he can. For a guy that still gets the label of “meathead” after a half decade, Campbell’s risk senses are genuinely elite. He’s not a guy that crunches the numbers on every given play, but his gut instinct is often in-line with what analytics say. This comes from being immersed in football for years as a player and as a coach. Simply put, he has the knack for knowing when to make a calculated risk, even if he is not actually doing that calculation. There have been moments where Campbell has taken risks and it has backfired, without doubt. However, I think you need to live with those mistakes because the reward is worth it. Campbell trusts his players and trusts their talent. If you need to get two yards, how many of us wouldn’t want to run Jahmyr Gibbs behind the likes of Penei Sewell? The execution can be flawed even when the logic was sound. Sometimes an opponent throws rock when you throw scissors—that is how football goes. I really believe that the Lions are a better team because Campbell trusts his instincts so often. This will lead to frustrating moments that can alter the outcome of a game, but I think this is a necessary consequence of a winning mindset. When a gamble fails, it is easy to have a knee-jerk negative reaction. However, often upon reflection, the gamble was actually revealed to have been a savvy move. Personally, I do not want Campbell to change his ways. Do you agree or disagree with my stance? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Lions injury update: No concern for Jahmyr Gibbs despite awkward slide
summary: On the play before the Detroit Lions’ game-winning kick against the Green Bay Packers, Jahmyr Gibbs had a clean path to the end zone, but stopped on a dime after earning the first down. He did that so Detroit could run off any remainder of the clock and kick the field goal as time expired—the […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions dives for a first down during fourth quarter of a game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images On the play before the Detroit Lions’ game-winning kick against the Green Bay Packers, Jahmyr Gibbs had a clean path to the end zone, but stopped on a dime after earning the first down. He did that so Detroit could run off any remainder of the clock and kick the field goal as time expired—the exact right thing to do But on the play, Gibbs fell awkwardly to the ground and got up slowly. That led many Lions fans to express significant concern about their bell-cow back. Thankfully, there is nothing to worry about. “We got him checked. He should be good,” coach Dan Campbell said after the game. Gibbs was all smiles in the locker room after the game, further indicating that there doesn’t appear to be any issues with his health. He also addressed the injury, saying he experienced some initial pain, but not anymore. “It did (hurt) at first, but it went away, though,” Gibbs said. “Yeah, it’s going to be fine.” Campbell said the scare did give him a little pause about the strategy at the end of the game. Rather than risk an injury, maybe it’s more important to just score and trust your defense to keep the Packers out of the end zone at the end of the game. “Is it really worth going down and try to finish the game or you just go score? Sometimes I question that,” Campbell said. “I don’t know, maybe we shouldn’t just, but all good. It’s a good win.” In the meantime, Gibbs joked that he may take some sliding tips from quarterback Jared Goff. “He needs to (teach me); that shit was awful,” Gibbs said.

title: 13 winners, 5 losers from Detroit Lions’ win over the Green Bay Packers
summary: Stress-free football this was not, but regardless, it will go down as a win for the Detroit Lions over the Green Bay Packers. Both teams did their best to win and lose this game, with a fair number of blunders and botches leaving points off the board. Despite a game in which both teams combined […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions celebrates a first down catch against the Green Bay Packers during the second quarter at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Stress-free football this was not, but regardless, it will go down as a win for the Detroit Lions over the Green Bay Packers. Both teams did their best to win and lose this game, with a fair number of blunders and botches leaving points off the board. Despite a game in which both teams combined for over 700 yards of offense, the final score was a mere 20-17. Thankfully for Detroit, they emerged on the winning side of that high-wire act. The bye week proved fruitful for the Lions, getting a win over one divisional foe. With the Minnesota Vikings on deck, here is hoping they can string two NFC North wins together. Which players emerged from an eventful Sunday tilt as a winner or loser? Note: The label of “loser” is used to evaluate and contrast in-game performance and is not an indictment of a player’s ability, value, or character. The term is not intended to be disrespectful in nature. Winners: Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR “The best way to keep the Packers’ defense honest and open is to test them deep with Jameson Williams.” That was a quote from Erik Schlitt in his keys to the game, and he hit the nail on the head. Even though Amon-Ra St. Brown led the team in receiving yards, I would argue that Williams was just as impactful. The speed of Williams was a genuine threat for the Packers defense and it facilitated a lot of the offense’s successes. The Packers boast a solid pair of safeties, but with their attention turned to covering Williams and the deep shots, that left a lot of room for St. Brown to dice up the defense. St. Brown was dynamite, recording nine catches for a whopping 153 yards. He was contributing in a multitude of ways, from catching the long bomb (40 yards) to churning out yards-after-the-catch. As for Williams, he was no slouch either, scoring two critical touchdowns and coming a toe away from a third. He ended the day with five catches for 91 yards and two touchdowns. It’s not hard to see how well these two compliment each other. On any given week, one or both of them could breakout—opposing defenses have to pick their poison. Loser: Cade Mays, C The much-anticipated debut of the Lions’ big ticket free agent went about as poorly as can be. Mays struggled in the trenches, perhaps a symptom of being out for over two months. In pass protection, he was often getting pushed back into the pocket (he was credited with the lone sack allowed). As for the run game, a majority of the Lions’ success came on plays towards the perimeter, away from Mays. Unfortunately for Mays, he was at the forefront of two pivotal fumbles. On the final drive of the first half with the Lions primed to at least score a field goal, Mays unintentionally forced a fumble on Jahmyr Gibbs, netting the Lions zero points. The Lions received the football to start the second half, but it was squandered on a botched snap between Mays and Jared Goff. Goff blamed himself for the play , but it is nonetheless an unfortunate stain on Mays’ debut. That fumble was recovered by the Packers. Instead of the Lions being up by multiple scores, the Packers were able to score and take the lead in a back-and-forth affair. Given that Juice Scruggs had been playing well prior to Mays’ return, there will be an active discussion about how the Lions should approach the center position going forward. I think it would be too harsh to bench him so soon, but I would like to see him rebound in his next start. Winner: Brian Branch, S Welcome back! The Lions needed a game-changer in the secondary and they got exactly that with Branch. The Lions still had their share of misplays in the defense, but adding Branch to the lineup gives them a higher ceiling and a higher floor. He made a great ball-hawking interception to give life to Ford Field after back-to-back drives ending in fumbles. His impact goes beyond picks, however, as he plays a pivotal role in run defense (four tackles, three of which were stops per PFF) and pass defense (one pass defended and zero receptions allowed, per PFF). With just Chuck Clark and Keith Abney at safety, they were having to shoulder the burdens of a struggling secondary. Now that Branch is in the mix, everyone’s job gets easier. Clark and Abney were solid on Sunday, while the secondary in general looked sharper. Branch’s snap count will continue to ramp up in the coming weeks, but it is clear that they need him on the field early and often. Loser: Sam LaPorta, TE On one hand, when St. Brown and Williams are humming, it is not unexpected to see them dominate the target share. However, given how often the Lions were airing it on (32 attempts from Jared Goff), you would expect to see LaPorta at least somewhat involved. Instead, LaPorta was a ghost. LaPorta had a mere two targets on the day, only one of which resulted in a catch. This was, to his credit, a big 18-yard gain to help spur a late-game drive, but those types of plays need to happen in every quarter, not the dying minutes of a game. This performance looms large after his public complaints regarding his contract status this past week. One game like this won’t change his price tag to Detroit or another suitor, but you would nonetheless hope for a bigger impact. Winner: Khalil Dorsey, CB Khalil Dorsey had been a special teams ace for the Lions, but he might be playing his way into a defensive role as well. He only saw limited action (14 snaps on defense), but he was nails when targeted. He was stride-for-stride with speedster Matthew Golden on an incompletion and later recorded a pass breakup on a deep shot to Bo Melton. He later added a tackle on Christian Watson along the sideline to limit him to a small gain of five yards. The Lions have been rotating cornerbacks all season long trying to find an answer, and Dorsey was next up this week. Overall, it was a success, but we have to acknowledge it was a small sample size. His play should warrant more snaps in the coming weeks, though this might be out of necessity with Ennis Rakestraw nursing an ankle injury: #Lions coach Dan Campbell says they're going to continue to use their full cornerback room, including Khalil Dorsey, going forward. — Nolan Bianchi (@nolanbianchi) October 26, 2026 Winner: Kelvin Sheppard, DC A paper tiger indeed . Despite the Packers coming into this game with a high-flying passing attack built on the YOLO ball (and fishing for defensive pass interference), the Lions had one of their best defensive showings on Sunday. The return of Brian Branch (who snagged himself an interception) undoubtedly helped with communication on the back end. Now, the Lions were limited to only a few busted coverages—progress! The tape will be an interesting one to review, but you have to credit Sheppard’s defense for locking up what can be a potent offense. Josh Jacobs, making his return from suspension, tallied just 36 yards on 11 carries—the Packers run game as a whole continues to struggle. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, the playmaking deep threats, combined for 11 catches for 96 yards. Tucker Kraft did get free for a touchdown, but you could also argue that Jack Campbell was interfered with by Watson running his route —whether legal or illegal, I will let you debate that. The Lions did get help from subpar officiating, multiple Packers drops, and some coaching buffoonery from Matt LaFleur, but the defense as a whole has now put together back-to-back solid outings. If they can further crack down on critical downs (the Packers were 3-for-4 on fourth down), it’s not hard to envision this defense looking adequate. Given how the season started, that is welcome growth. Loser: Drew Petzing, OC Overall, the offense was effective, and I would normally keep Petzing out of the “Loser”…

title: Dan Campbell explains 4th-down decision that could’ve cost Lions game vs. Packers
summary: In the fourth quarter of the Detroit Lions’ Week 7 game against the Green Bay Packers, Lions coach Dan Campbell made an aggressive fourth down decision—even by his standards. With the game tied at 17 and just under five minutes left, the Lions faced a fourth-and-1 (long 1, if we’re being honest) at Detroit’s own […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Dan Campbell and Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions interact prior to a game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the fourth quarter of the Detroit Lions’ Week 7 game against the Green Bay Packers, Lions coach Dan Campbell made an aggressive fourth down decision—even by his standards. With the game tied at 17 and just under five minutes left, the Lions faced a fourth-and-1 (long 1, if we’re being honest) at Detroit’s own 24-yard line. Instead of punting, Detroit opted to go for it, and Jahmyr Gibbs was tackled for a 2-yard loss that turned the ball over on downs and gave Green Bay the ball already in field goal range. The Lions, however, got a three-and-out defensive stop right after that, and the Packers’ go-ahead 35-yard field goal attempt was deflected by Lions defensive lineman DJ Wonnum and missed the uprights. That allowed the Lions offense to eat up the remainder of the clock and kick the game-winning field goal as time expired for a 20-17 win. Despite it all working out, Campbell certainly faced a lot of criticism for a decision that could’ve—and probably should’ve—been much more costly. However, Campbell had a strong defense of his decision. “Well, I thought we would get it, number one. I really believed we would get that (first down),” Campbell said. “Number two, I knew we would get the ball back if it didn’t work out.” It’s a simple enough response, but the second part is an important point. The Packers took over with 4:50 left at the Lions’ 22-yard line, so there was no real chance they would score and run out the rest of the clock. So, at worst, the Lions would have had plenty of time to either tie or win the game regardless of how Green Bay’s drive ended. Interestingly enough, there was at least one analytical model that approved of Detroit’s aggressive decision in that moment. ESPN’s Seth Walder said that their model had the probabilities in favor of going for it: Solid go on 4th down. This one will be second guessed because of where they are on the field. But value of possession is very high and conversion chance is high on a 4th-and-1. Remember: punts are turnovers ~100% of the time. pic.twitter.com/jD0zwJb2Ie — Seth Walder (@SethWalder) October 25, 2026 What do you think of Campbell’s call?

title: 5 takeaways from Detroit Lions’ 20-17 win against Green Bay Packers
summary: Coming off a bye week, the Detroit Lions got extra time to prepare for the Green Bay Packers in their first NFC North battle of 2026. This game was much closer than it should’ve been, as Detroit dominated and its own mistakes gave Green Bay life. It came down to a game-winning kick by kicker […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Penei Sewell #58 of the Detroit Lions leads a huddle prior to a game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming off a bye week, the Detroit Lions got extra time to prepare for the Green Bay Packers in their first NFC North battle of 2026. This game was much closer than it should’ve been, as Detroit dominated and its own mistakes gave Green Bay life. It came down to a game-winning kick by kicker Jake Bates, with Detroit winning 20-17. Here are my five takeaways from the Lions’ thrilling win against the Packers. When the offense was consistent, it was dominant Despite scoring only 20 points, the Lions offense was great when it clicked. They had an opening-drive touchdown for the first time this season, moving the ball downfield with ease as they scored in under four minutes on six plays to take the lead. Quarterback Jared Goff was wheeling and dealing, going 22-for-32 for 303 yards and two touchdowns. Jameson Williams' 2nd TD of the game and the Lions take the lead back! GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/crTR8JKgaZ — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Wide receiver Jameson Williams found the end zone for Detroit, catching five for 91 yards and two touchdowns. Lions’ leading receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had his biggest game of the season, getting nine catches for 153 yards. The passing attack was lethal and picked apart the Packers’ secondary, which relies on its safeties to bail it out. Play action worked with ease, given Green Bay’s lack of depth at linebacker. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs had highs and lows, finishing with 29 carries for 116 yards and five catches for 27 yards. His second-quarter fumble was costly, as it killed Detroit’s chance to at least take a six-point lead at the half after they got the ball back. In the end, Gibbs clutched up and helped set Bates up for the game-winning kick. The return of Brian Branch and Cade Mays was felt Two big pieces returned for the Lions on Sunday: safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays. Mays started at center, and the offensive line struck consistently in the passing game as play-action gave Goff time to let it rip. The running game showed flashes of success. Mays did make a mistake, though, and bumped into Gibbs on the first fumble of the game. Branch wasn’t on the field as often as Mays, as his Achilles injury will take time to adjust to playing again. Despite getting limited snaps, Branch had an impact with four tackles and a huge interception in the fourth quarter. The secondary did improve with Branch back, and Mays gave the offensive line a nice boost. These two players had a big impact in the win, and the team feels like it has a better identity on offense and defense. Branch back y'all pic.twitter.com/vjACYfESmQ — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 25, 2026 Defense crumbles on crucial downs Detroit’s defense has improved in its past two games, but its biggest problem this week was stopping the Packers on crucial downs. Green Bay was three-for-four on fourth-down attempts, getting 77 yards on those successful plays. On third-down, gotta-have-it stops, the Lions let the Packers go five-for-15. While that isn’t a high success rate, Green Bay converted on those downs and turned it into points almost every time. Opening drive – Converted fourth down, set up a field goal that was missed Second drive – Converted two third downs and one fourth down; result was a touchdown Third drive – Three-and-out Fourth drive – Converted one third and one fourth down; was stopped on downs on the lone failed fourth-down attempt Fifth drive – One rushing play before halftime Sixth drive – Scored touchdown pass on third down pass Seventh drive – Three-and-out Eighth drive – Interception on third down Ninth drive – Converted one third down, made field goal 10th drive – Missed field goal on four-play drive Detroit got bailed out by Packers kicker Trey Smack, who missed two field goals. If he’d made the first field goal, Green Bay might have kicked it on that fourth drive instead of going for it. Green Bay punted only twice all game, and if Detroit makes more stops, those punt numbers could rise. Penalties got cleaned up One issue Detroit has had this season is the number of penalties they’ve gotten in every game. From false starts to holding on either side of the ball, Detroit has been beating itself up in some games this season. On Sunday, Detroit got called for five penalties, a slight improvement from their average of seven per game, according to TeamRankings.com. Two were on special teams, one was a questionable penalty on linebacker Derrick Barnes, and the other two were false starts by the offensive line. The two offensive penalties didn’t hurt the team or stall the drive, which was good to see compared to earlier this year. Unfortunately, when they fix one problem, another one appears. Turnovers were costly While Detroit wasn’t beating themselves with penalties, they beat themselves up with fumbles. While the Gibbs fumble was friendly fire, it still made the game closer than it was. If Gibbs hadn’t fumbled it there, Detroit could have gone up by six to 10 at halftime. Detroit was moving the ball down the field with ease, and it killed the momentum. The second turnover was another awkward play by Mays and Goff; Mays hiked it, and I don’t know what happened. I don’t know if Goff didn’t grasp the ball or Mays snapped it too early, but it was kicked forward, and Green Bay got the ball to start both halves pretty much. While the first fumble didn’t give Green Bay points, the Packers capitalized on the second fumble and scored. Those two fumbles were big swings, and they almost turned this victory into a defeat. Detroit has to clean up the fumbles, and Goff threw multiple risky passes that should have been picked off; one was eliminated due to defensive pass interference on Green Bay. It was scary after the offense started strong, but if they can play clean football and avoid penalties and turnovers, this offense can stay one of the best in the NFL.

title: Detroit Lions hang on for wacky, wild win over Packers, 20-17
summary: It wasn’t the Detroit Lions’ prettiest win, a win over the Green Bay Packers is all the beauty I need to see in the world. It was a back-and-forth game with questionable coaching decisions and controversial officiating galore. It felt like the Lions had multiple opportunities to put the game away, but it took every […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 23: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions runs in action against the New York Giants at Ford Field on November 23, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images It wasn’t the Detroit Lions’ prettiest win, a win over the Green Bay Packers is all the beauty I need to see in the world. It was a back-and-forth game with questionable coaching decisions and controversial officiating galore. It felt like the Lions had multiple opportunities to put the game away, but it took every second of Sunday’s game to come away with the 20-17 win. Here’s how it all happened: First quarter The Detroit Lions won the toss, but unlike last game, they opted to defer to the second half. That put the Packers offense up first. A touchback on the opening kick gave Jordan Love good field position to start. An impressive 22-yard toe-tapping catch by Matthew Golden set them up in Detroit’s side of the field. Catch was good as Golden 👀 GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pwD104kt3K — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Then, facing a fourth-and-5 from Detroit’s 33-yard line, the Packers opted to go for it, and Love found Savion Williams for a huge 27-yard gain. 4th and 5 and Jordan Love and the @Packers get more than enough GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wcRJ5jXbcP — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 The Lions held strong in the red zone, though. On third-and-goal, pressure from Tyleik Williams forced Love out of the pocket and a low throw fell incomplete. This time, Green Bay would not go for it, and settle for a short field goal. But the Packers missed a 26-yard field goal and went empty-handed. The Lions finally got a quicker start on offense. They picked up an early third down with a toss to Jahmyr Gibb for 7 yards. Then it was three straight explosive passing plays: a 28-yard toss to Amon-Ra St. Brown , a 24-yard dart to Jameson Williams, and a 16-yard touchdown pass to a crossing Jamo for a six-play, 80-yard drive. 7-0 Lions. Waymooooo 🏄‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/N96lN27N8w — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 25, 2026 The Packers took over and dink and dunked their way to midfield. They faced a fourth-and-2 around the logo, and went for it again. Detroit had a coverage bust and left Tucker Kraft wide open for a 22-yard gain. A 4th down conversion from Tucker Kraft on National Tight Ends Day 💪 GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OaWEKaBqhe — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Aidan Hutchinson nearly picked off Love on second down in the red zone, setting up a third-and-9 from the 14-yard line. Love scrambled away from pressure and found Kraft wide open after Jack Campbell fell down in coverage. 7-7 tie. Who else to score the TD but the tight end Tucker Kraft? GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3gr4X4gNTy — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 The Lions looked to answer back quickly with another explosive passing play. Goff hit St. Brown for 40 yards on the first play of the drive. Goff airing it out for Amon-Ra and a 40-yard pickup pic.twitter.com/ApoHbXWppY — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 25, 2026 Then Gibbs slipped through a small crease and picked up 12 yards down to the Packers’ 25-yard line to end the first quarter. Second quarter Detroit’s drive came to a screeching halt after Gibbs was stopped for a 5-yard loss to open up the second quarter, and the Lions followed it up with a false start. A 15-yard pass to Gibbs set up a manageable third-and-5, but a quick screen to Gibbs was completely sniffed out by Green Bay. The Lions settled for a 40-yard field goal, and Jake Bates drilled it. 10-7 Lions. Another Bates touchback put the Packers on the 35 with an opportunity to take their first lead of the game. But, instead, they went three-and-out. That was largely thanks to Aidan Hutchinson’s sack Love for a 10-yard loss to start the drive. Wolverine coming thruuuuu pic.twitter.com/kQ8WtDUGxN — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 25, 2026 On third down, Love couldn’t find Christian Watson, with Ennis Rakestraw in tight coverage. Detroit ensuing drive got off to a promising start with a 17-yard pass to St. Brown. However, Goff fumbled the ball on the next play, and fell on it for a 7-yard loss. Back-to-back incomplete passes ended the drive and Jack Fox’s punt bounced in the end zone. Green Bay avoided another three-and-out with a big third-down conversion. Love found Williams for a 20-yard gain against an aggressive blitz call with Roger McCreary closing too late. They faced another third-and-long at midfield, and while they didn’t convert, they set up a fourth-and-3. Then Love found Watson wide open down to the Lions’ 13-yard line. In the red zone, Green Bay opted to go for it again on fourth down—their fourth attempt this half—but this time D.J. Reed made the open field tackle on Golden to turn it over on downs. Lions defense shuts down the 4th down play! GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QbkLxFrZSS — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Detroit took over deep in their own zone with 3:41 left and a chance to add to their lead before halftime. A screen to St. Brown kept the drive alive early, and he picked up another 15 to move toward midfield. A couple impressive Gibbs runs moved the Lions into Packers territory while eating up the majority of the remaining clock. St. Brown picked up back-to-back catches of 11 and 18 yards to move into the red zone. But Gibbs had an ill-timed fumbled and the Packers recovered with 19 seconds left in the half. Packers force a red zone turnover! GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/4fRkpI62sY — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Green Bay was happy to call it there, and it was 10-7 Lions at halftime. Third quarter Detroit’s offense picked up where it left off… as in they fumbled again. Goff and center Cade Mays, in his first game, couldn’t connect on the snap exchange, and the Packers recovered at the Lions’ 42-yard line. Packers recover another fumble! GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/J8dZ1qLvyQ — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 A few plays later—on third-and-6—Loe checked down to Josh Jacobs, who broke a few tackles and went 25-yard for the score and the Packers’ first lead of the game. 14-10 Packers. Oh my goodness! 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/JxepR2jP24 — Green Bay Packers (@packers) October 25, 2026 The Lions’ offense—fresh off back-to-back turnovers—moved the chains once with an Isaac TeSlaa third-down grab for 10 yards. Then Goff found Williams for 30 yards into Packers territory. A couple Gibbs runs earned af irst down, then Detroit was gifted a personal foul penalty on the Packers to move down to Green Bay’s 11-yard line. Two plays later, Goff found Williams for a 10-yard touchdown to re-take the lead. 17-14 Lions. Smooth route from Penei and it's TD No. 2️⃣ for Jamo pic.twitter.com/2KfdeEFr1A — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 25, 2026 The Packers responded with a three-and-out. Reed made a very nice play breaking up a deep shot to Matthew Golden that looked like it was originally going to be caught. Then Love’s YOLO ball on third down to Golden overshot the receiver. The Lions had yet another shot to push their lead to two scores, starting with the ball on their own 35-yard line. Detroit was the beneficiary of another questionable call—a roughing the passer after the Lions’ failed to convert a third down. Then Gibbs converted a third-and-1 with a 9-yard gain into the red zone. Then an obvious pass interference penalty on the Packers erased what would’ve been an interception. Detroit then got aggressive. Facing a fourth-and-5 from the Packers’ 6-yard line, they opted to go for it. Goff connected with Williams, but he was pushed out of bounds before being able to get his feet inbounds. Can't get the feet in and the @Packers will take over GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zf5ArjFmU8 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 The Packers got out of the shadow of their own…
