title: Winners & Losers: Rams stop bleeding, right ship in win over Raiders
summary: The challenges the Los Angeles Rams faced in Sunday’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders were symbolic of their early season results. After jumping out to a 28-6 halftime lead, the Raiders scored 15-straight to start the fourth quarter. For most of the season, the Rams have lacked obvious leadership and execution. Falling to 2-5 […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 25: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams and Konata Mumpfield #4 celebrate against the Las Vegas Raiders during the fourth quarter at Allegiant Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The challenges the Los Angeles Rams faced in Sunday’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders were symbolic of their early season results. After jumping out to a 28-6 halftime lead, the Raiders scored 15-straight to start the fourth quarter. For most of the season, the Rams have lacked obvious leadership and execution. Falling to 2-5 would have put their playoff hopes on life support. Instead, Matthew Stafford, Tyler Higbee, and Blake Corum stepped up to stop the bleeding and keep LA on the path to victory. That is exactly what the Rams have been missing up to this point. Sunday’s win could be a sign they’ve dispelled their demons and are ready to become the team we expected them to be at the start of the year. But let’s not get ahead of ourselves. There is still much work to be done . Before we turn the corner, let’s review the individual performances that helped LA finish in the win column. Winners Kyren Williams & Blake Corum, RB Any time two running backs earn a spot on the “winners” list we should also credit the offensive line. The big guys up front cleared running lanes for Williams and Corum. They also protected Stafford well in what might have been the quarterback’s most efficient game of the season. Corum received the bulk of the work, even though the box score reflects a relatively even split. Williams received a handful of carries at the end of the game that brought the workload closer to 50/50. Williams: 16 rushes for 99 yards (6.2 avg), 1 TD, 1 fumble lost; two catches for 22 yards Corum: 17 rushes for 93 yards (5.5 avg), 1 TD; one catch for eight yards With Davante Adams expected to miss significant time, it was clear the Rams needed to renew their commitment to the run game. Fans knew that. The Raiders knew that. The duo were still effective even if the outcome was predictable. Credit to them. Kyren Williams extends the lead for the Rams 💪 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F2PBZOlOQf — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Colby Parkinson & Davis Allen, TE Speaking of Adams, it was unclear who would step up in the receiver’s absence. The Rams lack depth at receiver. It makes sense that the team attempted to replace Adams in the aggregate from the tight end position. Colby Parkinson finished with five catches for 48 yards. That’s close enough to Adams usual output in a game where Puka Nacua is healthy, although the tight end was held out of the end zone. And the Rams also found ways to replace Adams’ touchdown production. Davis Allen caught four passes for 20 yards and found the end zone twice. Both outcomes are encouraging, and Terrance Ferguson should be nearing a return to health if the Rams can keep their playoff hopes alive long enough. Make that TWO touchdowns for Davis Allen on National Tight Ends Day 🔥 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7Vs3QenCPQ — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Shaun Dolac, MLB I don’t like pouring salt on the wound in light of an injury. However, second-year linebacker Shaun Dolac may actually be an upgrade over entrenched starter Nate Landman. Dolac was reliable in run defense and stingy in coverage. Most importantly, you didn’t really notice him on the end of negative plays. Landman usually finds himself on the opposite end of that spectrum. Jaylen Watson, CB Tre Tucker is Vegas’ receiver that is primed for the big play. He poked through for a 41-yard touchdown in the second half. LA kept him bottled up in the first half and for most of the game, especially when Kirk Cousins and company needed to score late. Jaylen Watson deserves credit for locking Tucker down in the first half. The result was often an incomplete pass was Cousins looked Tucker’s direction with Watson in coverage. Matthew Stafford, QB Stafford won’t be proud of his box score in this game. He finished with 23 completions on 29 passes (79.3%) with 195 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception. The Rams allowed only a single sack, which came on the opening drive. But this was the most accurate and efficient performance we’ve seen from Stafford on the season yet. The short passing game isn’t his or Sean McVay’s bread and butter. They want to kill you with a deep shot rather than death by a thousand cuts. Stafford kept to the script, minimized mistakes, and made key plays when his team needed him to most. It was a winning performance by LA’s signal caller today. Puka Nacua adds six more to the board for the Rams 🐏 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CJMINNvBOA — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Losers Special teams (a weekly entry) Again the Rams allowed a long kickoff return to open the game. The Raiders averaged nearly 40 yards on two returns. They also operated at a 13 per clip in the punt return department. The Raiders also caught LA by surprise for a fourth down conversion. Punter AJ Cole completed a 13-yard pass that setup a score for Vegas. Former Rams coordinator Joe DeCamillis was the architect of the play. It’s fitting after McVay has seen his coordinators come and go through the revolving door in recent years. Maybe coordinators are not the main problem . New set of downs, brought to you by AJ Cole 🙌 #LARvsvLV | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/crJSfyl69f — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) October 25, 2026 Josaiah Stewart & Wesley Bailey, EDGE Myles Garrett cannot return fast enough. The defense is treading water and holding up in bend-don’t-break fashion. They don’t yet feel lethal. The main reason for this is the lack of consistent production from the EDGE rushers who are playing in place of Garrett: Stewart and Bailey. Stewart is usually sound in run defense. He missed multiple assignments Sunday. The Rams also asked him to drop into coverage often, which is probably a telling sign about his pass rushing prowess. Does the coaching staff feel that they are better bringing a blitzer and dropping Stewart in their place? It’s a possible explanation. And Bailey was fine in run defense but he offers very little upside as a pass rusher. I don’t follow why he’s ahead of Desjuan Johnson on the depth chart. Both are strong run defenders. Johnson should offer more in the pass game. The Rams sacked Cousins only once while Vegas has an open competition on their offensive line. Not great.

title: Rams-Raiders takeaways: Sean McVay finally leans into run game
summary: The Los Angeles Rams entered their Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders needing a convincing performance to regain momentum, and the result offered plenty to evaluate on both sides of the football. From Stafford’s command of the offense to the ground game’s effectiveness and the defense’s ability to control the Raiders in the […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams entered their Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders needing a convincing performance to regain momentum, and the result offered plenty to evaluate on both sides of the football. From Stafford’s command of the offense to the ground game’s effectiveness and the defense’s ability to control the Raiders in the first half, here are the biggest takeaways from the Rams’ Week 7 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . 1st Down: Matthew Stafford is now Rams all time TD leader Stafford’s three touchdowns in the first half officially made him the all-time passing touchdown leader for the Rams franchise. Stafford’s record breaking moment puts in a category of his own. He is now first all-time for both the Lions and Rams organizations. His 156 touchdown passes surpassed Roman Gabriel, who played 11 years with the Rams from 1962-1972. 🚨 NFL HISTORY Matthew Stafford is the FIRST quarterback in NFL history to hold the all-time passing touchdown record for TWO different franchise! Detroit Lions- 282 Los Angeles Rams- 155 pic.twitter.com/cgzSKxkZMU — Novig (@Novig) October 25, 2026 2nd Down: Rams lean into run game Through the first six weeks of the season, Los Angeles was throwing the ball about 65% of the time. The game plan was different this Sunday as Kyren Williams and Blake Corum were given 33 rushing attempts and worked that to the tune of 192 rushing yards. It was a huge effort to get the ground game going and make the LA offense multi-dimensional again. Rams offense with a casual 75% success rate on offense against the Raiders. If it holds, that’s the highest success rate by any team since 2016 ( @NextGenStats era) — Asa (@AsaArnold4) October 25, 2026 3rd Down: Rams 3 tight ends come up big The Rams trio of tight ends combined for 11 receptions, 82 receiving yards, and two touchdowns. Colby Parkinson led the group with 5 receptions and 48 yards. Davis Allen collected the first two touchdowns and nearly added a third. As for Higbee, he hauled in a huge third down conversion to prevent any thought of a Raiders comeback. What a throw by Matthew Stafford and catch by Tyler Higbee 🔥 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6p15WoLfO0 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 4th Down: Defense was good enough In the first half, the defense was stout. The interior defensive line was a stout despite being without Kobie Turner and Poona Ford. Aaron Donald, Ty Hamilton, and Braden Fiske held the Raiders to 48 rushing yards on 17 rushing attempts (2.8 per attempt). The secondary forced multiple incompletions including three 4th down stops. Things got a little dicey because of some sloppiness on the offensive side and putting the defense in short fields. Despite being without 4 defensive starters, the Rams defense got the job done with a few backups like Shaun Dolac and Emmanuel Forbes being good enough in the win.

title: Rams beat Raiders: 5 key plays that led to L.A.’s win
summary: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Las Vegas Raiders 35-21 on Sunday, getting back into the win column and keeping hope alive in the NFC playoff race with plenty of time left in the season. Despite getting hit with a wave of recent injuries, the Rams could get back Myles Garrett soon and in time […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Las Vegas Raiders 35-21 on Sunday , getting back into the win column and keeping hope alive in the NFC playoff race with plenty of time left in the season. Despite getting hit with a wave of recent injuries, the Rams could get back Myles Garrett soon and in time for one more push in the NFC West. Week 7’s matchup against the Raiders featured several pivotal moments that helped shape the outcome of the game. While the final score tells part of the story, the pivotal moments throughout the afternoon help explain how Los Angeles built its advantage and managed the Raiders’ attempts to respond. Here are the five key plays that defined the Rams’ Week 7 win against Las Vegas . 1. Stafford connects with Nacua for 11 yard Touchdown Matthew Stafford’s third touchdown of the day went to Puka Nacua, giving LA a 21-3 lead. It was a fantastic job by Puka to come back to the ball, giving himself momentum to cut up the middle of the field and find the end zone. Often times, wide receivers left the ball travel to them as opposed to working back to the football. Matthew Stafford finds Puka Nacua for an 11-yard touchdown! It's been all Rams in the first half! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/0FCTsJ4PGQ — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) October 25, 2026 2. Emmanuel Forbes collects PBU on 4th & 3 Normally, Forbes finds himself on the unfortunate end of some big plays. But this time, he was the responsible party for a huge pass break up on 4th & 3 from the LAR 48. Forbes went around the top of Cody White to knock the ball away and give Los Angeles great field position. LA turned the turnover on downs into 7 points… Great coverage by Emmanuel Forbes Jr. 👏 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fHpuq5XfJX — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 3. Kyren Williams scores 17 yard Touchdown Kyren Williams capped off a dominant first-half performance with a 17-yard touchdown run against the Las Vegas Raiders, extending the Rams’ lead to 28–6 with 1:19 remaining in the second quarter. On 2nd & 7, Williams took a pitch from Stafford around the left end and broke a tackle to hit paydirt. The pitch and the spin for six! 📺 @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/CUeovtoJfl — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 25, 2026 4a. Defense gets 4th & 2 stop The Raiders offense managed to drive the ball a little bit more effectively in the second half but LA’s defense came up with a big stop. Kirk Cousins tried to find Cody White in the endzone but the Rams coverage in the secondary was sticky. 4b. Defense gets 4th & 5 stop On the next Raiders drive, the Raiders got to the Rams 25 yard line and elected to go for it to try and stay in the game. While Kirk Cousins had Nailor open toward the sideline, the pass was a little long and Nailor couldn’t keep control of the football as he went to the ground, resulting in an incomplete pass and another turnover on downs. 5. Higbee’s leaping grab on 3rd & 2 to move chains After momentum swung in favor of Las Vegas, the Rams had to put together a drive to put the game on ice. On 3rd & 2 from LA’s 43, Higbee’s made a leaping grab from a Matthew Stafford bullet. Higbee has made a habit this year of being one of Stafford’s go-to guys when the offense needs a play. What a throw by Matthew Stafford and catch by Tyler Higbee 🔥 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6p15WoLfO0 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026

title: Rams vs. Raiders final score: L.A. pulls back into playoff race
summary: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Las Vegas Raiders 35-21 on Sunday, as Matthew Stafford threw three touchdowns and climbed back into the NFC West race at 3-4. Sean McVay and defensive coordinator Chris Shula dialed up a great gameplan for both sides of the ball that the players executed, for the most part. With […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams beat the Las Vegas Raiders 35-21 on Sunday, as Matthew Stafford threw three touchdowns and climbed back into the NFC West race at 3-4. Sean McVay and defensive coordinator Chris Shula dialed up a great gameplan for both sides of the ball that the players executed, for the most part. With the San Francisco 49ers losing to the Atlanta Falcons and dropping to 6-1, not all hope is lost. The Rams dominated the Raiders for stretches of this contest, but there were real mistakes made by L.A. as the final score doesn’t tell the whole story. Self-inflicted wounds like poor special teams play, turnovers, penalties and an inability to put games away have been the story of the Rams in 2026 more often than not, and each of those negative trends showed up in Week 7, but unlike the last couple weeks, the Rams found a way to win. Credit the Raiders for hanging around, playing tough and fighting despite being down throughout the match, but the Rams gave the Raiders chances because the Rams made mistakes. The Rams jumped out to a hot start and took a 28-6 lead into halftime with Stafford throwing three passing touchdowns, and Kyren Williams adding another score on the ground. The Rams set themselves up to take control with a dominant first half, but the second half was a bit shaky as the Rams struggled greatly in the third quarter and parts of the fourth. The mistakes The Raiders converted a fake punt in the third quarter to keep a drive alive as the Rams continue to be out-played in the third phase of the game. L.A.’s defense held strong. New set of downs, brought to you by AJ Cole 🙌 #LARvsvLV | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/crJSfyl69f — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) October 25, 2026 Later on, Williams fumbled setting the Raiders up for points off the turnover. L.A.’s defense contined to hold strong after the fumble and forced the Raiders to a turnover on downs. On the Rams next offensive drive, Blake Corum was given some carries after the Williams fumble, and Corum was able to take a run to the house, but it was called back due to a facemask penalty on L.A. The Rams were forced to punt a few plays later. In the fourth quarter, Stafford threw an interception when Colby Parkinson popped the intended pass in the air as the Rams continued to get in their own way. HouDEANi 🪄 #LARvsLV | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/Usq1etAyG1 — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) October 25, 2026 The Rams had chance after chance to put this game away, and they failed to do so as the Raiders kept the pressure on. The victory Now, the Rams did pull away in the end as Corum capped off the offensive day with a rushing score of his own late in the game. The Rams did enough, they won, but it was closer than it needed to be as this Rams team continues to be far less dominant than expected going into 2026. Blake walks it in for 6! 📺 @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/mLCPw4ZC1s — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 25, 2026 Headed home with the W. pic.twitter.com/MzkMKikel0 — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 25, 2026 The Rams won in Week 7, but the same old mistakes, the penalties, the turnovers, the weak special teams play, those were all on display. The Rams will try to continue to and clean up their act in Week 8 when they take on another struggling franchise, the Los Angeles Chargers.

One development working in their favor: receiver Puka Nacua is active after injuring his calf in Thursday’s practice. We know […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams runs after a catch against Kalen King #35 of the Arizona Cardinals in the fourth quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have their backs against the wall on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. LA is in danger of falling to 2-5 and effectively out of playoff contention with a road loss. One development working in their favor: receiver Puka Nacua is active after injuring his calf in Thursday’s practice. We know the defense will be short-handed. They are missing Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, Trent McDuffie, and Nate Landman this week and in some cases much longer. While the Rams defense has been the strongest unit on this team, the tables must reverse moving forward if LA is going to get the season back on track. That starts with Matthew Stafford and company. All five starters on the offensive line are healthy for the Vegas contest. While Davante Adams is out for the foreseeable future, there is still sufficient firepower with Nacua and a deep cast of tight ends. Blake Corum and Kyren Williams should see a heavy workload on the ground. There are no excuses. The Rams have enough talent on offense to come out with a win and offset the defensive losses. But an encouraging offensive performance requires a step forward from their season baseline. Their usual won’t be good enough to take down Kirk Cousins and the Raiders. LA is average in most offensive rankings: 10th in EPA/play 9th in success rate 15th in explosive play rate 16th in points per drive 13th in red zone efficiency 20th in offensive turnovers Stafford and the Rams offense don’t look like their usual selves. It’s difficult to put a finger on the exact root cause. But you can usually count on Stafford to pull it together when his back against the wall. It’s not only the playoffs; Stafford is playing for his job. Stafford’s tenure with the Rams draws nearer to a close with each loss. Rookie first-round pick Ty Simpson would reasonably start once LA is out of playoff contention. The Rams need to keep winning to make the playoffs. Stafford needs to keep winning in order to save his job. Will LA take care of business in Vegas?

title: Puka Nacua expected to play vs. Raiders
summary: The Los Angeles Rams appear poised to have Puka Nacua available for their Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders despite the star wide receiver suffering a minor calf injury during Thursday’s practice. While the injury raised some concerns heading into the weekend, Nacua is expected to suit up, giving Matthew Stafford and the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 12: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams appear poised to have Puka Nacua available for their Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders despite the star wide receiver suffering a minor calf injury during Thursday’s practice. While the injury raised some concerns heading into the weekend, Nacua is expected to suit up, giving Matthew Stafford and the Rams offense a significant boost as they look to get back on track. Nacua’s injury status headed into today is questionable. Rams are optimistic that WR Puka Nacua, who is questionable for Sunday’s game due to a calf injury, will play vs. the Raiders. Nacua was feeling better Saturday and, as one source said, “as long as there aren’t any setbacks, we feel good about him being available to play.” pic.twitter.com/mI22MZNcCj — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 25, 2026 Nacua’s availability is especially important given the injuries he has already dealt with throughout the 2026 season. The third-year receiver has been a central figure in Los Angeles’ passing attack, and keeping him healthy will be critical as the Rams navigate the middle portion of their schedule. The latest calf issue is another reminder of the physical toll Nacua has endured this season. Although the injury is reportedly minor, any setback involving one of the team’s most important offensive players warrants attention, particularly with the Rams needing consistency from their passing game. Nacua previously battled a groin injury that forced him to miss Weeks 2 and 3. His absence during that stretch left Los Angeles without one of its most productive and dependable receiving options, putting additional pressure on Stafford and the rest of the receiving corps to compensate. That importance becomes even greater with Davante Adams placed on injured reserve and expected to miss 6-10 weeks with a ruptured hamstring. The Rams need their receiving group to remain productive, and having Nacua available would provide some much-needed stability as Los Angeles prepares to face Las Vegas. Still, the Rams will need to monitor Nacua’s condition closely. Even if he plays Sunday, managing his workload and ensuring the calf injury does not become a longer-term concern will be worth watching. For now, the expectation is that Nacua will be on the field against the Raiders.

title: Will Byron Young get a sack (or two) against Raiders?
summary: Will Byron Young have a massive game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday? Young has been a good player for the Los Angeles Rams, he’s been great at times, but this year the defense isn’t generating enough sacks. That includes Young. The team is getting pressure, but the defense and Young need to finish […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 20: Gardner Minshew #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders runs with the ball from Byron Young #0 of the Los Angeles Rams during the fourth quarter at SoFi Stadium on October 20, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Joe Scarnici/Getty Images) | Getty Images Will Byron Young have a massive game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday? Young has been a good player for the Los Angeles Rams, he’s been great at times, but this year the defense isn’t generating enough sacks. That includes Young. The team is getting pressure, but the defense and Young need to finish with sacks. Pressures aren’t enough against the best quarterbacks in the league. It’s been a theme for 2026 that this Rams team is good some important areas. They are generating yards, they are holding teams out of the endzone, there are positive in this 2-4 season. But the Rams aren’t scoring enough points to win, and the defense isn’t making the key stops at the end of games. The special teams are a mess. So, can the Rams get right on Sunday? Young having a big game would help. 3 Bold Predictions in the Los Angeles Rams’ Showdown With Kirk Cousins and the Raiders (athlonsports) “ Los Angeles Rams fans will make the drive up I-15 this weekend for a team that badly needs a road win. The Rams are 2-4 after an 18-16 loss to Arizona, they’ve lost Davante Adams for six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, and Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders are waiting at Allegiant Stadium. Sean McVay has said the Rams’ depth can handle it for now. Byron Young sacks Kirk Cousins twice Byron Young has 29 pressures, sixth among 115 edge defenders, and his 22 hurries lead the position, according to PFF . He has only four sacks, though, and the Rams have just eight as a team despite one of the league’s best pressure rates. They turn pressure into sacks just under 10% of the time, second-worst in the NFL , and we called the pressure-to-sack gap the first fix before Cousins this week.“ Top Rams News: Previews and predictions for Rams at Raiders on Sunday in Las Vegas for Week 7 (therams.com) “Here’s a collection of analysts’ predictions and previews for Rams-Raiders: Nine of the 11 ESPN experts chose the Rams to come out on top on Sunday against the Raiders. Picks for every game can be viewed here . Three of the five NFL.com analysts picked the Rams to beat the Raiders. All their picks are here . Six of the eight Sports Illustrated staffers picked the Rams to win against the Raiders. All of their Week 7 predictions can be seen here .“ Lawrence McCutcheon Dies at 76 After Parkinson’s Diagnosis, Rams Legend Made 5 Pro Bowls (bleacherreport) “Former Los Angeles Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon, a five-time Pro Bowler who amassed four 1,000-yard seasons, has died at the age of 76 after a lengthy battle with Parkinson’s disease. The McCutcheon family revealed news of his passing via a statement, which the Rams shared on Friday.“ Rams’ defensive front shuffling ahead of Raiders matchup (ocregister) “But the Rams will have to rely on players like Tyler Davis and Larrell Murchison to play bigger roles this week and into the future. “Definitely felt terrible,” Davis said of when he learned about Turner and Ford’s injuries. “But also just wanted to get in the mindset just step up for my guys, for real.” For Davis, whose role has grown with the Rams over the past two-plus years, he will try to keep things to his usual process, not changing the way he studies or prepares even with more snaps coming his way. “Just focus on our core four and then having the right mindset to go out there and execute, play throughout the full down and fall in love with the process of it,” Davis said with a tablet playing practice tape on his lap. “Just get to it.” Rams have a prime chance to get the run game in rhythm vs. Raiders (ramblinfan) “Not only does McVay need to get Williams in rhythm, Blake Corum finally showed signs of life as well last week. His nine carries for 42 yards made for his best rushing performance since Week 2 versus the Giants. For the Rams’ run game to really get going, both Williams and Corum need to be effective. Williams only carried 10 times against Arizona, for 50 yards. He has 393 rushing yards on the season, on 4.9 yards per carry, plus 217 yards receiving. The Rams don’t need to force-feed Williams on the ground if Corum is also productive, but they should look to get him touches one way or another. His 13 touches in Week 6 were his fewest of the season.“ 3 Critical Matchups the Rams Must Win vs. Raiders to Avoid Falling to 2-5 (si.com) “The Los Angeles Rams are set to play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7. This will be a must-win game for the Rams as they look to avoid a 2-5 start. While the Raiders may have been seen as a guaranteed win in recent years, that’s not the case this season. The Raiders have played well and nothing is guaranteed with this Rams team. Let’s dive into the three biggest matchups to watch. RT Warren McClendon Jr. vs. EDGE Maxx Crosby For the most part, Warren McClendon stepped in well for an injured Rob Havenstein. So much so that when Havenstein was healthy at the end of the year, the Rams simply stayed with McClendon and then didn’t draft a replacement when they could have in the first round. However, there were signs that McClendon may not be what the Rams needed when he allowed 11 pressures over three playoff games, including five against the Carolina Panthers and four against the Seattle Seahawks.“ 3 causes for concern for Raiders Week 7 vs Rams (sports.yahoo) “3. Raiders banged up running back room Speaking of running back duos. The Raiders are on the other end of the spectrum in terms of their running attack this season. They were already 31st in the league in terms of yards per attempt (3.0). Much of that has been due to Ashton Jeanty not being quite himself while fighting through ankle and foot injuries. Now backup Mike Washington Jr is also hurt. The rookie back showed up on the injury report this week with foot and back injuries, causing him to miss Friday’s practice and be Questionable for the game. With Jeanty averaging under 2.5 yards per carry the past couple weeks, the Raiders really need to Washington as the change-up.“ Vegas, baby, Vegas! Why the Rams’ season could go bust in Sin City (nypost) “Because what began as a season filled with Super Bowl aspirations has become a five-alarm fire, and the team that dreamed of playing for a Lombardi Trophy in its own stadium might need a miracle just to escape the NFC West basement . After consecutive home losses, including Sunday’s humiliating 18-16 defeat to the previously 1-4 Arizona Cardinals, the Rams (2-4) head to Allegiant Stadium for a Week 7 showdown against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3).“ Rams’ 5 keys to victory vs. Raiders on Sunday (ramswire) “Do not let the Raiders isolate Quentin Lake or Jaylen McCollough on Bowers, and bait Las Vegas into throwing the out route. They always look for it; setting it up will give a defender inside leverage to stop those attacks, and Cousins throws it blindly. Regardless, if the Rams stop Bowers, their offense should do enough to win.“ Rams need a new kind of offense to overcome injuries and mend inconsistency (ramblinfan) “New injuries have lengthened the growing list of benched veterans. Kicker Blake Grupe and nose tackle Poona Ford are now out for the season . Entering Week 7, LA has eight players from the 53-man roster on injured reserve. But injuries continue to occur. Right now, the casualty count has reached nearly a dozen. For a team trying to turn the corner, injuries create unwanted uncertainty. The Rams’ struggling run defense will be strained to its limits without Ford and Landman. They will face the Las Vegas Raiders also without defensive tackle Kobie Turner, one of the recent IR additions. The offense could be without its top two receivers. LA has already targeted Nacua and Adams more than 100 times this season; their joint absence would force…

summary: With a 3-0 start to the season, the Las Vegas Raiders looked like a potential postseason sleeper. However, the Week 7 35-21 loss to the Los Angeles Rams makes it four in a row for the Silver and Black, dropping the Raiders’ record to 3-4. That results in Las Vegas’ playoff hopes sliding as we […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images With a 3-0 start to the season, the Las Vegas Raiders looked like a potential postseason sleeper. However, the Week 7 35-21 loss to the Los Angeles Rams makes it four in a row for the Silver and Black, dropping the Raiders’ record to 3-4 . That results in Las Vegas’ playoff hopes sliding as we take a look at the updated AFC playoff picture. AFC playoff standings 1. Kansas City Chiefs (5-1, 5-0 AFC for tiebreaker over BUF) 2. Buffalo Bills (5-1, 3-1 AFC) 3. Cleveland Browns (5-2, win over PIT for AFC North lead) 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) 5. Denver Broncos (5-2, 2-1 AFC for 1st Wild Card spot tiebreaker) 6. Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2, loss to CLE, 2-2 AFC) 7. Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) 8. New England Patriots (4-3, 4-1 AFC for tiebreaker over BAL) 9. Baltimore Ravens (4-3, 2-2 AFC) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) 11. New York Jets (2-5, 2-2 AFC for tiebreaker over IND) 12. Indianapolis Colts (2-5, win over HOU, 1-4 AFC) 13. Houston Texans (2-5, loss to IND) 14. Miami Dolphins (1-5) 15. Tennessee Titans (1-6) 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) So, as it stands, the Raiders’ best chance at earning a playoff spot is for the third and final AFC Wild Card spot. They’re a game-and-a-half behind the Bengals for the seventh seed, and one game behind the Patriots and the Ravens. However, New England owns the tiebreaker over Las Vegas with the head-to-head win, so the Raiders are really a game-and-a-half behind the Patriots too. The Raiders head to the Jets next week for what feels like as close to a midseason elimination game as possible for both teams. Meanwhile, the Bengals host the Titans, New England is at Miami, and the Ravens are on the road against the Bills.

title: Raiders-Rams:16 things we learned
summary: The joy of the Las Vegas Raiders strong start to the 2026 season is over. The season is not lost, but things have to change. Sunday, the Las Vegas Raiders suffered a tough lose, a 35-21 defeat to the undermanned Los Angeles Rams at home. Don’t be fooled by the two-possession final score. The Rams […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The joy of the Las Vegas Raiders strong start to the 2026 season is over. The season is not lost, but things have to change. Sunday, the Las Vegas Raiders suffered a tough lose , a 35-21 defeat to the undermanned Los Angeles Rams at home. Don’t be fooled by the two-possession final score. The Rams led 28-6 at halftime after scoring touchdowns on four straight series. They took their foot off the pedal in the second half. According to the Associated Press, this was the Raiders’ worst deficit at halftime at home since Week 1 of the 2015 season when they trailed the Cincinnati Bengals 24-0. Despite playing without the likes of Myles Garrett, Poona Ford, Kobie Turner, Davante Adams, Nate Landman and Trent McDuffie, the Rams, who were a disappointing 2-4 going into the game, looked like the Super Bowl contenders they were supposed to be against the Raiders. Some have been holding onto the fact that the Raiders, have been competitive during this four-game losing streak. But this wasn’t a competitive game. The Raiders are lacking on both sides of the ball. There are worry spots such as the run game on both sides of the ball and in the red-zone on both sides of the ball. First-year coach Klint Kubiak acknowledged he has a lot to fix moving forward. The Raiders, who won their three games against losing teams, play at the 2-5 New York Jets on Sunday. If they can’t beat Geno Smith, this season will be on life support. Let’s look at the key aspects of this game: Defense is gutted: Rob Leonard’s unit isn’t getting it done. The Raiders have allowed 170 points in the past five games. According to the Associated Press, this ties a franchise record for allowing, at least, 27 points in five straight games and they have also allowed, at least, 30 points in four straight games. The Rams ran for 199 yards and made it look easy. The Rams were five-for-five in the red zone. The Raiders have allowed touchdowns in eight of 10 opponents’ trips to the red zone in the past two games. Mendoza talk: Kubiak raised some eyebrows when asked after the game if he is thinking about replacing quarterback Kirk Cousins with rookie Fernando Mendoza. Kubiak gave a long answer in which he said he thinks the team has to think about everything. But he was mentioning other problems. So, while it could be possible, it seems like Kubiak knows the Raiders’ problems run deeper than the quarterback. The Raiders’ offense threw 44 time sand ran 17 times. Kubiak knows that must change. Still can’t run the ball: Another game and another poor performance in the running game. The Raiders had 48 rushing yards. Starter Ashton Jeanty’s troubles have extend on the ground. He had 15 yards on eight carries. This is a major issue. Red zone woes continue: The Raiders couldn’t convert on fourth down in the red zone on two straight drives in third quarter. They were one of five in the red zone and are 3 of 10 in the past two games. It’s a problem. Rogers keeps job: Second-year guard Caleb Rogers was in the starting lineup for the second straight week as he continued to replace the benched Jackson Powers-Johnson. Impact in passing game: Jeanty scored his eighth career touchdown pass. It’s the most by any running back in the NFL since the start of last season. It’s the most receiving touchdowns by a running back in their first two seasons in franchise history. He had eight catches for 61 yards. Tucker strikes again: Raiders’ wide receiver Tre Tucker had a 41-yard catch in the third quarter. It was his fourth pass play of 40 plus yards this season, which is tied for the NFL lead. It’s a fake: On their first drive of the third quarter, the Raiders ran a fake punt on fourth and five from their 30. Punter A.J. Cole hit Connor Heyward for a 13-yard gain. It was a pretty play, but the Raiders didn’t score on the drive. Ugly home stat: According to the Associated Press, the Raiders trailed by double digits at home Sunday for the 29th time in 55 games at Allegiant Stadium. That is the second most by a home team since 2020. The lowly New York Jets have done that 31 times. Better in third quarter: The Raiders entered the game being outscored by 26 points in the third quarter. Neither team scored in the third quarter Sunday. The Raiders did score to open the fourth quarter. QB sneak: After suffering with the Heyward Tush Push this season, the Raiders had Cousins sneak on third and short in the first quarter. CB rotation: Darien Porter started at an outside position again, but rookie Zeke Masses did rotate in and replace him some. Laube is a weapon: Raiders’ kick returner Dylan Laube had kick returns of 38 and 42 yards in the first quarter. He is a leading returner in the league. Change of plans: The Raiders won the coin toss an expect to receive the ball. They had been deferring to the second half in previous games they won the coin toss. It didn’t work as they went three and out to start the game. Defensive tackle shuffle: The Raiders inactivated veteran defensive tackles Thomas Booker and Jonah Laulu. J.J Pegues and practice squad elevation Tim Keenan were actvie. Slone sits again: For the second straight game, the Raiders elevated rookie pass-rusher Cian Slone from the practice squad only to inactivate him. He can be elevated form the practice squad just once more this season.

The Rams, who were missing several key players, hammered the Raiders. Turning point of the game: The Rams scored touchdowns on four straight series in the first half handled 28-6 at halftime. Injury report: Reserve tight end Ian Thomas hurt his shoulder. He did return to the game. Reserve defensive end Patrick Johnson had a stinger in the fourth quarter. title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 7 win over the New York Jets
summary: I guess the Dolphins’ bye week came at just the right time! On Sunday, on the road against the New York Jets, the Miami Dolphins earned their first victory of the year — the first victory of head coach Jeff Hafley’s tenure with the team — by downing their AFC East rivals by a score […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins and Caleb Douglas #7 of the Miami Dolphins look on after their win against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images I guess the Dolphins’ bye week came at just the right time! On Sunday, on the road against the New York Jets, the Miami Dolphins earned their first victory of the year — the first victory of head coach Jeff Hafley’s tenure with the team — by downing their AFC East rivals by a score of 28-25. After a hot start allowed Miami to take a 21-7 halftime lead, the team cooled on both offense and defense in the second half, but held on by the skin of their teeth — sealing the victory with a 4th and 1 tush-push by quarterback Malik Willis with less than two minutes on the clock. No, it wasn’t a perfect game from the Dolphins, but the squad did enough to earn the hard-fought win — and maybe enough to convince a frustrated fanbase that patience is the right approach when it comes to letting Miami’s new regime build a successful organization after being forced to tear it down to the screws this past offseason. GOOD Malik Willis has best game in Dolphins uniform For the first time this season, Dolphins fans have a legitimate reason to feel encouraged about quarterback Malik Willis. Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns without having a turnover. He also added 37 rushing yards and a touchdown with his legs, giving Miami’s offense another dimension that has largely been missing this year. Not a bad afternoon for a guy who entered the game with plenty of fans questioning his ability to lead this offense. Miami scored touchdowns on their first two offensive drives, with Willis connecting with rookie receiver Caleb Douglas for a 7 yard touchdown in the first quarter before the Dolphins extended their lead with a rushing touchdown from Ollie Gordon II on the next drive. Willis then capped a 91 yard scoring drive late in the first half by scrambling into the end zone for a two yard touchdown. Miami’s lone second-half touchdown game on a short throw to Douglas who would make a man miss before taking the rock to the house for a 63 yard score. There is still plenty of work to do, and one good performance against the Jets doesn’t suddenly anoint Willis the organization’s savior at quarterback, but he deserves credit for delivering a win in this one. For a team that has spent the first several weeks looking for something to build on, Willis finally gave Miami a performance worth celebrating. BAD Dolphins pass defense has rough afternoon The Dolphins have enough problems without helping opposing offenses discover their next star receiver. Unfortunately, Miami’s pass defense apparently decided to give Jets’ rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. a helping hand on Sunday. Cooper finished the game with 5 receptions for 115 yards and a touchdown, averaging a whopping 23 yards per catch. That’s the kind of production offensive coordinators dream about from their receivers, and the kind defensive coordinators spend the week trying to prevent. Cooper wasn’t the only New York pass catcher to find success either. Tight end Mason Taylor added 5 receptions for 62 yards and two touchdowns, while their running backs contributed nine catches for 79 yards. Quarterback Geno Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards and three touchdowns. Although Smith also threw an interception — good work, Michael Taaffe — his 77% completion rate illustrates just how comfortable New York was moving the football through the air all day long. Miami won the game, so nobody needs to spend the evening writing a eulogy for the entire secondary (fair self-burn), but allowing that kind of production against a subpar offense is concerning. If Miami wants to build on Sunday’s victory, their pass defense needs to do a much better job limiting explosive plays and preventing opposing receivers from turning routine opportunities into game-changing moments. UGLY Poor second-half nearly costs Miami game The Dolphins entered the locker room at halftime with a comfortable two touchdown lead. Then the second half happened. Miami was outscored 18-7 after halftime, allowing the Jets to turn what should have been a relatively stress-free afternoon into a 28-25 nail-biter. New York kept chipping away at the lead, and Miami struggled to maintain the offensive momentum it had established during the opening half of play. Douglas’ 63 yard touchdown reception helped Miami push its advantage to 28-17, but even that explosive play wasn’t enough to make the final minutes peaceful. The Jets continued to fight, and Miami’s inability to put the game away left the door open for a comeback. The box score tells the story of two very different halves. Miami had 231 yards of offense by halftime, but the second-half struggles — just 129 more offensive yards during the final two quarters — prevented the Dolphins from building on that production and putting the game beyond reach. The defense deserves some criticism here too. After allowing just 114 yards to the Jets’ offense in the first-half, Miami gave up 263 second-half yards to Geno Smith and company. No bueno, muchacho. We can credit the Dolphins for hanging on and getting the win. Winning a close game requires making plays when they matter, and Miami did enough to survive. But Sunday’s game was also a reminder that a two touchdown lead isn’t necessarily safe when your offense stops moving the football and your defense starts giving up explosive plays. ___ The Dolphins have plenty of reasons to celebrate their first victory of 2026. They also have plenty of film to review before next week’s game. Still, they are no longer winless on the season, and head coach Jeff Hafley can finally breathe a sigh of relief in that regard. Do you think they can continue to build momentum with a victory against the visiting New England Patriots next week? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up !

title: Dolphins vs. Jets final score, immediate reactions, winners and losers as Miami gets first victory of 2026
summary: The Miami Dolphins entered Week 7 with a 0-5 record and looked like a team in a rebuild. Over the first five games, they showed flashes of success, but mistakes erased any gains. Facing the New York Jets after the bye week, Miami came out looking like a very different team. Miami scored on the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins reacts during the first quarter against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins entered Week 7 with a 0-5 record and looked like a team in a rebuild. Over the first five games, they showed flashes of success, but mistakes erased any gains. Facing the New York Jets after the bye week, Miami came out looking like a very different team. Miami scored on the opening drive, taking a lead for the first time this season. After the Jets tied the game on their first possession, Miami answered with a second first-quarter touchdown. They added another score in the second quarter, before battling through a lull in the third quarter only to open it back up in the fourth and put the game away. The Dolphins are still a team that is looking to establish their foundation and build for 2027 and beyond, but on Sunday, they looked much more like a team that can put together a full-game performance this season and, for the first time this season, they put a mark in the win column. Final Score Dolphins 28 – 25 Jets Immediate reactions Snap Winners and Losers Winners Greg Dulcich, tight end – On National Tight Ends Day, Dulcich came to play. He caught five passes for 87 yards in the first half. The Jets shut him down in the second half, but Dulcich’s first-half performance was the spark that started a fire for Miami’s offense. Malik Willis, quarterback – A lot has been said over the past couple of weeks about how Willis, in his first year as a starting quarterback, needs to play better. Just as much needs to be said this week about how well he played in this game. He was decisive. He was accurate. And he was not afraid to use his legs to make plays. He finished the game 14-for-21 for 208 yards, along with six runs for 39 yards. He had two passing touchdowns and a rushing score. Ollie Gordon II, running back – The Dolphins running game was supposed to stall out with the injury to De’Von Achane. Gordon has not just stepped up, but has flourished. Against the Jets, he carried the ball 25 times for 103 yards and a touchdown. He has been outstanding in Achane’s absence and Miami will continue to feed him the ball throughout the season. Losers Note: “Losers” is not a judgment on the talent or character of any individual. It is simply a categorization of the play in one game – no disrespect is intended or should be inferred. The Jets – They lost. That is pretty straightforward. I cannot wait to see the fall-off in the SB Nation Reacts fan confidence survey at Gang Green Nation this week. This was written off as an easy win for the Jets, only for everything to go Miami’s way. Immediate thoughts The bye week adjustments worked… What a difference from the team that headed into the bye week. Miami’s offense came out executing everything they wanted to do this week. Head coach Jeff Hafley said they would do self-scouting over the bye and figure out what adjustments they needed. He was not lying. Offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik called a great game. Quarterback Malik Willis was decisive. The first-half offense looked much better this week than at any point through the team’s first five games. Miami led 21-7 at the break and had gained 231 yards. …until the halftime break… The second half was a completely different story for the Dolphins’ offense. The came out of the break with a five-yard three-and-out, then a nine-play, 28 yard drive that ended with a punt, followed by another three-and-out, this time picking up two yards. Miami’s first three drives of the half averaged 2.9 yards per play. That won’t cut it. …only for Caleb Douglas to turn it around. Miami’s fourth possession of the second half began with a five-yard run from Gordon and a five-yard holding penalty against the Jets. Then Gordon picked up three more yards on a run. Miami looked like the struggles were continuing when Willis dropped back and was immediately under pressure, but he dumped the ball short to rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas, and Douglas tip-toed his way down the sideline for the 63-yard score. Miami’s lead was extended to 28-17 and the early second-half struggles were forgotten. It was not perfect, but it was enough The Dolphins jumped out to a lead, held on through a second-half salvo from the Jets, and then did enough to win. It was not always pretty, but when it was, it was gorgeous. There were issues at nearly every position group, but there was also greatness at nearly every position group. This is what Miami needs to expect every week – learn from the mistakes, make corrections, and keep moving forward.

summary: The Miami Dolphins return from their bye week today to face the New York Jets. It’s been a rough start to a complete rebuild, but has it been bad enough to shake […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Members of the Miami Dolphins celebrate a two-point conversion against the Cincinnati Bengals during the fourth quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins return from their bye week today to face the New York Jets. They continue to look for their first victory of the season, having lost each of their first five games before their off week. It’s been a rough start to a complete rebuild, but has it been bad enough to shake fans’ confidence in the team? According to FanDuel Sportsbook odds , the Dolphins have their best chance to pull off a win so far this year, with just a +3.5-point spread for today’s game. Dolphins fan confidence Our weekly SB Nation Reacts poll asks fans whether they are confident in the Dolphins’ direction. Heading into the bye, fan confidence fell from a season-high 87 percent positive responses to 71 percent. While that is still a really high mark, especially for a 0-5 team, a 16 percent drop is significant. Would the bye week change anything? No. Our poll, run through the bye week, held fairly steady, with 72 percent of the responses saying they are confident in Miami’s direction. Now facing the Jets in Week 7, will the fans continue to think the Dolphins are headed in a positive direction in the next edition of our poll? Miami Dolphins 2026 Season Fan Confidence Results: Preseason – 80% Week 1 – 79% Week 2 – 63% Week 3 – 65% Week 4 – 79% Week 5 – 87% Week 6 – 71% Week 7 – 72% Dolphins fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! Take Reacts surveys, create Dolphins polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Phinsider readers. Then discuss the results with other diehard Fins fans. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Bye week improvement We also asked this week what the biggest area of improvement for the Dolphins needs to be coming out of the bye week. In what is probably the least surprising result, 84 percent of fans said quarterback play needs to improve. Malik Willis, in his first year as a full-time starter, has struggled, as if he wants to find the perfect play rather than take the play the defense gives him. He has taken sacks he did not need to, forced passes into bad spots, and preferred to stay in the pocket rather than use his legs to gain yards. Will we see improvement following the self-scouting the team did during the bye week? The pass rush was second in the poll, receiving 12 percent of the vote. The Dolphins have four sacks this season, half of the league’s second-lowest total through Week 6. Miami’s four sacks came in one game, and no one has pulled down the opposing quarterback in four of Miami’s five games. That has to change if the Dolphins want any chance of success this year. The offensive line and the team’s health each received two percent of the vote. Do you agree with the Dolphins’ fan confidence poll results? Let us know in the comments.

Taylor has had four or more receptions only once this year, last week against the Patriots. The Dolphins have struggled to defend tight ends this year. I think Taylor will have opportunities, and I expect him to tally at least four catches.

title: Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets: Three Reasons Why
summary: The Miami Dolphins return to the playing field this week to face one of their biggest rivals: the New Yorks Jets.  For the first time this season, the Dolphins will face a team that doesn’t have a winning record or even a .500 record.  The Jets are a scrappy but bad team, just like the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 07: A fan looks on during the second half between the New York Jets and the Miami Dolphins at MetLife Stadium on December 07, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins return to the playing field this week to face one of their biggest rivals: the New Yorks Jets. For the first time this season, the Dolphins will face a team that doesn’t have a winning record or even a .500 record. The Jets are a scrappy but bad team, just like the Dolphins. They will have their own set of challenges for the boys in aqua and orange, so let’s get to it. 3 REASONS FOR HOPE REINFORCEMENTS MAY BE ON THE WAY The Dolphins got one of their key contributors back against the Bengals in week 5 in defensive tackle Kenneth Grant, though he only played 18 snaps. He will likely be ramped up in this contest. But the Dolphins may also be getting back their top receiver in Caleb Douglas as well as rookie safety Kyle Louis. Both players are practicing and may return to face the Jets . Douglas began the season as the go-to WR for Malik Willis but left in week 2 with an ankle injury. Even if he doesn’t get a ton of stats, his presence will force the Jets’ defense to play differently to account for him. He may be on a pitch count, but it will help the offense regardless. Louis is a bit of a different evaluation as he only played 3 snaps on the season before going on IR. He is also switching from being a college LB to an NFL safety. The Dolphins safety group is playing decent right now with fellow rookie Michael Taaffe and sophomore Dante Trader Jr. being the primary safety duo. But Louis will fill the role as a big nickel and has the athleticism and coverage skills to perhaps limit damage from the tight end position that seems to plague the Dolphins. THE RUN GAME SHOULD CONTINUE DRIVING THE ENGINE Ollie Gordon II is now leading the charge for the Dolphins run game. With NFL’s NextGenStats, OG2 is tied with the league’s leading rusher Kenneth Walker III for 2nd in efficiency . The efficiency stat measures how north/south a runner gets. OG2 barrels downhill quickly and runs with power. Right now, he is averaging 5 YPC, which is tied for 6th best. The Dolphins as a team are averaging 4.9 YPC, which is 5th best. The Dolphins also added rookie Kaytron Allen from Washington via the waiver wire. He is listed at 5’11”, 217 lbs. and profiles as another downhill, north/south, power rusher. He was acquired just before the Cincinnati game but has had 2 full weeks to get into the system. He will likely get some game action when also considering Jaylen Wright aggravated an injury against the Bengals. Even if he’s active, Wright may have limited touches. The Dolphins can lean on the two bruisers to power the run game and keep the chains moving regardless. The Jets are towards the bottom end of the league in rushing yards allowed, ranking 25th with 738 yards allowed. They are also middle of the pack in YPC allowed, ranking 19th with 4.4 YPC allowed. The Jets also haven’t faced a running threat at QB like Malik Willis. I’ve mentioned in other posts and comments several ways for the passing game to help Willis get into a rhythm and build confidence. But another way for the offense to stay in rhythm is for the QB to pick up some yards with his legs. This is a matchup that favors the Dolphins. THE DEFENSE CAN MAKE A STAND It often takes some time for a new defense to gel and start playing up to the expectation. It could take even longer with a defense with so much inexperience. Statistically, the Dolphins aren’t as bad as their record suggests. They are 21st in yards per play allowed. They are 16th in passing yards per game allowed. They are 16th in rushing yards per game allowed. They are 8th in YPC allowed. Of course, they have that pesky completion percentage allowed issue. But as we’ve seen in the 2 most recent games, the offenses are content to throw short for completions rather than try to push the ball downfield. Given the Jets’ personnel – TE heavy – they will probably stick to the same gameplan. Standout WR Garrett Wilson leads the team in targets, but his yards per reception is 11.9, which is indicative of heavier slot usage. However, they don’t have a combination of elite offensive talent and/or an elite QB. Geno Smith is playing better than expected and could present a problem. However, the Dolphins secondary is playing better than expected also. The 2 outside CBs are doing well in press coverage and Chris Johnson is improving in the slot. Miami’s edge group is heating up. Both Robinson and Uche are excelling in generating pressure when going 1-on-1 . Despite not having the sack numbers, Chop is one of the best in the league at generating pressure and generating it fast. The Jets are not a dominant offense. They are lower than Miami in yards per play. Their passing game, while better than Miami’s (everyone’s passing game is better except Tennessee), they still do not average more than 200 yards per game, ranked 23rd at 196.2. They aren’t a dominant rushing team either, ranking 23rd in total yards (567) and 26th in YPC (3.6). This plays right into Miami’s top ranked YPC allowed (3.7) so I would not expect the Jets to have a great day rushing. Altogether, the Dolphins defense has a chance to get some stops and give the offense a chance to get the ball back. 3 REASONS FOR CONCERN THE JETS PASS DEFENSE Even without the passing game issues for the Dolphins, the Jets present a problem for opposing passing attacks. The Jets overall allow only 4.8 yards per play, which is tied for 5th best. They allow 4.2 YPC on run defense, so it is shaky. But the passing defense is stout, allowing 185 yards per game, 4th best in the league. They have faced 3 teams in the top 10 in passing yards per game. Each was held well below their season averages. They are especially good at that in their building. In 2 homes games thus far, they’ve held Green Bay, who averages 269.3 passing yards per game to a measly 136 passing yards. They held the Browns, who average 173.5 passing yards per game to 102 passing yards. Green Bay pulled out a win in OT, but the Jets got a win over the Browns. The Jets are 9th in CP allowed at 61.5%. Not only that, but the Jets can dial up the pressure also. The Jets are 7th in sack percentage at 8.1%. They are 10th in pressure percentage at 24.3%. They are also 5th in blitz percentage at 36.0%. Former Packer Kingsley Enagbare is tied for 7th in pass rush win rate at 27% and rookie David Bailey is tied for 6th in the league with 5.0 sacks. A stout pass defense with a high blitz rate is bad news for Miami’s struggling passing game. The good news for the Dolphins’ offense is the Jets have allowed 130+ yards rushing in 3 of the last 4 games and none of those teams average more per carry than Miami. The Dolphins can likely do damage on the ground, but I would not expect this to be the “breakthrough” game for Malik Willis. In fact, the passing game may be uglier than ever this game. CURSE OF METLIFE STADIUM MetLife Stadium has seemingly been cursed for players to be injured. It’s a tough road environment, despite the MetLife Takeover. But the field surface is always a major concern. Just because the Dolphins aren’t contending this season doesn’t mean potential injuries aren’t bad. Just like with any team, the Dolphins can ill afford major injuries. Maybe not for the win column aspect, but with the developmental arc of most of this team. Maybe I’m overly concerned about this, but that stadium and field scare me in this regard. Praying for good health for the players over anything else. ON THE ROAD AGAIN The Dolphins will have their 4th road game in 6 contests. That in and of itself is tough. Add in the struggling offense, hit-or-miss defense, and the divisional aspect, and this will be a rough go for the Dolphins. The Jets are 2-4 and just lost a division game against the Pats. The Pats will go on the…

title: Week 7 Vikings Stock Market Report
summary: The Minnesota Vikings extended their unbeaten streak to six games, beating a struggling Indianapolis Colts team 16-10 with a familiar if frustrating formula: conservative, ball control offense, efficient special teams and a dominant defense. There were a couple cracks in the later two phases as the Vikings had a field goal blocked and the defense […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Blake Cashman #51 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates after a play during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game against the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings extended their unbeaten streak to six games, beating a struggling Indianapolis Colts team 16-10 with a familiar if frustrating formula: conservative, ball control offense, efficient special teams and a dominant defense. There were a couple cracks in the later two phases as the Vikings had a field goal blocked and the defense allowed an explosive 38-yard run for the Colts’ only touchdown. And the Vikings offense was not able to take advantage of a struggling Colts defense. A variety of errors resulted in stalled drives. Not being able to convert 3rd and 4th and one, dropped passes or slightly inaccurate passes also killed a few drives, as did a holding penalty that negated what would have been a first and goal at the 3-yard line on an explosive pass to Jordan Addison. But the offense also did not turnover the ball, and tying or winning the turnover battle has given the Vikings a 90% win rate in the Kevin O’Connell era and sure enough, the Vikings won again. But an offense that finally had all its starting skill players on the field still failed to shift into a higher gear. That continues to be the most troubling aspect of the Vikings undefeated streak, particularly as the Vikings haven’t faced particularly strong defenses. With that, here is this week’s stock market report. Stock Up Blake Cashman. He was all over the field against the Colts, racking up 6 pressures including 2 sacks, 3 pass break ups in coverage, and 12 tackles according to preliminary PFF tracking. That was probably his most complete game as a Viking. Harrison Smith. He picked off his 40th pass of his career and joined Hall of Famers Ronde Barber and Charles Woodson as the only players in NFL history to accomplish the feat along with 20 sacks. He also recorded a sack and was solid in run defense as well. Jauan Jennings. There were signs of life from Jennings as part of the Vikings offense. He had two receptions for 34 yards and a shot at a difficult catch for a touchdown that he wasn’t able to make, but overall some improvement for Jennings and his getting more involved in the Vikings passing game. Kyle Van Noy. He is the highest PFF-graded edge rusher for the Vikings this season, largely based on run defense. He’s been an invaluable addition and contributor who’s helped tighten up the defense at key moments. Stock Down Aaron Jones. He looked like a nearly 32-year old back overworked the past four games. Outside of one toss run later in the game, everything looked tough for Jones, who averaged just 3.3 yards per carry. He just isn’t able to force any missed tackles. Buy A patient, conservative, ball control approach as the Vikings offense tries to ramp things up. Sell How long it’s taking for the Vikings offense to ramp up. Buy The Vikings defense’s ability to make plays when needed. Sell The Vikings offense’s ability to do the same. The Vikings travel to Detroit next Sunday and their high-powered offense. It’s an important division game that should be a big test and the start of a grueling midseason stretch that will an immense challenge to the Vikings’ 11-game unbeaten streak. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Harrison Smith Joins Exclusive Club with Game-Clinching INT
summary: Harrison Smith has already said that this will, without question, be his final season with the Minnesota Vikings. On Sunday in the Vikings’ 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, he found his way into a very exclusive club as he made the game-clinching interception. Smith’s interception of Daniel Jones to seal the Vikings’ win on […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 4: Harrison Smith #22 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on against the Miami Dolphins during the second quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Harrison Smith has already said that this will, without question, be his final season with the Minnesota Vikings. On Sunday in the Vikings’ 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, he found his way into a very exclusive club as he made the game-clinching interception. Hall of Fame Harrison Smith 📺: @nfloncbs pic.twitter.com/YU6ebbntKZ — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) October 25, 2026 Smith’s interception of Daniel Jones to seal the Vikings’ win on Sunday afternoon was the 40th of his illustrious career. That made him just the third player in the history of the National Football League with at least 40 career interceptions and 20 career quarterback sacks. The other two players on that list are Charles Woodson and Ronde Barber. Both of those men have their busts displayed in Canton. One day, Harrison Smith will have his there as well. Smith has spent his entire career in purple after the Vikings selected him with the 29th overall pick in the 2012 NFL Draft out of Notre Dame. The only two players who have played more games in team history as a member of the Vikings are Jim Marshall and Mick Tingelhoff. He’s truly one of the greats in the history of the Vikings franchise, and it’s awesome to see him put his name beside two Hall of Famers in a club like this one. Congratulations to Harrison Smith on making history this Sunday afternoon as part of this Minnesota Vikings victory!

title: Defense Rules The Day Again As Vikings Hold Off Colts To Move To 6-0
summary: The Minnesota Vikings continue to find ways to win, even when the defense needs to drag the rest of the team kicking and screaming into the winner’s circle. This time, they got a couple of fortunate breaks as well, but that’s how it goes sometimes. The Vikings once again struggled on offense, but the defense […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Dallas Turner #15 and Harrison Smith #22 of the Minnesota Vikings sack Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts in the second quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings continue to find ways to win, even when the defense needs to drag the rest of the team kicking and screaming into the winner’s circle. This time, they got a couple of fortunate breaks as well, but that’s how it goes sometimes. The Vikings once again struggled on offense, but the defense sacked Colts’ quarterback Daniel Jones four times, and Colts’ kicker Spencer Shrader missed a pair of field goals as the Vikings moved to 6-0 on the season with a 16-0 victory over Indianapolis at U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 7 action. The Vikings won the coin toss and elected to receive, as they’ve done on most occasions they’ve won the toss this season. Myles Price got things off to a fast start, as he took the opening kickoff and returned it into Colts territory at the 47-yard line, giving the Vikings great field position to start things off. Unfortunately, the Vikings wasted that field position as they handed the ball to Aaron Jones on four consecutive plays. The fourth one came on a 4th-and-1 play that saw Jones get swarmed in the backfield for a turnover on downs, bringing the opening possession to a screeching halt. The Colts took over after the turnover on downs and moved the ball down the field, converting a pair of third downs on completions from Daniel Jones to Keenan Allen and Josh Downs. Then, the Colts turned to their home run threat, running back Jonathan Taylor, and he did the rest, slicing through the Vikings’ defense for a 38-yard touchdown run to give the Colts a 7-0 lead just six minutes into the game. The Vikings got things moving on their next possession with a quick pass to Jordan Addison for 11 yards and a first down and picked up another first down on a defensive holding penalty, but the drive stalled out after that, and the Vikings punted it away, putting the Colts’ offense at its own 11-yard line. The Vikings then avoided another disaster as they ran a quarterback sneak with Murray on another 4th-and-1 play, this one in their own territory, and a virtual measurement determined that they just got the first down. The drive continued, and the Vikings pushed into Colts territory in a drive that spanned the break between the first and second quarters. Murray’s pass on 3rd-and-8 from the Indianapolis 10 fell incomplete, and the Vikings settled for a 26-yard field goal from Will Reichard to make it 7-3 early in the second quarter. The Colts took over possession and were quickly to midfield after a couple of carries by Taylor. Their drive stalled and was ended on a sack by Dallas Turner, forcing them to punt it away. Thanks to a great special teams play to keep the ball out of the end zone, the Vikings had to start the next drive from their own 4-yard line. Murray found Jefferson for a 20-yard gain to get the ball away from the end zone, and then found Gavin Bartholomew for 17 more to get the ball near midfield. A completion to Jauan Jennings. . .yes, Jauan Jennings. . .moved the ball into Colts territory, where Murray found Jefferson to convert another third down. But the drive stalled out, meaning the Vikings called on Reichard again, and he did what he always does, connecting on a 47-yard attempt to make it 7-6 with six and a half minutes left in the half. That field goal by Reichard gave him the Vikings’ record for the most consecutive made field goals by a kicker, passing the mark that had been held by Gary Anderson. Congratulations to the Baby-Faced Assassin™ on setting a new standard. The Colts took the ball and pushed down into Minnesota territory and even got into a goal-to-go situation at the end of the half, but the Vikings’ defense stood firm and forced Indianapolis to settle for a field goal attempt. Spencer Shrader came on and put it through the uprights from 43 yards out as time expired, allowing the Colts to take a 10-6 lead into the locker room at halftime. The Colts also got the ball to start the second half, thanks to the Vikings taking the ball to start the game. The Colts got a quick first down from Taylor, but then the Vikings picked up back-to-back sacks, one coming from Jalen Redmond and Eric Wilson and the second from Dallas Turner and Blake Cashman, to stop the drive. The Vikings got the ball with solid field position, but as has been the case so often this season, the offense could do nothing with it, as they quickly went three-and-out and punted it back to the Colts. Indianapolis, once again, put together a sustained drive and put themselves in a position to add more points. On a 4th-and-2 from the Minnesota 38-yard line, they brought on Spencer Shrader to attempt a 56-yard field goal. Shrader put his leg into it, but it was an ugly-looking kick, and he pushed it wide to the left to give the Vikings the ball in good field position once again late in the third quarter. On the first play of the fourth quarter, the Vikings faced a 3rd-and-8 from the Colts’ 40-yard line, and Murray made his biggest play of the day, as he got out of the pocket and avoided defenders to sprint down to the Indianapolis 5-yard line to set the Vikings up with a first-and-goal. Kyler Murray with a 35-yard run to pick up the first down 🏃 INDvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GSqLond1o9 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 On the very next play, the Vikings finally got into the end zone, as Murray found T.J. Hockenson for a 5-yard touchdown to take their first lead of the day at 13-10. A TD for T.J. Hockenson on National Tight Ends Day 😌 INDvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/E0aOAL9M10 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 The Colts got to near midfield on their next possession, but their drive stalled out, and they punted it away once more. The Vikings moved the ball down the field a bit and decided to roll the dice on a 59-yard field goal try from Reichard, and for the first time in a long time, the result was not a successful one. Colts’ defensive lineman Grover Stewart got a hand up and blocked the attempt, giving the Colts the ball at their own 41-yard line with eight and a half minutes left in regulation. Indianapolis took the ball and moved back into Minnesota territory and got Shrader into position to try to tie it and, once again, Shrader failed to come through. This time, he pushed his attempt wide to the right, keeping the Vikings ahead by three points with just over four minutes left in regulation. Minnesota then moved the ball into Colts’ territory again and attempted to position themselves to add to the lead. Murray appeared to have a big play to Jordan Addison at the two-minute warning that would have given the Vikings the ball at the Colts’ 2-yard line, but a holding penalty on Blake Brandel negated it. The Vikings did, eventually, extend the lead, as Reichard connected on a 52-yard attempt to make it 16-10 with 1:39 left on the clock. The Colts got the ball back, and Harrison Smith ended it by making NFL history. Harrison Smith seals it for the Vikings as they move to 6-0 🔥 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/2WGaXhpqfQ — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) October 25, 2026 Harrison Smith intercepted Jones’ pass, and in doing so became the third player in the history of the National Football League to register at least 40 interceptions and at least 20 quarterback sacks. The other two. . .Charles Woodson and Ronde Barber. . .have their busts displayed in Canton. One day, Harrison Smith will likely join them. The interception allowed the Vikings to kneel out the clock and push their record to 6-0 in another ugly game. Ugly wins are still wins, however, and with the San Francisco 49ers currently losing to the Atlanta Falcons, there’s a chance that the Vikings could end the day as the only undefeated team in the NFC.…

full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Will Reichard #16 of the Minnesota Vikings kicks for a field goal during an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Cesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The long, terrible darkness of the bye week is over, and another Minnesota Vikings game day is officially upon us!
