title: TreVeyon Henderson still enjoys Patriots’ trust despite quiet season so far
summary: There were moments during his 2025 rookie season that TreVeyon Henderson looked like a superstar in the making and potential future difference maker for the New England Patriots offense. Seven weeks into his sophomore campaign, that future has not yet arrived. In fact, the opposite has been the case. Henderson has been largely quiet and […]
full_text: There were moments during his 2025 rookie season that TreVeyon Henderson looked like a superstar in the making and potential future difference maker for the New England Patriots offense. Seven weeks into his sophomore campaign, that future has not yet arrived. In fact, the opposite has been the case. Henderson has been largely quiet and is trailing his rookie production so far. However, he still enjoys the Patriots’ full support as head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed after the young running back played only 13 of 54 snaps during last Thursday’s loss to the Chicago Bears. “We had some things for him, packages or personnel groupings,” Vrabel said. “TreVeyon will help us, but I wanted to see where we were with Corey [Kiner] getting a couple carries too.” Henderson’s limited usage against the Bears appears to be the result of two factors: third running back Corey Kiner coming off a solid performance four days earlier versus the New York Jets, and the 24-year-old himself being just 11 days removed from suffering a reported high ankle sprain. In general, Henderson has been limited by injuries for much of 2026 so far. Besides his recent sprained ankle, he also suffered an ankle injury in late August that forced him out multiple weeks into the regular season. Since his return in Week 2 against Pittsburgh — a game that saw him score a 39-yard touchdown reminiscent of his 2025 form — he has touched the ball 57 total times for 248 scrimmage yards and that one score. Those numbers put him on track for around 700 yards and three touchdowns this season, a far cry from the 1,132 and 10 TDs he had last year. Obviously, the circumstances do not work in his favor so far; besides his own injury woes, RB1 Rhamondre Stevenson has been reliable both in terms of availability and production. That said, Henderson himself is also still dealing with some of the same issues that plagued him as a first-year pro: his vision remains underdeveloped and his pass protection a work in progress. Even so, his head coach is confident that the Patriots will find a way to get him involved at a higher rate. “TreVeyon will help us plenty here down the stretch and helped us a little bit tonight,” Vrabel said on Thursday. With the Patriots entering their upcoming game against the Dolphins off a mini-bye, and the extra rest it brings, Henderson might get his chance to help the team as early as Week 8.

title: Patriots vs. Bears snap counts from Week 7
summary: Leading up to Thursday’s game in Chicago, New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel spoke about the challenge the Bears’ ability to control the flow of games presents. They entered Week 7 having run the second-most offensive plays in the league, while simultaneously also ranking second in fewest plays to defend. “They just haven’t had […]
full_text: Leading up to Thursday’s game in Chicago, New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel spoke about the challenge the Bears’ ability to control the flow of games presents. They entered Week 7 having run the second-most offensive plays in the league, while simultaneously also ranking second in fewest plays to defend. “They just haven’t had a lot of plays against them,” said Vrabel on the eve of the game. “So, that’s the challenge, being able to flip the script a little bit, not let them run 73 plays and only have to defend 50.” The split wasn’t quite that drastic in the actual game, but not too far off either: the Patriots offense was on the field for a season-low 54 snaps after averaging 63.8 over the first six weeks of the season. Likewise, their defensive workload jumped from a season-long average of 57.2 to 69. That split, which also is reflected in the time of possession numbers from the game, contributed to the eventual outcome. New England’s offense, after all, was fairly efficient moving the football but after going only 3-for-8 on combined third and fourth downs simply didn’t have enough opportunities to hang with the Bears; one more possession in a one-score game could have been all that was needed for the result to change. Alas, that didn’t happen. Here is our full snap count report from the Patriots’ 30-24 loss . Offense Total snaps: 54 | Time on the field: 26:24 | * denotes starter QB Drake Maye* (54; 100%), LT Will Campbell* (54; 100%), LG Walter Rouse* (54; 100%), C Jared Wilson* (54; 100%), RG Matt Pryor* (54; 100%), RT Morgan Moses* (54; 100%), WR A.J. Brown* (49; 91%), TE Hunter Henry* (41; 76%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson* (37; 69%), WR DeMario Douglas* (35; 65%), WR Efton Chism III (34; 63%), TE Eli Raridon (29; 54%), WR Kyle Williams* (21; 39%), RB TreVeyon Henderson (13; 24%), RB Corey Kiner (6; 11%), TE Cameron Latu (4; 7%), OT/TE Caleb Lomu (1; 2%) Let’s start with one of the game’s silver linings: for the first time since Week 4, the Patriots offensive line was able to go wire-to-wire. Granted, the unit is currently relying on backups at both left and right guard, but they at least managed to come out of the game unscathed. With three guards already on injured reserve (Alijah Vera-Tucker, Mike Onwenu, Greg Van Roten) and another also nursing an injury (Ben Brown) that is a positive development. At wide receiver, A.J. Brown played a high number of snaps in just his second game back from a high ankle sprain that had sidelined him for four weeks. His production doesn’t look the part yet, but his conditioning seems to be at the appropriate level after his time missed. DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism were the primary wideouts used alongside him, with Kyle Williams still little more than a package option. Even though the Patriots operated out of 11-personnel quite bit on Thursday, their wide receivers were relatively quiet in terms of production. Of Drake Maye’s 24 pass completions, 17 went to either a tight end or running back. The former spot saw no surprises from a playing time perspective, with Hunter Henry the top option and rookie Eli Raridon as TE2. At running back, meanwhile, Rhamondre Stevenson carried the bulk of the load while TreVeyon Henderson — 11 days removed from spraining his ankle — played only 13 snaps while effectively sharing RB2 duties with Corey Kiner. Defense Total snaps: 69 | Time on the field: 31:23 | * denotes starter LB Robert Spillane* (69; 100%), LB Christian Elliss* (69; 100%), CB Christian Gonzalez* (69; 100%), S Craig Woodson* (69; 100%), CB Marcus Jones* (67; 97%), S Kevin Byard III *(65; 94%), ED Elijah Ponder* (57; 83%), ED Dre’Mont Jones* (44; 64%), DT Cory Durden* (43; 62%), DT Milton Williams* (41; 59%), CB Charles Woods* (38; 55%), ED Gabe Jacas (36; 52%), DT Christian Barmore (35; 51%), DT DaQuan Jones (28; 41%), DT Leonard Taylor III (18; 26%), S Jaylen Reed (5; 7%), S Mike Brown (4; 6%), LB Darius Muasau (1; 1%), S Brenden Schooler (1; 1%) Even though he was a late addition to the injury report due to an illness, Christian Gonzalez ended up playing all 69 defensive snaps against the Bears — one of four players to do so. Not among that group was usual 100-percenter Kevin Byard, who briefly exited with an apparent shoulder injury in the second quarter but stayed out for only four plays before his return. In those four plays, Mike Brown took the field as the second safety next to Craig Woodson. Brown, who opened the season on the practice squad, was one of three backup safeties seeing the field on defense. Jaylen Reed played five snaps as a slot and box defender, while Brenden Schooler played one third-down snap as a quarterback spy against Caleb Williams. Also heavily involved in the secondary was Charles Woods, who started his third straight game as an injury replacement on the defensive perimeter. He filled Carlton Davis’ spot in the lineup, but entered the field in nickel packages with Marcus Jones typically bumping inside into the slot in that case. Up front, Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss again manned the linebacker spot even though Darius Muasau also entered for one snap. The edge rotation also looked as it normally does, with second-year man Elijah Ponder continuing to play a high-volume role. On the interior, Cory Durden played a season-high 43 snaps — eight more than Christian Barmore, who was used primarily on passing downs and had what could have been a game-changing sack in the late fourth quarter (if not for Bears kicker Cairo Santos making a 58-yard field goal afterwards). Special teams Total snaps: 28 | Time on the field: 2:13 S Brenden Schooler (24; 86%), S Jaylen Reed (24; 86%), S/PP Mike Brown (24; 86%), LB Namdi Obiazor (23; 82%), TE Cameron Latu (21; 75%), LB Erick Hunter (18; 64%), LB Darius Muasau (17; 61%), ED Benton Whitley (13; 46%), DT Cory Durden (11; 39%), ED Elijah Ponder (11; 39%), ED Gabe Jacas (11; 39%), P/H Mitch Wishnowsky (9; 32%), LS Julian Ashby (8; 29%), RB/KR Corey Kiner (7; 25%), WR/KR Kyle Williams (7; 25%), DT Milton Williams (7; 25%), DT DaQuan Jones (7; 25%), K Andy Borregales (7; 25%), CB Kindle Vildor (6; 21%), DT Christian Barmore (5; 18%), DT Leonard Taylor III (5; 18%), OT Will Campbell (4; 14%), OT Caleb Lomu (4; 14%), OL Walter Rouse (4; 14%), OL Matt Pryor (4; 14%), OL Xavier Newman-Johnson (4; 14%), CB/PR Marcus Jones (2; 7%) The Patriots used seven players in a core-four role on Thursday. Brenden Schooler, Jaylen Reed, Mike Brown, Namdi Obiazor, Cameron Latu, Erick Hunter and Darius Muasau were on the field as part of the kickoff return, kickoff coverage, punt return and punt coverage units. Two recent roster additions, Elliott Davison and practice squad elevatee Benton Whitley, played on three units. New England also attempted its first onside kick this season, and it was punter Mitch Wishnowsky taking it rather than typical kickoff specialist/place kicker Andy Borregales. The kick was recovered by Chicago to seal the game. Did not play QB Tommy DeVito, TE Tanner Arkin, OT Dametrious Crownover A close, competitive game can only mean one thing: Tommy DeVito not seeing the field. For a sixth time in seven games this year, the Patriots’ backup quarterback spent all 60 minutes on the sidelines. This time, however, he had company. Rookies Tanner Arkin and Dametrious Crownover, who have mostly resided on the inactives list this year, dressed for the game but were emergency options only. This meant that there were two open spots on the inactives list entering Thursday. With their game in the books, 13 others await […]
full_text: For the New England Patriots, Week 7 was a disappointment. The team of head coach Mike Vrabel dropped its Thursday night meeting with the Chicago Bears with a final score of 30-24 , falling to 4-3 on the season and out of the current AFC playoff picture . With their game in the books, 13 others await between Sunday morning and Monday night. Let’s find out who to root in all of them. Sunday 9:30 a.m. ET Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) at New Orleans Saints (2-4) : Go Saints! The Patriots do hold the head-to-head advantage over the Steelers, but a loss against the Saints would still be the preferred outcome to keep New England ahead in the standings. And yes, we know it might have a negative effect on the sixth-round draft pick acquired in the Ja’Lynn Polk trade. | NFL Network 1 p.m. ET San Francisco 49ers (6-0) at Atlanta Falcons (2-4) : Go good game! Neither team is on the Patriots’ schedule or has a draft pick in 2027 tied to the team. | FOX Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) at Baltimore Ravens (4-2) : Go Bengals! We could be rooting for a tie here, but. the odds favor somebody winning this one. In that particular case, we are going with the club that currently has fewer wins on its record. | CBS Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5) at Carolina Panthers (3-2) : Go good game! Like the 49ers-Falcons matchup mentioned above, this one has no direct impact on New England. | FOX New York Giants (3-2-1) at Houston Texans (2-4) : Go Giants! The class NFC vs. AFC battle that has us rooting for the team not in the Patriots’ conference. It also might impact the sixth-round pick the Texans sent to New England as part of the Marte Mapu trade. | FOX Indianapolis Colts (2-4) at Minnesota Vikings (5-0) : Go Vikings! Like the game above, this one features an NFC and and AFC team going at each other. It also is a chance for the Patriots’ strength of schedule to improve. | CBS Miami Dolphins (0-5) at New York Jets (2-4) : Go Dolphins! An opportunity for some scouting, as the Patriots will head to Miami next Sunday. While a Dolphins win would give them some momentum, it also would hurt the Jets in the race for the AFC playoff spots. | CBS Cleveland Browns (4-2) at Tennessee Titans (1-5): Go Titans! Two AFC teams going against one another, so naturally we are rooting for the one that currently has the worse record. | CBS 4:05 p.m. ET Denver Broncos (4-2) at Arizona Cardinals (2-4) : Go Cardinals! Another AFC vs. NFC matchup with clear rooting affiliations. | CBS 4:25 p.m. ET Green Bay Packers (4-2) at Detroit Lions (3-2) : Go good game! The Patriots have both teams on their schedule, meaning this all-NFC North battle has no impact whatsoever on their own fortunes yet. | FOX Los Angeles Rams (2-4) at Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) : Go Rams! The Patriots would still beat out the Raiders in the standings due to their win over them in Week 5, but that doesn’t mean they should be rooted for. When in doubt, always go with the NFC team in games like this. | FOX 8:20 p.m. ET Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) at Seattle Seahawks (3-3) : Go Seahawks! Once again, we are picking the NFC side over the one representing the AFC. | NBC Monday 8:15 p.m. ET Dallas Cowboys (2-4) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-4): Go good game! Week 7 closes with a game that is not relevant from a Patriots perspective. | ESPN/ABC

title: Sunday Patriots Notes: Rookie class making an early impact
summary: The New England Patriots dropped a competitive 30-24 contest to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. After a long weekend off, they’ll soon turn their attention to the Miami Dolphins. Most of our attention on this week was on the Bears game. With little time to do so, let’s clean out the notebook from Thursday […]
full_text: The New England Patriots dropped a competitive 30-24 contest to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. After a long weekend off, they’ll soon turn their attention to the Miami Dolphins. Most of our attention on this week was on the Bears game. With little time to do so, let’s clean out the notebook from Thursday night and the week. Welcome to the latest edition of our Sunday Patriots Notes. Rookie report The New England rookie class projected largely as a developmental group following this past NFL Draft. But through the first seven weeks of the season, the group has been relied upon. The Patriots have seen their rookies play the second most amount of special teams snaps in the league this season, while the team’s first three selections have impressed. OT Caleb Lomu The Patriots’ first-round pick remains the third tackle on the depth chart behind Will Campbell and Morgan Moses. That hasn’t kept Lomu off the field, as he has seen extensive action twice as an injury replacement while additionally taking on the jumbo tight end role. Lomu has been impressive in his 160 offensive snaps, showing intriguing traits as a pass protector such as his ability to anchor and recover. He allowed just one total pressure in the two games in which he saw extensive action playing both left and right tackle. “Just trying to get ready each and every week. It’s a lot of new things for him,” Mike Vrabel said. “It’s a new league for him. Coming from college, being 21, and it’s a tough position to be able to go out there and play. I think he’s gotten better.” ED Gabe Jacas The power rusher continues to look more and more comfortable as the season continues. His performance Thursday night in Chicago may have been his best as a pro as Jacas tallied five pressures — flashing his patented bull rush on one instance to power through left tackle Ozzy Trapilo. Jacas’ raw strength and power are legit, and his emergence has helped make an edge group that seemed like a position of weakness a strength through seven weeks. TE Eli Raridon New England’s third-round pick has established himself in the offense playing 44% of the offensive snaps as the No. 2 option behind Hunter Henry. Raridon’s athleticism has translated to the pros and Josh McDaniels has done a strong job using the tight end on runaway routes to get him on the move. While the coaching staff has been impressed with Raridon’s growth as a run blocker, it’s expectedly still a work in progress for the rookie, who was at the point of attack for several run stuffs in Chicago. But the work as a receiver, and the mismatches he can create, leaves excitement for the future as Raridon becomes a bigger and bigger piece of the offense. “I think he’s tried to figure out how to block people at this level,” Vrabel said. “I think he blocks better now than what he had shown in previous exposure. I think that he’s growing and gaining confidence each and every day. He’s an exciting young player that’s fun to work with.” Maye’s performance Outside of the interception and some pre-snap issues identifying pressure, Drake Maye was excellent Thursday night as he kept the Patriots competitive with the Bears. Chicago head coach Ben Johnson left impressed. “He’s an outstanding player. It’s very hard to bottle him up,” Johnson said. “You only rush four, and he finds a way if he doesn’t see anything down the field to find an open gap and skirt on through. And then I think what’s really impressive is how he can find these little outlets and these dumps where they’re still running vertical for catch-and-run opportunities… “He’s caught his rhythm now at this point of the season and probably will continue to do that.“ Brown’s performance Following Brown’s return against the Jets, we were encouraged in his movement and separation ability in his return from a high ankle sprain. The same explosiveness did not look present against Chicago, which hopefully is a byproduct of playing two games in five days after returning from an injury that can linger. The Bears did work to take A.J. Brown out of the equation Thursday night, often clouding his side of the field and taking away his intermediate routes. But, the Patriots will need more from their No. 1 wide receiver moving forward regales. Vrabel vs. Refs Mike Vrabel was one of three head coaches — joining Aaron Glenn and Nick Sirianni — who were fined $250,000 this week for conduct towards officials. The fine could reportedly be repealed with good behavior, which perhaps influenced Vrabel’s post game words when discussing Will Campbell’s questionable false start penalty. “I don’t know. I’m not in good favor with the officiating department so I probably shouldn’t say anything.” A.J. and Hurts Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the season with blood clots. When asked about the situation this past week, Brown sent love and prayers to his former quarterback. “It’s a tough situation, man,” Brown said. “I’ve got a lot of love and respect for him, praying for him. I didn’t know how serious it was. I think all of us kind of found that out, but he’s a tough guy. He’s a tough guy, and he can handle anything. I don’t mean that lightly. I know it’s serious. But he can handle it, and I pray God continue to keep his hand on him. It’s a lot of love and respect from this way. Speedy recovery, and a lot of love.” NFLPA The Patriots elected Drake Maye as their NFLPA Voting Player Representative this past week. Maye will serve on the 32-member Board of Player Representatives and hold the team vote. “I think it’s an honor,” Maye said. “It’s an honor to represent this team, represent the Patriots and to represent the players and the players in this league. I’m going to try to gain some knowledge about how the league works and knowing that this position carries a lot of weight in this league … I know Coach Vrabel was the player rep here. Just trying to make sure that the coaches and players are doing all right.” Maye was elected along with altnerates Will Campbell, Marcus Jones and Brenden Schooler. Jolly Ranchers During halftime of the Raiders game, cornerback Charles Woods had a different request for Mike Vrabel. A grape jolly rancher. The following week against the Jets, Vrabel made sure to keep the grape-flavored candy in his pocket. He gave one to Woods in the fourth quarter and soon after, the cornerback hauled in his first career interception to help seal a Patriots victory. “I kind of like him. He’s got a little street rat in him,” Vrabel said of Woods. “The story was, he was like, ‘Coach, can I get a Jolly Rancher?’ I was like, ‘Are you serious?’ I’m like, ‘Yes.’ At halftime, it was like I was coaching one of the kids’ teams in ninth grade, 9-year-old football. I was like, ‘Yeah, sure, have a Jolly Rancher.’ “Then we won the game and then I joked about it when he got a game ball. We called him Jolly Rancher, JR now for short. Then last week I said, ‘I’m ready to go. I got your grape Jolly Ranchers.’ Put one in, and the next play, he got an interception. I was like, ‘This is crazy.’” Week ahead After enjoying the weekend off, the Patriots will return to the facility on Monday before resuming a typical in-season schedule before next Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins. This means Mike Vrabel media availability on Monday, off-day on Tuesday, and three straight practices plus injury reports from Wednesday through Friday. The team will then hold a final walkthrough on Saturday before departing for Miami.

title: Giants-Texans ‘things I think’: The Giants are in it to win it
summary: “We’re going to be in this thing until the end now.” That was New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh after Sunday’s stunning 27-21 overtime victory over the Houston Texans. The words got my attention. Because they, stunningly, feel like the truth. The Giants are 4-2-1 and leading the NFC East. They will still be […]
full_text: John Harbaugh shares a post-game hug with Tyrone Tracy on Sunday. | Getty Images “We’re going to be in this thing until the end now.” That was New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh after Sunday’s stunning 27-21 overtime victory over the Houston Texans. The words got my attention. Because they, stunningly, feel like the truth. The Giants are 4-2-1 and leading the NFC East. They will still be leading the division after the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys, both 2-4, play on Monday Night Football. The outside world can, and will, snicker at the NFC East. They can, and will, snicker at the Giants. It is hard to blame them. The Eagles have had a stunning fall. They are without Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the season, and the situation surrounding his blood clots could embarrass both the Eagles and the NFL. They have myriad injuries beyond Hurts, and an offensive line that does not resemble the dominant one they possessed not long ago. The Cowboys are, well, the Cowboys. In the current landscape, they probably have the most talent in the division. They keep, though, doing things Cowboys teams have done for three decades. Consequently, they keep falling short of expectations. The Washington Commanders are 1-4-1, winless in three tries in the division, and don’t seem to be able to tell time. They seem to be marking time at this point until owner Josh Harris fires head coach Dan Quinn. The Giants? It is pretty clear that nearly halfway through the season they are the only team in the division that feels good about itself. Why not? The Giants are already on their third starting quarterback, with their No. 1 — Jaxson Dart — out for the season. That’s usually a death knell for NFL teams. J.J. McCarthy, though, is clearly not an ordinary No. 3 quarterback, and he and the Giants appear to be a match. Maybe someone should tell Kevin O’Connell, whose team is somehow 6-0 without good quarterback play, that he might have traded the Giants his best QB. The Giants have lost defensive star Brian Burns for the season. They have also lost starters Tremaine Edmunds and Chauncey Golston, and never had 2025 starting defensive tackle Roy Robertson-Harris. A year ago, the Giants kept spitting the bit and turning victories into losses. This year, they keep finding heroes and winning games at the wire. The Giants now get to go into their bye week in first place. They will also come out of it in first place, as the best the Eagles and Cowboys could do is get to 4-4 before the Giants return to action. “It’s a massive energy shot in the arm. It’s a reward,” Harbaugh said after the game. “Now, you’ve got to make something of it. It doesn’t mean anything if you don’t build on it, right? But it means something, but it doesn’t mean we’re going to win a championship yet. It means we have an opportunity, though.” When the Giants return from their bye, they will face the Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field and then host the Commanders. “We have an opportunity to get ready for the next two games starting with Philadelphia, and then a quick turnaround, so we’ll be thinking about two games as a coaching staff over the bye week,” Harbaugh said. ”The two most important games of the season will be coming up after we come back from the bye, which will set the direction for the rest of the season, really. But we’re going to be in this thing until the end now. This was a pivotal game. This was a really high-pressure game for our team. We didn’t talk about that, but they all knew how important this game was, and they responded accordingly.” ‘Failure is not final’ Nothing really seems to shake the belief of this Giants team. That belief was built in the summer heat, when Harbaugh worked his team harder and longer than most NFL players are accustomed to being worked in an NFL that is much softer than it once was. Harbaugh’s team faced plenty of challenges leading up to Sunday’s game, not the least of which was going winless in its previous two games. Harbaugh changed quarterbacks despite Jameis Winston having lost just once in four starts. He said it was an “obvious choice” to go with McCarthy, but it could have backfired. To pare down the four-way timeshare Najee Harris complained about a week ago, Harbaugh cut Harris. Cam Skattebo was coming off a week in which he was taught a lesson the hard way, getting just six snaps and no touches. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson took the highly unusual public step of calling some of his players “traitors” for lack of effort against the New Orleans Saints. One of those traitors, Jihad Ward, was cut. The Giants lost Edmunds for the season during the week, and played Sunday without two starting defensive backs. Yet, the Giants went in to Houston as 10.5-point underdogs, made it clear from the start that they were playing to win, and came out with a critical, confidence-building victory. “I think that’s exactly the story. To me, that’s the point,” Harbaugh said. “It tells you who they are. You might have thought before the game, we’re going to find out about our guys. We’re going to find out about who they are, and we did, and you saw it. They did; they took the bull by the horns, and they got the job done.” Up until now, analysts and fans of other NFC East teams have looked at the Giants and said, basically, yeah, they’re in first place, but the Giants can’t really win the division. Can they? Maybe they will win it. Maybe they won’t. But it looks like everyone is going to have to get used to the idea that it actually is a possibility. That reality is starting to settle in for at least some analysts. Queue ESPN’s Dan Graziano on Sunday night: No one has wanted to take this seriously, but the first-place Giants are 4-2-1 and will carry at least a 1.5-game NFC East lead into Week 8 regardless of what happens between the Cowboys and Eagles on Monday night. Harbaugh has made a major difference in his first season as Giants head coach. They’re avoiding mistakes, overcoming injuries, and finding ways to win. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy called an outstanding game for McCarthy. Skattebo bounced back after last week’s soft benching and said after the game that he agreed with and appreciated the way it was handled by the coaching staff. Edge rusher Abdul Carter basically dominated the second half on defense. Cornerback Deonte Banks shadowed Nico Collins effectively. The Giants are playing very good team football right now. Given what we saw in Minnesota, McCarthy is a tough guy to count on. But he’s also talented enough to have been picked 10th in the 2024 NFL draft, and it’s entirely possible that what he needed was a new situation. There is a world where he flops completely. There is a world where he’s inconsistent the rest of the way, and the Giants don’t have enough around him to cash in. But there’s also absolutely a world in which he and they play just well enough to win a bad NFC East. Right now, the math tells us that it’s absolutely possible, and the Giants are the betting favorite to win their division. Harbaugh was asked Sunday when he realized his team had the mental fortitude to handle getting knocked down. “I would say just a lot of moments stacked on top of each other because they just didn’t bat an eye and they continued to work hard and fight,” he said. “Every type of situation, they met the same way. Maybe it started with [QB] Jaxson Dart, then it went to the next, the next, the next, to [ILB] Tremaine Edmunds this week. “I don’t know, I just think it’s an ongoing type of a thing. That’s how you build — it’s shared experiences. It’s fighting through all these things together that draws people close together, and that’s how a team is built.” The new quarterback is also a survivor. A former first-round pick banished to third-string in Minnesota and traded away without hesitation. “Guys have scars. He [McCarthy] has scars. He’s been wounded. He’s been broken. He’s been battered. But you heal stronger, and you become better because of…

title: 4 things we learned from the NY Giants’ victory over the Houston Texans
summary: I don’t know what’s in John Harbaugh’s past, but he seems to have had a severe case of bad karma recently. First, Tyler Loop misses a 44-yard field goal that would have sent the Baltimore Ravens to the playoffs, and it costs Harbaugh his head coaching job in Baltimore. Then he takes the Giants’ job, […]
full_text: New York Giants fans had a lot to celebrate on Sunday in Houston. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect I don’t know what’s in John Harbaugh’s past, but he seems to have had a severe case of bad karma recently. First, Tyler Loop misses a 44-yard field goal that would have sent the Baltimore Ravens to the playoffs, and it costs Harbaugh his head coaching job in Baltimore. Then he takes the Giants’ job, leads them to a stirring opening win over Dallas, but loses his quarterback for the season in the first quarter of the next game. Then in the next game he loses his best pass rusher for the season. Then last week he loses a starting linebacker for the season, as well as a starting safety for this week at least. Whatever the gods were displeased with, it now seems to be over. Harbaugh’s New York Giants played probably there best game of the season on Sunday … and were rewarded with a thrilling 27-21 overtime win over the Houston Texans. The Giants now have won six straight against Houston after losing to them as an expansion team in 2002. Today was the day the Giants were supposed to be exposed as frauds. Instead, it may be time to take them seriously. (Cue the Jim Mora “Playoffs?” meme.) What did we learn from this impressive victory? Maybe Kevin O’Connell isn’t a QB guru after all? Last week I shared an X post jokingly pointing out how quarterbacks that O’Connell have tutored have fared much better after leaving the Vikings following J.J. McCarthy’s remarkable fourth quarter in his Giants debut as a real quarterback (i.e., not just RPOs) against New Orleans. This week, McCarthy had a chance to play a full game even up rather than in mop-up duty, and with a week of preparation, against a team with a great pass rush and good cornerbacks. No one would have been surprised if he came back down to Earth. Wow! If you hadn’t followed the last three NFL seasons, you would have said to yourself, yeah, this guy looks like you’d expect/hope the 10th pick in the draft in his third NFL season to look. McCarthy was lights out vs. the Texans especially in the first half. He cooled off in the second half, but he was getting rushed a lot more by that point in the game. Early in the game, McCarthy looked like the reputation he brought to New York, throwing these fastballs that he’s been criticized for … but being right on target with them. One of them was dropped by Malik Nabers, and that might not have happened with a bit more touch on the ball. But then, with less than a minute to go in the half, McCarthy beautifully layered a throw over the first level of the pass defense to hit Nabers (who had his fourth consecutive 100+ yard receiving game today) and put the Giants into field goal position. Earlier, McCarthy threw one of his lasers with anticipation on an out to Malachi Fields, perfectly placed so the defender couldn’t reach it, and Fields scampered downfield for 47 yards. For a guy that the coaches were afraid to do anything with except run RPO keepers a couple of weeks ago, McCarthy looks like he is in complete control of the offense. He “only” finished with 252 passing yards this time, and did not have a TD pass, but he looks like the real deal and is one of the biggest reasons the Giants won Sunday. Watching him made it hard to understand how he could have crashed and burned in Minnesota. I have to give props to offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan, who seem to have created an offense that McCarthy is comfortable in and that takes advantage of his strengths in a fairly short period of time. In Nagy’s defense, he did get the most out of Mitch Trubisky in his first two NFL seasons, so maybe he knows what he’s doing. I’m getting ahead of myself, but if this keeps up, what do the Giants do with him next year when Jaxson Dart returns? And I do mean next year. The Giants are not flipping him to a contender for a high draft pick just before the trade deadline. The Giants find themselves with what could be two of the most exciting young quarterbacks in the NFL. It’s a good problem to have. What to do with Dominic Zvada? The postscript to McCarthy’s beautiful layered pass to Nabers is that shortly thereafter, Dominic Zvada missed a 44-yard field goal attempt, after missing a 58-yard field goal attempt earlier in the game. It hurt because the Texans’ kicker, Ka’imi Fairbairn, made two field goals, including his own 58-yarder. Unlike Zvada’s misses in Washington, which came in bad weather and where he seemed to be hooking the ball, there were ideal conditions for a kicker today and both misses were straight and true … but just aimed poorly. Zvada clearly has the leg, and he’s hitting the ball well, but this game should never have reached overtime. Unfortunately he has two weeks to stew over it, as does Harbaugh. Harbaugh seems to be pretty decisive with underperforming players, but do the Giants want to get into the kicker merry-go-round they’ve been on for the last three seasons? I don’t know the answer. I’d like to hope it’s a small adjustment. But at 4-2-1 and with a two game lead in the NFC East heading into the bye, Harbaugh may be thinking about the circumstances that precipitated his exit from Baltimore and decide to make a change. Deonte Banks has arrived There may be nothing more remarkable than the fact that Deonte Banks, who seemed on his way out the door this summer when the new coaching staff arrived, has suddenly become, maybe not exactly a shutdown corner, but not far from it in his fourth NFL season. Banks gave up three receptions on six targets today, and was the responsible defender on Xavier Hutchinson’s 3-yard TD catch. But his three completions against went for a total of … 10 yards. Against Nico Collins, one of the best receivers in the NFL, Banks gave up one catch for 4 yards. It’s hard to mention just one player on this defense, which played well overall against a potent offense. Abdul Carter continued his really good season with six pressures, and Kayvon Thibodeaux had four of his own and almost had an interception. He was more visible today than he’s been in a long time. The Giants’ run defense is still somewhat suspect, but kept Houston under 100 yards today. They’re more promising with D.J. Reader, who’s having a great season and played well again today, in the middle. Players stepped up on the run offense Cam Skattebo was released from the doghouse and responded today with 124 yards and a touchdown. His 42 yard run in overtime put the Giants in position to win, which they promptly did when Devin Singletary followed up with a 30-yard run for the winning TD. Part of the Giants’ successful run game today was having Skattebo back in Harbaugh’s good graces. Part, though, was the Giants’ offensive line blocking better for the run than they probably have all season. Not Jeff Stoutland-Eagles-offensive line good, but well enough for a player like Skattebo to have a fair chance of getting yards after contact (except when he’s flagged for unnecessary roughness for lowering his helmet – ridiculous) and for Singletary to run almost untouched on the winning TD. If the Giants can develop a consistently dangerous running game, their passing game could become devastating to opposing offenses.

title: NY Giants vs. Texans: 15 winners, just one loser as Giants beat Houston in OT
summary: Let’s review Sunday’s thrilling 27-21 overtime victory by the New York Giants in our unique ‘Kudos and Wet Willies’ style. Kudos to … Cam Skattebo — Sunday was how you respond after being taught a lesson in getting just six snaps and no touches a week ago. Skattebo had the first 100-yard rushing game of […]
full_text: Devin Singletary scores Sunday’s game-winning touchdown. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Let’s review Sunday’s thrilling 27-21 overtime victory by the New York Giants in our unique ‘Kudos and Wet Willies’ style. Kudos to … Cam Skattebo — Sunday was how you respond after being taught a lesson in getting just six snaps and no touches a week ago. Skattebo had the first 100-yard rushing game of his career with 17 carries for 124 yards, and a touchdown. Skattebo had a career-long 42-yard run in overtime to set up Devin Singletary’s game-winning 30-yard run. He broke two tackles en route to a 16-yard touchdown run, and had a 19-yard run off a fake Tush Push. Fantastic game, and fantastic response to adversity, from Skattebo. Devin Singletary — The third, and sometimes fourth, wheel in the Giants’ backfield this season took advantage of an opportunity when Tyrone Tracy left the game with a hamstring injury. Singletary made two fantastic cuts in the open field on his game-winning 30-yard run. Overtime TD for Devin Singletary ‼️ pic.twitter.com/TihbBHHs99 — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 25, 2026 The run game as a whole — The Giants got touchdowns from four different runners, including Tush Push specialist Jameis Winston. They ran for 188 yards on 34 attempts, 5.5 yards per carry. The ball control offense, which is the way they want to play, helped them hold the ball for 35:50 compared to Houston’s 26:45. Giants had TD runs from Tyrone Tracy, Cam Skattebo, Jameis Winston and Devin Singletary. The last time Giants had 4 players run for a TD in same game: 12/3/1950 in 51-7 win vs NY Yanks: Eddie Price, Gene Roberts, Charlie Conerly, Bob Jackson — Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) October 25, 2026 Quarterback J.J. McCarthy knew who to celebrate with after the game: @jjmccarthyy18 gave big love to his running backs 💙 pic.twitter.com/dM7lOt3067 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 J.J. McCarthy — McCarthy was fantastic in his first start. He finished 20 of 28 for 252 yards, and never put the ball in harm’s way. His ability to get the ball down the field with velocity, his ability to move around in the pocket, and simply the threat of using him in the designed run game changes the Giants’ offense. The Giants had five pass plays of at least 20 yards, two of more than 40. Head coach John Harbaugh said after the game that starting him against the Texans was the “obvious choice.” McCarthy absolutely made the coach right. Malik Nabers — The star wide receiver started the game hot, and finished with seven catches for 115 yards, his fourth straight 100-yard receiving game. Over that stretch, he has 36 receptions for 513 yards. That is 14.25 yards per catch, and 128.25 yards per game. Per NextGen Stats, Nabers’ 100-yard streak is the longest in the NFL. Matt Nagy — With McCarthy’s presence at quarterback opening up the playbook, the Giants’ offensive coordinator was in his bag throughout the game. McCarthy only ran the ball once in the game, on a quarterback sneak, but Nagy used the threat of McCarthy’s legs to create advantages for the Giants’ running backs. He used options, misdirection, the Tush Push, a sweep to Skattebo out of Tush Push formation, and a jet sweep to dial up ways to get the Giants’ struggling run game going. In the pass game, he took full advantage of McCarthy’s big arm — and his willingness to show it off — by dialing up a number of intermediate to deep shots that changed the offense from plodding to dangerous. Per Next Gen Stats, the Giants’ streak of four straight games with at least 27 points scored is their longest since Week 5-9 of the 2010 season. Deonte Banks — Dare I say that Banks played like a No. 1 cornerback on Sunday. He took Houston’s best receiver, Nico Collins, out of Houston’s offense. Deonte Banks against Nico Collins today 14 snaps (10/14 in man) 4 targets (2 PD) 1 catch | 4 yards Nico Collins finished the day with 2 catches for 6 yards on 5 targets. https://t.co/uQqwKOq2iq — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) October 25, 2026 Per Pro Football Focus, he gave up three catches in six targets for an average of just 3.3 yards per reception. He also finished with two passes defensed. Micah McFadden — In his return to the starting lineup following the season-ending injury suffered by Tremaine Edmunds, McFadden wasn’t perfect. He, typically, missed a couple of tackles. Also typically, his pass coverage wasn’t perfect. McFadden, though, had a team-high 10 tackles. Four of those went for STOPs. He had three pressures as a blitzer. He had a huge tackle of running back Woody Marks for no gain to start the overtime. McFadden also handled green dot play-calling duties. Abdul Carter — Yeah, yeah. I know. Carter didn’t have a sack. He had six pressures, though, per PFF, and drew two holding penalties. From what Harbaugh said in the post-game press conference, it was also Carter, just a second-year player, who commanded the locker room at halftime. "That was a player's win in every way… …as Abdul told the guys at halftime, no matter what empty the tank, no matter what come back in here with nothing left, and that's what they did" John Harbaugh's opening statement after the Giants' win: pic.twitter.com/GeQYuKpvi2 — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 25, 2026 John Harbaugh — In recent days, Harbaugh has tightened the screws on his players. He sent Skattebo a loud and clear message. He cut Najee Harris for lack of performance, and maybe for complaining. He cut Jihad Ward for lack of effort. His defensive coordinator blasted his players to the media. You know Dennard Wilson didn’t do that without Harbaugh knowing about it. Harbaugh demanded more. He has consistently laid out for his players the reality of the opportunity in front of them, and that they can be better than they have been. Sunday, they responded by going into Houston and winning a game in which they were 10.5-point underdogs. Giants are 2-0 when John Harbaugh tackles his own player pic.twitter.com/aHpKBBh8ne — Giants Nation Show (@GiantsNationPod) October 25, 2026 Run defense — Houston entered the game 29th in the NFL with an average of 3.6 yards per carry. The Giants didn’t let the Texans get started on the ground, holding them to 84 yards on 25 attempts, 3.4 yards per carry. Houston’s longest run was 11 yards. Kayvon Thibodeaux — I debated making Thibodeaux a ‘Kwillie’ after his dropped overtime interception, but why quibble and ruin the happy vibes. Thibodeaux played well. He covered quarterback C.J. Stroud to blow up a Philly Special near the goal line. PFF credited him with four hurries of Stroud as a pass rusher. I’ll cut him some slack. If he had hands, maybe he would be a tight end. D.J. Reader — The lynchpin of the Giants’ run defense was typically outstanding, with early PFF grades placing him above the ‘elite’ level of 90.0 on Sunday. Reader even had some impact in the pass rush, with three hurries. Jameis Winston — The veteran quarterback didn’t sulk during the week when he was replaced as a starter. On Sunday, he emerged as the Giants’ ‘Tush Push’ specialist, with 2 first downs and a touchdown in four carries on the play. Take that, Eagles! Malachi Fields — The rookie wide receiver had his career-best game with four catches for 83 yards, including a 47-yard catch-and-run on a perfectly thrown sideline pass by McCarthy. Wet Willies to … Dominic Zvada — You know there are placekicker issues when the head starts passing on field goals considered commonplace in today’s game. That’s what happened on the Giants’ first drive of the third quarter when John Harbaugh punted from the Houston 38-yard line. Yes, three of those misses are from beyond 50 yards. The ability to make those kicks, though, is one of the reasons Zvada is on the roster. title: NY Giants vs. Texans, instant grades: New York scores overtime victory
summary: The New York Giants started the J.J. McCarthy era won Sunday with a 27-21 overtime victory over the Houston Texans. New York’s defense played phenomenally, forcing four three-and-outs, including on the Texans’ first overtime possession. Tae Banks shut down Nico Collins, and Dennard Wilson called a more conservative game, with a lot of two-high looks, […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy (18) and shelby Harris celebrate the Giants’ victory on Sunday. | Getty Images The New York Giants started the J.J. McCarthy era won Sunday with a 27-21 overtime victory over the Houston Texans. New York’s defense played phenomenally, forcing four three-and-outs, including on the Texans’ first overtime possession. Tae Banks shut down Nico Collins, and Dennard Wilson called a more conservative game, with a lot of two-high looks, but he was judicious in bringing the pressure, which did harass C.J. Stroud. Quarterback McCarthy started the game HOT with two 40+ yard completions; one was a dime to Malik Nabers on a back shoulder throw, and the other was an excellent catch-and-run by rookie Malachi Fields on a well-placed out route. McCarthy and Fields had a real connection, as the Texans focused on Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers. McCarthy did not have to use his legs, but its presence helped the run game. McCarthy looked in control, had command, and made several high-level throws. He finished 20 of 28 for 252 yards, while taking three sacks. An excellent first start for the young quarterback. Also, great job by Jameis Winston on the sneaks. Grade: A+ Running back The Giants’ rushing attack exploded against Houston, capped off by a 42-yard and 30-yard run by Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary to secure the victory in overtime. To no one’s surprise, Skattebo played with energy and physicality; so much so that he was flagged for a personal foul for lowering his helmet after completely annihilating a Texans’ safety on an 8-yard run. Skattebo found the end zone again and the Giants’ rushing attack looked better against a tough run defense in Houston. Skattebo finished with his first 100-yard rushing game of his career. He averaged 7.3 YPC with 124 yards with a touchdown. Singletary rushed five times for 41 yards with the game-winning touchdown, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. left the game with a hamstring injury in the first half. The running backs had a poor season so far, but they get an A+ for today’s response and effort. Grade: A+ Wide receiver Malik Nabers went north of 100 yards AGAIN with seven catches for 111 yards, including a nice back shoulder 42-yard snap on the Giants’ opening drive. Darnell Mooney caught one target for 4 yards and continues to get nailed every time the ball is thrown in his direction. He also picked up a fourth-down end around that went for three yards. Malachi Fields had an elite catch-and-run on an out route. He took the pass 47 yards downfield to help set up a long Zvada field goal attempt that was missed. Fields had his best game as a professional. Fields finished with four catches for 83 yards. Grade: A- Tight end Isaiah Likely was held in check by the Texans’ defense, and it appeared like he was playing injured for much of the second half. Likely got up slowly a few times and looked to be hobbling, but he gutted it out. Thomas Fidone II got involved with an impressive TE leak play that went for 29 yards and nearly scored. Chris Manhertz threw his great blocks, per usual. Grade: B+ Offensive line The Giants were much better blocking up front. Cam Skattebo had multiple long runs, and the hole in overtime was MASSIVE on Skattebo’s 42 yard run. McCarthy had time in the pocket and the run game was able to get going, which, to be fair, can also be attributed to McCarthy keeping the defense honest with the zone read. However, the return of Jermaine Eleumunor was much needed. Andrew Thomas did surrender a sack to Danielle Hunter, but that’s good on good. New York averaged 5.5 yards per carry. There were holes for the Giants’ backs to hit, and the pass protection remained solid, despite three sacks surrendered. A great bounce-back game for the line. Grade: A Defensive line D.J. Reader has been sensational through seven games, and he continues to be a dominant run defender, as well as adding some interior pass-rushing juice, which was most on display when he hit C.J. Stroud with eight minutes left in the fourth quarter, forcing an incomplete pass. Houston’s struggles on the ground continued, as they averaged just 3.5 YPC. New York did an excellent job forcing Houston to become one-dimensional. Grade: A+ Edge Although Abdul Carter had a few run-block losses, his consistent pressure drew two penalties and forced Stroud to maneuver in the pocket. One penalty was in overtime on an incomplete pass. Trace Ford played more after the release of Jihad Ward, and he looked solid from my vantage point. Kayvon Thibodeaux had a few stops in the run game, along with at least one pressure. Thibodeaux also did a great job covering Stroud on the Philly Special with a minute left in the game. Thibodeaux almost secured his first interception in overtime, but he dropped it. Grade: B + Linebacker Arvell Reese was flying around the field making plays, per usual. He blew up a few screen passes near the line of scrimmage and continues to be an asset for the Giants. Tremaine Edmunds was placed on I.R. over the weekend, and Micah McFadden looked adequate in relief of the offseason addition. He recorded a few STOPs at the line of scrimmage and looked solid in run support. McFadden was in the area code of Harrison Jr. on the new Texans’ receiver, but the route concept isolated the linebacker in zone against the former Cardinal. Grade: B+ Cornerback Tae Banks SHUT DOWN Nico Collins. Dennard Wilson called MEG ( man everywhere he goes ) on several zone plays, and Banks answered the call. His redemption arc continues to be an excellent storyline this season. Banks was outleveraged on the Xavier Hutchinson end around and he had at least one other missed tackle. Still, elite job in coverage. Marvin Harrison Jr. was not seen until his late touchdown in the first half, as the Texans offense looked sloppy and unprepared for much of the first half, but that was scored up the seam, near McFadden. Paulson Adebo was activated off injured reserve, and he looked fine. Dru Phillips, however, was not the elite pass rusher he’s become over the last two weeks, but he did regress to his grabby self in coverage. He took a defensive holding penalty and was called for pass interference. Grade: A Safety Jason Pinnock briefly left the game but did return. Ar’Darius Washington took a pass interference penalty on a pass to Nico Collins. Washington did, however, look good in run support, making tackles in the alley near the line of scrimmage. Grade: B Special teams Dominic Zvada missed a 58-yard field goal in the first quarter that would have given the Giants a touchdown lead. Zvada then missed a 44-yard field goal that would have given the Giants a 17-14 lead at halftime. The shakiness of the rookie kicker is more than evident at this point and changes must be considered. Jordan Stout flipped the field after the Giants went three-and-out at the start of the second quarter. He booted the football 62 yards. Stout’s second punt only netted 23 yards after McCarthy took a sack, knocking the Giants out of Zvada FG range; it was a makeable kick, but the rookie had already missed two. Stout pinned the Texans down at the 14 yard line. Would like a better kick, but it’s difficult to really hold Stout’s feet to the fire when the decision was made because of Zvada’s ineffectiveness. Nevertheless, it’s all special teams. Tank Dell had a 14-yard return after Stout punted the ball 48 yards from his own goal line. Houston started their drive in plus territory with just over five minutes to go, down by seven. The Giants gained just 17 yards on their kick return with 46 seconds left in the game, giving McCarthy the football at the 20-yard line. The special teams weren’t too special against the Texans. Grade: D

full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 12: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Las Vegas Raiders runs the ball during a game against the New York Jets at Allegiant Stadium on November 12, 2023 in Las Vegas, Nevada. This loss came against a Dolphins team that had never held a lead at any point in the season prior to today. Today the Dolphins never trailed. It was a humiliating performance by the Jets. The horrendous Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-5 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Now the Jets look to get back on the winning track as they stay home to take on the 3-4 Las Vegas Raiders in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Raiders have lost four straight games after starting the season 3-0. Their latest loss came at the hands of the Los Angeles Rams by a 35 – 21 score. The Raiders’ defense has collapsed in their four game losing streak, surrendering 30+ points in each of the four games. With the Raiders making the long trip east for this game and suffering through the early game start, on paper this looks like a get well game for the Jets. title: Jets vs Dolphins: Dolphins Deal Disgraceful Jets Humiliating Loss
summary: In the New York Jets’ seventh game of the 2026 season, on a gorgeous, warm and sunny day in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Jets lost to the Miami Dolphins, 28 – 25. The game opened with the Jets on defense. It did not go well. The Dolphins marched right down the field, mixing runs […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Michael Taaffe #16 of the Miami Dolphins and teammates celebrate his second quarter interception against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the New York Jets’ seventh game of the 2026 season, on a gorgeous, warm and sunny day in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Jets lost to the Miami Dolphins, 28 – 25. The game opened with the Jets on defense. It did not go well. The Dolphins marched right down the field, mixing runs and passes effectively against a Jets defense that provided only token resistance. A few minutes into the first quarter Malik Willis connected with Caleb Douglas in the end zone for an early 7 – 0 Dolphins lead. It was the first lead the Dolphins have had all season. The Jets quickly struck back. A long catch and run to Omar Cooper got the Jets within striking distance of the end zone. A couple of plays later Geno Smith found Mason Taylor in the end zone and the game was tied at 7 – 7 midway through the first quarter. The Dolphins stormed back with a 14 play drive, having their way with a Jets defense that couldn’t do anything against an offense that was one of the worst in the NFL before they faced the Jets. The Dolphins eventually ran the ball in for a 14 – 7 lead as the first quarter drew to a close. On the next Jets drive the Jets moved the ball well before Geno Smith threw a damaging red zone interception. This was not a promising start to a game the Jets needed to win. Neither team could get much going on offense for most of the second quarter until the Dolphins put together another long, punishing drive late. With six seconds left in the half Malik Willis ran the ball in for a touchdown and a 21 – 7 Dolphins lead going into the locker room. The Jets were on the precipice of a humiliating loss to a winless Dolphins team. The Jets opened the third quarter on offense. They had some success running the ball and drove down inside the Dolphins’ 25 yard line before the drive bogged down. Jason Sanders doinked a field goal attempt off the uprights and the Jets came away without any points. After the Jets held the Dolphins without any points on the next drive, the Jets took over on offense and drove down the field. The drive was highlighted by a long catch and run to Omar Cooper, and ended when Geno Smith found Cooper in the end zone a few plays later. The score was now Dolphins 21, Jets 14 and the Jets had some life with a little less than six minutes remaining in the third quarter. The third quarter ended with the Jets on offense and the score still 21 – 14 in favor of the Dolphins. The Jets got the ball all the way inside the Dolphins’ one yard line with a first and goal. They then proceeded to go backwards on each of the next three plays before settling for a short field goal. It was a failure at the goal line that had the potential to cost the Jets the game. The score was now Dolphins 21, Jets 17 with nine minutes left in the game. After the Jets and Dolphins exchanged fruitless drives the Dolphins got the ball and scored on a long catch and run pass to Caleb Douglas. The score was Dolphins 28, Jets 17 and that blown opportunity with first and goal at the one yard line was looming large for the Jets with less than five minutes left in the game. The Jets put together a nice drive ending in a touchdown pass to Mason Taylor with a little more than three minutes left in the game. Mason Taylor caught the two point conversion pass and the Jets trailed 28 – 25. The Jets never got the ball back. On a 4th and one with two minutes left and the Jets with no timeouts, the Jets were unable to stop the Dolphins from converting. The Dolphins ran out the clock and the Jets lost a game at home to a team that had never held a lead this season prior to today. Final score: Dolphins 28, Jets 25 . The loss brought the Jets’ record to 2-5. Any realistic playoff hopes are gone, as the Jets would probably need an 8-2 finish to secure playoff berth. Based on what we’ve seen to date, does anyone believe the Jets have that kind of run in them? The Jets stay home next week to take on a surprisingly competitive Las Vegas Raiders team, looking to not embarrass themselves.

full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 07: Tyrel Dodson #25 of the Miami Dolphins intercepts a pass intended for Mason Taylor #85 of the New York Jets during the first quarter at MetLife Stadium on December 07, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week the New York Jets failed to take advantage of an opportunity to get to .500 on the season and move into 2nd place in the AFC East when they lost a close game to the New England Patriots. The Jets got to within a touchdown with more than seven minutes remaining in the game. Then the Patriots, behind a makeshift offensive line missing most of their starters, put together a soul crushing, clock crunching, game sealing drive in which they basically ran the ball right down the Jets’ throats, and the Jets were helpless to stop it. It was a humiliating end to a pretty good overall performance by the Jets. The loss gave the Jets a 2-4 record on the season. Today the Jets are home at MetLife Stadium as they try to get back on the winning track against a winless Miami Dolphins team. Kickoff is scheduled for shortly after 1 PM EDT. The Dolphins have had a challenging schedule to start the 2026 season. They have yet to face a team with a losing record. The Jets will be their first such opponent. Coming off a tough loss against a division rival, the Jets could be set up for a letdown against the Dolphins. It’s up to the coaches and players to make sure that doesn’t happen. The Dolphins have dismantled the Jets on a regular basis in recent years. They have won 16 of the last 20 games played between these two teams. If the Jets want to compete for a playoff spot that will need to change. The Dolphins are a team in the midst of a clear tank. The Jets are the better, more talented team, and they are getting back close to full strength after a string of injuries hurt the team in the early part of the season. Can the Jets take care of business at home today? We’ll find out soon enough. It’s the Jets and the Dolphins in game 7 of the 2026 season. Enjoy the game everyone.

title: Jets vs Dolphins Pre-Game Ball
summary: Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - OCTOBER 18: Kenyon Sadiq #16 of the New York Jets checks with the line judge as Omar Cooper Jr. #11 and Tim Patrick #17 join during a game between the New England Patriots and the New York Jets on October 18, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit. One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it. The Jets pre-game ball for the Jets game against the Miami Dolphins goes to (drum roll please) – Kenyon Sadiq! The Dolphins have played pretty good run defense this season. Pass defense, on the other hand, has been a problem. The Dolphins have allowed an atrocious 115 passer rating against them this season, second worst in the NFL. They have allowed 11 passing touchdowns in five games, They have sacked opposing quarterbacks just four times all season, by far the fewest in the NFL. This is a bad Dolphins pass defense. Much of the damage has been done by opposing tight ends. With the Jets having all their primary weapons in the passing game on the field this week for the first time since early in the game on opening day, there will be opportunities for many Jets receivers to have a big game. It could be Garrett Wilson or Omar Cooper or Adonai Mitchell, but I’m going with Kenyon Sadiq. In five games opposing tight ends have combined for 381 yards and three touchdowns against the Dolphins. Sadiq could have a field day if Frank Reich stops playing inferior tight ends ahead of him. This is a game the Jets should win. They are the more talented team. They are better on offense and on defense. The Dolphins running game will likely give the Jets defense some problems, but overall the Jets should have their way against a Dolphins team that has failed to score more than 13 points in all but one game this year and has allowed 24+ points in all but one game this year. Kenyon Sadiq is an uber talented tight end playing against a Dolphins team that has struggled mightily against tight ends. If Frank Reich remembers that, Sadiq should feast on Sunday. Kenyon Sadiq, come on down! It’s time to make people remember what you’re capable of. You get your opportunity on Sunday. Let’s see you run with it. What about you? Who would you give the pre-game ball to? Let us know in the comments.

title: Eagles News: Will Howie Roseman sell ahead of the NFL trade deadline?
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! If the Eagles go 0-3 in three straight division games coming up to drop to 2-7 overall, it’ll be safe to say the season is over … if it’s not already. If the Eagles reach that point, it’s hard not to […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JULY 29: Philadelphia Eagles Executive Vice President and General Manager Howie Roseman reacts during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on July 29th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! If the Eagles go 0-3 in three straight division games coming up to drop to 2-7 overall, it’ll be safe to say the season is over … if it’s not already. If the Eagles reach that point, it’s hard not to think Howie Roseman will be selling. But it’s hard to envision a full on fire sale. He’s not going to trade players unless the price is right. Roob’s Observations: Why a Howie Roseman trade deadline sell-off is unlikely – NBCSP WHY MAJOR HOWIE MOVES ARE UNLIKELY: I keep hearing about all the players Howie is going to unload before the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10. Guys like Saquon Barkley, Moro Ojomo, Zack Baun, Riq Woolen, Landon Dickerson and Dallas Goedert. Basically, older players who may not fit into the Eagles’ future or players on the final year of their contract situation who may be unsignable. Don’t count on it. While a sell-off is possible if this thing continues to spiral, there’s two important things to remember. First of all, you’re never going to trade a player for less or equal what he might bring you in the comp pick equation. Moro Ojomo for example is probably going to bring you a 3 rd -round comp pick and you’re not going to get a 2 nd -rounder for him. Howie Roseman values picks the same whether they’re a year later, so he’d rather have a comp 3 rd -round pick in 2028 than a 4 th -round pick in 2027. The second thing to remember is that in the current NFC East landscape, there’s a chance the Eagles will still be in the playoff race when the trade deadline arrives on Nov. 10. They have the Cowboys, Commanders and Giants before the deadline, combined record 6-10-1. And 0-7-1 vs. teams with a winning record. So as grim as things look right now, they look just as grim for everyone else in the division, and if the Eagles win two of these next three Howie isn’t going to start selling off pieces at 4-5. He owes it to Jeff Lurie and the players and coaches and the city to keep the team intact if the Eagles are in contact with the division leaders. And the way things are going, it’s going to be hard not to be. Nobody likes to make trades more than Howie. But he likes to be in the playoffs even more. And he’s not going to unload any significant pieces while the Eagles still have any chance to win the division. Eagles Film Preview: Cowboys offense surprisingly difficult to project – BGN The Cowboys were a surprisingly difficult offense to break down this week. I watched the Texans game and saw an offense that could protect its quarterback and find plenty of ways to get the ball to its best players. Then I watched the Packers game and wondered where all of that had gone. This is still a talented offense, and I can’t shake the feeling that it will come together at some point. However, I thought the Cowboys were more creative last year, and their coaching staff isn’t getting enough from this group right now. With everything going on with the Eagles’ offense, the defense needs to play well if this team has any chance. There are opportunities to disrupt the Cowboys, but there is also enough talent here to make this a very uncomfortable matchup. Five Eagles thoughts: Jalen Hurts’ future, Tanner McKee’s present, and exploring a trade-deadline selling scenario – PHLY Eagles Saquon Barkley: This is possibly the trickiest one. There’s a compelling argument for getting value for Barkley if the season truly goes sideways. He’s 29 years old and still the type of player a real contender would likely view as the final piece for a title push. Do the Eagles view him as an important part of a potential turnaround in 2028 and beyond? He’s under contract through 2029 if so, but getting out of a significant investment at the running back position makes some sense to me. I’d say yes, but certainly not for a discount. Dallas Goedert: Leaning yes. He’s only under contract through this season and has been seeking a better deal for multiple years now. If a contending team offers an early-Day-3 pick, wouldn’t it make sense to clear the way for Eli Stowers to get some developmental snaps? NFL Week 7 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more – ESPN Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers — Tanner McKee, QB, Philadelphia Eagles (4.6%). McKee is an intriguing sleeper with quarterback Jalen Hurts out for the season (blood clots). He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers last week and now faces a Cowboys defense that has allowed 21.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks (fifth most in the league). Dallas has also given up 11 passing touchdowns this season. McKee attempted 45 passes last week, and he has the targets to reach the end zone with DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert (both questionable to play). He’s worth considering in deeper single-QB leagues and as a QB2 in superflex formats. NFL Week 7 picks: Upset and score predictions, matchup breakdowns for every game – NFL.com Why Bobby picked the Cowboys: Because Dallas simply has to win. The Eagles surely feel the same way, but they aren’t nearly as close to full strength as the Cowboys — and probably won’t be for the rest of the season now that Jalen Hurts is out due to blood clots. For as bad as the past two weeks have been for the Cowboys, they feel like a safer pick to turn things around in a division that is wide open. Dallas has been disappointing, but the Eagles have been in such disarray during the month of October that offensive lineman Jordan Mailata reflected on Week 5 as the “week from hell,” only to realize midweek last week that he “might have jumped the gun” describing it as such after problems continued to pile up. Since then, the Eagles lost their fourth straight and the aforementioned news on Hurts dropped, so be on the lookout for Mailata’s latest re-evaluation of how low things can go. In a battle between Tanner McKee and Dak Prescott, I choose Prescott, who is due for a turnaround performance. He’s too good and surrounded by too many weapons to stay in a rut. Considering the Commanders are on a bye and the Giants are facing a resurgent Texans squad, the NFC East’s winless stretch could very well run from Oct. 5 through Oct. 25, rectified at long last by Dallas in prime time. From Cowboy to Eagle, Joe Milton III finds himself on the other side of the rivalry – PhiladelphiaEagles.com “I definitely learned a lot over there,” Milton said. “Development-wise, it’s going great. It’s amazing. I love to learn. Taking notes again and learning the new offense.” Part of the Cowboys’ practice squad this year, Milton was surprised when his agent called him before practicing last week and said that the Eagles wanted to sign him. “Just because it is a rivalry and it was just like, ‘Dang, no way.’ My agent called me and mentioned it to me. … I went to practice like it was a normal day and tried to operate under a Dallas Cowboy at the time,” Milton said. ”I went home, but really when I got in my car, everything’s just changed. I was just like, ‘What am I going to do? Am I going to stay on the practice squad or should I show up for my opportunity?’ I’m here.” NFLPA has yet to launch “full investigation” of Jalen Hurts situation – PFT Hurts has a potential lawsuit against the doctors who provided his care, independent of any more limited rights against the Eagles or the league. While it could get complicated — especially if Hurts may have to file a lawsuit in the U.S. and in England — a “superficial” blood clot in his leg resulting from being cleated during the Week 4 game against the Rams became a deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in each lung. It’s fair for…

full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: DeVonta Smith #6, Makai Lemon #9, and Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final injury report of the week on Saturday in advance of their Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles ruled four players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Nolan Smith, and Michael Carter II. Smith missed practice all week due to a hamstring injury while Wicks missed practice all week due to an ankle injury. The Eagles being without their top two wide receivers certainly isn’t ideal. The team will roll with Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore, Hollywood Brown, and Britain Covey. The Cowboys’ defense is so bad that these players could still have chances to succeed on Monday night. Smith missed practice all week while in the concussion protocol. He might be able to return in Week 8. Carter II has been unavailable since getting injured in Week 5. The Eagles will go with Andrew Mukuba and Cooper DeJean as their top two safeties in base packages with Kenny Moore playing on the back end of the defense in nickel formations. The Eagles ruled seven players QUESTIONABLE: Saquon Barkley, Landon Dickerson, Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Eli Stowers, Grant Calcaterra, and Jakorian Bennett. Barkley was full go on Saturday after being limited on Thursday and Friday. It sure seems like he’s going to give it a go on Monday night. Dickerson was a full participant in Saturday’s practice. Seems like the Eagles will activate him from injured reserve to start at left guard. If so, it will be interesting to see how he fares after he really did not look great in Week 1. Greenard did not practice on Friday or Saturday after being listed as limited on Thursday. He talked about being a game-time decision. Even if Greenard does suit up, he’ll likely be on a pitch count. Not great. Hunt was limited in practice all week. With the Eagles looking thin at edge rusher, it would be nice if he can play. We’ll see. The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Monday to activate any or all of Dickerson, Stowers, Calcaterra, and Bennett from injured reserve in order to play against the Cowboys. The team has some open roster spots to fill, so, we’ll see how they handle things. title: Steelers finally find success on third down in win over Saints
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense wasn’t a fireworks show against the New Orleans Saints, it was a cement truck. Pittsburgh out rushed New Orleans 148-18 and averaged just under five yards per carry. This efficiency in the run game allowed the Steelers to establish long drives of eight, 13, 11, 14, and 11 plays. The Steelers […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense wasn’t a fireworks show against the New Orleans Saints, it was a cement truck. Pittsburgh out rushed New Orleans 148-18 and averaged just under five yards per carry. This efficiency in the run game allowed the Steelers to establish long drives of eight, 13, 11, 14, and 11 plays. The Steelers had just one three-and-out on the day, which was a welcome change from the five they had against the Buccaneers. A big part of establishing those long drives was their efficiency on third down. Pittsburgh entered the week as the NFL’s worst team on third down in terms of EPA per play, and they were 28th in conversion percentage. On Sunday, Pittsburgh converted a season-high 10 third downs on 16 attempts. Their biggest play of the game came on 3rd-and-14 when Aaron Rodgers extended the play and found DK Metcalf for a 51-yard completion, which set up the Darnell Washington touchdown. The run game working so well helped the Steelers stay within a respectable distance on those third downs, as their average play on third down was under six yards, per Sumer Sports . With the majority of those plays being 3rd-and-short or 3rd-and-medium, this allowed Pittsburgh to run on a good chunk of their third down plays. Ahead of Week 7, the Steelers didn’t run the ball on third down more than three times – they did so seven times on Sunday and converted six of them into first downs, which doubled their previous season-high of three rushes for first downs on third down. There were points left on the board, and Aaron Rodgers said as much after the game. They were unable to finish two drives in which they made it to the red zone and had to settle for field goals, and another drive reached the Saints’ 29 yard-line that also ended with a field goal. However, it’s much better to see that while still being 5-2 and in first place in the division than it would be had they found a way to lose to New Orleans. The scoreboard may not have been pretty, but the way they got there was beautiful – running the ball well, succeeding on third down, and sustaining long drives. Those are the characteristics of an efficient offense, and you can beat just about anybody if you can do that on a consistent basis. Let us know what you think in the comments .
