Should the 49ers manage to win, they will head into their bye week at 7-0 and maintain their modest 3-game (at least—depending […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Jordan Elliott #92 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates making a stop with teammates during the second half of an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers’ injuries keep coming, and they keep winning anyway. Now they go into Week 7 with their most injury-depleted wide receiver room yet and travel to face the Atlanta Falcons. Should the 49ers manage to win, they will head into their bye week at 7-0 and maintain their modest 3-game (at least—depending on what happens Sunday night) lead in the NFC West. At the same time, even the 49ers have to give up a game at some point, and the Falcons may have the makings of a trap game. This will be a morning game on FOX with the dreaded 10:00 AM start time. Kenny Albert will handle play-by-play, while Greg Olsen will provide color. The 49ers are playing on a shortened week after beating the Washington Commanders 23-17 on Monday Night Football. The recap is simple: The 49ers offense showed up in the first half, and then the defense saved everyone’s bacon in the closing seconds. The Commanders could have stolen that game had the defense not stepped it up in the final seconds, or Malik Mustapha wasn’t flying around the field laying the wood. Where did things go sideways? It can be pinpointed to when wide receiver Mike Evans went into the locker room. Once that happened, the 49ers offense took a step backwards. At the end of the day, the 49ers defensive line, without Nick Bosa, stepped up and made some plays to save the game and put the 49ers up 6-0. They won, but these injuries make them increasingly vulnerable. The Falcons appeared to be looking like a sleeper team after their Week 3, 35-14 victory over the Green Bay Packers. They followed it up in Week 4 with a 45-24 thumping of the New Orleans Saints. Some were saying this was a possible playoff team thanks in part to their running game led by running back Bijan Robinson. During this two-game stretch, it was argued he may be the best running back in the league. Unfortunately, both the Packers and Saints had losing records entering those games. After those victories came losses to the Baltimore Ravens and Chicago Bears—two teams that entered their games against the Falcons with a winning record and two teams Robinson failed to amass at least 100 yards rushing against. The Bears in particular held the Falcons to seven points until the fourth quarter. The offense goes through Robinson and if the 49ers can find a way to slow him down, that seems to be the key to defeating the Falcons. Could this be a trap game? The 49ers are favored by only 2.5 points on the road and have injuries that somewhat level the playing field. Evans’ injury in the aforementioned Monday Night game was revealed to be Achilles soreness, which will keep him out for this game. Like Robinson, the offense runs through Evans, so this is a major blow. They did get some help with activating wide receiver Christian Kirk; he’ll make his season debut against Atlanta . Evans, as we’ve said, is out. This is along with Nick Bosa (calf), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), safety Marques Sigel (ankle), linebacker Luke Gifford (groin), and linebacker Garret Wallow (hamstring). Special teamer Siran Neal and cornerback Upton Stout are questionable. Should the 49ers get through this week, they can enter the BYE and get some much-needed rest for the second half-ish of their schedule. In a strange twist, the Falcons injury report is longer than the 49ers though the names of players out for Sunday are not on the level of people like Evans and Bosa. Out for the Falcons is running back Brian Robinson Jr., linebacker Divine Deablo, defensive back Billy Bowman Jr., and offensive tackle Michael Jerrell. title: Buccaneers Week 7 Top Performers at Carolina Panthers
summary: The Buccaneers’ season might still amount to nothing, but on Sunday they showed plenty of fight is left in the roster. Tampa looked dominant from the get-go in a must-win contest against a hated division foe, as the Bucs marched down for an opening-drive touchdown and proceeded to blast the Carolina Panthers with both barrels […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 25: Zyon McCollum #27 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers reacts after a play during the second half of a football game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buccaneers’ season might still amount to nothing, but on Sunday they showed plenty of fight is left in the roster. Tampa looked dominant from the get-go in a must-win contest against a hated division foe, as the Bucs marched down for an opening-drive touchdown and proceeded to blast the Carolina Panthers with both barrels in a 43-13 flogging. It’s easily the best all three phases have looked in a single game in an entire calendar year. The Bucs looked controlled and focused on offense and vicious and unrelenting on defense. The ground game flourished with nearly 26o rushing yards, and defense and specials teams forced four turnovers and scored 9 points (more on that later). We need to see more results like this stacked together before making any claims about significant progress, but there’s no doubt it’s exactly the kind of game the team needed to reignite their spirit. Time to dole out plenty of praise! Offensive Top Performer: RB Bucky Irving I could really just put the entire run-game operation in the header, but it all started with Bucky ripping the Panthers to shreds from the jump. Irving became the first player this season to notch 10+ touches and a touchdown in a single drive when he carried the Bucs to an opening score. He did his part to keep the pressure on, totaling 24 carries for 106 yards and 2 touchdowns. Bucky Irving put the team on his back 💪 🏈 11 touches on 14 plays 👏 47 rushing yards 🙌 1 touchdown 📺: #TBvsCAR on FOX pic.twitter.com/zfBBLQ2JLs — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) October 25, 2026 Kenny Gainwell got his licks in too, toting the rock 14 times for 88 yards — including a highlight-reel 29-yard scamper. Easily his best game as a Buccaneer. Sean Tucker put the finishing touches on the day with an easy 46-yard touchdown jaunt. The driving force behind all of it was the offensive line, which completely brutalized the Panthers front 7 all day long. An overall yards per run average of 5.3 on 49 carries (and that’s with 2 Jalon Daniels kneeldowns) will get the job done most days. It couldn’t have been a more ideal return to the field for Baker Mayfield, who barely needed to test his healing thumb. He threw 11 passes…total…and completed 7 for 64 yards and a score. Extremely limited sample, but he looked more calm in the pocket and made some nice early plays out of structure. He’ll get tested more against an aggressive Falcons pass rush next week, but good first step back. Baker Mayfield scrambles and finds Tez Johnson in the end zone 🔥 TBvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uK061HPeSd — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Defensive Top Performer: EDGE Yaya Diaby Same kind of deal as above. I could put the entire pass rush up here but we’ll give the big bouquet to Diaby, who’s been slow to start hunting the quarterback this season but looked dominant Sunday with 3 out of the Bucs’ 5 sacks on the day. How did Yaya Diaby still make this sack? TBvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/WGfJpnx47b — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 Diaby led a unit that didn’t let Young get comfortable through any of the 3 quarters the latter played. He finished 14-of-27 for only 163 yards, 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions. Vita Vea logged a sack, as did Al-Quadin Muhammad (who also forced a fumble on his). David Walker created good pressure on his snaps once again, and Rueben Bain pushed the pocket on multiple rushes as well. Back-to-back banner weeks for the remade pass-rushing unit. Young got forced into three turnovers — one fumble, which Calijah Kancey returned for a touchdown, and two picks by Zyon McCollum and Tykee Smith — to completely turn the tide of the game and ensure the Panthers couldn’t establish any consistent rhythm with its talented receiver duo of Tet McMillan and Jalen Coker. Calijah Kancey with the scoop and score 🗣️ TBvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Qz80nMfjih — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 The whole defense looked disciplined, aggressive, and focused, and it’s generally been an upper-tier unit this season when it’s not needing to get critical stops. Maybe we’ll finally see tangible progress. Special Teams Top Performer: CB Zyon McCollum You know everything is turning up aces when the Bucs are even generating impact special teams plays. In this instance, Tampa immediately dampened a Panthers touchdown by blocking the extra point, which caromed right into McCollum’s grasp. He proceeded to race end to end and secure the Buccaneers’ first-ever two-point special teams return in franchise history, which essentially resulted in the Panthers getting only a 4-point touchdown. An extra sweetener for McCollum considering what he also did on defense. Something you NEVER see: A blocked PAT turns into Zyon McCollum's 2-pointer. pic.twitter.com/p268pVNAky — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 25, 2026 It would’ve made a big difference in closely contested game, but even in a blowout it still served as important tone-setting moment in a snowballing string of them. The Bucs also recovered a muffed kick which set up another offensive score. All things considered, I’m sure Chase McLaughlin happily took the reduced responsibility (he still recorded a perfect day with 2 field goals and 5 extra points).

title: NFL Week 7 Recap: Buccaneers dominate Panthers in 43-13 victory behind strong defensive performance
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered Sunday’s matchup against the Carolina Panthers desperately needing a victory. They responded with their most dominant performance of the season, cruising to a 43-13 win at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte. With quarterback Baker Mayfield returning to the starting lineup after missing three games due to a thumb injury, […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 25: Zyon McCollum #27 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers reacts after an interception during the first half of a football game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered Sunday’s matchup against the Carolina Panthers desperately needing a victory. They responded with their most dominant performance of the season, cruising to a 43-13 win at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte. With quarterback Baker Mayfield returning to the starting lineup after missing three games due to a thumb injury, Tampa Bay (2-5) established control early and never looked back. The Buccaneers’ rushing attack and opportunistic defense carried the way as Carolina (3-3) struggled to find answers throughout the afternoon. Tampa Bay wasted little time establishing its ground game, marching 70 yards on a 14-play opening possession that consumed more than seven minutes. Running back Bucky Irving carried much of the offensive workload, while Mayfield connected with wide receiver Tez Johnson for a key 19-yard completion on third-and-10. Irving eventually capped the drive with a four-yard touchdown run to give the Buccaneers an early 7-0 advantage. The Buccaneers’ defense forced Carolina to punt on its opening possession, and a special teams mistake late in the first quarter gave Tampa Bay another scoring opportunity. Panthers returner David Moore muffed a punt that was recovered by tight end Ko Kieft at Carolina’s 18-yard line. Although Tampa Bay couldn’t reach the end zone, Chase McLaughlin connected on a 22-yard field goal early in the second quarter to extend the lead to 10-0. Things quickly unraveled for Carolina from there. Following a sack by Yaya Diaby, linebacker Al-Quadin Muhammad stripped Panthers quarterback Bryce Young on the following play. Defensive tackle Calijah Kancey recovered the loose football and returned it 32 yards for a touchdown, pushing Tampa Bay’s lead to 17-0. Carolina briefly responded with a 50-yard touchdown pass from Young to tight end Darren Waller. However, even that scoring play came with a setback for the Panthers. Tykee Smith blocked the ensuing extra-point attempt, allowing cornerback Zyon McCollum to recover the football and return it for a defensive two-point conversion, making the score 19-6. The Buccaneers continued pounding the football on their next possession, with Kenneth Gainwell breaking free for a 29-yard run before Irving scored his second touchdown of the afternoon from one yard out. Tampa Bay’s defense delivered another opportunity before halftime when McCollum intercepted Young and returned the ball 18 yards to Carolina’s 32-yard line. Mayfield capitalized on the takeaway, finding Johnson for a 14-yard touchdown pass with 12 seconds remaining in the half. The Buccaneers entered the locker room with a commanding 33-6 advantage after scoring 26 points in the second quarter. Carolina’s offensive struggles continued after halftime as Diaby recorded two more sacks on the Panthers’ opening possession of the third quarter. The Buccaneers’ defense later forced another turnover when Smith intercepted Young near Carolina’s 32-yard line. Although Tampa Bay’s offense slowed considerably in the third quarter, McLaughlin added a 44-yard field goal to extend the lead to 36-6. The Panthers eventually put together a sustained drive deep into Buccaneers territory, but Tampa Bay’s defense stood firm. Facing fourth-and-1 at the Buccaneers’ five-yard line, Young threw an incomplete pass, turning the football over on downs. Tampa Bay carried its 30-point lead into the fourth quarter and continued controlling the clock with its ground game. The Buccaneers put together a nine-play, 94-yard drive that consumed more than six minutes, highlighted by a 46-yard touchdown run from Sean Tucker to increase the advantage to 43-6. Carolina added a late touchdown on a 12-yard run by Anthony Tyus III with backup quarterback Kenny Pickett leading the offense, but the outcome had long been decided. Irving finished with 106 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 24 carries, while Mayfield completed seven of 11 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown in his return. Tampa Bay’s defense recorded five sacks and intercepted Young twice, with Diaby leading the charge with three sacks. The Buccaneers will now look to build on the victory when they return home to face the Atlanta Falcons in another important NFC South matchup next Sunday.

title: Tyler’s Take – Is Commanders GM Adam Peters using Dan Quinn as his fall guy?
summary: It’s rare you see an NFL general manager say, “Yeah, that was on me. I messed up.” However rare, it’s very refreshing. Former Broncos general manager John Elway once admitted in an interview that his biggest mistake was passing on Josh Allen in the 2018 NFL Draft. Just this year Eagles general manager Howie Roseman […]
full_text: It’s rare you see an NFL general manager say, “Yeah, that was on me. I messed up.” However rare, it’s very refreshing. Former Broncos general manager John Elway once admitted in an interview that his biggest mistake was passing on Josh Allen in the 2018 NFL Draft. Just this year Eagles general manager Howie Roseman admitted to Sports Illustrated that trading a late-round pick for Andy Dalton was a mistake . These are small blips on the radar compared to the Vikings… General Manager Kwesi Adolfo-Mensah was fired by ownership less than 24 hours after he publicly admitted that letting Sam Darnold walk because they had drafted J.J. McCarthy was a mistake. Maybe the above is why Adam Peters has kept relatively quiet on his mistakes. Is Peters forcing “his guys” on the coaching staff? On Oct. 9, Commanders beat reporter Candi Waller tweeted this: #Commanders GM Adam Peters is the final decision maker on the roster, per HC Dan Quinn. Question asked by @BenStandig — Candi "CWall" Waller (@cwallse) October 9, 2026 From the outside, this tweet looks pretty innocuous. But a bit later, Candi followed up her original tweet with this: I promise I would not have even tweeted this if it didn’t matter folks. USE YOUR CLUES. https://t.co/FKCgfyC18k — Candi "CWall" Waller (@cwallse) October 9, 2026 So, the “USE YOUR CLUES” in all CAPS definitely raises some eyebrows. She then used this same phrase as a reply to many people who had quote-tweeted her original tweet. So, what does Candi know that the average fan may not? I think this is pretty obvious! Peters wants his draft picks to be successful. To be successful, they have to play. Coaches are the ones who decide who plays – PERIOD! No general manager should have a say in who plays and when and where they do. However, Candi may be suggesting that there are internal struggles between Peters and the coaching staff about who plays. My guess is a lot of this stemmed from the release of Kaytron “Fatman” Allen from the active roster but grew in lore with the benefit of some hindsight. Mike Sainristil , who had a good rookie year followed by a poor second season, began the year as a starter on the outside opposite Amik Robertson. After struggling mightily to begin the season, his reps slowly began decreasing week after week. Now he’s a reserve playing special teams. Tight end Ben Sinnott has seen a more prominent role as evidenced by his increase in snaps, however, he’s still not being targeted in the passing game. There COULD BE and SHOULD BE a time where the struggling left tackle Brandon Coleman is benched, but could Peters be behind his former 2024 third-round pick staying in the lineup? Another question begs to be asked: Did Adam Peters force Nick Allegretti on the coaching staff? Did he force HIS draft pick Matt Gulbin on Quinn at right guard when starting right guard Sam Cosmi first went out with a concussion, even though it was evident to even the most novice fan that Gulbin had NO BUSINESS being on the field? If Candi is correct with her tweet, I think you may have the answer to this question… Roster Mistakes Every general manager makes mistakes. Hell, if you have above a 60% hit rate on draft picks and top free agent acquisitions, you are considered a genius. The difference between a good general manager and a poor one is the ability to see your mistake and move on with a better plan. At this point, I don’t think Adam Peters has the ability to do so. He is still relying on the “aging vet” model that we saw him go to in 2025: Stefon Diggs (albeit a good signing) Austin Ekeler Craig Reynolds Van Jefferson Lucas Patrick (a necessary signing after the “Allegretti experiment”) Rasul Douglas Fabian Moreau Isaac Yiadom We’ve seen him lose two valuable running backs — one who was signed off the practice squad (Robert Henry Jr.), and Fatman, who was cut with hopes he’d revert to the practice squad but was claimed by the Dolphins. The “wonder boy” experiment at center this offseason is a move that should be investigated by ownership… Going into the season with limited depth along the offensive line has CRUSHED the team this far. The “staff” appears to finally be moving on from Sainristil as a starter, but you have to wonder how much Peters pushed back on this before realizing he’s not playable. Are Newton, Sinnott, Coleman and McCaffrey next? There is ZERO doubt in my mind that Adam Peters wants this to be his team and he probably views head coach Dan Quinn as a dead man walking, which is why he may be, as Candi subtly hints, meddling. Is Adam Peters using Dan Quinn as his “fall guy”? Does he TRULY believe his players are not the problem and it’s more on the coaches? Let us know in the comments below:

title: Why are you still optimistic about Jayden Daniels, Commanders chances?
summary: The Commanders are 1-4-1. That’s where we’re at after some tough one-score losses, quarterback injuries and, simply put, unacceptable game mismanagement. All, however, is not lost. A one-win team is still somehow in the divisional race considering how bad the other three teams are. Like, check the standings. The Giants have three wins in six […]
full_text: The Commanders are 1-4-1. That’s where we’re at after some tough one-score losses, quarterback injuries and, simply put, unacceptable game mismanagement. All, however, is not lost. A one-win team is still somehow in the divisional race considering how bad the other three teams are. Like, check the standings . The Giants have three wins in six chances entering Week 7, and that’s the target to shoot for. And the Giants have a quarterback controversy. The Eagles have lost Jalen Hurts and most of a previously excellent offensive line. And the Cowboys are struggling, a standard for the Jones era. So, despite the fact that it at times feels like Washington’s sky is falling, the Commanders can still pull out a division title. True freaking story. I’m in the former camp. I truly believe the Commanders can turn the corner. Here are a few reasons why. You’ll be able to follow the rationale, guaranteed. Here are some bullet points on why the Commanders can win the division. These aren’t detailed observations. They’re simply reasons to be optimistic starting with a Week 8 meeting with the Philadelphia Eagles coming off the bye. Jayden Daniels turns into JD5: The young quarterback can legit carry a team when he’s on one. The third-year pro is trying to find a balance between being a playmaker and an operator of David Blough’s system. There’s a fair belief that he’ll get there. If he can get on 2024’s level, Daniels can bring the Commanders to great heights. Odafe Oweh wakes up: The Commanders biggest free-agent purchase can get scorching hot collecting sacks — he did so last year — and this would be a great time to go on a run. The Commanders pass rush is essential to defensive success. That has been proven in the early going, with coverage unable to hold up for long. Play callers lessen their learning curves: The Commanders have a pair of rookie (NFL) play callers in offensive coordinator David Blough and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, and we’ve seen some mistakes in game planning and game-day game planning. Washington must be more consistent and help play to their players’ strengths moving forward. Here’s believing they can do that. Penalties get cleaned up: The Commanders have been plagued by penalties, especially the pre-snap variety that have wiped out some explosive/game-changing plays in games that went the other way. Fewer flags, especially all those false starts and illegal shifts. That should be something easy to fix. That’s why I think there’s optimism for better Commanders football after the bye. Let us know why you’re confidence remains high in the comments below:

title: Five Washington Commanders questions needing answers out of bye week
summary: The Commanders have one win in six attempts and yet remain in the NFC East race. Yep. That’s how bad their division is at this stage. It’ll remain so all season, especially with the injury hits and awful defense being played by the four teams battling for a title.   That gives the Commanders hope […]
full_text: The Commanders have one win in six attempts and yet remain in the NFC East race. Yep. That’s how bad their division is at this stage. It’ll remain so all season, especially with the injury hits and awful defense being played by the four teams battling for a title. That gives the Commanders hope when there would otherwise be none at this stage, especially with a 0-2-1 mark against their top NFC East rivals. That leaves the Commanders with some work to do coming out of the bye, with a series of wins vaulting them right back into the division race. “As difficult and frustrated as we are, there’s also a golden opportunity this year in our division, and it’s gonna take the whole year,” head coach Dan Quinn said in his Monday press conference . “And so, I think they know that, and they’re gonna fight their ass off every time to make sure, we’re gonna give ourselves the best chance to do that. “It’s my job as the coach to set the whole thing to say environment, strategy of how to go about taking that on after this bye, and I’m very much looking forward to doing it with these guys. Like, I absolutely believe in them.” The Commanders must play better in order to accomplish their end goal, with these five questions needing to be addressed as the season progresses: Will Jayden Daniels go on a heater? We’ve seen Jayden Daniels do some spectacular things during this young season. None of it, however, resulted in a win. The season’s only victory came during Week 3, when Marcus Mariota was at the helm against the Seattle Seahawks. Everything else has been in defeat, a stark contrast to how his rookie season worked out. The Commanders went 8-4 in one-score games during Daniels’ rookie campaign, largely due to Daniels’ heroics. The Commanders are 0-2-1 in one-score games that Daniels has played to this point, despite him playing well late in games. Those situations are often a crap shoot, though Daniels has the clutch gene. The Commanders will need him to turn the tides a bit, especially after a tie versus the New Yorks Giants and a loss to the 49ers where his lack of situational awareness cost his team dearly. Getting that right could help the Commanders stack some wins, which must happen right away against what is a relatively soft schedule. This season will hinge on how Daniels responds out of the bye week. If he’s the hero he can be, this campaign could get interesting. But his margin for error is so slim at this point. He must get hot and stay there for this Commanders season to stay interesting. Can Daronte Jones get the defense worked out? While this current Commanders defense won’t scare you, there’s clear potential in the scheme. The creativity within Daronte Jones’ pressure package is clear. It is reliant on three things: 1. Players must communicate quickly and communicate well, getting into the right call before the snap. 2. The back end must cover well in short spurts and sometimes without the bodies needed to do so. 3. The pass rush has got to get home. Washington has had issues with all three of those elements at times. It has also struggled dealing with opposing adjustments, making it vulnerable to second-half surges. Jones has tried to tighten communications and what the players must do to get into the right call. The Commanders must come out of the bye more impactful rushing the passer, while maintaining solid run defense, and preventing the explosive plays that have killed them to this point. Can Washington’s run game get going? Washington just put Bill Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve with a groin injury that has bothered him since the summer. That has impacted his efficiency throughout the season, even before this injury became public knowledge. That puts the onus on Rachaad White to crank things up. The overall rushing statistics look halfway decent thanks to quarterback runs, but the backs are only averaging just 3.64 yards per carry. That isn’t good enough. While it’s easy to point fingers at those carrying the football, the run blocking hasn’t been good. That’s especially true on the interior, the bedrock of any rushing scheme. You can’t live on the outside. Adam Peters acknowledged on @JunksRadio today that the Commanders' run game issues are at least somewhat based on run-blocking issues: "We need to get better, I don't think there's any skirting around that. We need to get better, we need to get more on the same page.. We're six… — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) October 23, 2026 Are there quick fixes for this problem? Probably not. The personnel up front is what it is at this point. The commitment to the run game is solid and steadfast. They’ve got to churn out tough yards and find the third-and-manageable situations that have alluded them to this point. And, if the traditional run game isn’t working, can a short passing game take its place at times? That’s up to the coordinator to find ways to move the ball on early downs and make sure those chains keep advancing. Will the pass rush pick up? The Commanders rank No. 21 with 1.8 sacks per game. They rank No. 13 with a 24% quarterback pressure rate, which is aided in part by the fact that they bring so many bodies. As we all know, the Vikings defense is the gold standard for a scheme largely based on what Brian Flores does up north, and Minnesota leads the league with a 36.7% pressure rate . That’s what Washington aspires to, but it’s not where they are. There’s a clear learning curve involved with the system and the Commanders should get better operating it. The real issue is on the back end. There’s no superhero coming to save that unit. That’s why Odafe Oweh , Dorance Armstrong and even Joshua Josephs must level and start hitting the quarterback with regularity. Can Dan Quinn make it through the season? There are people calling for Dan Quinn to be fired in-season. That reached a fever pitch after the brutal Week 5 tie that will be forever viewed as a game-management disaster and what not to do in moments of crisis. The fact Washington rallied versus the 49ers and heading into the bye affirmed owner Josh Harris’ preference to avoid in-season firings is a plus for letting Quinn see this through. It would take something wild to fire him now, like a complete meltdown over the next several weeks. Despite some fans’ desire to see Quinn go, that’s a worst-case scenerio. That’s less about Quinn and more about schematics on both sides of the ball. Continuity is required here. The schemes are good. The team needs to rep it out and become proficient at what they’re doing. Starting from scratch doesn’t help anyone, especially the quarterback. Keeping Quinn means keeping the coordinators and letting them cook.

The quarterback the Commanders will face that day is Tanner McKee, who went 26-of-45 for 215 yards, a touchdown, and no interceptions in Philadelphia’s 25-14 loss to Carolina last week. Washington will get another look at McKee when the Eagles play Dallas on Monday. They can watch for adjustments Philadelphia makes after his first start this season and how he responds to whatever the Cowboys throw at him. Washington also has the bye week to settle into the reality that Terry McLaurin will not be back this season. We’ll have to wait and see whether they use that time to develop a plan to get the other receivers more involved or if one receiver will shoulder Terry’s entire load. The time off should give Washington an edge, even though they entered the bye week at 1-4-1 and gained only 90 yards in the first half of their last game. If the offense comes out better prepared and the defense has an answer for the Eagles’ adjusted passing game, you’ll know the break was needed. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders’ Defense Has an NFL-Worst Problem Before Third Down Even Arrives Against the Washington Commanders, opposing offenses have a 49.7% success rate on 169 plays run on first down, ranking the defense last in the NFL, according to HB Analytics. Looking for a fix to that should have been near the top of defensive coordinator Daronte Jones’ to-do list during the bye. That percentage doesn’t mean opponents picked up a new set of downs on nearly half of those plays. Success rate measures whether a play improved the offense’s expected scoring outlook. A five-yard gain on first-and-10 leaves a team with plenty of options for its next call. Hold the same run to a yard or force an incompletion, and the offense has more work to do. Washington has time to settle on the calls it can execute consistently before it returns against Philadelphia on November 1. I’d make getting everyone set and playing fast the starting point for that plan. Jones needs his defense to win on first down more often and create the second-and-long situations it has handled well. title: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, chances for top pick, more

full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

 So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

title: NFL Week 7: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 7.
full_text:
The Sunday slate for Week 7 of the  2026 NFL season  kicked off in Paris between the Saints and the Steelers. Pittsburgh dominated in the run game, with Jaylen Warren leading the way on 18 carries for 101 yards, and the Steelers held off New Orleans in the NFL's first game in France.

 Later in the afternoon, the Buccaneers dominated the Panthers in QB  Baker Mayfield 's return, the Vikings remained undefeated and the Bengals handled business in Baltimore. 

 In the evening slate, the Broncos stole a win in Arizona, and the Lions outlasted the visiting Packers in a duel. The Seahawks finished things off Sunday night by handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season.

 Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Michael Florio also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

 Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

 
 Jump to: 
 KC-SEA |  LAR-LV |  GB-DET 
  DEN-ARI  |   NYG-HOU  |  TB-CAR 
 CLE-TEN  |  MIA-NYJ  |  SF-ATL 
 CIN-BAL  |  IND-MIN  |  PIT-NO 

 Catch up on Thursday's game: 
 NE-CHI 

 
 

 

 Seattle 20, Kansas City 3 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap  | Instant analysis 

 

 Seahawks 
 Was this a step in the right direction for Sam Darnold ? Darnold was rolling in the first half, completing 13 of his first 17 attempts for 178 yards and a touchdown, until he made another mistake that he can't make. His throw on second down into traffic in the back of the end zone during the final seconds of the first half was intercepted, costing Seattle at least three points heading into halftime. That was Darnold's eighth interception over the past five games. Overall, though, this was a better performance for the embattled quarterback (20-of-28 for 257 yards). He got the ball out quickly -- not getting sacked after taking five in each of the previous two games -- and extended plays when he had to.

 Key stat to know: Jaxon Smith-Njigba leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns. Per ESPN Research, he's the first player in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) with at least 850 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns in his team's first seven games of a season. His 129 receiving yards in the first half were the most in any half in his NFL career and the most in any half by a Seahawk since Tyler Lockett in 2020 (133 in the first half at Arizona).

 Best quote from the locker room:  Smith-Njigba on the Seahawks' mentality entering Sunday's game. "Our backs were against the wall. How we came out here as a brotherhood and fought ... the resiliency of our team is something special, and we're going to keep going." -- Brady Henderson 

 Next game: vs. Bears (Nov. 2, 8:15 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Chiefs 
 Should the Chiefs be looking to trade for receivers? Brett Veach, the Chiefs' general manager, should continue to be interested in acquiring another receiver ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline after the lack of production from the position Sunday. Without  Rashee Rice , who missed Sunday's game because of a strained right hamstring, and Tyquan Thornton , who is on the injured reserve list after having surgery to repair his dislocated left ankle, the Chiefs' receivers -- Xavier Worthy , rookie Cyrus Allen , Justin Watson , Andrew Armstrong and Jalen Royals -- produced only six receptions for 39 yards.

 Most surprising performance: Entering Sunday, the biggest spotlight was on running back Kenneth Walker III , who became the first Super Bowl MVP to play his former team the next season. Walker also began the week leading the league with 665 rushing yards. The Seahawks, who spent most of the game playing two deep safeties, never allowed Walker to rush for at least 10 yards on a single carry. Walker finished the game with just 36 yards on 14 carries. -- Nate Taylor 

 Next game: at Broncos (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Fantasy football takeaway: Patrick Mahomes ' fantasy struggles continued, as he scored a season-low six fantasy points. He threw for only 165 yards and has topped 250 passing yards once in his past four games, and has not thrown a touchdown in either of his past two games. Overall, he has averaged 12.4 fantasy points per game in his past four games and is not a must-start option at the moment. Fantasy managers might want to avoid next week's matchup against Denver if they have another viable QB option. -- Florio 

 

 

 L.A. Rams 35, Las Vegas 21 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Rams 
 Will leaning on Puka Nacua and tight ends be the Rams' offensive identity without Davante Adams ? Outside of Nacua, just one Rams wide receiver had a catch: Konata Mumpfield , for 15 yards. Instead, the Rams turned to their tight ends ( Davis Allen , Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee ) and their running backs ( Kyren Williams and Blake Corum ). It led to their highest-scoring game of the season. Most of the points came in the first half, when Los Angeles scored on four-straight possessions. The Rams will be without Adams, who injured a hamstring in Week 6, for another five to nine weeks.

 Key stat to know: After fumbling on the Rams' second drive of the second half, Williams has nine lost fumbles since becoming the Rams starter in 2023. According to ESPN Research, that is the most of any running back over the span. -- Sarah Barshop 

 Next game: vs. Chargers (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

 

 
 

 Raiders 
 Is the clock ticking on  Kirk Cousins ' time as a starter? Not necessarily. The Raiders have lost four straight and are below .500 for the first time this season. Sure, Cousins didn't have his best game overall. He missed open targets a fair amount of time, and his lack of mobility was noticeable. But he has not been the sole problem during his team's losing skid. He threw a pair of touchdowns in the fourth quarter, increasing his season total to 16. Cousins has his limitations, which are exposed when frequently blitzed, as he was Sunday. At the same time, he hasn't done anything major that's worth making a switch for No. 1 draft pick Fernando Mendoza .

 Trend to watch: Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard's seat might start feeling a bit warm. The Raiders have allowed 30-plus points for the fourth straight game. Since Week 3, Las Vegas is last in points (34) and total yards (405.4) allowed. Yes, the Raiders have gone against tough QBs. But that's not an excuse for their inability to generate consistent pressure or stop the run. -- Ryan McFadden 

 Next game: at Jets (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Fantasy football takeaway: In the Rams' first game without Adams, we saw more tight end usage from coach Sean McVay, but the key fantasy targets haven't changed. Nacua (21.8 points), Williams (18.1 points) and QB Matthew Stafford (17.5 points) led the way, while Corum (17.1 points) continues to provide solid flex value. -- Bowen 

 

 

 Detroit 20, Green Bay 17

title: National Tight Ends Day 2026: Davis Allen, Mason Taylor put on a show during holiday
summary: The fourth weekend in October means National Tight Ends Day, and the NFL's tight ends made sure to bring their best.
full_text:
Aside from Super Bowl Sunday, many NFL fans recognize another holiday that is specifically designated for a position.

 

 Sunday marked National Tight Ends Day, which is recognized league-wide to honor players at the position.

 The holiday dates back to 2018, when then- San Francisco 49ers tight end Garrett Celek caught an 11-yard touchdown from Jimmy Garoppolo . With possession of the ball, Celek was held by two defenders, whom he dragged into the end zone for the score.

 National Tight Ends Day was born.

 "We were on the sidelines after Celek's score when Jimmy asked, 'What is it, like National Tight Ends Day?'" 49ers tight end George Kittle said . "I was like, 'Yeah, it's National Tight Ends Day. It's a holiday. Tight ends all over the league are scoring touchdowns.' That's how it came to be. We just kind of rolled with it."

 The holiday has evolved from a day of recognition to a day of domination by the position. Here's a look at how tight ends celebrated the day on the gridiron this year.

 

 Trey McBride , Arizona Cardinals 

 Arizona was down 20-6 with 3:54 left in the third quarter. On second-and-goal, McBride stutter-stepped past his defender before finding open space into the end zone, where he caught a 7-yard touchdown pass from Jacoby Brissett . McBride finished with 10 receptions and 111 receiving yards.

 

 

 Darnell Washington , Pittsburgh Steelers 

 The mismatch was evident, and Washington immediately took advantage of it. The 6-foot-7, 264-pound tight end was defended by 5-foot-11 New Orleans Saints cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry . Washington called for the ball, and quarterback Aaron Rodgers threw a 4-yard pass, which Washington snagged with his left hand, barely catching the touchdown in the Steelers' 16-10 win in Paris.

 

 

 Davis Allen , Los Angeles Rams 

 Davis Allen, have yourself a day -- a holiday that is. The Rams' tight end scored the first points Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders . Quarterback Matthew Stafford found Davis in the end zone for an easy 6-yard touchdown pass.

 

 In the second quarter on first-and-goal, Allen blocked for Stafford and slipped toward the end zone for an easy reception for his second touchdown of the day.

 

 

 Kyle Pitts Sr ., Atlanta Falcons 

 Atlanta opened the dome against San Francisco, who jokingly created National Tight End Day. And for that day, Pitts made himself available. On first-and-goal at the beginning of the third quarter, Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . turned the corner and connected with Pitts for a 5-yard touchdown pass to give Atlanta a 19-14 lead over San Francisco. He also recorded five receptions for 22 yards.

 

 

 Mason Taylor , New York Jets 

 What better way to start a game on National Tight Ends Day than with a touchdown from a tight end? Such was the case for Taylor, who helped get the Jets' first points after they trailed by a touchdown early in the first quarter.

 Geno Smith found Taylor in the end zone despite tight coverage by Miami Dolphins cornerback Jason Marshall Jr . Taylor caught the 13-yard passing touchdown over Marshall's head and was fired up.

 

 Taylor caught a second touchdown in the fourth quarter, a 12-yard pass from Smith, and also scored on a 2-point conversion.

 

 

 Tucker Kraft , Green Bay Packers 

 Similar to Taylor, Kraft jump-started the Packers' offense. Down 7-0 to the Detroit Lions on third-and-9, quarterback Jordan Love scrambled to avoid a sack attempt and fired a 14-yard dart into the end zone. Kraft made a diving catch and then spiked the ball for Green Bay's first points of the game.

 

 

 Darren Waller , Carolina Panthers 

 You must feel a different type of swagger when you connect on a big play on your designated day. Down 17-0 in the second quarter, Waller turned on the jets to get behind the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' defense for a touchdown. Bryce Young launched a 50-yard pass and connected with Waller.

 

 

 T.J. Hockenson , Minnesota Vikings 

 Heading into "Sunday Night Football," Minnesota and Kansas City are the only teams in the league boasting an undefeated record. Hockenson kept the Vikings rolling Sunday. Down 10-6 to the Indianapolis Colts at the start of the fourth quarter, Hockenson darted left and caught a 5-yard pass from Kyler Murray . Hockenson was off-balance when he caught the ball and displayed his body control as he angled for a touchdown, which was a big play in the Vikings' 16-10 win.

title: Seahawks troll Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce to top NFL Week 7's petty posts
summary: The Seattle Seahawks' petty post at Taylor Swift and Kansas City Chiefs' Travis Kelce leads the way for NFL's Week 7 trolls.
full_text:
Handing a team its first loss of the season can be enough to rattle an opponent. But that wasn't enough for the Seattle Seahawks after they beat the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3  on "Sunday Night Football."

 

 Seattle's defense stymied Kansas City's offense, allowing just three points and 213 total yards. The Chiefs' three points are their fewest in a game started by quarterback Patrick Mahomes since Week 7 in 2021, according to ESPN Research.

 The Seahawks had a Taylor Swift-themed troll after the game, posting a friendship bracelet that spelled out: "Seahawks Win." The bracelet is a reference to Swift's fans making custom bracelets during her Eras Tour. Concertgoers would then trade them with each other .

 Travis Kelce attended a Swift show in July 2023 and attempted to give the pop star a bracelet with his number on it. The Chiefs tight end was unable to deliver it, but the two ended up starting their relationship two months later. They wed in July of this year.

 Seattle knew all about the lore and decided to poke fun at Swift and Kelce. It captioned the post: "End Game," which is the name of a track from Swift's 2017 album, "reputation."

 

 Here are the other top trolls from Week 7.

 

 Atlanta Falcons 29, San Francisco 49ers 20 
 The Atlanta Falcons ended the San Francisco 49ers ' undefeated season with a home victory.

 Michael Penix Jr . threw three touchdown passes and the Falcons scored 13 points off four turnovers to hand the 49ers their first blemish of the year.

 Afterward, Atlanta delivered a simple troll in its postgame caption. Referencing San Francisco's "Faithful to the Bay" motto, the Falcons instead wrote: "Faithful to the A," as in Atlanta.

 

 
 New York Giants 27, Houston Texans 21 
 It required overtime, but the New York Giants escaped Houston with a big win over the Texans .

 Houston seemed to have momentum after a late touchdown that forced OT. But New York's defense responded immediately, forcing a three-and-out by Houston on their first possession. After a big Cam Skattebo 42-yard rush, Devin Singletary  scampered 30-yards for the game-winning touchdown.

 The saying goes "everything is bigger in Texas," and New York applied it to its postgame trolling.

 It first referenced Houston's "battle red" uniforms with the caption: "left them on red." The Giants also paired an image of SpongeBob SquarePants' body morphed into a Texas silhouette and captioned the post: "Wins are bigger in Texas." Even the Texas grocery store H-E-B caught a stray as the Giants put a spin on the logo by spelling out "W-I-N."

 

 
 Cleveland Browns 27, Tennessee Titans 24 
 Another late drive from the Cleveland Browns led to another victory.

 Cleveland and the Tennessee Titans were tied at 24 when the Browns got the ball back with 58 seconds left. Four plays later, Andre Szmyt kicked a 32-yard field goal to win the game. It capped off the fifth game-winning drive for Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson this season -- the most by a Browns quarterback in a single season this century, according to ESPN Research.

 Playing in Nashville, home of the famous Broadway Street, Cleveland advertised a new addition to the neighborhood: the "Dawg Pound Saloon."

 

 

 Los Angeles Rams 35, Las Vegas Raiders 21 

 The Los Angeles Rams are back in the win column after a dominant road victory over the Las Vegas Raiders.

 Los Angeles held a 28-6 halftime lead following four straight touchdown drives to end the half. Quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns -- two of which went to tight end Davis Allen. Raiders signal caller Kirk Cousins threw for 295 yards and two scores as the team dropped its fourth consecutive game.

 The Rams referenced Las Vegas' casinos with an image of a Rams-themed slot machine that included three Rams logos to signal a "Win." And instead of "Viva Las Vegas" in the caption, it was: "Viva Los Angeles."

 

 

 Detroit Lions 20, Green Bay Packers 17 

 A wild ending resulted in a huge win for the Detroit Lions against the Green Bay Packers .

 The Packers seemed primed to go ahead with 3:25 left in the game. However, their 35-yard field goal was blocked, keeping the score tied at 17. The Lions took advantage by keeping possession and kicking a field goal to win as time expired. The game was close throughout, as each team scored a touchdown in the first and third quarters. Lions quarterback Jared Goff had 303 passing yards and two scores, while Packers quarterback Jordan Love threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns.

 After defeating its division rival, Detroit made sure to poke fun at Green Bay. The Lions posted an image of kicker Jake Bates and wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa celebrating with the caption: "say cheese," a nod to Wisconsin's famous dairy industry and Packers fans calling themselves "cheeseheads."

full_text:
Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback room set the fashion standard high Sunday in Paris, simulating European-style looks from their favorite show "Peaky Blinders" with three-piece suits and flat caps. 
 
 

 The idea spawned from backup quarterback Mason Rudolph , who reached out to clothing designer Mitch Purgason to have the suits custom-made for this game.

 Rudolph explained that the Steelers quarterback room bonds over "Peaky Blinders." The show is extremely British, not French. But Rudolph's idea was to lean into United Kingdom experience and display with energy that they connect with personally.

 Purgason said he flew up to Pittsburgh to custom-fit the Steelers quarterback room 13 days ago, then he and his associate stylist, Rachel Leskowsky, went to work making the suits in about nine days. Purgason then flew up to hand-deliver the fits last minute before their flight to Paris.

 The work is worth it for looks as clean as the Steelers quarterback room. They posed for pregame pictures in Paris, and it exuded boss energy. Will this lead to more NFL positional groups leaning into translating their personal connection niche into fashion?

 Here are Week 7's most fashionable NFL player gameday fits that caught our eye:

 

 Sunday's best 
 A return game for Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III on "Sunday Night Football" prompted a simple, yet sleek outfit. He wore all-white ahead of his first game against the Seattle Seahawks since signing with Kansas City in the offseason. His fellow teammates, Patrick Mahomes , Travis Kelce , Chris Jones and L'Jarius Sneed , all rocked suits.

 

 It was tracksuits galore in the afternoon slate, with Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald styling a black look with a pair of shades. Meanwhile, Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby broke out a white jumpsuit, showing off his ink with an unzipped jacket. 
 
 
 
Though Sunday marked a holiday in National Tight Ends Day, that didn't stop Rodgers and the Steelers quarterback room from channeling their inner "Peaky Blinders" in Paris with coordinated suits, boots, flat cap and all. 
 
 

 

 
Thursday's looks 
 Caleb Williams kept it sharp ahead of "Thursday Night Football," pairing a navy suit with a black crewneck shirt. The Chicago Bears quarterback skipped the tie but not the wired earbuds. Naturally, he had his matcha drink in one hand and a structured brown leather bag in the other.

title: NFL execs, coaches rank the league's top five MVP candidates entering Week 7
summary: Brock Purdy? Josh Allen? Or maybe even a non-QB? Sixteen execs and coaches voted on the top five contenders for the MVP award through six weeks.
full_text:
We're already one game into Week 7 . And with more than a third of the 2026 NFL regular season  officially behind us, it's time to start taking the temperature of the MVP race. Which players are making a memorable impact with their play?

 We polled 16 NFL front office executives, coaches and personnel people with a simple question: Who is your league MVP through the first six weeks? From there, we were able to form a top-five list. One coach joked that MVP is basically a quarterback-only award so there's no need to list players at other positions. And yes, there are two early QB favorites. But our ballot shows just how wide open this race is this season, with multiple running backs and even a wide receiver landing in our top five.

 There is still a lot of time to shift things, but here is where a sample of people around the league feel things stand right now.

 

 

 1. Brock Purdy , QB, San Francisco 49ers -- 6 votes 
 Stats: 69.6% completion rate, 1,460 passing yards, 14 passing TDs, 2 INTs; 156 rushing yards, 1 rushing TD

 The case for Purdy: Purdy leads the NFL with an 83.1 QBR and is tied for the league lead with 14 touchdown passes. He also has just five sacks on the season, and his effectiveness as a runner has made him even more difficult to defend. But Purdy's superpower is his accuracy. He has a 5.1% completion percentage over expectation, per NFL Next Gen Stats, and he completes an NFL-high 88% of his passes to open receivers (3-plus yards of separation).

 The 49ers look like the NFL's best team at this stage with a 6-0 record, and it's largely because Purdy is having the best season of his career. He has helped San Francisco overcome an NFL-high 22 players being placed on injured reserve. As one AFC assistant general manager said, " Josh Allen is the easy answer. But my pick is Brock Purdy because of impact in that scheme despite all their injuries. He just finds a way to win. His numbers and the way he does it may not be as gaudy as Allen, but he's very valuable."

 

 He has had his MVP moments, too. Purdy's Week 2 performance vs. the Dolphins was the best QBR performance by any QB this season, with a near-perfect 99.7 rating. At one point, he completed 18 consecutive passes. He was the first QB in NFL history to throw for 250-plus yards with a 90% or higher completion percentage while also adding 30-plus rushing yards.

 Purdy's best pass of the season came a few weeks later -- a 55-yard deep connect with receiver Mike Evans vs. the Commanders on Monday to cap Week 6. Pressure was swarming fast, but he stuck in the pocket and delivered a dime to Evans.

 A common theme in talking to executives about Purdy is how he has redefined his narrative from being a system QB who is just a product of Kyle Shanahan's scheme to now seeing his unique feel for playing the position. "It looks easy and instinctual for him," one NFC coach said.

 Another AFC personnel director who selected Purdy said, "When you accept that all QBs need a system and support, it levels the playing field. MVP is who is playing the best, not just talent, so [Patrick] Mahomes, Allen and Matt Stafford can't win every year." Maybe this is Purdy's year.

 The case against Purdy: Purdy is only 14th among QBs in yards per game. He has been efficient but lacks the consistent explosive flash this season that we've seen from other contending quarterbacks, like Allen.

 There's also strength of schedule to consider. It doomed Drake Maye last season, as the Patriots played a relatively easy slate. And while the 49ers are in the tough NFC West, they have played just one team that currently has a winning record -- the 4-2 Broncos -- and aren't set to play one above .500 again until Week 11 (vs. the Vikings). Could the injuries catch up to the 49ers as the schedule tightens in the second half? The defense and receiver room have been decimated; San Francisco -- and Purdy -- seemingly can't afford many more blows.

 
 

 2. Josh Allen , QB, Buffalo Bills -- 4 votes 
 Stats: 66.7% completion rate, 1,504 passing yards, 9 passing TDs, 4 INTs; 240 rushing yards, 8 rushing TDs

 The case for Allen:  No one makes football look like a backyard football game quite like Allen, and he might be the most dangerous dual-threat playmaker in football with an NFL-high 17 total touchdowns. Is there a "fun to watch" factor in MVP voting? Because Allen would surely get a boost there.

 

 But this award is really about value, and it's easy to picture the Bills as a non-playoff team without Allen at the helm. His defense has performed worse than any candidate on this list -- Buffalo has given up 29-plus points in five of its six games. But the Bills are still 5-1 largely because of Allen's play on the other side of the ball.

 The way Allen performed late in their 37-34 OT victory over the Rams  is the most memorable MVP moment of any QB performance this season. Allen did it primarily with his legs, rushing for career-high 121 yards -- including 91 in the fourth quarter and overtime. Allen had a 93.3 QBR in that win. As one NFC defensive coach said, "It's gotta be Josh Allen right now. He won the game vs. the Rams by himself!! Damn he's good!!"

 Coach Joe Brady has empowered Allen to be himself as a loose playmaker more than ever, and so far, the reward has outweighed the risk. Allen's "no, no, nooo ... yes!" shovel touchdown pass to Keon Coleman in last week's win over the Raiders is a perfect example of him putting on his superhero cape to save the day in unorthodox and often wild ways.

 The case against Allen:  Although Allen makes memorable plays, his completion percentage and passing yards per game rank toward the back end of the top 10 among QBs. Allen has referenced working through mechanical tweaks in his throwing motion. And if he ultimately loses the award to Purdy, the slight edge in accuracy could be the difference.

 And while Allen's aggressiveness is a fun asset, it occasionally burns him into making a bad turnover -- like he did in throwing an interception into double coverage in Week 4 loss to the Patriots . Allen will have to keep the turnovers down to win this award.

 
 

 3. Kenneth Walker III , RB, Kansas City Chiefs -- 3 votes 
 Stats: 106 rushes, 665 rushing yards, 6 rushing TDs; 14 catches, 95 receiving yards, 2 receiving TDs

 The case for Walker:  Walker leads the NFL by far with 52 broken tackles, per NFL Next Gen Stats, breaking a tackle on a league-high 43% of his touches. But it's not just power. Close your eyes, critics of Walker's speed: According to Next Gen Stats, he has reached 15-plus mph on 23 different carries this season (tied for the second most in the league) and has two of the four running plays leaguewide to hit 21-plus mph. It has helped him to a healthy 6.3 yards per carry on the season.

 Walker said coach Andy Reid had a summer conversation with him stating the belief that Walker could be a three-down player and prove that he was more than the bruiser back he had been stereotyped as due to limited receiving reps. Walker has become a reliable passing game playmaker, forcing defenses to remain honest in their defensive scheme.

 

 And Walker's destruction has really forced defenses to completely change how they play the 5-0 Chiefs. An AFC wide receiver coach who picked Walker said, "Biggest thing is he's taken off so much load from Mahomes coming off injury. He's the center of their offense right now. He's been the best free agent pickup in [the] whole league."

 The case against Walker: The last non-QB to win MVP was Adrian Peterson , who rushed for more than 2,000 yards and came just 8 yards from the single-season rushing record in 2012. Despite his excellent start, Walker shares a backfield with Patrick Mahomes, who will likely garner more MVP love and offensive workload share as the season goes on and is more removed from his ACL surgery .

 Chiefs coaches have also been open about decreasing Walker's workload and giving more touches to rookie Emmett…

title: Judging overreactions to NFL Week 7: McCarthy-led Giants are NFC East favorites?
summary: Will J.J. McCarthy bring the Giants to the postseason? Are the Vikings headed for a bye? How bad do the 49ers need Mike Evans back? Let's overreact to Sunday's games.
full_text:
Well, if one of your Week 6 takeaways was that the Texans were going to be just fine after all, Week 7 might have suggested you were overreacting.

 That's the beauty of the middle of the NFL season, isn't it? Just when we think we have stuff figured out, the league still shows the ability to surprise us. The Falcons handed the 49ers their first loss of the season. The Steelers and Browns are 5-2 and tied for first place in the AFC North. J.J. McCarthy is winning road games for the Giants.

 So we keep doing this weekly exercise here because it's fun, and we do it fully aware that we have no idea what the rest of the season -- or even next week! -- will bring. Here's our Week 7 overreactions column, where we look at five potential takeaways from all the action and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational stretches. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the bottom.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 McCarthy can lead Giants to playoffs? 
 49ers can't afford to be without Evans? 
 Bengals need to trade for a star RB? 
 Vikings will be the NFC's top seed? 
 Nix, Broncos offense are back? 
 Fantasy overreactions 

 
 

 

 J.J. McCarthy can lead the Giants to the playoffs 
 Acquired from the Vikings in a trade almost a month ago, McCarthy got his first start for the Giants on Sunday in Houston. He threw for 243 yards in the fourth quarter the week before in a relief effort against the Saints, which was enough to earn him the No. 1 spot on the Giants' QB depth chart for Week 7. He drew a tough assignment against Houston's fearsome defense, but Giants coach John Harbaugh decided McCarthy was up for it, and he was right.

 

 McCarthy looked extremely comfortable and confident all day, ripping throws into tight windows and operating the offense cleanly. Giants coaches wanted to see a smooth operation, and after the game Harbaugh pointed out that there were no procedural penalties or glaring errors. The run game sprang to life, gaining 188 yards on 34 carries and winning the game in overtime when Cam Skattebo got New York into field goal range with a 42-yard run and Devin Singletary rendered the kick unnecessary with a 30-yard touchdown run on the next play. McCarthy was 20-for-28 for 252 yards and no turnovers. He looked very much like he belonged.

 Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION 

 No one has wanted to take this seriously, but the first-place Giants are 4-2-1 and will carry at least a 1.5-game NFC East lead into Week 8 regardless of what happens between the Cowboys and Eagles on Monday night. Harbaugh has made a major difference in his first season as Giants head coach. They're avoiding mistakes, overcoming injuries and finding ways to win. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy called an outstanding game for McCarthy. Skattebo bounced back after last week's soft benching and said after the game that he agreed with and appreciated the way it was handled by the coaching staff. Edge rusher Abdul Carter basically dominated the second half on defense. Cornerback Deonte Banks shadowed Nico Collins effectively.

 

 The Giants are playing very good team football right now. Given what we saw in Minnesota, McCarthy is a tough guy to count on. But he's also talented enough to have been picked 10th in the 2024 NFL draft, and it's entirely possible that what he needed was a new situation. There is a world where he flops completely. There is a world where he's inconsistent the rest of the way and the Giants don't have enough around him to cash in. But there's also absolutely a world in which he and they play just well enough to win a bad NFC East. Right now, the math tells us that it's absolutely possible, and the Giants are the betting favorite to win their division.

 
 

 The 49ers can't afford to be without Mike Evans 
 Evans' Achilles injury left him unable to go in San Francisco's Week 7 game in Atlanta. With Deebo Samuel Sr . also out , the Niners were down to four wide receivers. Brock Purdy targeted Jacob Cowing , Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks a combined 14 times. He targeted his running backs 14 times and his tight ends 10 times. It was Purdy's worst game of the season, as his two interceptions doubled his 2026 total and his 54.3 QBR was his first time under 65 this year. In another first, the 49ers lost to the Falcons to fall to 6-1.

 

 Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION 

 One reason the 49ers were able to survive their ridiculous rash of injuries and start 6-0 was that they hadn't really suffered a significant injury to any of their pillars. I'm talking about Purdy, George Kittle , Christian McCaffrey , Fred Warner and Trent Williams . (When I said this on TV last week, some people yelled "But Nick Bosa !" at me, but Bosa has missed 22 games over the past three seasons. If he's a pillar, he isn't exactly a load-bearing one.)

 Evans is so new there that I hesitated to initially count him in that group, but the 49ers looked lost without him Sunday. Evans' ability to win contested catches, particularly in the red zone and end zone, gives the 49ers an element their other wide receivers don't -- even when all the other guys are healthy. Not having him made the Niners easier to defend, and the fact that McCaffrey left this game for a while with an injury of his own didn't help, either.

 

 Purdy has a QBR of 90 this season when Evans is on the field, and the quarterback has thrown 10 touchdown passes to two interceptions. When Evans isn't playing, Purdy's QBR drops to 56, with five touchdown passes and two interceptions. The 49ers head into a much-needed Week 8 bye, after which they hope to get Evans and a few other key guys back. Evans was an important pickup this offseason as the 49ers were able to lure the longtime Buccaneer out of Tampa Bay. He has shown why when he has played, and he also showed why when he didn't.

 
 

 The Bengals need to trade for Saquon Barkley or Jonathan Taylor 
 Cincinnati basically took the first half off Sunday and still managed to crush the Lamar Jackson -less division-rival Ravens 35-13 . The Bengals outscored Baltimore 35-0 in the second half, which sounds crazy because it is. The last team to be outscored by 35 or more points in a second half was the 2015 Colts, who got outscored by 39 by the Jaguars. Baltimore had never been outscored by 35 in a half until Sunday.

 After trailing 13-0 at halftime, the Bengals dominated the second half on the strength of Joe Burrow 's arm. The quarterback was 22-for-30 for 292 yards and four touchdown passes. When everyone is healthy, the Bengals' passing offense is about as reliable a unit as there is in the league. The Bengals' run game this season has been anything but. Cincinnati entered Sunday's action ranked 27th in the league with 82.8 rush yards per game, and it ran for 73 yards on 20 carries Sunday. The Bengals are 4-2 and a half game behind that weird Pittsburgh/Cleveland first-place tie in the division, but the Bengals have not been able to run the ball at all, and they would love to find a way to balance the offense if they're going to make the run they expect to make.

 

 Verdict: OVERREACTION 

 Before I start, I want to make it clear that we have no idea whether the Eagles or Colts have or will have any interest in trading their star running backs. But even if they do, it would be very unlike Cincinnati to surrender draft capital for them. Chase Brown has been a very good back for several seasons now. He ran for 990 yards and seven touchdowns in 2024 and 1,019 yards and six touchdowns in 2025. And even though he hasn't been good on the ground this season, Brown is still a factor in the passing game.

 

 Brown isn't the only problem with the Bengals' run game, and his track record indicates a good chance of him improving as the season goes along. If I were the Bengals, I'd be looking harder at potentially available linebackers or defensive backs ahead of the trade deadline than running backs.

title: Breaking down Cowboys-Eagles MNF matchup in wide-open NFC East
summary: Both teams enter the game 2-4, looking far from formidable and staring up at the 4-2-1 division-leading Giants.
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle Kenny Clark summed up the state of the NFC East pretty darn well last week. 

 "We lost and we're seeing everybody else lose," he said. 

 From Weeks 5 to 6, the NFC East is the first division in NFL history to go winless in consecutive weeks in which all teams in the division played a game, according to ESPN Research. The New York Giants  (4-2-1) and Washington Commanders  (1-4-1) came into the season without great expectations, but the Philadelphia Eagles and Cowboys were supposed to be the class of the division and Monday's game ( 8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN/ABC ) is a matchup of two potential NFC powers looking to get an early advantage in playoff positioning. 

 Instead, both teams enter 2-4, looking far from formidable and staring up at the division-leading Giants. 

 

 The Eagles can vouch for Murphy's Law. They've dealt with one blow after another, the most recent being the loss of franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts because of blood clots in his lungs . They've scored 24 points or fewer in nine straight games and are losers of four straight.

 The Cowboys needed an uptick in defensive play this season to complement their high-flying offense. Instead, the defense has been about as giving as ever and the offense has gotten worse from a season ago. 

 So, it's not how either team drew it up. But with every team scrambling, the NFC East crown is as gettable as ever. 

 "You're not looking too far ahead, but the NFC East is struggling and the NFC East is really asking for someone to take it over," Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said. "It's going to be a team that figures it out and starts playing at a high level. We have the opportunity. We have that chance. Even with all these injuries and with all the crazy things that are happening, we have a lot of talent." 

 ESPN's Eagles reporter Tim McManus, Cowboys reporter Todd Archer and national NFL reporter Dan Graziano dive deep on two of four NFC contenders before their "Monday Night Football" matchup.

 

 

 Where do things stand with Eagles' and Cowboys' head coaches? 

 

 Nick Sirianni has a 61-28 record since taking over as coach in Philadelphia, has led the team to five playoff appearances in as many seasons and has gotten to the Super Bowl twice, winning one of them. You'd think he'd have a good bit of equity built up. 

 That's being tested in 2026 with the Eagles in a four-game skid, dropping their record to 5-9 over the past 14 games dating to last season. Sirianni's in-game decision-making has had a hand in the current losing streak, though a depleted roster hit by injury, retirement ( Lane Johnson ) and trade ( Cam Jurgens ) is the primary culprit. 

 The offense is lost right now and has had its share of issues during his tenure. Sirianni is a former offensive coordinator but the Eagles have outsourced a good chunk of those responsibilities, with mixed results. If they hit on their offensive coordinator, the team tends to have great success and that OC often moves on to become a head coach. If they miss, the offense sags, the OC gets let go and they're back on the merry-go-round. It remains to be seen if that's a ride management wants to continue to sign up for. -- McManus 

 

 

 Brian Schottenheimer is not on the hot seat. Remember, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones has made only one in-season coaching change, and that came in 2010 when he had head-coach-in-waiting Jason Garrett on Wade Phillips' staff. He does not have such a potential replacement on this staff.

 Schottenheimer, however, has to figure out what ails the Cowboys, and the questions aren't only about the defense. He is the playcaller for an offense that was one of the best in the NFL last season but has been streaky, at best, through six games and off-kilter the past two.

 Schottenheimer's game management has come into question. How the Cowboys' 34-31 Week 3 loss to the Baltimore Ravens ended in Rio de Janeiro could tell the story of the season, as the mistakes made in the final 28 seconds let a potential overtime win turn into a loss.

 He is 9-13-1 in his first 23 games. If the Cowboys finish below .500 for a third straight season -- second under Schottenheimer -- with the moves Jones made in the offseason, the calls for the owner to make a coaching change will be loud.

 Criticism "comes with the territory. I think some of it is deserved. We've got to play better. I've got to coach better," Schottenheimer said.

 "When you grow up in a family that your dad's a head coach for over 20-something years, you understand that this is part of the job description. No one likes it. I block out most of it. Some of it gets to me doing this job and having to speak to you guys is part of that. But at the same time, I've got strong shoulders. I know what a great coach I am. I know what this team is capable of, and that's what I focus on." -- Archer 

 

 

 What to make of the quarterback matchup? 

 

 Tanner McKee , the 2023 sixth-round pick out of Stanford, will be making his fourth career start. This season has thrown a lot at him. The Eagles traded for Andy Dalton and had Dalton and McKee battle it out in the summer, with Dalton ultimately winning the job. Dalton threw a costly pick against the Bears in spot duty in Week 3  and was demoted to the No. 3 QB, then later released , giving the job back to McKee. 

 He got the start Sunday against the Carolina Panthers after learning late in the week that Hurts would be sidelined with blood clots. McKee did OK, going 26-of-45 for 215 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. 

 McKee is a rhythm thrower by nature. He'll test the middle of the field and can get hot. He doesn't have great escapability, though, meaning the patchwork offensive line will have to button up its protection, particularly against the blitz, which has been a major problem area to date. -- McManus 

 
 

 At the end of last season,  Dak Prescott  expressed frustration that his level of play did not correlate into wins when the Cowboys finished 7-9-1. He threw for 4,552 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions, but it didn't matter.

 Prescott has struggled in the past two games -- four interceptions and the offense has totaled 29 points -- but in the first four games he had eight touchdown passes and one pick. Yet the Cowboys were still only 2-2.

 Making it worse for the Cowboys, Prescott has been healthy.

 He is 33 and signed through 2028 but the defense has not been able to deliver, forcing the Cowboys' offense to be close to perfect. In the past two years, the Cowboys have had six games in which they have scored 24 points and lost, tied with Detroit and the Los Angeles Rams for most in the NFL. -- Archer 

 

 

 New coordinators: Why are they struggling to find their footing? 

 

 It was a bold initiative to attempt a significant scheme change on the fly with a first-time coordinator for a team that viewed itself as a contender. Sean Mannion played in the league as recently as 2023 and was handed the reins to the Philly offense despite entering with just two years of coaching experience. 

 Bumps were expected. But the success of the operation was always predicated on the offensive line holding up its end and that simply hasn't happened. Communication issues have run rampant along the makeshift front. It has been common to see defenders come free into the backfield while multiple offensive linemen try to block the same person, especially when facing a blitz look. 

 "I always want to point the finger at myself first and what can I be doing better as a teacher, as a leader of this offense, in terms of what schemes we're putting in and making sure it's crystal clear in terms of who's supposed to be doing what," Mannion said.

 In-game adjustments have been a big problem. The Eagles' offense ranks last in second-half points per game (5.0), total yards (101.2), first downs (5.3) and three-and-out rate (50%).

 Mannion has been lauded for his acumen and work…
