title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, stifling defense help Seahawks hand Chiefs first loss
summary: Seattle's bread and butter from its Super Bowl championship season -- Jaxon Smith-Njigba and defense -- was too much for the Chiefs.
full_text:
SEATTLE -- The Kansas City Chiefs  signed the Super Bowl MVP away from the Seattle Seahawks , but the defending champions still have the AP Offensive Player of the Year. Jaxon Smith-Njigba reminded everyone of that Sunday night.

 For all the attention Kenneth Walker III received this week as he prepared to face his former team amid a scorching start to the season, Smith-Njigba was the best offensive player at Lumen Field. His 150 receiving yards plus more dominant defense from coach Mike Macdonald's unit and a good-enough performance from Sam Darnold equaled a 20-3 Seahawks win over the previously unbeaten Chiefs (5-1).

 The Seahawks (4-3) snapped their two-game losing streak and picked up a game in the NFC West standings, with the San Francisco 49ers (6-1) losing earlier Sunday. Even with Darnold throwing another interception, Brian Fleury's offense took a noticeable step forward, as it totaled 410 yards and went 11-of-16 on third down.

 "Our backs were against the wall," Smith-Njigba said. "How we came out here as a brotherhood and fought ... the resiliency of our team is something special, and we're going to keep going."

 Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

 

 

 

 Seattle Seahawks (4-3) 
 Trend to watch:  Macdonald's defense has now gone 36 consecutive games without allowing a 100-yard rusher, the longest such streak in the NFL. Walker looked like the toughest test the Seahawks would face since that streak began midway through the 2024 campaign. He was leading the league in rushing despite the Chiefs having already had their bye, and he had rushed for at least 117 yards in four of their five contests. Seattle held him to 36 yards on 14 carries and allowed only 213 yards overall. Darnold and Seattle's offense haven't been consistent enough to completely quiet the questions about that side of the ball, but it's clear that the Seahawks can count on their defense -- which is allowing the second-fewest points of any team -- to keep them in every game.

 QB breakdown:  Darnold was rolling in the first half -- completing 13 of his first 17 attempts for 178 yards and a touchdown -- until he made another mistake that he can't make. His throw on second down into traffic in the back of the end zone in the final seconds of the first half was intercepted, costing Seattle at least three points. That was Darnold's eighth pick over the past five games. Overall, though, it was a better performance for the embattled quarterback (20-of-28 for 257 yards). He got the ball out quickly -- not taking a sack after taking five in each of the previous two games -- and extended plays when he had to.

 Stat to know:  Smith-Njigba leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns. Per ESPN Research, he's the first player in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) with at least 850 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns in his team's first seven games of a season. His 129 receiving yards in the first half Sunday were the most in any half in his NFL career and the most in any half by a Seahawk since Tyler Lockett in 2020 (133 in the first half at Arizona). --  Brady Henderson .

 Next game: vs. Chicago Bears  (Nov. 2, 8:15 p.m. ET)

 
 

 

 Kansas City Chiefs (5-1) 
 Even with Patrick Mahomes and Walker, players who have won a Super Bowl MVP, the Chiefs' best chance to score a touchdown Sunday was when cornerback Nohl Williams had the ball in his hands. The Chiefs' offense never reached the red zone, getting no closer than Seattle's 27-yard line. And even then, kicker Harrison Butker missed his second field goal, part of an unfulfilling night for Kansas City.

 Kansas City's offense struggled mightily against the Super Bowl champs, especially without its best tackles ( Josh Simmons and Jaylon Moore ) and wideouts ( Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton ). Mahomes was pressured on eight of his 15 dropbacks (53%) before halftime, pressure that led to an interception and only 37 first-half passing yards.

 One of the few bright spots for the Chiefs occurred in the final minute of the second quarter. Williams, a second-year player, made a leaping interception on Darnold's pass in the back of the end zone that was intended for wide receiver Rashid Shaheed . Williams even gave the Chiefs' offense a chance for points by returning his pick 65 yards. But that was the only real highlight for a Kansas City team that fell for the first time in 2026 -- and that has a trip to AFC West rival Denver lurking next week.

 Defensive breakdown:  Midway through the third quarter, the Seahawks had possessed the ball twice as much as the Chiefs and had run more than twice as many plays (51 to 24). The reason for such a disparity was that the Chiefs' defense couldn't get off the field, as the unit allowed the Seahawks to convert on 11 of 16 third downs. Even when longtime defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo blitzed, Darnold was able to find the easy answer. Most often, that answer was to throw the ball to Smith-Njigba, who shredded the Chiefs' secondary repeatedly. No other Seahawks pass catcher had double-digit targets. The Chiefs also never sacked Darnold, who was able to escape pressure a couple of times to gain 17 rushing yards.

 Most surprising performance:  Entering Sunday, the biggest spotlight was on Walker, who became the first Super Bowl MVP to play his former team the next season. Walker also began the week leading the league with 665 rushing yards. The Seahawks, who spent most of the game playing two deep safeties, never let Walker have a rush in which he gained at least 10 yards. Walker finished with just 36 yards on 14 carries.

 Trend to watch:  Brett Veach, the Chiefs' general manager, should continue to be interested in acquiring another wide receiver ahead of the trade deadline on Nov. 10 after the lack of production from the position. Without Rice, who missed Sunday's game with a strained right hamstring, and Thornton, who is on the injured reserve list after having surgery to repair his dislocated left ankle, the Chiefs' collection of wideouts -- Xavier Worthy , rookie Cyrus Allen , Justin Watson , Andrew Armstrong and Jalen Royals -- produced just six receptions for 39 yards. - Nate Taylor 

 Next game:  at  Denver Broncos  (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

title: Patriots must improve turnover differential if they want to win, other notes
summary: It's one of Mike Vrabel's four pillars of the team identity -- and New England is struggling with it after losing to the Bears on Thursday.
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

 1. Turnover differential: The 4-3 Patriots have not won the turnover differential in a game this season and posted a minus-1 in Thursday's competitive 30-24 road loss to the Bears .

 Looking for one thing that needs to change if the team hopes to get where it desires? Start there.

 Mike Vrabel's team, which thrives on a four-part identity  that prioritizes "ball security and ball disruption," is a shocking minus-7 in turnover differential entering next Sunday's road game against the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots' 14 giveaways are the second most in the NFL behind the winless Chargers' 15. And despite having a goal of creating three turnovers per game on defense, New England has totaled just seven overall.

 "We just have to keep working at it. Just within the defense, we have to find a way to manufacture those -- whether it's punching the ball out ..." said veteran safety Kevin Byard , who led the NFL last season with seven interceptions but is still looking for his first in 2026.

 

 Byard pointed to himself first, highlighting a fourth-quarter play Thursday night against quarterback Caleb Williams that could have helped turn around the turnover struggles. The Bears were deep in their own territory on third-and-9 with 4:59 remaining, holding a 27-21 lead, and Byard and fellow defensive backs Marcus Jones and Christian Gonzalez were in zone coverage. Williams delivered a laser to receiver Rome Odunze for 21 yards, just between Byard's outstretched diving reach and narrowly in front of Jones.

 "That play to Rome, the ball went maybe a millimeter above KB's finger. If it was a little lower, KB would have tipped it, and who knows what would have happened?" Gonzalez said.

 It was a big-time throw from Williams, a reminder of his rising stardom, which Byard acknowledged. But it also had potential to be a big-time defensive play.

 "Almost being able to get that window, Caleb made a terrific throw. But the way I see it for me, it's 'go make that play for your team.' It's millimeters, but that's how it is. This is a game of inches, and the story is Caleb made a helluva throw, but if I can get just a little bit closer, it's 'KB helped his team win the ballgame.' So that's the stuff I look at, to make those plays," he said.

 "That's what I was brought here to do, so I'm disappointed on my end from that point. One play doesn't obviously lose a game, but I just want to be able to make that play for my team."

 One of the first things Vrabel said after the game was, "We need to turn the ball over [defensively], and we have to tackle better."

 In games the Patriots have forced at least one turnover, they are 4-1. In games they haven't forced a turnover, they're 0-2 (Seahawks, Bears).

 

 Meanwhile, the one offensive turnover against the Bears -- quarterback Drake Maye 's inaccurate end zone pass in the second quarter to rookie tight end Eli Raridon  -- further highlighted the issue.

 Maye played well other than the miscue, which he called one of the turning points and a reminder of how one mistake can be the difference against a high-caliber opponent. Unlike some of his early-season turnovers, which were more decision-based, the pick was more about execution because the play could have been made -- as evidenced by Maye connecting with Raridon for a touchdown on the same play later in the game.

 "He'll learn from it, like he always does. I'm glad he's ours," Vrabel said.

 Last year, the Patriots finished with a plus-3 turnover differential -- 19 takeaways and 16 giveaways.

 2. Quiet A.J.: Since his return from a high right ankle sprain, receiver A.J. Brown has played 101 of 122 offensive snaps and been targeted 16 times, while totaling just six receptions for 75 yards.

 Not ideal, but he isn't discouraged.

 Brown said offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels attempted to get him involved early in Thursday's game, but a combination of the Bears focusing on taking him away and Maye making the right play by taking what was there led to Brown not registering his first catch until late in the first half.

 "I'm a vet. I understand how the game goes. I know what type of player I am," Brown said. "Every time I line up, I get a lot of attention, so teams try to take me away, and it gives a lot of opportunity for other guys to make plays -- and soften it up for me. And whenever I get my shots, I have to make them, too."

 

 One area Brown didn't address was his blocking, which showed up as a deficiency Thursday -- including on a first-quarter wide receiver screen in which he missed his assignment. It was a reminder that the Patriots could benefit from Brown showing more consistently the relentless mentality that has defined his career.

 3. AVT's contract: One of the unique aspects of the three-year, $42 million contract that guard Alijah Vera-Tucker signed with the Patriots in March is that he receives a record $250,000 for every game he is on the 46-man game-day roster. So with Vera-Tucker landing on injured reserve Thursday, forcing him to miss at least four games, that means he loses out on at least $1 million.

 4. TreVeyon's time:  During the past three weeks, running back TreVeyon Henderson 's usage has declined sharply, part of which can be traced to the ankle injury he sustained against the Raiders on Oct. 11. But after averaging 28 snaps per game in his first three contests of the year, he has averaged just 14.5 over the past two games he has played from start to finish.

 "TreVeyon will help us plenty here down the stretch," Vrabel said when asked about Henderson's limited action.

 Through seven games, Rhamondre Stevenson leads Patriots running backs with 64% of the snaps, followed by Henderson (27%) and Corey Kiner (12%).

 5. 'Close' theme: If there was a theme in the Patriots' locker room after Thursday's loss, it was that Vrabel reminded them about the importance of margin for error against top opponents -- if a play or two goes the other way, the result might be reversed. It was a more positive vibe than one might expect.

 Cornerback Marcus Jones said that Vrabel also told players, "We're close ... to being the team we want to be. Understanding how to respond is very important as well. That's something we've learned we can do."

 

 6. Snapping to it : Four topics with second-year center Jared Wilson , who has played 97% of the offensive plays through seven games:

 
 Moving from left guard to center : "Things have been going great. Of course, you have things here or there you want to clean up -- not perfect, we're all human ... every aspect can always get better, but mainly in the run game, for sure." 
 Why center is his favorite spot:  "Once they moved me over at Georgia, I was like, 'This is where I need to be.' I feel like I can show my athleticism there. I just love the position. It was something Kirby [Smart] thought I'd be really good at, and I trusted him. I just wanted to get on the field. Now I'm here, and love it." 
 How a bond is built with Maye:  "The reps are important. But also sitting down at lunch and talking. There's the [weekly] O-line dinners he pops in to." 
 Favorite parts about New England: "I like Boston. A really clean city." 
 
 7. Van Roten eligible : The Patriots have to be judicious with their decisions of whom to designate to return from injured reserve -- there's a limit of eight overall -- and some of those spots have already been accounted for (e.g. Brown, Marcus Bryant , etc.), while others seem like they will be decisively reserved (e.g. Mack Hollins , Romeo Doubs , etc.).

 A question potentially to be answered this week is whether veteran center/guard Greg Van Roten (hip) will be one of them? He's eligible for the first time and has been around the locker room of late, and the Patriots were so thin on the interior that they elevated Xavier Newman-Johnson  on Thursday from the practice squad as their backup…

title: Saints looking to regroup, fix run game going into bye week
summary: Katherine Terrell breaks down the Saints' historically bad performance running the ball vs. the Steelers.

title: Even Tyler Shough can't save Saints as run game falls to new lows
summary: The Saints' run game wasn't just bad in the loss to Pittsburgh -- it struggled on levels unseen in several decades.
full_text:
New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough tried to do it all against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris on Sunday.

 Shough ran right at defenders, dove for potential scores and led the team with 7 total rushing yards. Shough played the role of a quarterback who tried to put the team on his shoulders to win, but the odds weren't in his favor in the 16-10 Week 7 loss .

 The second-year quarterback entered the game with an injured left hand and took a hit to his right hand during the game as well. The Saints' run game came into the week ranked 21st with 97.3 yards per game and reached new lows with no other player eclipsing double digits in rushing.

 "Seventeen runs for 18 yards, it's going to be hard to win football games doing that," New Orleans coach Kellen Moore said.

 

 The Saints' run game wasn't just bad Sunday -- it struggled on levels unseen in several decades. It was just the third time in team history, and the first since the 1993 season, that a Saints player had not rushed for at least 10 yards in a game. Their 1.06 yards per rush was the fewest for a team with at least 15 attempts since the Carolina Panthers averaged 1.0 yard per rush in a Week 5 game in 2017 (28 rushes).

 Shough has admitted this season that he has tried to play too perfect, but with the way the Saints were failing to run the ball, the team would have needed a perfect game from him to win Sunday. They didn't get that, as Shough threw an interception in the red zone in the third quarter, his sixth interception and ninth turnover of the season.

 But Shough's play overall was a bright spot amid the struggles in the run game. He completed 30-of-38 passes for 278 yards and a touchdown. The score, a 1-yard pass to Devaughn Vele , capped a 52-yard drive in which 49 yards came through the air.

 Shough spent the game trying to play hero ball, but didn't get a chance to be the hero in the end, as the Steelers controlled the ball for the final 5:52. He did not get the ball back after the Saints punted following a final disastrous sequence on offense -- two batted-down passes and a sack.

 The Steelers sealed the game as 42-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers scrambled for 8 yards and a first down. Rodgers' run eclipsed the run totals for several Saints -- Shough's 7 yards, Kendre Miller 's 6 and Alvin Kamara 's 5.

 After the game, Shough admitted the lack of run game wasn't conducive to future success.

 "Yeah, it's not sustainable as far as they're going to -- they know what's coming in certain situations and they're a good defense," Shough said of the Steelers.

 

 When asked to clarify his comments about the lack of a run game, Shough said the one-dimensional game limits the ability to open up the offense.

 "We have a really dynamic passing game, and we can attack them in different ways, and we're able to do that, but in order to win against defenses like that, and you saw it kind of later in the game, they were able to just read and batted some balls down," Shough said. "It's tough in those scenarios whenever you have to get it out."

 Shough has had to hand off with his right hand at times due to a previous injury, and he appeared to injure his right hand as well after taking a sack from Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt .

 He got the hand looked at by athletic trainers and explained later that there was some pain but said it didn't affect his performance. However, per ESPN Research, Shough averaged 10.4 air yards per pass attempt before the sack and only 2.7 yards after.

 Moore waved off the notion the Saints were asking too much of Shough without a run game to help him.

 "You could say that about any quarterback," Moore said. "Any quarterback gets to team up with the run game, it just allows the mixed downs to look better, less obvious pass situations, and that's certainly something we have to address."

 

 The Saints head into their Week 8 bye with the run game on their minds and the intention to "really dig in and solve this thing," Moore said. Injuries have played a part, as left tackle Kelvin Banks has been on injured reserve for a month following ankle surgery, right guard Cesar Ruiz was out this week with a knee injury and running back Travis Etienne Jr . has also been on IR for a month with a hamstring issue.

 But the run game issues predate the Banks and Etienne injuries. Sunday marked the fifth game this season in which the Saints had fewer than 100 yards rushing per game.

 "We obviously have a bye week, we have to put a lot of work into it," Moore said. "I'm thinking there's too much ebbs and flows. There's weeks where it's good, there's weeks where it's not."

 Moore admitted there was frustration, especially after running the ball well against the New York Giants in Week 6, one of two games the Saints rushed the ball well this season. Moving forward, they'll have to figure out how to balance the load and take weight off Shough's shoulders.

 "Again, we've got to run the football better," Moore said. "We can't have a week like we did last week where we feel good about it, respond and put ourself in the situation we did today."

title: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
summary: The Pittsburgh QB is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."
full_text:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

 In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots . In Week 6 of 2026, he moved into a third-place tie with Peyton Manning with 539.

 "Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

 Rodgers supplanted Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in a loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025. But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that growing list of historic accomplishments.

 Among the milestones for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 7 he has appeared in 294), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. And after Week 7, he needs 2,027 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards . 

 This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

 
 Weeks: 
 Preseason | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 
 Remaining schedule 

 
 

 

 
 Preseason: 0-for-0, 0 yards, 0 INT, 0 sacks, 0 rushes 
 Despite early hints that Rodgers would take the field during the Steelers' first preseason under McCarthy, the veteran quarterback instead spent two games on the sideline and one on his couch at home. With Rodgers' top two receivers in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr . sidelined with preseason injuries, McCarthy opted to also keep his quarterback under wraps.

 

 Rodgers isn't a stranger to sitting out the preseason in recent years. He didn't play in any preseason games for the Steelers in 2025, nor for the New York Jets in 2024 following his season-ending left Achilles tear in Week 1 of the 2023 season.

 
 

 Week 1:  Steelers 20, Falcons 13 
 Rodgers' stat line: 221 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for -1 yard 
 Rodgers didn't break any records this week, but he pulled within one touchdown pass of Peyton Manning for fourth most in NFL history with his second-quarter throw to tight end Pat Freiermuth  for 6 yards. The touchdown toss was Rodgers' 232nd of the regular season. Rodgers had 26 pass attempts in the first half, his most attempts in the first half of a game since 2020 at Minnesota as a member of the  Green Bay Packers , per ESPN Research.

 After Sunday's game, coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to find more balance in his offense, which ran the ball just 21 times to Rodgers' 40 pass attempts. Rodgers, though, didn't mind all the throwing.

 "No, keep doing it," Rodgers said, urging his coach to keep calling passes. "Keep doing it."

 And although Rodgers and the Steelers got the win, the quarterback struggled under the pressure from the Falcons' front. He completed 3 of 12 attempts under pressure and was sacked twice. And continuing the trend from last season, Rodgers was also 3-of-12 on throws of 15 or more air yards. Some of those incompletions, though, were the result of drops by his receivers.

 

 "I liked the plan from Mike," Rodgers said. "I liked the playcalling. We took some shots. I felt like we had really close to having one of those really good games. If we come down with a couple of those, it obviously looks a little different on the scoreboard and stat sheet and stuff, but love my guys, love  DK [Metcalf] .

 

 

 Week 2: Patriots 20, Steelers 3 
 Rodgers' stat line: 187 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT, 4 sacks, 1 rush for 5 yards 
 Rodgers set two personal Steelers milestones in the team's Week 2 loss -- and not in a good way. Rodgers was off target on 26% of his throws (nine attempts) in the loss, his worst as a Steeler. The Patriots frustrated Rodgers with heavy pressures and blitzed on 19 of 44 dropbacks (43%), the second-highest rate he has faced with Pittsburgh. Against the blitz, he was 8-of-17 for 42 yards with two sacks and an interception. And he had his first interception against the blitz as a member of the Steelers.

 

 "It's frustrating, for sure," Rodgers said of not getting into the end zone at New England on Sunday. "The defense has been playing great. They've been holding [opponents to] 13 points a game in two games, and offensively I think we're averaging like eight points a game. That's not winning football."

 

 

 Week 3: Steelers 30, Bengals 27 
 Rodgers' stat line: 292 yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for 10 yards 
 It turns out Rodgers still has plenty left in the tank. A week after one of his worst performances as a Steeler, Rodgers bounced back with three passing touchdowns to help the offense put up a season-best 30 points and 411 yards in the win against the Cincinnati Bengals . Rodgers aired it out in the first quarter with two touchdown throws and 143 passing yards -- the most he has thrown in the first quarter since Week 6 of 2018 against the 49ers (170). Each of his touchdown passes traveled at least 20 air yards, marking his first time with multiple touchdowns of 20-plus air yards since he joined the Steelers. Entering Sunday's game, Rodgers was 0-of-9 on pass attempts of 20-plus air yards.

 "We definitely needed it because it was just uncharacteristic of us," Steelers wide receiver Ben Skowronek said of the offense's bounce-back performance. "Throughout camp, we felt really confident in what we were doing, moving the ball. And the first two weeks we just weren't us. So credit to the coaching staff, the guys in the building, we locked in this week and we knew we had to have it. We knew we could do it."

 

 After two weeks without much movement in the record books, Rodgers is starting to make some headway. Sunday's win marked the 165th of his career, tying him with Ben Roethlisberger for fifth most by a starting quarterback since positions were first tracked in 1950. With his first-quarter 38-yard touchdown throw to Roman Wilson , Rodgers also recorded his 233rd career game with at least one passing touchdown, tying Peyton Manning for the fourth most such games in NFL history.

 

 

 Week 4: Browns 27, Steelers 24 
 Rodgers' stat line: 299 yards, 3 TDs, 2 INTs, 5 sacks, 0 rushes 
 Rodgers spent a lot of time on the turf at Huntington Bank Field in what's scheduled to be his final Thursday night game (barring a late-season flex). Rodgers took 10 quarterback hits thanks to Cleveland's aggressive game plan, protection breakdowns and the quarterback's decisions to hold on to the ball as he looked for his pass catchers to get open against man coverage.

 

 All five of the sacks against Rodgers came as he faced man coverage, and on the season, he has been sacked an NFL-worst 12 times when facing man coverage -- seven more than any other quarterback. And while the offense largely stagnated through the second and third quarters, it came alive in the fourth as Rodgers aired it out with 43-, 28- and 22-yard completions to wide receiver DK Metcalf and a 21-yard touchdown throw threaded to Darnell Washington .

 Rodgers even tied the score at 24 with a quarterback sneak for a successful two-point conversion with less than two minutes to go.

 "I felt like there was no chance they'd be expecting that," Rodgers said. "So I just told them in the huddle, if I can this one, I'm going to sneak it.'"

 

 With the loss, Rodgers still has 13 wins on Thursdays and remains tied with Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott for second most all time.
